title: Retinal Neuroprotection: Exploring Novel and Repurposed Therapeutics
summary: Retinal neuroprotection is a critical area of research focused on preventing or slowing the degeneration of retinal neurons, which are essential for vision. Various retinal diseases, such as glaucoma, age-related macular degeneration (AMD), and diabetic retinopathy, can lead to significant vision loss or blindness due to the death of these neurons. Understanding the mechanisms underlying retinal neurodegeneration and finding effective neuroprotective strategies remains an urgent priority in ophthalmology. Recently, the concept of repurposing existing drugs that are already approved for other conditions has gained traction, offering a potentially expedited path to discovering effective treatments for retinal diseases.
image_alt: Retinal Neuroprotection: Exploring Novel and Repurposed Therapeutics

title: Smart sensors
summary: This Collection showcases original research that explore new materials and device architectures, sensor fusion strategies, and integration with machine learning or energy-harvesting technologies. Studies demonstrating scalable fabrication, robust operation in complex environments are particularly welcome.

Academic Stress and Mental Health in Higher Education: Integrative Approaches from Neurobiology to Institutional Contexts
summary: Academic stress is one of the most prevalent and impactful forms of stress experienced in higher education, with growing evidence linking it to adverse outcomes in mental health, cognitive functioning, emotional regulation, and academic performance. Traditionally addressed from a psychological lens, recent studies have demonstrated that academic stress also has biological, behavioral, and contextual dimensions, reflecting its complexity as a multifactorial phenomenon.

title: Best Practice Approaches for Mixed Methods Research in Psychological Science: Volume III
summary: Mixed methods research in psychological science has undergone significant evolution since its origins in the 1980s, emerging as a powerful paradigm capable of bridging the longstanding divide between qualitative and quantitative methodologies. While early debates revolved around entrenched positions and the feasibility of integration, recent decades have witnessed a surge in scholarly activity, widespread adoption, and deeper methodological innovations. Despite this progress, the rapid growth has resulted in a wide spectrum of approaches, conceptual disagreements (such as the distinction between mixed methods and multimethods), and variable design taxonomies. The field still grapples with the challenge of achieving true integration and conceptual clarity, particularly as mixed methods approaches become increasingly predominant across psychology and the broader social sciences.
image_alt: Best Practice Approaches for Mixed Methods Research in Psychological Science: Volume III

title: Contemporary Sports Coaching Pedagogies and Methodologies
summary: The role of sports coaching has evolved significantly over the past two decades, moving beyond traditional command-based approaches towards more holistic, learner-centered methods. Influenced by educational theory, sport psychology, and motor learning research, contemporary coaching pedagogies emphasize athlete autonomy, decision-making, and psychosocial well-being alongside performance outcomes. Concepts such as ecological dynamics, nonlinear pedagogy, and athlete-centered coaching have gained prominence, offering innovative ways to design learning environments that replicate the complexities of real-game situations. Despite growing academic interest, there remains a need to better understand the psychological and behavioral mechanisms underpinning these approaches and how they influence both skill acquisition and athlete development across different sports and performance levels.
journals: Frontiers in Sports and Active Living

title: Glial interfaces in neuroinflammation and neurodegeneration: Mechanisms to therapies
summary: Glial cells have emerged as central regulators of neural homeostasis, immune surveillance, and disease propagation throughout the central nervous system (CNS)—including the brain, spinal cord, and retina. Their dynamic interactions with neurons and components of the neurovascular unit play a pivotal role in maintaining brain homeostasis and determining the outcome of neuroinflammatory responses. Increasing evidence highlights that their interactions with neurons and the neurovascular unit are fundamental in shaping the onset and progression of neurodegenerative diseases such as Alzheimer’s disease. Disruptions in glial communication and signaling at the neurovascular interface lead to impaired blood-brain barrier integrity, persistent inflammation, and neuronal dysfunction, thereby accelerating neurodegeneration. title: Neurogenic Shoulder Abduction Disorder
summary: Neurogenic shoulder abduction disorder is caused by trauma- or non-trauma-induced damage to the C5 nerve root or its branches, resulting in denervation of the muscles (supraspinatus, infraspinatus, and deltoid). It is a common shoulder joint disease that seriously affects patients' daily lives and work abilities. The etiology of non-traumatic C5 nerve root lesions causing shoulder abduction disorder is complex, such as neuritis, nerve root diseases, etc. Currently, drug therapy - including vitamin B1, B6, mecobalamin, and coenzyme Q10 - is mainly used. However, the therapeutic effect is limited. For traumatic C5 nerve root injuries, surgical repair is primarily employed at present, such as accessory nerve transfer to the suprascapular nerve, triceps branch of the radial nerve transfer to the axillary nerve, or intercostal nerve transfer to the axillary nerve, etc.

title: AI and Robotics for Smart Agriculture
summary: Robotics and Artificial Intelligence (AI) have been a cornerstone in many global industries including transportation, manufacturing and aerospace. Meanwhile, the global demand for plant and livestock production is rising rapidly due to the growing population. The agricultural industry around the world is facing a critical challenge to meet this demand because of a lack of arable land for expanding current production, shortage of farm labor, and worker health and safety issues such as exposure to chemicals, ladder falls and repetitive motion injuries, as well as the impact of extreme weather events and the changing climate. Many researchers and technology companies have been developing and evaluating new approaches and applications of AI and robotic technologies in agriculture to address these challenges. image_alt: AI and Robotics for Smart Agriculture

title: AI for Neuroergonomics: Decoding the Brain and the Body in the Wild
summary: Neuroergonomics lies at the intersection of neuroscience, neuroengineering, artificial intelligence, and human factors. It aims to understand and support brain and body function during real-world tasks, where noise, movement, context changes, and safety constraints can limit the direct translation of laboratory findings into operational environments. In parallel, AI is rapidly reshaping how we analyze neurophysiological and behavioral signals, design user-friendly neurotechnology, and enable new forms of human–machine symbiosis and interaction.
image_alt: AI for Neuroergonomics: Decoding the Brain and the Body in the Wild

title: AI, Robotics, and Digital Health - Transformative Potential of AI and Robotics in Mental Health: Insights into Hybrid Care Paradigms
summary: The convergence of artificial intelligence (AI) and robotics with digital health is redefining psychological and medical care. This interdisciplinary Research Topic interrogates how these technologies reshape health psychology and healthcare—from AI and robotic mental health interventions to ethical dilemmas in algorithmic care.

title: Advanced interventions for self-regulation and neuroplasticity, Volume II
summary: A variety of interventions have shown strong potential for enhancing self-regulation and fostering neuroplasticity. These interventions include neurofeedback, neuromodulation, virtual reality, mental imagery, and music-based approaches. They have demonstrated significant promise in modulating neural and cognitive processes, thus facilitating adaptive responses to various stressors and challenges. Understanding the efficacy, mechanisms, and potential applications of these interventions is crucial for promoting mental well-being and regulating nervous system functions.

title: Anti-Amyloid Immunotherapy in Alzheimerʼs Disease: Two Years of Clinical Experience and Emerging Real-World Evidence
summary: Since the landmark approvals of lecanemab and donanemab, anti-amyloid immunotherapy has marked a paradigm shift in the pharmacological treatment of Alzheimerʼs disease. Beyond controlled trials, clinicians now face questions of implementation, monitoring (including ARIA), biomarker validation, treatment sequencing, and equitable access. Regional differences in health policy, reimbursement, and infrastructure have produced variable adoption rates, creating an urgent need for shared global and pharmacological insights.
image_alt: Anti-Amyloid Immunotherapy in Alzheimerʼs Disease: Two Years of Clinical Experience and Emerging Real-World Evidence

title: Applications of Telehealth in Clinical Neuropsychology and Geriatric Psychiatry
summary: Advances in telehealth in recent years have prompted a rapid transformation in how neuropsychological and psychiatric services are being delivered. These developments have augmented traditional approaches, facilitating examination and remote access to neuropsychological and psychiatric assessment and intervention. Notably, this is beneficial for vulnerable individuals, such as the population of older adults. While this shift presents opportunities for optimizing neuropsychological and psychiatric care, significant challenges persist regarding the effectiveness, accessibility, and personalized application of telehealth modalities. Recent studies showcase digital platforms and artificial intelligence's potential in enhancing the quality and reach of neuropsychological and psychiatric services. However, discussion continues around their broader applicability and ethical considerations like access to physical examination, the ability of older adults to use modern technologies and privacy c
image_alt: Applications of Telehealth in Clinical Neuropsychology and Geriatric Psychiatry

title: Artificial Intelligence and Advanced Digital Processing Techniques to Improve Biomedical Imaging
summary: Over the past few decades, artificial intelligence has steadily become a major driver of innovation in the field of medical imaging, transforming how clinical images are acquired, analyzed, and interpreted. Advanced machine learning, deep learning, and computational techniques are enabling more accurate diagnoses, faster clinical decision-making, and increasingly personalized treatments. At the same time, the integration of digital systems and intelligent devices has opened new avenues for non-invasive, scalable, and cost-effective diagnostic solutions. Despite the remarkable progress achieved, the use of these technologies in personalized healthcare continues to evolve rapidly, presenting substantial opportunities for further research and development.
image_alt: Artificial Intelligence and Advanced Digital Processing Techniques to Improve Biomedical Imaging

title: Bio-inspired Robots at the Air-Water Interface
summary: The field of bio-inspired robotics at the air-water interface is rapidly advancing with the miniaturization of environmental sensing technologies. This evolution, characterized by developments like low-cost environmental DNA (eDNA) methods and integrated solid-state sensors, positions small-scale robotics as pivotal players in aquatic data collection. Recent studies have highlighted the limitations of current aquatic monitoring systems, which often rely on large, costly vehicles needing deployment from research vessels. The need for more extensive environmental sampling expands the scope beyond what a single, expensive agent can accomplish, posing significant questions regarding operational modes, range, and autonomy necessary for successful aquatic system monitoring.

title: Biomarkers for Optimizing Immunotherapies in Multiple Sclerosis and Autoimmune CNS Diseases
summary: Multiple sclerosis (MS) is the most debilitating, immune-mediated, and neurodegenerative disease among young adults, although there are patients at both ends of the age spectrum, with pediatric or late-onset forms.

title: Brain Injury after Hypoxia/Ischemia: Mechanisms, Pathogenesis, and Potential Therapeutic Interventions
summary: Brain injury resulting from hypoxia (oxygen deprivation) or ischemia (restricted blood flow) represents a major challenge in medical research and clinical practice. Such injuries, often due to stroke, cardiac arrest, or asphyxiation, lead to significant consequences, including motor deficits, cognitive impairments, and increased mortality. The pathogenesis of these injuries involves a complex interplay of cellular and molecular events, including oxidative stress, inflammation, metabolic disruptions, excitotoxicity, and apoptosis. A deep understanding of these mechanisms is essential for developing effective therapeutic interventions. This research topic aims to thoroughly investigate the mechanisms driving hypoxia/ischemia-induced brain injury and identify novel therapeutic strategies to mitigate damage, promoting neuronal recovery and survival.
image_alt: Brain Injury after Hypoxia/Ischemia: Mechanisms, Pathogenesis, and Potential Therapeutic Interventions

title: Camouflaging, Masking, and Compensation Strategies in Autism, ADHD, and other Neurodevelopmental Conditions
summary: In recent years, research into camouflaging in autism, i.e., masking or compensating for autistic traits to appear neurotypical, has gained momentum. Empirical studies have provided insights into the nature of the phenomenon and its potential consequences for functioning and mental health. Lived-experience accounts suggest that camouflaging may, in certain contexts, support social participation and employment. However, autistic individuals also report significant costs, including energy depletion, burnout, identity confusion, and reduced access to support. These experiences are increasingly supported by quantitative data, although the current evidence base remains largely correlational. Additional research, employing diverse methodologies, including qualitative and quantitative, cross-sectional and longitudinal designs, are required to deepen our understanding of camouflaging and its impacts.
image_alt: Camouflaging, Masking, and Compensation Strategies in Autism, ADHD, and other Neurodevelopmental Conditions

title: Cognitive Changes in Neurodegenerative Diseases: Early Markers, Clinical Management and Therapeutic Avenues
summary: Neurodegenerative diseases represent a major challenge for healthcare systems worldwide, with cognitive decline being among their earliest and most disabling manifestations. Understanding how cognitive processes deteriorate across different disorders is crucial for identifying reliable early markers and tailoring clinical interventions. This Research Topic aims to bring together studies investigating cognitive alterations in neurodegenerative conditions such as Alzheimer’s disease, Parkinson’s disease, frontotemporal dementia, and related disorders. We welcome contributions exploring neural and behavioral signatures of cognitive impairment, novel assessment tools, and predictive models of disease progression. Equally encouraged are papers addressing the management of cognitive symptoms, as well as innovative approaches to cognitive rehabilitation and digital therapeutics. By integrating evidence from neuroscience, neuropsychology, and clinical practice, this collection seeks to advance

title: Eco-Affective Cognition: How Environmental Change Shapes Perception, Emotion, and Decision-Making
summary: As global environmental change accelerates, humans are increasingly exposed to a spectrum of climate-related stressors such as extreme weather events, ecosystem degradation, pollution, biodiversity loss, and landscape instability. These pervasive conditions impact not only physical health but also fundamental processes of perception, attention, risk evaluation, emotion–cognition interactions, and higher-order decision-making. Growing evidence shows that environmental instability shapes how people detect threats, allocate attention, interpret uncertainty, and engage in reasoning. Climate-related emotional states—such as eco-anxiety, solastalgia, ecological grief, and future-oriented worry—influence judgment, memory, executive function, and behavioural intentions, while hope, agency, and collective efficacy are key drivers of adaptation and engagement. Despite a surge in relevant studies, contributions remain fragmented across fields and lack integrative cognitive frameworks, pointing to
image_alt: Eco-Affective Cognition: How Environmental Change Shapes Perception, Emotion, and Decision-Making

title: Empowering Women in Sport: Enhancing Health and Well-being Through Exercise for Female Oncology Patients
summary: The role of physical activity (PA) and exercise in the lives of female cancer survivors is increasingly recognized for its profound impact on their recovery, long-term well-being, and reintegration into sports settings. While cancer treatment can lead to fatigue, muscle loss, and decreased physical function, structured and individualized exercise programs have been shown to improve strength, endurance, and overall physical and mental health, significantly influencing their ability to participate in athletic activities. Despite this growing body of evidence, research focusing specifically on the intersection of oncology and sports participation for female survivors remains limited.
journal: Frontiers in Sports and Active Living

title: Impacts of substance use/exposure on early brain: Volume II
summary: The developing brain is highly susceptible to the effects of substance use, making it particularly vulnerable during the early stages of life. Recognizing the specific impacts that substance use can have during this critical period is important for the promotion of brain health and preventing long-term consequences. This article collection aims to delve deeply into the intricate relationship between substance use and the developing brain, shedding light on the complex neurological, cognitive, and behavioral consequences that arise.

title: Multimodal Mechanisms of Depression and Suicidal Behaviour: Integrating Genetic, Neural, and Environmental Perspectives
summary: Depression and suicidality remain among the most pressing public health challenges worldwide and are major contributors to premature mortality. Despite decades of research, the biological mechanisms linking depressive symptoms and suicidal behavior are still not clearly understood. Increasing evidence suggests that disturbances in brain function and stress regulation, together with genetic and environmental influences, may play important roles in this relationship. Integrating insights from neuroimaging, electrophysiology, genetics, and related disciplines holds promise for identifying biomarkers and advancing our understanding of the complex pathways underlying depression and suicidality. This Research Topic welcomes contributions that explore these multimodal mechanisms and support the development of targeted strategies for prevention and treatment.
image_alt: Multimodal Mechanisms of Depression and Suicidal Behaviour: Integrating Genetic, Neural, and Environmental Perspectives

title: Multimodal Perception and Biosignal Integration for Adaptive Healthcare Robotics
summary: Robotics is playing an increasingly vital role in healthcare, particularly through systems that monitor, assist, and respond to patient needs. A key enabler of this transformation is the integration of biosignals and multimodal perception—leveraging physiological data such as heart rate, EEG, EMG, and thermal imaging to adapt robot behavior in real time. These signals, when fused with visual, auditory, and contextual information, allow healthcare robots to provide personalized, safe, and effective interventions. However, challenges remain in standardizing biosignal interpretation, real-time data fusion, and ensuring robustness in clinical and home environments.
image_alt: Multimodal Perception and Biosignal Integration for Adaptive Healthcare Robotics

title: Nature and Youth Mental Health: Pathways, Practices and Community-Based Approaches
summary: Nature is increasingly recognized as a valuable resource for supporting mental health and well-being, particularly among adolescents and young adults. This population is especially vulnerable to psychological distress due to rapid emotional, cognitive, and social transitions. While growing evidence shows that contact with natural environments can reduce stress, improve mood, and enhance resilience, nature remains underutilized in youth mental health strategies.
topics: adolescent and young adult mental health

title: Neural Computation in real and artificial neural networks
summary: Neural computation is fundamental to understanding intelligence and adaptive behavior in both biological organisms and artificial systems. From the intricate dynamics of the brain to the powerful algorithms driving modern AI, the ability to process information, learn, and make decisions arises from complex networks of interconnected units. While biological neural networks have evolved to achieve improved efficiency and robustness, artificial neural networks draw inspiration from these principles to solve challenging computational problems. The interplay between these two domains offers a rich landscape for scientific inquiry, with advances in one often illuminating pathways for progress in the other, driving our understanding of intelligence itself. This Research Topic aims to explore this fascinating intersection.

title: Neuroplasticity and Neuromodulation in Stress-Related and Affective Disorders: Mechanisms and Translational Applications
summary: Chronic stress and affective dysregulation profoundly impact brain function and mental health. Alterations in neuroplasticity, cortical excitability, and network connectivity are increasingly recognized as key mechanisms underlying stress-related psychiatric disorders, including depression, anxiety, and substance-use conditions. Understanding how these neurobiological changes occur—and how they can be modified through neuromodulation and other interventions—is essential for advancing next-generation treatments. This Research Topic aims to explore the mechanisms of brain plasticity in stress and affective disorders and to highlight neuromodulation-based strategies that target these mechanisms to improve cognitive and emotional outcomes. By bridging clinical psychiatry, neuroscience, and neurotechnology, the collection seeks to deepen our understanding of how stress alters brain systems and how plasticity can be harnessed for therapeutic benefit. title: Physical Literacy Across the Lifespan
summary: At the beginning of the 21st century, the concept of physical literacy (PL) gained significant popularity, building on decades of research in physical education, motor development, and health promotion. This marked a shift away from traditional approaches focused on sport-specific skills or fitness testing, toward a more holistic understanding of human development. Over time, PL has gained substantial traction globally and continues to evolve. It is increasingly recognized as a foundational element for lifelong participation in physical activity—particularly in response to growing concerns around sedentary lifestyles and physical inactivity levels across all age groups.

title: Plant Adaptations in Extreme Environments from Wild Species to Crop Systems
summary: Plants growing in extreme environments, such as arid deserts, high-altitude and latitude, and regions with saline soil, are exposed to severe abiotic stresses including drought, temperature fluctuations, high UV radiation, and elevated salinity. Understanding how plants physiologically and genetically adapt to these challenging conditions is essential for revealing underlying mechanisms of adaptation and evolution, as well as informing strategies to improve plant resilience in the face of increasing global environmental stresses. Recent studies have highlighted specific physiological responses, such as osmotic adjustment, antioxidant defense mechanisms, and distinct cellular alterations that plants use to mitigate stress, including polyploidization and genome dosage effect in crop species. image_alt: Plant Adaptations in Extreme Environments from Wild Species to Crop Systems

title: Redefining Resilience: Advancing Public Health through Individual, Family, and Community Adaptation in A Changing World
summary: Resilience research within public health explores how individuals, families, and communities withstand, adapt to, and recover from adversity. In an era marked by ecological disasters, economic volatility, pandemics, and increasing social inequities, understanding resilience as a multifaceted, systemic process has never been more crucial. While significant insights have emerged across psychological, social, and ecological domains, questions remain about the mechanisms that foster resilience and the complex interplay between individual, familial, and community factors. Recent studies have advanced our knowledge regarding resilience-building, yet gaps persist in linking these insights to health equity and the ability of health systems to respond to ongoing crises. Systems theory is now being leveraged to better understand how resilience functions across multiple levels—offering a more integrative approach that underscores the necessity for interdisciplinary research and practical implemen

title: Resource‑ and Energy‑Aware Multi‑Robot Operations: Scheduling, Recharging, and Long‑Horizon Persistence
summary: Battery capacity, recharge logistics, and computational budgets are now the primary bottlenecks for scaling multi robot systems from short demos to dependable, 24/7 operations. Long horizon missions—warehousing, inspection, agriculture, environmental monitoring, and public safety—require fleets to coordinate tasks, routes, and recharge events while accounting for battery aging, stochastic demand, uncertain travel times, and heterogeneous platforms. Classical planning or perception advances alone are insufficient: persistence hinges on resource models, predictive energy usage, and infrastructure aware scheduling that closes the loop between algorithms, chargers, and the physical environment. This Research Topic focuses on the algorithmic and systems foundations that make multi robot autonomy sustainable and economically viable over days to months, emphasizing measurable mission availability, throughput, safety under energy constraints, and total cost of ownership.
image_alt: Resource‑ and Energy‑Aware Multi‑Robot Operations: Scheduling, Recharging, and Long‑Horizon Persistence

title: Reticulate Evolution and Speciation Dynamics in Beetles (Coleoptera)
summary: Beetles (Coleoptera) represent one of the most diverse radiations on Earth, occupying an extraordinary diversity of ecological niches. Understanding the processes that generate and maintain this diversity is fundamental to evolutionary biology. While classical models of beetle diversification emphasize divergent, bifurcating speciation, growing genomic evidence indicates that reticulate evolution - through hybridization, introgression, and other mechanisms of interspecific gene exchange - may be more widespread than previously recognized and play a significant role in shaping species boundaries. In many beetle groups, contact zones arise in varied ecological settings, including mountain systems, islands, forest edges, and anthropogenic landscapes. These zones provide opportunities for hybridization, allowing alleles to move across species boundaries and influencing adaptation, ecological niche expansion, or the breakdown or reinforcement of reproductive barriers. title: Risk and Resilience in Forensic Psychiatry
summary: Forensic psychiatry occupies a unique position at the intersection of mental health, criminal justice, and public safety. Historically, research and clinical practice in this field have emphasized the identification and management of risk—especially in relation to violent offending, sexual offending, and the likelihood of relapse or recidivism. While understanding risk remains crucial, there is growing recognition of the importance of resilience: the array of protective factors and adaptive responses that help individuals overcome adversity and avoid criminal behavior. Exploring both risk and resilience not only enhances public safety but also promotes better recovery, rehabilitation, and reintegration outcomes for forensic populations.

title: The Co-Construction of Self, Identity, and Culture in a Global World
summary: Cultural psychology is built on the principle of mutual constitution, which posits a dynamic interplay where individuals and their cultural contexts continuously shape one another. While research has explored identity through broad cultural categories, the contemporary era of globalization, digital immersion, and social change presents unprecedented complexity. Individuals now navigate multiple, intersecting cultural streams such as local and global, online and offline, inherited and chosen, creating intricate lived experiences at the confluence of cultural worlds. This reality necessitates an intersectional lens to understand how overlapping systems of culture, power, and social position (such as race, gender, class, and language) co-constitute the self.

title: The Hidden Burden of Multiple Sclerosis: Exploring Depression, Fatigue, Pain, and Cognitive Impairments
summary: Multiple sclerosis (MS) is a chronic neurological disorder characterized by a wide array of symptoms that can vary in severity and manifestation. While the visible effects, such as mobility issues, are often recognized, the invisible symptoms play a significant yet often overlooked role in the lives of those affected. These include fatigue, depression, cognitive impairments, pain, and sexual dysfunction, all of which are common among people living with MS. These invisible symptoms profoundly impact quality of life by contributing to individual, marital, and social difficulties. Despite advancements in medical research, there is still a critical need to comprehensively address and manage these symptoms to improve overall patient outcomes and quality of life.
image_alt: The Hidden Burden of Multiple Sclerosis: Exploring Depression, Fatigue, Pain, and Cognitive Impairments

title: The Role of Cellular Metabolites in Neuronal Excitability in Health and Disease
summary: This Research Topic aims to explore how cellular metabolites (intermediates or end-products of metabolic processes) influence neuronal activity in both healthy and pathological states, with a particular focus on excitability-related disorders (including but not limited to epilepsy, genetic metabolic disorders with epileptic manifestations, fragile X syndrome, migraine, Alzheimer’s disease and traumatic brain injury).
image_alt: The Role of Cellular Metabolites in Neuronal Excitability in Health and Disease

title: The Role of Clinical Psychology in Chronic Illness and Disease
summary: Chronic diseases, such as diabetes, cardiovascular conditions, autoimmune disorders, and cancer, represent an escalating global health challenge, exerting not only physical but also deep psychological and psychopathological burdens on affected individuals. In this context, Clinical Psychology and Psychiatry play a pivotal role in identifying, understanding, and treating the complex mental health issues that often accompany chronic illness.

title: Towards a Better Understanding, Managing and Engineering of Environmental Microbiomes in a Changing World
summary: Microbial communities are ubiquitous, inhabiting nearly every ecological niche and performing essential functions that underpin vital ecosystem services like food production, nutrient cycling, and water purification. However, in our rapidly changing world, these microbiomes face numerous natural and human-induced stressors. The consequences for microbial communities and the critical services they support are largely unknown. By applying the conceptual frameworks of microbial ecology and microbial ecotoxicology, we can better understand the structure, function, and dynamics of microbial communities and their roles in ecosystem health and sustainability. This topic seeks studies that investigate microbiomes through the lens of microbial ecology, spanning a wide range of ecosystems from pristine natural environments to those under extreme human pressure.
image_alt: Towards a Better Understanding, Managing and Engineering of Environmental Microbiomes in a Changing World

title: Transforming Work Environments: The Impact of Healing Workplaces on Employee Wellbeing and Organizational Performance
summary: The new health insurance data is alarming: days of absence due to mental illness increased dramatically again from 2023 to 2024. Mental illness has become one of the main causes of incapacity for work. Employees in all professions are affected by burnout, especially but not limited to the healthcare and education sectors. Those affected are often stigmatized, which makes it difficult to take advantage of prevention offers. In the healthcare sector in particular, it is often seen as a weakness of the individual to suffer from burnout. The personal suffering for each individual is high, the costs for employers and health insurance companies are enormous, and the risk of developing life-threatening secondary illnesses such as depression is massive. A shift in thinking must take place if companies want to remain competitive in the long term. title: 75th Annual Meeting of the Italian Society of Physiology: Innovations and Emerging Directions in Physiological Research
summary: To be held in Torino in September 2025, the Annual Meeting of the Italian Society of Physiology will celebrate its 75th anniversary with a Joint Symposium with the Slovenian Physiological Society (https://sif2025.azuleon.org/). The congress will highlight cutting-edge research across physiological domains, from molecular mechanisms to clinical translation. Contributions will cover calcium signaling in health and disease, cardiometabolic dysfunction, and the heart-brain axis, alongside topics such as astrocyte diversity, cerebellar circuit dysfunction in neurodevelopmental disorders, and cancer physiology at the interface of cell signaling and microenvironment. Keynote lectures will address cardiovascular protection by remote ischemic conditioning, highlighting the roles of neural and humoral mechanisms, nanoscale cAMP signaling in cardiomyocytes, and neuromodulation therapies restoring function after spinal cord injury. title: AI and Learning: Exploring Artificial Intelligence in Education, Psychology, and Online Environments
summary: Artificial Intelligence (AI) is reshaping the educational landscape as well as many other disciplines, redefining how individuals learn, interact, and engage within digital environments. AI-powered tools - ranging from personalised learning systems to emotion-aware technologies - offer significant opportunities for supporting both cognitive development and emotional well-being. Innovations in adaptive learning, emotional monitoring, learner motivation, and psychological support demonstrate promising benefits for students’ academic performance and overall well-being. At the same time, the rapid integration of AI raises important concerns regarding autonomy, privacy, emotional safety, and the preservation of authentic human connection.
image_alt: AI and Learning: Exploring Artificial Intelligence in Education, Psychology, and Online Environments

title: AI-Driven Decoding of Brain and Physiological States: Advances in Neuro-Signal Analytics and Multimodal Data for Neuroscience and Clinical Neurology
summary: The rapid advancement of Artificial Intelligence (AI) is reshaping the landscape of neuroscience and clinical neurology. In recent years, deep learning, graph neural networks, and multimodal fusion algorithms have demonstrated tremendous potential in the analysis of neural and physiological data such as electroencephalography (EEG), functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI), and structural MRI (sMRI). These technologies enable researchers to decode neural activity patterns with unprecedented accuracy and uncover complex relationships between brain function, cognition, and behavior. This Research Topic aims to bring together cutting-edge studies and perspectives exploring how AI can drive breakthroughs in brain and physiological state decoding, from foundational modeling to clinical translation.
image_alt: AI-Driven Decoding of Brain and Physiological States: Advances in Neuro-Signal Analytics and Multimodal Data for Neuroscience and Clinical Neurology

title: Advanced Biocontrol Strategies: Blending Phylogenetics, Symbiosis, And Nanotech For Nematode Control
summary: Nematodes significantly affect global agriculture and present challenges to human and animal health, emphasizing the need for advanced management approaches. In agriculture, plant-parasitic nematodes can lead to substantial crop losses, while parasitic nematodes in humans and livestock contribute to diseases and morbidity. Traditional chemical control measures raise concerns regarding their impact on the environment, resistance development, and the harm they may cause to non-target organisms. These drawbacks highlight the urgency for innovative, eco-friendly control strategies that effectively target nematode infestations while minimizing adverse effects.

summary: Evolutionary psychology provides a powerful theoretical framework for understanding the origins of human and non-human behaviors, focusing on the adaptive functions of psychological mechanisms shaped by natural and sexual selection. Increasingly, these evolutionary insights are being translated into real-world contexts, offering new perspectives and solutions for challenges in fields as varied as organizational behavior, education, health, morality, and religion. For example, evolutionary theories of cooperation, empathy, and group dynamics inform approaches to fostering ethical behavior and understanding religious practices, while principles of sexual selection and social cognition have direct implications for improving teamwork, leadership, and workplace culture. Applied evolutionary psychology thus bridges fundamental research with practice, enabling both interdisciplinary research and innovative applications that address contemporary social, organizational, moral, and media-related

title: Artificial Intelligence in Public Health: Advancing Multidisciplinary Applications for Population Health
summary: Artificial Intelligence (AI) is revolutionizing the public health landscape by enabling sophisticated data analytics, enhancing diagnostic capabilities, and improving healthcare delivery systems. With the exponential growth of healthcare data - ranging from electronic health records and genomic data to wearable device outputs - AI offers unprecedented opportunities to address critical public health challenges. Machine Learning (ML), Deep Learning (DL), Large Language Models (LLMs), and natural language processing (NLP) are being increasingly integrated into public health applications, from epidemiological analysis to clinical decision-making. These technological advancements provide transformative potential in areas such as disease prediction, early detection, automated medical coding, and personalized healthcare planning. However, challenges remain in ensuring data quality, algorithmic bias, ethical considerations, and interdisciplinary collaboration, making this an evolving and dynam

title: Autism Spectrum Disorders and Metal Dyshomeostasis, Volume III
summary: Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) is a multifaceted neurodevelopmental condition with substantial individual and societal impact. Prevalence estimates vary by region and surveillance method, and ASD is widely understood to arise from complex interactions among genetic susceptibility and environmental and biological co-factors. ASD etiology remains incompletely resolved, in part due to genetic heterogeneity and the likelihood of multiple converging mechanisms. Alongside genetic contributions, prenatal and perinatal exposures, nutritional status, and other biological variables have been associated with ASD likelihood in epidemiological and mechanistic studies. Among these, increasing attention has focused on the potential role of disrupted homeostasis of essential metals during critical windows of neurodevelopment.
image_alt: Autism Spectrum Disorders and Metal Dyshomeostasis, Volume III

title: Beyond Taxonomy: Trait-based Approaches to Understanding Soil and Rhizosphere Interactions and Processes
summary: Rhizosphere and surface soil are the hotspots of belowground biological interactions and processes. Understanding the roles of roots and microbiota in such region is essential for explaining soil biogeochemistry. Plant traits, such as root architecture, tissue chemistry, and resource-use strategies, determine the quantity and quality of organic inputs entering soil, shaping microbial substrates and microhabitats. Microbial traits, including but not limited to enzyme production, growth efficiency, sensing and mobility, govern how these inputs are transformed in soil and what the downstream feedbacks on plant performance are. Recent advances in technological approaches allow deeper understanding of both plant and microbial traits, which improves our ability to predict soil responses to environmental changes, such as drought, nutrient deficiency or deposition, and land-use shifts, and helps integrate plant–microbe interactions into biogeochemical models.
image_alt: Beyond Taxonomy: Trait-based Approaches to Understanding Soil and Rhizosphere Interactions and Processes

title: Biomarkers and Extracellular Vesicles Across the Dementia Spectrum: From Discovery to Clinical Implementation
summary: The landscape of dementia diagnostics is undergoing a paradigm shift with the emergence of liquid biopsy, blood-based biomarkers (BBMs), and blood-derived extracellular vesicles (bEVs). These innovative tools offer minimally invasive, scalable, and cost-effective alternatives to traditional diagnostic approaches such as cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) analysis and positron emission tomography (PET) imaging, with profound implications for early detection, differential diagnosis, and disease monitoring.

Bridging Language and Consciousness: Insights from Brains, Minds, and Machines
summary: Language and consciousness are highly intertwined hallmarks of human cognition, but the precise nature of their relationship is yet to be understood. Indeed, the debate about the relationship between language and consciousness involves several disciplines. The philosophical debate focuses on the language of thought and the role of language in higher-order consciousness. On the other hand, psychological sciences study the impact of language (e.g., inner speech) on perception and neurosciences investigate the brain networks linking language and consciousness. Again, computational models simulate and reproduce language and conscious processes in artificial systems, thus creating a bridge between the human mind and machines. Finally, large language models robotic architectures take advantage of knowledge about language and consciousness (natural language processing, cognitive robotics, machine consciousness, etc.), providing deep insights into the human mind. title: Bridging the Gap: Technology-Driven Solutions for Underachievement and Unlocking Potential
summary: Underachievement has been a longstanding focus in talent development, gifted education, and related areas of psychological and educational research. Despite high potential, many individuals do not consistently translate their abilities into academic or developmental achievement. Research has shown that underachievement does not affect all groups equally. It is particularly prevalent among learners from socioeconomically disadvantaged backgrounds, twice-exceptional individuals, and girls and women in STEM-related domains. Over more than a century of research and intervention efforts, a wide range of explanatory models and support strategies has emerged. Nevertheless, persistent gaps between potential and achievement suggest that existing approaches have achieved only limited and often uneven success. At the same time, rapid advances in digital technologies—such as learning analytics, adaptive learning systems, and intelligent tutoring environments—have begun to reshape how learning and

title: Case Reports in Schizophrenia and Psychotic Disorders: 2026
summary: Frontiers in Psychiatry is proud to present our Case Reports series. Our case reports aim to highlight unique cases of patients that present with an unexpected/unusual diagnosis, including complexity and differential diagnosis and/or co-morbid diagnoses, treatment outcome, or clinical course. Case reports provide insight into the differential diagnosis, overlapping diagnoses and the increased complexity (such as treating schizophrenia and obsessive-compulsive disorder), decision-making, and clinical management of unusual cases as a valuable educational tool.

title: Comparing Altered States of Consciousness: Phenomenology, Physiology, and Neural Mechanisms
summary: While research on altered states of consciousness has made considerable progress, much of the existing literature compares these states only to normative wakefulness. What remains largely underexplored is the direct comparison between different altered states themselves, particularly in terms of their subjective features and neurophysiological signatures.

title: Computational Models of Memory and Attention: Advancing Mechanistic Understanding of Brain with Artificial Intelligence and Beyond
summary: Human memory and attention are core cognitive functions that shape perception, learning, and decision-making. And whilst decades of research have provided valuable empirical insights, the underlying neural mechanisms remain an open challenge in neuroscience. Computational neuroscience offers powerful tools for modeling these processes, and recent advances in artificial intelligence have created new opportunities to develop models that capture the complexity and dynamics of biological cognition. By simulating brain function, computational models not only replicate behavioral and neural phenomena but also generate testable hypotheses, unify diverse findings, and move beyond description toward mechanistic understanding. However, despite their impressive performance, many AI models lack clear links to biological plausibility. This Research Topic aims to bridge that gap by highlighting state-of-the-art computational and AI-driven approaches that reveal how memory is formed, consolidated, an

title: Computational perspectives on consciousness
summary: Consciousness remains one of the most profound and complex questions in neuroscience and philosophy. Understanding how subjective experience arises from neural activity is a central challenge for brain science. Computational neuroscience offers powerful tools to explore this mystery by modeling the neural dynamics, network structures, and information processing mechanisms thought to underlie conscious states. By simulating aspects of attention, perception, integration, and awareness, computational models provide testable frameworks that bridge empirical data and theoretical insights. Recent advances in brain imaging, neural decoding, and machine learning have enabled deeper investigations into the correlates and mechanisms of consciousness across different states—such as wakefulness, sleep, anesthesia, and altered states. This Research Topic, Computational Perspectives on Consciousness, aims to highlight interdisciplinary work that uses computational approaches to investigate the neura
image_alt: Computational perspectives on consciousness

Data-Informed Nutrition Technologies for Sustainable Animal Production
summary: Current scientific research is focused on finding new technologies for sustainable agricultural production. Options have been developed to predict conditions or diseases based on behaviour and data. Telemetry in agricultural output works as a tool that generates real-time information and, with the help of artificial intelligence, enables real-time decision-making. Furthermore, microencapsulation improves the efficiency of feeding programmes for ruminants and monogastric animals, while also helping reduce greenhouse gas emissions.

title: Digital Game Design, Behavioural Intention, and Sustainability Education: Gamified and Immersive Approaches for Motivating Pro-Environmental Action
summary: Rapid technological change is impacting aspects of how learners currently engage with global sustainability challenges; for example, platforms, interactive media, and game-based environments whose role in awareness, motivation and behavioural intention towards recycling, consumption and environmental action are becoming better understood. Digital tools are being increasingly adopted in educational settings, facilitating interest in how these pertinent environments, alongside game design, gamification, persuasive technology and immersive media can be leveraged to promote meaningful pro-environmental behaviour.

title: Emerging Technologies and the Apparel Industry: Bridging Virtual and Physical Fashion Realms
summary: The digitization of the apparel industry is increasingly shaped by the integration of digital technologies and advances in computer science, making fashion a hybrid field that merges virtual and physical elements. Tools such as 3D body scanning and computer vision have introduced new levels of precision concerning sizing accuracy and consumer interactivity, offering remote customers vivid shopping experiences. VR and XR technologies are transforming consumer engagement and enriching fashion education by presenting immersive retail settings and digital classroom environments. Additionally, CAD and apparel simulation systems facilitate garment visualization and prototyping, improving communication between manufacturers and consumers, and reducing reliance on physical samples and material waste. Finally, the incorporation of data-driven approaches, digital twins, and human-computer interaction strategies expands further possibilities across design, supply chain management, and education.
image_alt: Emerging Technologies and the Apparel Industry: Bridging Virtual and Physical Fashion Realms

title: Emotion Recognition in Human-Robot Interaction
summary: As robots transition from industrial settings to human-centric environments—such as homes, clinics, and classrooms—their ability to perceive and respond to human emotions has become a cornerstone for effective interaction. Emotion recognition enables robots to go beyond mere task execution, allowing for more natural, adaptive, and meaningful engagement. The evolution of affective computing, multimodal sensing technologies, and intelligent behavior modeling has propelled the integration of emotional intelligence into robotic systems. However, challenges remain in interpreting complex human affect, especially in real-world, culturally diverse, and ethically sensitive contexts. To advance these capabilities, a deeper interdisciplinary collaboration among robotics, neuroscience, psychology, and AI is essential. This Research Topic aims to explore the state-of-the-art in emotion-aware robotics and its transformative potential across domains.

title: Energy-efficient neural computation
summary: The human brain remains the premier exemplar of energy-efficient information processing, performing complex cognitive tasks while consuming approximately 20 Watts of power, roughly the energy needed to power a dim lightbulb. In stark contrast, modern deep learning models and large-scale artificial intelligence (AI) systems require massive computational resources and cooling infrastructure, leading to significant environmental and economic costs. This disparity has sparked a renewed interest in understanding the fundamental biological principles that govern metabolic efficiency. Biological systems utilize a suite of strategies, including event-based communication via spikes, sparse coding, local learning rules, and homeostatic regulation, to minimize energy expenditure without sacrificing performance. As the demand for edge computing and sustainable AI grows, computational neuroscience is uniquely positioned to bridge the gap between these biological insights and the development of the

title: Event Cognition: Interactions Between Mental and Physical Architectures
Evolutionary Development and Adaptation of Microbial Resistomes in Human-Impacted Environments
summary: Antimicrobial resistance (AMR) represents a rapidly growing concern at the intersection of environmental microbiology and evolutionary developmental biology. The microbial resistome—the entire collection of antimicrobial resistance genes (ARGs) in a microbiome—has emerged as a dynamic system profoundly influenced by human activities. Anthropogenic pressures such as agricultural intensification, pollution, and wastewater inputs reshape microbial habitats, prompting the development, recruitment, and spread of resistance traits. Recent studies highlight how developmental gene regulation, horizontal gene transfer, and ecological selection combine to drive both the evolutionary diversification of ARGs and the adaptation of microbial communities. Yet, despite advances in phylogenetics and molecular ecology, major gaps persist in linking the developmental origins of ARGs with their evolutionary trajectories and ecological outcomes under environmental transformation.

title: Future perspectives on ethical and explainable AI for cognitive computing
summary: Cognitive computing represents an innovative frontier within computer science, merging artificial intelligence, machine learning, and computational neuroscience to emulate human-like cognitive functions. With rapid developments in natural language processing, pattern recognition, and decision making, cognitive systems have begun to reshape key industries such as healthcare, finance, and education. The field is propelled further by the convergence of big data analytics and the Internet of Things, enabling dynamic, responsive, and highly personalized applications. Despite its potential, the proliferation of cognitive technologies raises pressing concerns related to ethics, trustworthiness, bias, and explainability, prompting vigorous debate and increasing regulatory scrutiny.

title: Genetic Diversity and Evolutionary Ecology of Medicinal Plants: Global Perspectives on Conservation and Resilience
summary: Medicinal plants across the world are exemplary models for studying the evolutionary and ecological processes that shape plant diversity, adaptation, and resilience. Regions of exceptional biodiversity—such as the Himalayas, the Andes, Southeast Asia, and tropical mountain systems—harbor a tremendous range of medicinally significant species. Many of these plants face mounting pressures from habitat loss, overharvesting, and climate change, threatening their persistence and the ecological functions they support.

title: Integrating Nutraceutical and Biotechnological Therapies for Retinal Neurodegeneration
summary: Neurodegenerative disorders present one of the most challenging fronts in modern medicine, with diseases like Alzheimer’s and Parkinson’s disease impacting millions globally. These conditions are characterized by the progressive degeneration and death of nerve cells, which is a complex interplay of genetic, oxidative, and inflammatory factors. The conventional therapeutic strategies are often inadequate, mainly due to their inability to target multiple pathological pathways simultaneously. As such, there is a critical need for innovative approaches that address these limitations effectively. In addition to central nervous system disorders, neurodegenerative conditions affecting the retina, such as age-related macular degeneration (AMD) and retinitis pigmentosa (RP), represent significant challenges. These retinal neurodegenerations share common pathological mechanisms with other neurodegenerative diseases, including oxidative stress, mitochondrial dysfunction, and chronic inflammation.

title: Karst Ecosystems Under Climate Change: Hydrology, Weathering, and Ecological Security
summary: The total area of global karst regions is approximately 22 million square kilometers, accounting for roughly 15% of the Earth's land surface. These regions are widely distributed across the globe, boasting abundant natural resources and unique ecosystem characteristics. However, karst ecosystems are currently facing increasingly severe challenges: global warming, shifts in precipitation patterns, and the frequent occurrence of extreme climate events are profoundly impacting hydrological processes, soil weathering, ecosystem functions, and biodiversity in karst areas—rendering regional water resource management, vegetation restoration, and ecological security particularly complex undertakings.
image_alt: Karst Ecosystems Under Climate Change: Hydrology, Weathering, and Ecological Security

title: Leadership for Emerging Technologies in Schools: Roles of Educational Leaders in Driving Digital Innovation
summary: Emerging technologies, such as Artificial Intelligence (AI), Virtual Reality (VR), Mixed Reality (MR), educational robotics, and learning analytics are reshaping teaching, learning, and school management. Their rapid incorporation into educational systems demands new leadership approaches capable of guiding pedagogical innovation, supporting teachers’ digital competence, and ensuring safe and ethical implementation. Research shows that teachers and headmasters or other types of leaders play a decisive role in whether emerging technologies are meaningfully adopted or remain underused. Yet current studies often focus either on technology or on leadership separately, leaving a gap concerning how both interact to influence school transformation. This Research Topic aims to address this gap by exploring how educational leadership shapes, enables, or restricts the integration of emerging technologies in schools.
image_alt: Leadership for Emerging Technologies in Schools: Roles of Educational Leaders in Driving Digital Innovation

title: Mental health and suicide prevention in sensory impairment populations: volume II
summary: According to the World Health Organization, worldwide there are 2.2 billion people with vision impairment and it was projected that 700 million will have severe disabling hearing loss by 2050. There are also approximately 160 million people who suffer from Deafblindness. These numbers are projected to increase as the population ages. People with sensory impairment (PwSI) – hearing, visual, and/or dual - have a higher risk of mental health (MH) disorders, suicidal ideation, and past suicide attempts. Key to the effective management of mental illness is early identification and treatment to prevent long-term sequelae as well as the deleterious impact on quality of life. PwSI, however, face barriers in accessing healthcare services and information. Studies have also shown that low health literacy levels and negative attitudes and beliefs could impact the health-seeking behavior of PwSI. title: Metabolic Pathway Modulation: Innovative Therapeutic Approaches for Neurodegenerative Diseases
summary: Neurodegenerative diseases are marked by the progressive and irreversible decline of neuron function within specific brain regions, including Alzheimer's, Parkinson's, Huntington's, multiple sclerosis, and amyotrophic lateral sclerosis. These disorders involve significant changes in cerebral glucose metabolism and lipid processes, which are crucial for both cellular function and molecular mechanisms. Despite growing interest and research into metabolic pathways as targets for therapy, there remains a substantial gap in understanding how metabolic dysregulation aids disease advancement and how it can be effectively targeted.

summary: This Research Topic explores breakthroughs in genetic research and molecular technology to enhance resilience to environmental stresses in both crops and tree species. Environmental challenges such as drought, salinity, and temperature extremes pose significant threats to productivity within agricultural and forestry systems, thereby impacting global food security and ecological stability. To address these challenges, it is critical to identify genetic traits and molecular pathways that bolster resilience across diverse plant systems.

title: Multi-Omics Integration for Aquatic Microbial Systems Biology
summary: Microbial communities in aquatic habitats are among the most complex and dynamic biological systems on Earth, providing essential functions in biogeochemical cycling, ecosystem resilience, and water quality regulation. These communities comprise several species interacting through complex networks of genes, metabolites, macromolecules, and environmental variables, providing highly integrated systems that maintain ecosystem function. Understanding this complexity requires comprehensive, systems-orientated approaches that transcend reductionist perspectives of discrete elements.

title: Network science and topological data analysis for understanding brain disorders
summary: The brain’s function and integrity emerge not only from properties of individual regions, but, more fundamentally, from the intricate web of connections linking them into complex networks. In recent years, network science and topological approaches have provided powerful new perspectives for understanding how these connections—and the patterns they form—relate to both healthy brain function and neurological disorders.

title: Neural interfaces for motor control
summary: The profound impact of neurological injuries and diseases, such as stroke, spinal cord injury, and neurodegenerative disorders, often manifests as devastating loss of motor function, severely compromising independence and quality of life. The field of neural interfaces has emerged as a beacon of hope, offering unprecedented opportunities to restore lost motor control by directly interfacing with the nervous system. By translating neural activity into control signals for prosthetic limbs, exoskeletons, or functional electrical stimulation, these technologies hold the promise of empowering individuals to regain autonomy and re-engage with the world.

title: Showcasing FAIR² Data Articles in Digital Health: Unlocking Trustworthy, AI-Ready Data for Reuse and Impact
summary: Scientific knowledge is fundamentally built on data; yet, for too long, research datasets have remained siloed, poorly documented, and inconsistently formatted. As science becomes increasingly data-intensive, with analyses driven by artificial intelligence, merely sharing data is no longer sufficient. To enable responsible and trustworthy reuse, data must be well-structured, machine-actionable, ethically aligned, and rich in contextual meta-data. Addressing this challenge, Frontiers has introduced a new article type: the FAIR² Data Article , a citable, peer-reviewed publication format that elevates datasets to become first-class research outputs.

By bridging neurosurgery, cancer neuroscience, and translational oncology through artificial intelligence and clinical informatics, this collection underscores the multidisciplinary evolution of modern neurosurgical oncology. We welcome submissions that advance our understanding of next-generation neurosurgical practice, including original research, technical innovations, translational frameworks, and operative case insights. The Role of Genome Features and Components in Ecology and Evolution
summary: Advances in sequencing technologies and bioinformatics now provide unprecedented insights into genome composition, function, and evolution, as well as their links to phenotype, environmental responses, and speciation. Genome aspects—such as size, structure, and chromosomal organization—along with components like genes, transposable elements, and pseudogenes, and processes such as whole-genome duplication or horizontal gene transfer, all influence organismal ecology and evolution. Even elements once considered non-functional, including transposons, simple sequence repeats (SSRs), and non-coding DNA, are increasingly recognized as important for adaptation and evolutionary change. Yet, the precise contributions of nuclear and organellar genome features to ecological and evolutionary dynamics remain poorly understood.

title: Understanding the Complexity of Neuropsychiatric Symptoms in MCI and Dementia
summary: Neuropsychiatric symptoms, also known as Behavioral and Psychological Symptoms of Dementia (BPSD) include several distinct neuropsychiatric manifestations, such as agitation, apathy, depression, anxiety, delusions, hallucinations, disinhibition, irritability, aberrant motor behavior, appetite disturbances, sleep disorders, and euphoria. These symptoms are highly prevalent, affecting up to 90% of individuals with dementia, and can emerge in the prodromal phase of Mild Cognitive Impairment (MCI). BPSD not only exacerbate cognitive and functional decline but also increase caregiver burden and healthcare costs. Despite their clinical significance, the underlying mechanisms remain elusive due to the multifactorial nature of BPSD, involving genetic predispositions, neuroanatomical changes, neurotransmitter imbalances, inflammation, and environmental triggers. Moreover, the heterogeneity of symptom presentations complicates diagnosis and therapeutic interventions. Recent advances in neuroimag

title: Unraveling the Roles of Membrane Transporters in Metabolic, Neurological and Oncological Diseases
summary: Membrane transporters regulate the movement of charged substances and macromolecules across biological membranes in living organisms, therefore playing a crucial role in maintaining physiological homeostasis. Transporters play a pivotal role in normal development and are implicated in the progression of certain diseases or their responses to therapy. In conjunction with endo- and xenobiotic-metabolizing enzymes, transporter function is directly relevant to pharmacokinetics and toxicokinetics. Transporter research is therefore an integral part of physiology, pathology, pharmacology, and toxicology, and has a critical impact on the drug development process.
image_alt: Unraveling the Roles of Membrane Transporters in Metabolic, Neurological and Oncological Diseases

title: Veterinary Respiratory Infections: Immunity, Host Interaction and Treatments
summary: Respiratory infections represent a significant burden across veterinary medicine, impacting companion animals, livestock, poultry, and wildlife species. These infections, caused by diverse viral, bacterial, fungal, and parasitic pathogens, lead to substantial morbidity, mortality, and economic losses. Understanding the intricate interplay between host immune defenses and pathogen evasion strategies is crucial for developing effective interventions. Furthermore, the rise of antimicrobial resistance (AMR) and the need for holistic approaches under the One Health framework underscore the urgency of advancing knowledge in this field.

title: Yoga: understanding its neural mechanisms and clinical applications in brain health
summary: Yoga, an ancient practice encompassing physical postures, breathing techniques, meditation, and ethical principles, has long been revered for its profound impact on physical and mental well-being. In the modern scientific era, there is an increasing interest in elucidating the neurobiological substrates underlying these benefits, particularly their role in promoting and preserving brain health. Accumulating evidence suggests that regular yoga practice can significantly modulate brain structure and function, leading to enhancements in mood, cognitive performance, and overall resilience against neurological and psychiatric challenges.

title: AI-Driven Advancements in Neural and Neurovascular Imaging
summary: The fields of neural and neurovascular imaging are undergoing a rapid transformation, providing high-resolution, quantitative insights into the nervous system. These advanced techniques (e.g., MRI, PET, CT, Ultrasound) are crucial for characterizing a broad spectrum of pathologies, including: neurodegenerative disorders (e.g., Alzheimer's, Parkinson's), vascular and ischemic diseases (e.g., stroke, cerebral small vessel disease), neoplasms (tumors), inflammatory conditions, demyelinating diseases (e.g., multiple sclerosis), infectious diseases, traumatic brain injury and epilepsy. The massive, high-dimensional datasets generated across these diverse conditions pose a significant challenge for efficient clinical translation, accurate diagnosis, and prognostic prediction.

Transdiagnostic approach in studying mental health conditions: The contribution of fundamental and translational research for precise interventions, Volume II
summary: Personalized treatments have become a key focus in translational psychiatry and psychology. To provide individualized interventions for people suffering from mental health conditions, it is crucial to enhance our understanding of both the etiology and pathophysiology of psychiatric disorders. Identifying neural networks associated with mental illnesses and disordered psychological processes in each clinical situation is essential. A comprehensive understanding of mental disorders requires insight into both the underlying biological deficiencies and the maladaptive psychological processes and behavioral dysfunctions. This is achievable through translational research, which bridges fundamental research findings with clinical applications, thereby contributing to the overall improvement of healthcare and the industry.

title: VR, AR, and AI for Industry 5.0: Human-Centric and Sustainable Ecosystems
summary: Across industrial sectors, the way humans interact with machines, data, and complex systems is rapidly changing. Virtual Reality (VR), Augmented Reality (AR), Mixed Reality (MR), and Artificial Intelligence (AI) are no longer confined to research laboratories or pilot projects: they are increasingly embedded in factories, logistics chains, energy systems, healthcare delivery, and smart infrastructure. Together, these technologies are shaping the transition toward Industry 5.0, where human factors and sustainability are built in from the start, not added at the end.

title: AI in Precision Psychiatry and Neurodevelopmental Disorders: From Subjective Diagnosis to Objective Biomarkers
summary: Psychiatric conditions (such as depression, anxiety, bipolar disorder, and schizophrenia) and neurodevelopmental disorders (including ADHD and autism spectrum disorder) differ significantly from neurodegenerative diseases and brain tumors, which often show clear structural abnormalities. The diagnosis of these psychiatric and neurodevelopmental disorders is highly complex, as current clinical practice relies heavily on subjective interviews and behavioral checklists (like DSM-5 criteria). This reliance frequently results in high rates of misdiagnosis, increased heterogeneity within patient cohorts, and trial-and-error treatment strategies.

title: Multisensory integration: unveiling the complexities of perception, Volume II
summary: Our world is a rich tapestry of sensory information, constantly bombarding our nervous system with a vast array of stimuli. How does the brain make sense of this cacophony of inputs to create a coherent perception of reality? The answer lies in the fascinating process of multisensory integration. Multisensory integration refers to the brain’s ability to combine information from different sensory modalities to create a unified perceptual experience. This process is not simply additive; rather, it involves complex neural mechanisms that can enhance, suppress, or alter the perception of individual sensory inputs. Recent advances in neuroimaging and electrophysiological techniques have shed light on the neural substrates of multisensory integration. The traditional view of sensory processing as a hierarchical, modality-specific system has given way to a more nuanced understanding. title: Pediatric neurodevelopment, neural injury, and neuromodulation
summary: The developing nervous system in children is highly dynamic and vulnerable, with neurodevelopmental processes intricately shaping cognitive, motor, and behavioral outcomes. Disruptions in these processes—whether due to genetic factors, perinatal complications, environmental insults, or acquired neural injury—can lead to long-term neurological deficits and functional impairments. Understanding the mechanisms underlying pediatric neurodevelopment, as well as the pathways leading to neural injury, is crucial for improving diagnosis, intervention, and rehabilitation strategies.

title: The Role of Oxytocin and Vasopressin Signaling in Health and Disease
summary: Oxytocin and vasopressin are evolutionarily conserved neuropeptides, recognized for their fundamental roles in regulating social behavior, emotional processing, stress responsivity, fluid balance, and cardiovascular function. Beyond their classical actions in reproduction and osmoregulation, growing evidence underscores their broader influence on neural circuit development, synaptic plasticity, autonomic control, immune modulation, and metabolic homeostasis. Dysregulation of oxytocinergic and vasopressinergic signaling has been implicated in a wide range of neurological, psychiatric, and systemic disorders, including autism spectrum disorder, anxiety and depression, neurodegeneration, cardiovascular disease, and metabolic dysfunction. Progress in molecular genetics, neuroimaging, and circuit-level neuroscience has advanced our understanding of how these neuropeptides orchestrate brain–body communication in both physiological and pathological contexts.

title: Reviews in Evolutionary Systems Biology
summary: The field of Evolutionary Systems Biology stands at the intersection of evolutionary theory and systems-based analyses, offering powerful new perspectives for understanding the dynamic complexity of biological systems. By integrating high-dimensional data, computational models, and evolutionary frameworks, researchers have begun to reveal how interactions at the molecular, cellular, individual, and ecological levels shape patterns of adaptation and biodiversity. Despite remarkable advances, key challenges persist in drawing equivalencies between micro- and macro-evolutionary processes, unraveling the genetic basis of complex traits, and predicting organismal and ecosystem responses to rapid environmental change. A growing body of studies now employs systems biology not only to map genetic networks and evolutionary pathways but also to tackle critical issues such as climate change impacts, robustness and epistasis, and the mathematical properties of phylogenetic trees.

title: Advances in Neuromorphic Systems and Hardware: Circuits, Architectures, and Brain-Inspired Computation
summary: Recent advances in materials, devices, and system architectures are driving a new generation of computing beyond traditional CMOS, with neuromorphic engineering emerging as a pivotal field. The growing demand for energy-efficient, scalable, and application-tailored neural computation - in AI, biomedical signal processing, autonomous systems, and edge computing - motivates research into hardware that implements biologically inspired and event-driven information processing principles. Neuromorphic systems, devices, and architectures are enabling more robust, efficient, and brain-like computation, highlighting the need for interdisciplinary study and innovative engineering approaches.

title: Synergistic Adaptation of Wetland Communities under Multiple Stressors
summary: The integrity and functioning of wetland ecosystems are sustained by dynamic, finely tuned interaction networks among their biological constituents. Plants, microorganisms, and waterbirds form the core of the wetland “living community,” serving respectively as primary producers, drivers of biogeochemical cycles, and higher-level consumers. This interconnected network responds to environmental variation through inherent synergistic and feedback processes that govern a wetland’s resilience to cumulative stressors and shape its long-term ecological trajectory.

summary: Global environmental crises, including climate change, desertification, depletion of energy resources, and the pollution of air, water, and soil, along with the accelerating loss of biodiversity, represent some of the most urgent and complex challenges facing contemporary society. Addressing these interconnected issues demands more than technical solutions; it requires a fundamental rethinking of the relationship between human societies and nature.

title: Institutional and Ecosystem Approaches to Human-AI Partnership in Higher Education
summary: Human tutoring remains a foundational and irreplaceable influence on student learning, particularly in fostering higher-order thinking, affective engagement, disciplinary judgement, and personalised guidance. At the same time, Generative Artificial Intelligence (GenAI) is rapidly reshaping educational environments, offering new possibilities for feedback generation, adaptive scaffolding, assessment support, and personalised learning pathways. As GenAI becomes embedded within higher education systems, the question is no longer whether it will influence teaching and learning, but how such influence can be intentionally designed, governed, and sustained.

title: Comparative Oncology: Bridging Human and Veterinary Medicine
summary: Comparative oncology is an interdisciplinary field that merges human and veterinary cancer research, focusing on the genetic, molecular, and clinical similarities between cancers in humans and companion animals like dogs and cats. Despite traditional research efforts being separated into human and veterinary domains, there is substantial evidence that spontaneous cancers in companion animals closely resemble human cancers, offering a unique platform for translational research. This integration is pivotal in understanding cancer biology, drug response, and resistance mechanisms, as it leverages the natural tumor occurrence in animals like dogs, which share similar living environments and exposures with humans. Such models present a higher translational relevance than traditional murine models, thus enhancing preclinical study outcomes.
