title: Multisystem Consequences of Psychological and Physical Trauma: From PTSD to Neurobiological Mechanisms and Neurorehabilitation
summary: Psychological and physical trauma exert profound and long-lasting effects on the central and peripheral nervous systems. Post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD), traumatic brain injury (TBI), polytrauma, and chronic pain frequently coexist with stress-related neuroinflammatory processes, producing complex neuropsychiatric and functional outcomes that challenge conventional diagnostic and therapeutic frameworks. While individual conditions such as PTSD and TBI have received considerable research attention in isolation, their overlapping pathophysiology, including shared neuroinflammatory cascades, neuroendocrine dysregulation, disrupted stress circuitry, and impaired neuroplasticity, remains insufficiently understood. The result is a fragmented evidence base that limits the development of integrative, mechanism-driven approaches to treatment and rehabilitation.

title: Rethinking neurodegeneration through multidomain neurorehabilitation and neurotechnologies
summary: Neurodegenerative disorders such as Parkinson’s disease, Alzheimer’s disease, frontotemporal dementia, and multiple sclerosis, conceived as a chronic neuroinflammatory and neurodegenerative disease, challenge traditional treatment paradigms with their complex, overlapping cognitive and motor impairments affecting individuals’ autonomy, participation, and quality of life. Yet, rehabilitation approaches often treat these domains separately. These conditions have typically been approached through parallel treatment strategies, often isolating cognitive rehabilitation from motor recovery. Recent behavioral neuroscience, neurorehabilitation, and technological innovation point toward the need for integrated, multidomain interventions that reflect the real-life complexity of human functioning. There is tight interdependence between these domains, putting forward a rethinking of how we conceptualize and respond to neurodegeneration.

summary: Neuroscience research has increasingly highlighted the intertwined roles of neuroinflammation and neurodegeneration in the development and progression of major neurological disorders, such as Alzheimer’s, Parkinson’s, and multiple sclerosis. The relationship between neuroinflammation—characterized by the activation of glial cells and production of proinflammatory mediators—and neurodegeneration—marked by irreversible neuronal loss and structural changes—remains a subject of intense investigation and debate. Despite significant progress in the identification of biomarkers and therapeutic targets, many questions persist regarding how inflammatory processes drive or result from neurodegenerative changes, the temporal sequence of these events, and the extent to which they can be captured and differentiated in vivo. summary: The growing complexity of infectious disease emergence, especially zoonotic threats, demands a transformation in how veterinary epidemiology collects, analyzes, and acts on health data. In this evolving landscape, digital innovations are playing a central role in enhancing our capacity to detect, anticipate, and manage animal health risks. Tools such as AI-driven predictive models, interoperable surveillance platforms, remote sensing technologies, and real-time data systems offer new ways to monitor disease dynamics and support decision-making. These technologies are helping shift veterinary epidemiology toward more responsive, data-integrated approaches. Within a One Health framework, where animal, human, and environmental health are deeply interdependent, digital solutions can improve collaboration across sectors, provide early warnings, and support evidence-based interventions. title: Exercise and Physiotherapy Strategies for Movement, Postural Control, and Balance in Parkinson’s Disease
summary: Parkinson’s disease (PD) is a progressive neurodegenerative disorder marked by motor symptoms including bradykinesia, rigidity, tremor, and postural instability, all of which severely impact gait, mobility, and balance, leading to an increased risk of falls and a reduced quality of life. As one of the most prevalent and fastest-growing neurological conditions worldwide, PD imposes substantial challenges not only on individuals but also on healthcare systems and caregivers across different regions and socioeconomic contexts. Although pharmacological interventions have traditionally been central to symptom management, exercise and physiotherapy have become vital components of comprehensive care. Recent advancements in therapeutic exercise modalities and physiotherapeutic strategies demonstrate potential benefits in improving movement quality, postural control, and balance in individuals with PD. Yet, the diversity of approaches and inconsistent clinical results highlight a pressing need

title: Improving decoding of neuroinformation: towards the diversity of neural engineer, Volume II
summary: The Central Nervous System (CNS) provides information about how individuals collect information from their surroundings, how they process that information to make decisions, and finally, how they behave and act in their environment. CNS information can be gathered from three main sources: (1) electrical currents (e.g., electroencephalography – EEG) or electrocorticography (ECoG)), (2) magnetic fields (e.g., magnetoencephalography – MEG), and (3) level of blood oxygen or blood flow (e.g., functional near infrared spectroscopy – NIRS or functional magnetic resonance imaging – fMRI). This neuroinformation is being decoded to develop neural interfaces that aim to establish, re-establish and/or improve the neural interconnectivity of CNS in order to optimize the human-environment interaction. Not only decoding of neuroinformation has been pursued so far, but also finding the best way to recode neuroinformation by brain stimulation has been of interest in the scientific community.

title: 30 Years of Hypocretin/Orexin Research: Sleep–Wake Regulation, Reward, and Motivation
summary: The orexin/hypocretin system, first identified in 1998, is now recognized as a central regulator of energy balance, sleep–wake states, and arousal stability. Orexin-producing neurons in the lateral hypothalamus integrate circadian, metabolic, and environmental signals to promote wakefulness and stabilize sleep–wake transitions. Beyond arousal regulation, orexin signaling plays a key role in hedonic and motivational processes, as these neurons densely innervate limbic and reward-related brain regions. Disruption of this system has been implicated in sleep disorders, including narcolepsy type 1, insomnia, and hypersomnia, as well as substance use disorders. Emerging evidence further links orexin dysfunction to neurodevelopmental, neurodegenerative, and psychiatric conditions.

title: Advanced neuroimaging techniques in stroke management
summary: In recent years, the field of neuroimaging has undergone substantial advancements, significantly transforming stroke management. Stroke remains a leading cause of morbidity and mortality worldwide, demanding precise diagnostic capabilities for efficient treatment. Conventional imaging methods, though invaluable, often fall short in offering detailed insight into brain function and structure following a stroke. As a result, there is an ongoing endeavor among researchers to refine imaging techniques for improved diagnostic accuracy, timely interventions, and optimized patient outcomes.

Traditionally, fear memory—how the brain learns, stores, and recalls threat-related experiences—has been central to understanding conditions such as post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD). However, converging evidence now suggests that maladaptive fear memory processing may also influence, and be influenced by, the metabolic dysregulation observed in diabetes as well as cognitive and emotional changes during aging. Recent studies have highlighted the involvement of key physiological systems such as the hypothalamic–pituitary–adrenal (HPA) axis, autonomic function, inflammatory signaling, and neuroplasticity, in mediating these interactions. title: Alterations in brain structure and cognitive function caused by cerebrovascular diseases Volume III
summary: Cerebrovascular diseases manifest as disruptive and deteriorating conditions, gravely impacting cognitive functions by altering the neurophysiological structure of the brain. With particular attention to diseases like Moyamoya and vascular malformations, the occlusion of internal carotid arteries, and abnormal vascular networks, these diseases lead to progressive cognitive and functional impairments. Although recent researches have offered valuable insights into the pathophysiology, much remains hazy, including the mechanisms through which these diseases alter cognitive processes and brain structure.

title: Applied Artificial Intelligence in Education: Generative Tools, Learning Analytics, Assessment, and Governance
summary: Artificial intelligence is becoming increasingly embedded in educational systems through generative tools, learning analytics, educational data mining, automated feedback, adaptive assessment, and predictive models. These developments offer new possibilities to personalize instruction, support early identification of students’ needs, improve assessment practices, and strengthen data-informed decision-making across schools and universities. At the same time, the implementation of AI-based systems raises important questions regarding validity, explainability, fairness, privacy, transparency, and governance, as well as their practical implications for teachers’ work and institutional practice.

title: Impact of Invasive Species on the Ecology and Transmission of Pathogens
summary: Invasive species are recognized as a major threat to global biodiversity and ecosystem stability. Their introduction into new environments can reshape ecological networks, modify host community composition, and alter pathogen transmission pathways. Many invasive species carry pathogens from their native ranges or acquire local pathogens in the invaded ecosystem, potentially increasing disease risks for native wildlife, livestock, and humans.Veterinary pathology and disease ecology play a key role in understanding these processes. Pathological investigations can reveal the health impacts of invasive species and identify emerging disease patterns. At the same time, ecological and epidemiological studies help clarify how invasive hosts contribute to pathogen maintenance, amplification, or spillover events. Integrating these approaches is essential to better predict disease risks associated with biological invasions.

title: Intersections of Mental Health, Psychiatry, and Education in the Global South: Key Insights and Challenges
summary: The interaction between mental health systems, educational institutions, and contemporary psychiatric frameworks is deeply shaped by historical, cultural, and political factors. While global mental health initiatives have expanded substantially over the past two decades, models developed in high-income countries often fail to translate seamlessly into low- and middle-income countries (LMICs). This is particularly true when they insufficiently account for local epistemologies, institutional constraints, and entrenched social inequities. In many Global South contexts, psychiatric knowledge circulates alongside indigenous, community-based, and informal systems of care, producing mental health landscapes that challenge universalized assumptions about diagnosis, intervention and effectiveness. title: Proteomics and Multi-Omics Approaches to Brain Tumors and Multiple Sclerosis: Linking Neuroinflammation and Neurodegeneration
summary: Neurological diseases, from brain tumors to neurodegenerative and neuroinflammatory disorders, are among the most difficult to diagnose and treat. Conditions like gliomas, medulloblastomas, multiple sclerosis, Alzheimer’s disease, ALS, and other central nervous system disorders are marked by complex molecular and cellular diversity. Traditional single-omic methods often miss the interactions between genetics, epigenetics, protein function, metabolism, and the surrounding environment. New precision proteomics and multi-omics technologies have transformed the field. By studying proteins, their modifications, metabolic changes, and how different molecular layers interact, these tools provide insights that DNA and RNA analysis alone cannot offer. These constraints restrict trainees’ opportunities for hands-on practice during their curriculum. Cost-effective solutions that enable practice on any study case, at any time, and as often as needed are required.

title: Real-world epilepsy care: integrating neuroscience, diagnostic precision and treatment pathways across diverse clinical settings
summary: Epilepsy is a complex neurological disorder whose management increasingly benefits from advances in neuroscience, including neuroimaging, electrophysiology, and network analysis. Despite this progress, real-world clinical care still faces significant hurdles, such as delayed diagnosis, misclassification of seizure types, and variability in the application of evidence-based treatments. Recent studies demonstrate substantial potential for tools like EEG biomarkers, computational models, and novel imaging techniques to enhance diagnostic and therapeutic precision. However, gaps persist in translating these innovations into routine clinical practice, particularly in diverse clinical environments and among vulnerable populations, leaving many patients without optimal care.

Consequently, healthcare information systems, including electronic health records, telehealth platforms, and digital health infrastructure, have emerged as attractive targets for cybercriminals due to the high economic and strategic value of health data, which often fetches a premium on the black market. This material-driven design in robotics will bring a new wave of applications, such as environment-safe, mass-deployable robots for search and rescue missions, life-like edible robots that attract animals and provide nutrition when consumed, or appetitive robotic food that provides a gastronomic experience for humans, to name a few.

From the humble Drosophila, which has significantly contributed to our understanding of the molecular clock and these daily patterns, to human clinical work shaped by external cues like light, and in between, the nocturnal mouse is used ubiquitously across neuroscience. title: Echoes of Genocide: Transgenerational Trauma
summary: Genocidal events have consistently left profound psychological scars on affected populations, resulting in a legacy of trauma that persists through successive generations. Public mental health research has progressively acknowledged the importance of recognizing and comprehending the long-term effects of such violence and atrocities on minority communities. Investigations are increasingly demonstrating that trauma is not isolated to direct survivors, but rather transmits intergenerationally, impacting descendants who did not experience the events directly themselves. However, despite growing evidence of these transgenerational psychological impacts, there remain significant gaps in understanding exactly how mechanisms of trauma transmission occur, and how they influence community resilience, coping strategies, and overall mental health outcomes.

Advances in spatial computing, wearable sensing, haptics, telepresence, and AI-mediated interaction are expanding the ways users can experience body ownership, agency, and self–other boundaries in digital environments. At the same time, the field is maturing: researchers are increasingly expected to deliver robust experimental designs, stronger ecological validity, and clearer links between subjective experience and underlying neurocognitive mechanisms.

title: Exploring electrochemotherapy as a promising intervention in veterinary cancer care
summary: Electrochemotherapy represents an emerging modality in veterinary oncology, garnering attention for its targeted efficacy in treating various tumor types in animals. By combining chemotherapeutic agents, such a d bleomycin and cisplatin, with electric pulses, this technique enhances drug uptake in cancer cells, thus potentiating therapeutic effects while minimizing systemic side effects. This method is particularly valuable for its ability to treat cutaneous and subcutaneous tumors that might be otherwise challenging to manage with conventional therapies alone, especially surgery.

title: Exploring the Role of Energy in Robot Learning and Control
summary: Energy principles have long played a central role in physics and engineering, offering powerful tools for modeling and controlling dynamical systems. In robotics, they enable stable and robust interactions in uncertain environments and support the analysis and interpretability of control actions. However, energy also provides a natural interface between control theory and AI, unifying physical structure with data-driven flexibility. As robots increasingly operate in complex, unstructured settings, learning-based control methods have gained traction for their adaptability, but they often lack formal safety guarantees, require large datasets, and are difficult to interpret. Energy-based methods offer a promising alternative by embedding physical structure into control and learning architectures. They provide a modular, interpretable way to model and regulate energy flow across subsystems, which is particularly valuable for physical interactions. Their compatibility with learning and opti

title: Extended Reality and Experiential Modalities in Healthcare
summary: Tangible and intangible experiential technologies have emerged as significant positive disruptors in healthcare. Modalities like virtual, augmented reality (VR/AR) and 3d printing, are all catering to the immediate need for visualization both in the practice and in the education of healthcare professionals. Teaching complex relations of neuroanatomical structures is where 3d prints and VR/AR, jointly referred as eXtended Reality (XR), excel. These relations and structures cannot be easily visualized in two dimensional atlases, neither discerned in cadaver dissections, hence making experiential means essential for understanding them. On the other hand, visualizing complex 3d structures from imaging data in the pre-operative stage of surgical preparation is equally important and is a core medical practice challenge. title: From Dish to Disease: Human organoid models for advancing gene therapy in neurodegenerative disorders
summary: Neurodegenerative diseases (NDDs) represent a profound challenge to global health, characterized by progressive neuronal dysfunction and loss, leading to debilitating conditions with limited therapeutic options. The complexity of human brain architecture and disease heterogeneity has historically hampered drug discovery, often due to the reliance on animal models that fail to fully recapitulate human disease pathology. The advent of induced pluripotent stem cell (iPSC) technology and subsequent development of three-dimensional (3D) organoid cultures have revolutionized disease modeling. These human-relevant models offer an unprecedented opportunity to study disease mechanisms and test novel interventions in a more physiologically accurate context. Concurrently, gene therapy strategies have emerged as promising avenues for targeted treatment, offering the potential to correct genetic defects or deliver therapeutic cargo directly to affected cells. title: From Tools to Teammates: Bridging the Digital Literacy Gap in Health Professions Education
summary: The digital transformation of healthcare is no longer a future prospect; it is our current reality. From the ubiquity of electronic health records (EHRs) to the rapid integration of AI-driven diagnostics, technology has moved from the periphery of the clinic to the heart of the patient–provider encounter. Yet, while hospitals are becoming “smarter,” educational frameworks are often still playing catch-up. Proficiency with digital health tools is no longer a niche technical skill; it is a core clinical competency. However, many practitioners find themselves "learning on the fly", navigating complex systems and AI-generated insights without a formal roadmap. This Research Topic explores how we can move beyond fragmented, informal training and build a robust, evidence-based curriculum that prepares the next generation of clinicians to thrive in a technology-rich environment.

title: Generative AI and Multimodal Interaction in Mental Health: From Theoretical Foundations to Clinical Product Implementation
summary: The rapid emergence of Generative Artificial Intelligence (GenAI) and Large Language Models (LLMs) is catalyzing a paradigm shift in mental health research and service delivery. While traditional AI approaches in psychiatry have primarily focused on discriminative tasks such as diagnostic classification, GenAI introduces new capacities for scalable human-like interaction, personalized content generation, and the synthesis of complex multimodal data (e.g., language, voice, facial expression, and movement). These advances may create opportunities to strengthen mental health promotion, prevention, and care provision at the population level—yet the field faces two key challenges: an epistemological gap in understanding how GenAI reshapes mental health theory and constructs (e.g., digital phenotypes and risk/protective factors), and an implementation gap in translating algorithms into robust, clinically and publicly validated, equitable, and governable tools for real-world settings.

title: Global Challenges and Opportunities of Collaborative Intelligence in Education
summary: The rapid expansion of artificial intelligence (AI) technologies is profoundly transforming teaching, learning, and assessment. This research proposal emphasizes the importance of interdisciplinary perspectives to explore AI's role in education, aiming to foster collaboration among researchers, policymakers, AI developers, and educators. While AI offers new opportunities for personalization, feedback, and efficiency, its integration raises essential questions about the nature of the educational act and the evolving role of teachers in algorithm-supported environments. This Research Topic introduces the concept of collaborative intelligence, understood as a dynamic partnership between humans and AI that enhances learning while preserving human values, ethical responsibility, and pedagogical judgment. By fostering interdisciplinary perspectives, the Topic aims to explore how AI reshapes professional identities, decision-making, and the teacher–student relationship. In alignment with Sust

title: Global Challenges in Brain Banking for Neurology Research
summary: Exploration of human brain tissue is pivotal for advancing neurology and improving public health, especially as the world faces a growing health crisis linked to the aging population and associated neurodegenerative diseases. Traditional animal models fall short in mirroring human brain pathophysiology, necessitating the use of human post-mortem specimens to thoroughly investigate brain functions and mechanisms under both normal and pathological states. The development of brain banks—facilities that collect, store, and manage brain specimens—in different ethnic-geographical contexts and the sharing of protocols and information are critical to support the evolution of "precision neurology," which aims to integrate clinicopathological data with genomic and other omics-based methodologies to illuminate the causes of brain diseases.

title: Gut-Brain Interactions in Neurodegeneration: Microbiota's Role in Cognitive Aging
summary: The gut-brain axis is an intricate communication network between the gastrointestinal tract and the central nervous system. Recent advancements have shed light on how the composition and activity of the gut microbiome can influence the development and course of neurodegenerative conditions frequently seen in aging, such as Alzheimer's disease, Parkinson’s disease, Mild Cognitive Impairment, and various forms of Dementia. Emerging evidence highlights mechanisms involving microbiota-derived metabolites, immune system modulation, and neural signaling pathways as principal routes through which the gut influences brain health and function. Despite accelerating progress, there remain substantial gaps in our understanding of the exact causal mechanisms and their translation into viable prevention or treatment approaches for neurodegenerative diseases. Human-Swarm Interaction: Theory, Practice, and Real-World Deployments
summary: Robot swarms, much like natural swarms such as ants and bees, consist of many independent autonomous agents working together to achieve a common task. Due to their decentralized nature, robot swarms are inherently scalable and robust to individual failures. They are capable of covering large areas or engaging with many people simultaneously. These qualities have enabled swarms to prove useful in diverse domains from providing wide-area coverage with firefighting drones to engaging groups of children in STEM education.

title: Human-shaped Ecosystems: Processes, Trade-offs and Ecosystem Services in a Drying World
summary: Humans have been modifying natural environments for millennia, leading to a deep co-evolution between social and natural systems. As a result, areas perceived as biodiversity hotspots, such as the Mediterranean Basin, are commonly composed of human-shaped ecosystems. Human-shaped ecosystems can be understood as systems in which human management is required to maintain ecological structure and processes, and where its absence or alteration compromises ecosystem dynamics and resilience. Such human-shaped ecosystems, ranging from agrosilvopastoral mosaics to managed grasslands and rangelands, illustrate the intertwined evolution of social and ecological processes. While these systems have persisted under traditional management, ongoing changes in land use, lifestyle, and climate are reshaping the trade-offs that govern ecosystem dynamics. title: Innovative electrode and bioelectronic technologies for neural recording and stimulation
summary: Neuroengineering is an ever-evolving field that is transforming our understanding of the nervous system through the development of sophisticated electrode and bioelectronic technologies. Traditional neural electrodes face significant challenges in interface stability, biocompatibility, long-term signal fidelity, and resolution, which hinder their broader application in neuroscience research and brain–machine interfacing. Recent studies have introduced innovations such as flexible materials, nano-scale architectures, and minimally invasive designs that promise higher integration with neural tissues, reduced immune response, and improved longevity. Despite these advances, achieving seamless, durable, and high-resolution communication with neural circuits remains one of the central challenges in next-generation neural interfacing.

title: Integrating Environmental and Social Determinants of Mental Health Through a Life-Course Lens
summary: Environmental exposures such as air pollution, air toxics, noise, wildfire smoke, and extreme heat contribute significantly to the global burden of mental health conditions. Yet, their impacts are unevenly distributed across populations, reflecting entrenched social and spatial heterogeneity. Individuals in low-income or marginalized communities are often more likely to live in polluted areas, experience higher cumulative exposures, and have limited access to healthcare or adaptive resources. Life-course epidemiology offers a powerful framework to examine how such exposures interact with biological susceptibility, behavioral factors, and social determinants across time and have impact on mental health. Understanding how environmental stressors accumulate and interact throughout the life span is essential for uncovering mechanisms of environmental injustice and informing equitable public health interventions.

title: Interpretable AI and Neuroscience in Mental Disorders: Mechanisms and Advances in Neuropsychopharmacology
summary: The field of mental health care is undergoing rapid transformation driven by technological innovations and neuroscientific insights, with interpretable artificial intelligence (AI) emerging as a pivotal force shaping research and clinical practice. Traditional models of diagnosis and risk assessment are often constrained by subjective measures and the “black box” nature of conventional AI approaches, which can obscure underlying psychiatric mechanisms and contribute to variability in care quality. In recent years, AI technologies have demonstrated remarkable potential in enhancing the precision of neuropsychopharmacological research, improving predictive modeling of cognitive impairment, and enabling the design of personalized therapeutic interventions informed by pharmacogenetic factors. title: Learning on Trees and Graphs: Deep Learning & Graph Neural Networks for Phylogenetics and Eco‑Evolutionary Systems
summary: The fields of ecology and evolutionary biology are fundamentally structured by relationships represented as trees and graphs. Phylogenetic trees delineate evolutionary ancestry, while ecological interaction networks and gene-flow graphs capture intricate relationships such as predation, pollination, dispersal, and hybridization. However, real-world datasets present formidable challenges: incomplete sampling, noisy measurements, and co-occurring processes that entangle evolutionary, ecological, and environmental signals across different scales. The advent of large, multimodal datasets, integrating genomics, traits, climate variables, microbiomes, and remote sensing, adds complexity that often exceeds the capacity of traditional models.

title: Life Cycles and Reproductive Strategies in Medusozoa
summary: Medusozoa, a subphylum of Cnidaria, constitutes a fascinating and diverse group of marine organisms characterized by their ability to alternate between benthic (polyp) and pelagic (medusa) life stages. These transitions, along with the varied reproductive strategies—including both sexual and asexual reproduction—make them ecologically significant in marine environments. Factors such as genetic makeup, physiological conditions, and environmental influences, play critical roles in shaping their reproductive processes, which, in turn, have profound implications for species dispersal, food web interactions, and ecosystem stability.

summary: In today’s globalized digital era, media function as symbolic environments through which culture and society are more intertwined than ever. The creative and cultural industries operate within media-saturated, globally networked environments that transcend geographic boundaries. Digital platforms and communication systems not only facilitate the production and circulation of cultural content worldwide, but also shape how that content is experienced and how communities create meaning and identity around it. Audiences have become active participants in this ecosystem, engaging with media through social networks, sharing and remixing content, and even co-creating cultural narratives as part of collective meaning-making. This profound global intersection of media, culture, and society raises critical questions about how our evolving media environment is influencing meaning-making, cultural identities, creative labor, social values, and economic opportunities across diverse communities. title: Multimodal Social Robots for Wellbeing and Health Support
summary: In recent years, social robots have moved from experimental visions to tangible implementations in education, healthcare, therapy, and everyday support. Their ability to sense and respond through multi-modal channels, including voice, movement, haptics, bio-signals, gestures and facial expressions, positions social robots as promising companions for well-being. This trend aligns with a growing societal interest in non-clinical health interventions and inclusive technologies that enhance resilience, autonomy, and improve quality of life. Social robots are increasingly being used to support interventions aimed at stress reduction, emotional regulation, and physical exercise. While progress has been made, further research is needed to understand how these multi-modal social robots for wellbeing and health support can be ethically designed, inclusively applied, and effectively evaluated across diverse contexts and populations.

title: Neuroendocrine control of glucose homeostasis in health and disease
summary: The field of neuroendocrine control of glucose homeostasis is pivotal in understanding the complex interplay between metabolic diseases and brain disorders. These conditions, such as obesity and diabetes mellitus, significantly impact the quality of life for millions globally. The maintenance of glucose homeostasis is crucial for physiological functions, yet the precise mechanisms governing this balance remain a topic of intense debate. Recent studies suggest that the regulation of blood glucose levels involves a sophisticated interaction between hormones, neuropeptides, and neurotransmitters, primarily orchestrated by the brain, peripheral nerves, and pancreatic islets. However, the intricate communication pathways between the brain and pancreatic islets pose challenges in fully comprehending their role in glucose regulation. This gap in understanding underscores the need for innovative research to inform future clinical interventions aimed at preserving neurometabolic health.

title: Neurophysiological basis of rhythm and synchronization in motor activities
summary: Exploring the neurophysiological basis of rhythm and synchronization in motor activities is needed to further neuroscience knowledge and principles underlying rehabilitation and therapeutic approaches. Further, to engender a comprehensive understanding of complex behaviors, e.g., gait, movements that create dance and the motor production of music, carefully planned studies must be conducted. Avenues for clinical applications, include rehabilitation strategies for neurological disorders like Parkinson's disease, Alzheimer's disease, multiple sclerosis, and stroke. Current research has begun to reveal a window into how the brain and spinal cord orchestrate rhythmic movements and synchronize actions.

Historically, research in fish nutrition has prioritized the replacement of fish meal and fish oil with alternative ingredients to achieve nutritional adequacy, enhance production performance, and maintain organoleptic properties, primarily due to the high cost associated with feed ingredients.

Contemporary research reveals that intensive livestock production, substandard animal welfare, and unsustainable veterinary practices are contributing not only to environmental pollution and biodiversity loss, but also to adverse health outcomes such as metabolic, respiratory, and neurodegenerative diseases across species. Recent studies highlight that changes in animal nutrition, antimicrobial stewardship, and veterinary-led sustainability initiatives can profoundly influence food safety, zoonotic risks, and environmental resilience. summary: The study of Gondwana's paleontology sheds light on the remarkable biostratigraphic, paleoecological, and evolutionary processes that have shaped ancient ecosystems. With continents now separated, the legacy of Gondwana provides a unique opportunity to investigate the distribution and diversity of past life forms. Recent studies have highlighted the distinct biostratigraphic sequences across regions that once formed part of this supercontinent. Moreover, paleoecological reconstructions offer insights into the environmental factors that influenced species adaptations and extinctions. title: Perioperative Anesthetic Management in Veterinary Emergency Medicine
summary: The field of veterinary anesthesiology faces extraordinary complexity in the perioperative management of emergency patients. Emergency situations often involve animals with unstable physiological states, pre-existing illness, or trauma, making them particularly vulnerable to anesthetic complications. With time for preoperative stabilization often limited, anesthetic management must adapt rapidly to the dynamic and unpredictable nature of such cases. Despite advancements in anesthetic techniques and monitoring modalities, there remains a significant risk of perioperative morbidity and mortality among these high-risk patient populations. Recent literature highlights the need for tailored approaches that address both the physiological status and species-specific considerations, yet existing practices often draw heavily on protocols designed for elective procedures or human medicine, leaving important gaps in veterinary-specific guidance. title: Personalized Intervention: N-of-1 Trials Using Wearable Devices
summary: Personalized clinical research is gaining momentum as the limitations of population-based studies in guiding individual patient care become more apparent. Traditional clinical trials primarily aim to determine treatment effects at the cohort level, often producing results that best fit the "average" participant. However, this population-optimized approach can fall short when applied to single patients whose responses to treatments might differ significantly from group averages. As healthcare moves toward individualized medicine, the need for methodologies that generate actionable knowledge at the level of the single person is increasingly recognized.

Advances in human robot collaboration, responsive robotics, and AI in manufacturing enable production systems that dynamically adapt to human behaviour, environmental changes, and product variability. Central to this evolution are human digital twins, which model physical, cognitive, and ergonomic aspects of workers, and human intention prediction, allowing robots to anticipate actions and respond proactively. At the system level, responsive manufacturing supports rapid reconfiguration and mass personalization. title: The Motor System in Health and Disease: From Function to Recovery
summary: The motor system is fundamental for voluntary movement, coordination, and interaction with our environment, encompassing a complex network of interconnected brain regions and neural pathways. Recent advances in neuroscience have shed light on the sophisticated mechanisms behind motor planning, execution, and control, while also revealing how these processes break down in disease and injury. Despite significant progress, key questions remain regarding how the brain integrates sensory information, translates intention into action, and adapts to dysfunction through plasticity and compensation. Research in this area is critical not only for advancing our understanding of basic neurobiology, but also for informing clinical approaches to a wide range of neurological conditions – including stroke, Parkinson’s disease, spinal cord injuries, and other disorders that impair movement. While mechanistic and neurophysiological research has expanded rapidly, translation into consistent clinical practice has lagged. Audiologists often report uncertainty regarding optimal assessment batteries, counseling approaches, and outcome tracking, particularly for patients with comorbid conditions, sound intolerance, or hearing device use. Recent work has emphasized the importance of validated patient-reported outcome measures, structured counseling frameworks, and individualized management strategies that reflect patient goals and lived experiences. Additionally, growing attention to pediatric populations, lifespan perspectives, and health equity underscores the need for flexible, scalable clinical models. title: Trait-based Approaches to Inform Conservation and Restoration of Marine Ecosystems
summary: Biological and ecological characteristics of a species, or “traits,” provide an alternative essential unit to species for community analyses. A trait is a well-defined, measurable characteristic that reflects species morphology, physiology, phenology, life history, or behaviour, as well as its performance within ecosystems. We refer to effect or response traits if they indicate influence on ecosystem function or response to environmental or anthropogenic changes, respectively. Effect traits, therefore, help bridge species diversity with ecosystem functions and services, whereas response traits help identify sensitive species to threats. Acting as a “common currency” across taxa and ecosystems, traits enable comparisons among distinct ecosystems. title: Computational mechanisms of sensory and multisensory integration in perception and action
summary: While considerable progress has been made in mapping sensory and multisensory processing at behavioral and neural levels, key questions remain regarding the computational rules and neural implementations underlying integration. How does the brain weigh and combine inputs with varying reliability? At what stages and under what conditions are signals fused versus maintained separately? How do these processes differ between perception and action, and which neurobiological mechanisms are shared or distinct? This Research Topic aims to bring together interdisciplinary investigations that combine neurophysiology, psychophysics, computational modeling, and artificial intelligence to reveal new insights into the computational principles governing multisensory integration. By synthesizing experimental, theoretical, and applied approaches, we seek to clarify how the brain manages sensory uncertainties and coordinates perception with flexible, goal-directed action.

title: Developing Musical Expression, Communication, and Wellbeing
summary: Through music people express themselves, their ideas, thoughts and feelings. Music holds affordances for meaning making and communication that can be beneficial for health and wellbeing. Through various socially engaged practices, people use musicking to communicate with each other. Music can be used to enhance wellbeing in various contexts, including health care settings and as a tool for social impact. Musical expression and communication have the potential to enhance people's sense of wellbeing; however, this does not happen automatically and can be particularly challenging for those studying or working within the music profession. Therefore, it is vital to explore the variety of processes involved in developing musical expression and communication that enhance wellbeing for all involved. These processes include (but are not limited to) psychological, educational, and artistic domains.

Multiscale neural mechanisms mediating multisensory integration
summary: Multisensory integration is a cornerstone of cognitive function, allowing the brain to synthesize disparate streams of information into a coherent perceptual experience. Despite decades of research, a significant "explanatory gap" persists between our understanding of microscale cellular processes and macroscale behavioral outcomes. Current neurobiological approaches often operate in isolation, focusing either on the properties of individual neurons or the dynamics of large-scale networks. However, to understand how the brain resolves cross-modal information, it is essential to characterize the multiscale interactions occurring within and cross cortical and subcortical circuits. The advent of high-resolution recording techniques and advanced computational modeling now provides an unprecedented opportunity to bridge these domains. Novel Approaches to the Diagnosis and Treatment of Neuropsychiatric Disorders
summary: Neuropsychiatric disorders, encompassing conditions such as depression, schizophrenia, bipolar disorder, and Alzheimer’s disease, represent a leading cause of global disability. Despite significant research, their complex and often overlapping etiologies pose immense challenges for accurate diagnosis and effective treatment. Current diagnostic criteria largely rely on subjective clinical assessments, and many available therapeutics offer limited efficacy or carry substantial side effects. However, the convergence of advances in neuroscience, genomics, neuroimaging, and digital technology is fostering a transformative era. This Research Topic aims to capture and contribute to this momentum by exploring innovative, multidisciplinary strategies that promise to redefine our understanding and management of these debilitating conditions.

title: Hidden Signals - The Neurological, Nonverbal, and Physiological Foundations of Human Behavior
summary: The field of human behaviour increasingly recognizes the profound influence of signals that extend beyond explicit goals and verbal information. These “hidden signals” include neural and physiological processes within the body, as well as nonverbal cues such as voice quality, facial expression, posture, and movement. Such embodied dynamics often elude straightforward observation and description, particularly in research that prioritizes overt behaviour or verbal content. Together, these hidden signals represent a foundational yet relatively unexplored layer of human cognition and behaviour.

title: Mentalization Across Developmental Contexts: Applications in Childhood, Adolescence, and Family Systems
summary: Adolescent mental health care is a changing field at the intersection of clinical innovation and developmental science. Increasing attention has been given to mentalization – the capacity to understand oneself and others in terms of intentional mental states – as a key mechanism underpinning psychological and psychosocial development and therapeutic change. Mentalization-based treatment (MBT) was originally developed for adults, for people with BPD in particular, but has increasingly been adapted for children, adolescents, and families. These adaptations reflect the need for developmentally sensitive, relational, and contextually grounded interventions that account for the complexity of caregiving environments, attachment relationships, and broader social contexts. title: Software as a Medical Device in Diagnostic and Therapeutic Care: From Development to Real-World Implementation
summary: Software as a Medical Device (SaMD) is reshaping diagnostic and therapeutic pathways, from AI-enabled interpretation of clinical data and images to software that guides treatment selection, monitoring, and the delivery of digital therapeutics. Yet translation into routine care remains uneven. Evidence generation is frequently disconnected from regulatory qualification and classification, quality management, cybersecurity, and lifecycle obligations. Implementation failures often reflect workflow misfit, usability constraints, limited clinician trust calibration, and insufficient monitoring of real-world performance, drift, and subgroup inequities. In parallel, the European MDR/IVDR transition and the emergence of the EU AI Act are creating new compliance interfaces that many developers and clinical teams struggle to operationalize. title: Telemedicine in Epilepsy
summary: As a leading cause of neurological disability, Epilepsy continues to reveal marked disparities in diagnosis, treatment, and long-term management. Telemedicine has emerged as a pragmatic and scalable strategy to address these gaps across the care pathway: triage and referral, diagnostic workup, antiseizure medication (ASM) optimization, management of ketogenic dietary therapy, comorbidity screening, and surgical evaluation. In recent years there has been a rapid adoption of synchronous video consultations, remote EEG interpretation workflows, mobile seizure diaries, and device-integrated data sharing, demonstrating feasibility, patient acceptance, and potential cost-efficiency. Concurrent advances, such as wearable biosensors for seizure detection, home-based EEG/ECG, AI-driven event classification, and integrated electronic health records (EHRs), are enabling continuous monitoring and more personalized care plans. While the influence of pollutants on individual species and populations is an emerging area of study, the broader implications for developmental mechanisms, phenotypic variation, and ecosystem functioning remain underexplored. Soil ecosystems are dynamic interfaces where contaminants interact with diverse biota, including microbes, invertebrates, and plants, influencing crucial ecological functions such as nutrient cycling, organic matter decomposition, and soil structure maintenance. Recent research suggests that exposure to emerging contaminants may induce developmental plasticity, trigger epigenetic responses, and prompt novel adaptations. This Research Topic specifically emphasizes the role of applied field-scale solutions and cross-ecosystem interventions for the conservation and restoration of natural systems by mitigating contaminant impacts. title: Mitochondrial dysfunction in cerebrovascular diseases: mechanisms and neurological consequences
summary: Mitochondria are central regulators of cellular metabolism, redox balance, and cell survival in the nervous system. In recent years, growing evidence has highlighted mitochondrial dysfunction as a critical contributor to the pathophysiology of cerebrovascular diseases, including ischemic and hemorrhagic stroke, cerebral small vessel disease, and vascular cognitive impairment. Because neurons, astrocytes, microglia, and cerebrovascular endothelial cells have high metabolic demands and tightly regulated mitochondrial dynamics, disturbances in mitochondrial function can profoundly influence neural viability and neurovascular unit integrity during cerebrovascular injury.

title: Airborne Microbial Pathogens in Poultry: Transmission Pathways, Pathogenic Mechanisms, and Advanced Detection Strategies
summary: The intensification of poultry production has heightened concern over aerosolized microbial pathogens that traverse barn microclimates, ventilation systems, and surrounding environments. Bioaerosols, dust particles, and droplets can harbor viruses, bacteria, and fungi capable of surviving transport, evading host defenses, and initiating infection, thereby impacting flock health, productivity, biosecurity and even poultry farm workers. Airborne transmission also complicates control of antimicrobial resistance and zoonotic spillover risk at the animal–human–environment interface. Advances in aerobiology, high-resolution genomics, and real-time sensing now offer new opportunities to quantify pathogen load, viability, and dispersal, while integrative field, laboratory, and modeling studies can illuminate the drivers and consequences of airborne spread. title: Aquaporins, glymphatic dynamics, and the molecular mechanisms of neurodegenerative brain aging
summary: Aquaporins (AQPs) are fundamental membrane proteins involved in the regulation of water and solute transport across cellular barriers in the central nervous system. In recent years, the significance of AQPs, particularly AQP4, in maintaining cerebral homeostasis has been increasingly recognized, especially in the context of brain aging and neurodegenerative diseases. While their classical function centers on fluid balance, emerging evidence shows that aquaporins are implicated in processes such as neuroinflammation, glymphatic clearance, and blood-brain barrier integrity. Despite continued advances, major questions remain regarding the precise contributions of aquaporins to neurodegenerative pathology, the interplay between different AQP subtypes, and their potential as therapeutic targets for age-related neurological disorders.

title: Artificial Intelligence for the Prevention, Surveillance, and Control of Animal Infectious Diseases
summary: Animal infectious diseases remain a major threat to animal health and welfare, livestock and aquaculture sustainability, and public health through zoonotic risk. At the same time, Artificial Intelligence (AI) is emerging as a powerful tool for advancing the understanding, prevention, and control of infectious diseases in animal populations. Machine learning and related data-driven approaches are increasingly being used to model pathogen transmission, identify environmental drivers of disease emergence, predict outbreak risk, optimize vaccination strategies, strengthen antimicrobial stewardship, and integrate complex epidemiological, immunological, genomic, and ecological datasets. These developments offer new opportunities to support more targeted, timely, and effective infectious disease management across production animals, companion animals, wildlife, and aquatic species. title: Clinical application of large language models in sleep medicine
summary: The integration of large language models (LLMs) into healthcare has heralded a new era of digital transformation, particularly given the diverse and rapidly evolving landscape of both proprietary and open-source LLM architectures. Since the emergence of ChatGPT and its contemporaries, there has been an exponential growth in LLM adoption across key sectors, with healthcare at the forefront of this revolution. LLMs are streamlining clinical documentation, enhancing decision support, enabling research synthesis, and supporting education, fundamentally reshaping workflows and the delivery of care. Recent studies have demonstrated their ability to convert unstructured clinical data into structured, actionable insights and to assist in evidence-based treatment planning. However, the application of these technologies to specialized fields, such as sleep medicine, remains at an early but promising stage.

title: Ethical AI ecosystems: Balancing privacy and security challenges
summary: Artificial Intelligence (AI) has been rapidly advancing and integrating into numerous sectors, such as healthcare and finance, creating groundbreaking opportunities and transformative impacts. However, the incorporation of AI also brings forward critical concerns, particularly around privacy and security. As AI systems are entrusted with processing increasingly sensitive data, the challenge intensifies in maintaining stringent privacy and security standards within the ethical frameworks of these dynamic ecosystems. There is an ongoing discourse regarding how to balance the advantages AI offers with the adherence to ethical standards that protect user data and ensure trustworthiness.

title: Explainable, Interpretable, and Human-Aligned AI and Robotics
summary: As artificial intelligence and robotic systems become increasingly autonomous and complex, their deployment in real-world, human-centered environments raises critical challenges related to interpretability, transparency, trust, and safety. While modern learning-based approaches, particularly foundation models and reinforcement learning, have achieved remarkable performance, they often operate as opaque “black boxes,” limiting human understanding and oversight. This lack of explainability hampers user trust, accountability, and effective human–AI collaboration, especially in safety-critical robotic applications. Addressing these challenges requires interdisciplinary approaches that integrate cognitive modeling, causal reasoning, multimodal grounding, and human-aware system design. title: Fluid Biomarkers in Neurodegeneration: Revolutionizing Early Detection and Prognosis
summary: Over the past decade, fluid biomarkers have transformed the conceptual and clinical framework of neurodegenerative diseases. In Alzheimer’s disease (AD), cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) measures of amyloid-β peptides, phosphorylated tau, and total tau, together with emerging blood-based biomarkers such as plasma p-tau isoforms, neurofilament light chain (NfL), and glial markers, have moved from research settings toward clinical implementation. This shift has enabled the transition from a purely syndromic diagnosis to a biologically defined disease model, as reflected in the AT(N) framework. The AD model demonstrates that neurodegeneration can be detected years before clinical symptoms emerge, opening new opportunities for early intervention and disease-modifying therapies. Importantly, this paradigm is now extending beyond AD, influencing biomarker research in other neurodegenerative disorders related to aging, including Parkinson’s disease, frontotemporal dementia, and atypical parkinsonism
image_alt: Fluid Biomarkers in Neurodegeneration: Revolutionizing Early Detection and Prognosis

title: Innovation in Education and Healthcare: The Role of Virtual Reality and Immersive Technologies
summary: Immersive technologies—virtual reality (VR), augmented reality (AR) and mixed reality (MR)—represent a paradigm shift in healthcare training and clinical practice. In recent years, scientific evidence has shown that these technologies significantly improve the acquisition of clinical knowledge and skills, reduce training times, increase patient safety, and optimise operational costs.

title: Integrating attention and social cognition: from brain mechanisms to behavior
summary: Social cognition research explores how humans detect, interpret, and respond to social cues—capacities that are fundamentally shaped by attentional mechanisms. Recent advances in cognitive psychology and neuroscience have deepened our understanding of ‘social attention’, demonstrating how processes such as gaze following, joint attention, and sensitivity to emotional signals guide social engagement. While key findings emphasize the interplay between perceptual, emotional, and cognitive factors in social contexts, current knowledge remains fragmented across behavioral, neural, clinical, and theoretical domains. Bridging these diverse approaches is vital to clarifying how attention operates within complex and dynamic social environments, and to addressing unresolved questions about individual and developmental variability, underlying neural circuitry, and the impact of atypical attentional processing on social functioning.

title: Intercellular Communication and Vesicle-Mediated Pathology Propagation in Neurodegeneration
summary: The central nervous system (CNS) is governed by complex intercellular communication networks that extend beyond traditional synaptic signaling. Soluble factors, direct membrane contacts, and extracellular vesicles (EVs) all mediate the exchange of information between diverse cell types. EVs transfer proteins, lipids, and nucleic acids between neurons, glia, and vascular-associated cells, orchestrating dynamic communication within the CNS. Increasing evidence highlights the role of EVs in the propagation of neurodegenerative pathology. In Alzheimer’s disease, EVs transport tau species between neurons and glial cells, potentially facilitating disease spread. In Parkinson’s disease and related synucleinopathies, vesicle-associated alpha-synuclein is believed to drive the intercellular propagation of misfolded proteins. title: Perception in Virtual Worlds: Sensorimotor Contingencies, Perceptual Illusions, and Presence
summary: Immersive VR and XR now allow perceptual science to be conducted under rich, interactive conditions that approximate everyday sensorimotor engagement better than conventional screen-based paradigms. However, virtual worlds are not neutral containers: presence, embodiment, and agency can amplify attentional capture and reshape perceptual judgments, while device optics, latency, locomotion interfaces, and haptic realism can introduce systematic biases. As a result, findings obtained in virtual environments may diverge from classic laboratory outcomes in both magnitude and mechanism. A coherent research agenda is needed to explain when immersion improves ecological validity, when it compromises inference, and which design and measurement practices yield reliable and reproducible perception research in virtual worlds.

title: Social Determinants and Gender Dynamics in Suicide: Moving Toward Population-Level Solutions
summary: Suicide remains one of the most pressing yet complex public health challenges of our time. While the global conversation on mental health is expanding, the "gender paradox" in suicide—where women often report higher rates of suicidal ideation and attempts, while men typically account for a higher proportion of suicide deaths—remains a critical area of investigation. Understanding these differences requires moving beyond gender-neutral perspectives to examine how biological, psychological, social, and structural forces uniquely shape the suicidal process for individuals across the gender spectrum.

title: Technology-Enabled Neuropsychiatric Cognitive Care in Aging: Foundation and Implementation Opportunities
summary: Aging is accompanied by increasing rates of cognitive disorders and neuropsychiatric symptoms (NPS) including depression, anxiety, apathy, agitation, sleep disturbance, and psychosis across the cognitive spectrum. These symptoms often emerge in preclinical and prodromal stages, accelerate functional decline, increase caregiver distress, and contribute to earlier institutionalization. Mental health vulnerabilities intersect with biological risk factors, chronic stress, gender, socioeconomic inequities, and cultural barriers to care. At the same time, advances in innovative technologies, including immersive technologies (e.g., VR/AR), multimodal sensors, and advanced predictive analytics (e.g. machine learning) are reshaping opportunities for prevention, prediction, early detection, symptom management, and caregiver support. title: Translating neurodiversity: From predictive mechanisms to embodied systems
summary: Cognitive and social development emerge from unified neural mechanisms that support predictive processing and active inference. These mechanisms enable individuals to generate expectations about incoming sensory input, regulate internal states, and guide action based on learned internal models. Importantly, such mechanisms are thought to underlie cognitive development across domains, including both sensorimotor coordination and social interaction, within a common predictive framework. These internal models are shaped not in isolation, but through ongoing interactions with the physical, social, and sensory environment. In neurodiverse individuals, variations in these predictive processes and environmental interactions can lead to distinctive developmental trajectories, producing unique sensory profiles, regulation strategies, and expressive behaviors.
image_alt: Translating neurodiversity: From predictive mechanisms to embodied systems

title: UN World Creativity and Innovation Day: Creativity in Brain Health and Neuroscience Vol II
summary: The UN World Day of Creativity and Innovation takes place on the 21st April, presenting an opportunity to form a global, unified front to promote international awareness about the importance of creativity in all aspects of human development and functioning. In the spirit of forming a united front, Frontiers is launching a new article collection to coincide with this UN day. This Research Topic aims to address the impact of creativity on brain as well as mental health as well as the complex neural dynamics underpinning creativity processing in the brain.

These findings are essential for scientific progress and transparency. title: Know your rodent: Impact of rodent strain on learning, memory, cognition and animal models of brain disease
summary: The choice of rodent strain for neuroscientific research is often considered a secondary factor when selecting rat or mouse models for functional studies of the brain. The predominant backstrain for transgenic mice is the C57BL/6 mouse strain, which is also the most widely used strain in non-transgenic experiments. However, this mouse strain develops progressive deafness beginning in early postnatal life and also exhibits a variety of ocular dysfunctions that may influence behavioral outcomes. Other mouse strains display marked differences in learning propensity, emotionality, and cognitive performance, as well as variability in both the behavioral symptoms and mechanistic underpinnings of disease models. A similar pattern is observed in rats, whereby, for example, Albino strains exhibit differences in learning compared to pigmented rat strains, that may be associated with differences in excitation-inhibition balance derives from altered GABAergic regulation.
image_alt: Know your rodent: Impact of rodent strain on learning, memory, cognition and animal models of brain disease

Parkinsonism Across Age-Related Neurodegenerative Diseases: Vulnerable Circuits, Proteinopathies, and Multimodal Biomarkers
summary: Parkinsonism is a common motor phenotype across age-related neurodegenerative diseases and frequently coexists with cognitive and behavioral syndromes. Although Parkinson’s disease is the prototypical parkinsonian syndrome, parkinsonism also occurs in dementia with Lewy bodies, multiple system atrophy, frontotemporal dementia, and in dementia due to Alzheimer’s disease. These conditions frequently coexist with mixed neuropathologies, including α-synuclein, tau, TDP 43, and Aβ-amyloid pathology. These overlapping phenotypes interacting pathologies challenge traditional diagnostic boundaries and complicate clinical trial design, particularly in older adults where co-pathologies are common.

summary: Building on the foundations established in Volume I and Volume II , Volume III of Social and Affective Domain in Home Language Development and Maintenance Research seeks to advance the field by addressing emerging transformations in multilingual life in the 2020s. While earlier volumes have provided important theoretical and empirical insights into the social and affective dimensions of home language practices, Volume III places particular emphasis on new global conditions shaping multilingualism, including digitalization, increased transnational mobility, forced migration, and evolving language ideologies.

title: Attentional Restoration, Emotional Modulation, and Fatigue Mitigation: The Contributing Role of Biophilia
summary: Biophilia, defined as the innate human affinity for nature, has emerged as an important framework for understanding how natural environments support attentional functioning, cognitive recovery, emotional regulation, and broader psychological functioning. Increasing evidence suggests that exposure to natural elements, such as greenery, natural light, and landscapes, plays a significant role in attentional restoration, emotional modulation, and fatigue intervention.
image_alt: Attentional Restoration, Emotional Modulation, and Fatigue Mitigation: The Contributing Role of Biophilia

title: Exploring Bereavement and Public Health, Volume II: The Role of Informal and Professional Caregivers in Community Well-Being
summary: Bereavement and grief exert significant, measurable effects on the health and well-being of individuals and society. The clinical community has formally recognized these effects through the introduction of a new diagnosis, Prolonged Grief Disorder. This recognition highlights the profound impact that grief can have on people's lives. Recent studies show that individuals experiencing bereavement are at higher risk for, and more likely to engage in, unhealthy behaviors such as alcohol abuse, smoking, and even suicide. These findings underscore the importance of addressing the health risks associated with grief and loss.
image_alt: Exploring Bereavement and Public Health, Volume II: The Role of Informal and Professional Caregivers in Community Well-Being

title: Health Outcomes of Using Antipsychotics
summary: Antipsychotics are crucial medications for treating and managing psychiatric conditions. These medications, which include both first-generation and second-generation antipsychotics, have significantly transformed mental health care by reducing symptoms and enhancing patients' quality of life. However, antipsychotics are associated with a range of outcomes, encompassing both therapeutic benefits and potential adverse effects. The significance of this Research Topic lies in optimizing treatment strategies by examining long-term health implications, assessing drug efficacy, and exploring real-world evidence. A comprehensive understanding of the health outcomes associated with antipsychotic use is essential for developing effective treatment approaches.

title: Insights in Evolutionary, Population, and Conservation Genetics Vol I
summary: The fields of evolutionary, population, and conservation genetics are advancing rapidly, propelled by progress in high-throughput sequencing, spatial and temporal genomics, and increasingly powerful statistical and computational approaches. These developments are reshaping how we infer gene flow and connectivity, reconstruct demographic history, quantify effective population size, detect selection and local adaptation, and monitor changes in genetic diversity across landscapes and through time. At the same time, biodiversity is under growing pressure from habitat fragmentation, land-use change, climate change, invasive species, and emerging diseases, making rigorous population and evolutionary genetic inference central to effective conservation and sustainable management.
image_alt: Insights in Evolutionary, Population, and Conservation Genetics Vol I

title: Neural Circuits and Network Dysfunctions in Depression and Anxiety
summary: Within human neuroscience, recent advances have transformed our perspective on depression and anxiety, reframing them as conditions of network-level dysfunction rather than isolated regional brain disturbances. Substantial evidence now implicates large-scale brain circuits supporting threat anticipation, reward processing, salience detection, cognitive control, and social-affective behaviors as core substrates underlying these disorders. While pioneering neuroimaging, genetic, and computational studies have identified distinct connectivity alterations and disrupted dynamics across these networks, key questions remain. The field is grappling with how these dysfunctions interact transdiagnostically, predict clinical heterogeneity, or evolve across the lifespan. Importantly, the translation of these circuit-based insights into diagnostic, prognostic, and therapeutic tools is an urgent, ongoing challenge.
image_alt: Neural Circuits and Network Dysfunctions in Depression and Anxiety

title: Seizures in Autoimmune and Systemic Inflammatory Disorders: Immunologic, Genetic, Metabolic, and Lifestyle Modifiers
summary: Seizures are increasingly recognized as a prominent manifestation of autoimmune and systemic inflammatory disorders. Beyond classic autoimmune encephalitis, a wide range of conditions including systemic lupus erythematosus, vasculitis, sarcoidosis, thyroid disease, and other immune-mediated or inflammatory state can predispose patients to seizures through mechanisms involving neuroinflammation, autoantibodies, blood–brain barrier dysfunction, and metabolic disruption. Advances in antibody testing, neuroimaging, and neurophysiology have improved detection of immune-mediated seizures; however, diagnostic delays and therapeutic uncertainty remain common, particularly in patients without overt encephalopathy. In parallel, emerging evidence suggests that metabolic status, sleep disturbance, stress, diet, and physical activity may influence immune activation and seizure susceptibility. title: Digital Biomarkers and Ambient Intelligence for Aging-Related Neurological Disorders
summary: Aging-related neurological disorders, including Parkinson’s disease and related synucleinopathies, dementia with Lewy bodies, Parkinson’s disease dementia, and Alzheimer’s disease and related dementias, are an increasingly urgent global public health challenge as populations continue to age. Conventional clinical assessments, typically performed in controlled environments and at widely spaced intervals, provide only brief snapshots of an individual’s functional status. As a result, they may miss early changes, day-to-day variability, and real-world impairments that are important for diagnosis, prognosis, and treatment monitoring. There is a critical need for approaches that can objectively quantify clinically meaningful changes in daily life while also informing our understanding of brain aging, aging-related neural dysfunction, and disease progression.

title: Speech Biomarkers in Psychiatry
summary: A wide range of psychiatric disorders, including schizophrenia spectrum disorders, major depressive disorder, bipolar disorder, and other conditions affecting cognition, affect, and social communication impact millions worldwide and pose significant diagnostic and monitoring challenges. Traditional assessment methods rely heavily on subjective self-report, clinical interviews, and intermittent observation, all of which are vulnerable to recall bias, stigma, symptom fluctuation, and limited clinical contact time.
image_alt: Speech Biomarkers in Psychiatry

title: Tracing the Genetic Odyssey of Psychiatric Disorders: From Twin Studies to Genomic Insights
summary: Psychiatric disorders such as schizophrenia, bipolar disorder, depression, and autism spectrum disorders present a significant global health burden, with profound social and economic consequences. For decades, the search for their origins has spanned both environmental and biological domains, with genetics emerging as a cornerstone in unraveling the complexity of these conditions.

title: Advances and Applications of Artificial Intelligence in Cerebrovascular Diseases
summary: Cerebrovascular diseases, such as stroke, aneurysm, and vascular malformations, remain major contributors to global morbidity and mortality. Their complex pathophysiology and diverse subtypes demand precise diagnosis, risk assessment, and personalized treatment strategies. However, conventional diagnostic and therapeutic approaches are hampered by subjectivity, variable accuracy, and limited scalability, emphasizing the urgent need for objective, efficient, and reliable solutions in clinical practice.

title: Clinical Neuroinformatics: AI-Powered Precision Medicine for the Brain
summary: In the realm of clinical neuroinformatics, the incorporation of artificial intelligence (AI) stands at the forefront of transforming precision medicine for brain disorders. The convergence of AI with neuroinformatics aims to interweave neuroimaging, genetics, and clinical data, offering unprecedented opportunities to refine diagnosis, improve prognosis, and tailor personalized treatment strategies. Despite significant technological advancements, the field still faces challenges such as data integration complexities and the need for interpretable AI models. Ongoing debates center around balancing innovation with ethical standards, particularly regarding data privacy and transparency.

title: Marine Turtles: Understanding Life Cycles, Ecology, and Conservation
summary: Marine turtle research forms a vital part of conservation and restoration ecology, addressing the complexities of protecting migratory species that traverse international waters and interact with diverse ecosystems. As long-lived reptiles with intricate life cycles and broad-ranging habitats, marine turtles provide a unique lens through which to examine the success and challenges of conservation interventions and ecosystem management. Recent decades have illuminated the threats facing these species, including habitat degradation, climate-related changes to reproductive patterns, unsustainable exploitation, and bycatch. Innovative studies are highlighting the importance of broadly applied and forward-thinking solutions that consider ecological dynamics, temporal trends in populations, advancements in physiological and molecular understanding, and the interconnectedness of human and natural systems. title: Social Justice and Affirmative Approaches to Neurodiversity
summary: Neurodiversity includes a wide range of neurological and cognitive variations, such as autism, ADHD, intellectual disability (ID), dyslexia, dyscalculia, and Tourette syndrome. Core principles of a neuroaffirmative approach, informed by disability justice, emphasize the recognition and cultivation of the unique competencies, cognitive styles, and perspectives that neurodivergent individuals bring to diverse contexts. This framework advocates for the provision of individualized and flexible support systems that accommodate varying needs, while simultaneously promoting agency, autonomy, and self-determination. Rather than pathologizing difference, a neuroaffirmative perspective seeks to create environments that are responsive to neurodivergent ways of being, and that challenge normative assumptions about functioning, productivity, and value. The identification and integration of multiple perspectives is of critical importance in disciplines such as neurodiversity studies, where scientifi

title: AI-Enhanced Neuroimaging: Transforming Neurodegenerative Disease Management
summary: Neurodegenerative diseases such as Alzheimer's disease and Parkinson's disease present significant challenges due to their complex pathophysiology and varied clinical manifestations. These complexities often hinder accurate diagnosis and effective treatment. Neuroimaging techniques like MRI, PET, and CT have become indispensable in the early detection and management of these disorders. Recently, artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) have revolutionized neuroimaging, allowing for the analysis of detailed imaging patterns that traditional methods cannot discern. Through these AI-driven advancements, there is a promising potential to deepen the understanding of disease processes, enhance diagnostic precision, and open avenues for personalized patient care.

title: Advancing Cross-Cultural Measurement: Ensuring Validity and Equity in Psychological Assessment
summary: The field of cross-cultural assessment in psychology is increasingly grappling with the complexities of measuring psychological constructs across diverse populations. With the global expansion of psychological research and practice, ensuring that measurement instruments yield valid, reliable, and equitable results across linguistic, cultural, and socioeconomic groups is a pressing concern. Despite recognition of the importance of comparability, challenges persist around construct validity, translation bias, and culturally nuanced response patterns, often threatening the integrity of scientific conclusions and the fairness of resulting applications. Recent decades have seen a surge in sophisticated methodological approaches—such as measurement invariance analysis, differential item functioning detection, and item response theory modeling—yet the translation of these tools into routine practice remains inconsistent.
