Causal Machine Learning for Treatment Selection and Outcome Optimization in Mood Disorders
summary: Mood disorders represent a major global burden and are characterized by substantial heterogeneity in symptom profiles, treatment response, and clinical trajectories. Although numerous machine learning models have been developed to predict psychiatric outcomes, most existing approaches remain primarily predictive and provide limited guidance for treatment decision-making in clinical practice. In psychiatry, where treatment choices often involve multiple options and uncertain benefits, models that can estimate individualized treatment effects and support optimal treatment selection are particularly needed. Recent advances in causal inference and causal machine learning offer promising tools to address this challenge by enabling the estimation of heterogeneous treatment effects and the evaluation of intervention strategies using both clinical trial data and real-world evidence. title: Decoding the Grammar of Evolution: Foundation Models and deep learning Population Genomic Inference
summary: Population genomics is being reshaped by machine learning. Foundation models now read DNA sequences directly; neural simulation-based inference engines estimate parameters that were once intractable; generative models produce synthetic genomes with realistic linkage structure; and graph-based architectures are beginning to capture variation that linear references cannot. At the same time, the field faces hard questions. How do we trust what these models learn? How well do they generalize across species, populations, and genomic contexts? How do we connect their predictions back to evolutionary theory and biological mechanisms? When do they fail, and how would we know?

title: Emotional Intelligence and Social Competencies in the Health Professions: Impacts on Leadership, Teams, and Professionalism
summary: Emotional intelligence (EI) and social competencies (SC) are critical constructs and are now extending beyond the field of organizational psychology, especially in the high-stakes context of healthcare organizations. Healthcare settings are uniquely emotionally charged, requiring professionals to navigate patient care, interprofessional collaboration, and rapidly shifting work conditions, all while effectively managing their own emotions. Recent research highlights that healthcare workers with emotional intelligence and who demonstrate social competencies exhibit better teamwork, communication, and resilience, directly influencing patient safety, staff morale, and service quality. However, despite these findings, gaps remain regarding the mechanisms through which EI and social competencies influence workplace outcomes, the variability in significance across contexts and teams, and the most effective strategies for developing EI and SC among healthcare staff. title: History of Animal Behavior Sciences: Behavioral Natural History and Comparative Psychology in the period 1500-1975
summary: Scholars have devoted attention to animal behavior since Antiquity. One of the first was the Greek philosopher Aristotle, who described, for instance, the waggle dance of honeybees, the courtship kissing of pigeons and the parental transmission of singing behavior in songbirds. However, while there were notable naturalists in Antiquity, Middle Ages and Renaissance, it is only from the 17th century that animal behavior sciences underwent a steep growth. Historically, a wide variety of scholars contributed to animal behavior, under different labels, each of which has become a field of its own. In particular, in the period 1500-1975, three main fields contributed to the development of animal behavior science: natural history, comparative psychology and ethology.
image_alt: History of Animal Behavior Sciences: Behavioral Natural History and Comparative Psychology in the period 1500-1975

title: Just ‘Be Yourself’?: A Deep Dive into Authentic Leadership in Uncertain Times
summary: While it has long been said that we operate in a fast-paced ever-changing environment, recent global events and trends further concretize the fact that we live in times of uncertainty. As we navigate challenging times, individuals increasingly look up to leaders not for what they know, but for who they are. Authenticity is emerging as one of the most important factors that we value in leaders, as difficult decisions to be made often test leaders’ core beliefs, which allow stakeholders to see if a) leaders’ actions are aligned with their beliefs, and b) leaders’ beliefs are aligned with those of employees, the organization, and other relevant stakeholders. This Research Topic is focused on the role of authentic leadership in organizations, examining authenticity beyond “freely expressing oneself” but with a deeper look at authenticity of leaders that encompasses self-awareness and internal processing of values and behaviors in leading teams and/or organizations.

The clinical landscape is now characterized by more nuanced diagnostic strategies, a growing array of disease-specific therapeutic options, and a heightened need for practical frameworks that integrate evolving scientific knowledge into routine patient management. title: Cell Death Modalities in Neurological Disorders: Mechanisms, Crosstalk, and Translational Perspectives
summary: Cell death research has emerged as a cornerstone for understanding the pathogenesis of neurological disorders. Neurons and glial cells in the central nervous system are continually exposed to metabolic, oxidative, and inflammatory stressors, making them especially vulnerable to dysregulation in cell death pathways. Historically, apoptosis was viewed as the primary driver of programmed cell loss in neurodegenerative diseases. However, accumulating evidence demonstrates that this perspective is incomplete, with diverse regulated cell death modalities such as pyroptosis, ferroptosis, cuproptosis, disulfidptosis, necroptosis, and PANoptosis playing critical, context-dependent roles. Each of these pathways involves unique molecular machinery, metabolic dependencies, and tissue-specific manifestations, yet often display intricate crosstalk and compensatory interactions within the landscape of CNS pathology. title: Diagnostics and Detection of African Swine Fever Virus - Volume II
summary: African swine fever (ASF) is a highly transmissible and often fatal disease affecting domestic and wild suids, with profound consequences for global pork production and food security. Since its expansion beyond Africa in 2007, ASF has established endemicity across large areas of Europe and Asia, with sustained transmission cycles involving wild boar populations. The re-emergence of ASF in the Caribbean (Dominican Republic and Haiti) has further intensified concerns regarding potential introduction into ASF-free regions, underscoring the need for enhanced preparedness and surveillance capacity.

title: Digital Medicine for High-Risk Environments: Human Performance & Emergency Response
summary: Digital medicine is rapidly evolving beyond conventional clinical settings into high-risk and operational environments where human performance, safety, and resilience are mission-critical. Such environments—including disaster zones, search and rescue operations, military and emergency training contexts, spaceflight and space analog habitats, and nuclear emergency scenarios—pose constraints that challenge traditional digital health approaches. Limited connectivity, environmental stressors, isolation, time-critical decision-making, and scarce medical resources require digital medicine systems that are robust, adaptive, and operationally validated.
image_alt: Digital Medicine for High-Risk Environments: Human Performance & Emergency Response

title: Inclusive Digital Transformation in Dementia: Evidence, Design, Policy and social impact
summary: Digital tools and AI-enabled systems are redefining dementia support and care, with the potential to improve diagnosis, daily support, care coordination and long-term wellbeing for people living with dementia and their caregivers. Yet these technologies also raise critical ethical and practical questions around autonomy, privacy and data protection, evolving consent and capacity, equity and accessibility, algorithmic accountability, and the preservation of human dignity. This Research Topic asks how innovation can remain person-centred and relationship-enhancing, while avoiding digital exclusion, stigma or over-surveillance.

title: Neuromodulation and plasticity: Gateways to flexible memory and learning
summary: Flexible learning and decision-making are thought to rely on the brain’s capacity to reconfigure synaptic connections in response to experience. Foundational work across sensory systems has long suggested that synaptic plasticity supports both perceptual and associative learning. More recently, studies employing automated and ethologically relevant behavioral paradigms in freely moving animals have begun to uncover how neural circuits adapt perceptual strategies, shift between choice policies, and adjust sensorimotor behavior according to internal states and environmental contingencies.

summary: School shootings are an escalating global public mental health concern. It has profound and long-lasting mental health consequences for children, adolescents, families, educational systems, and community. In recent decades, increased media visibility and cross-national occurrence have shifted school violence from isolated criminal events toward recognition as a complex developmental, psychosocial, and systemic phenomenon. Contemporary research highlights that school shootings emerge from interactions among individual mental health vulnerabilities, adverse developmental experiences, family and peer dynamics, digital and social environments, and institutional responses. Despite growing awareness, prevention and response strategies remain fragmented, frequently emphasizing either individual psychopathology or security-based approaches while neglecting broader ecological and public mental health determinants. Advances in brain-computer interfaces: adaptive decoding, real-world applications, and neural data augmentation
summary: Research on Brain-Computer Interfaces (BCIs) stands at the intersection of neuroscience, engineering, and artificial intelligence, aiming to bridge communication between the brain and external devices. Despite major strides in the technical feasibility of BCIs, especially regarding neural signal acquisition and interface hardware, significant obstacles persist in translating laboratory advancements to real-world use. Key limitations include the adaptability of decoding algorithms to dynamic environments, the robustness of BCIs in daily life scenarios, and the challenges posed by limited or noisy neural data. Recent studies highlight the emerging importance of adaptive decoding—where algorithms learn and adjust to individual and contextual changes—and neural data augmentation techniques that compensate for sparse or imperfect datasets, both of which are critical for improving BCI reliability outside controlled settings.

title: Advancing Model Validation and Interpretability in Brain Connectomics
summary: Recent advances in connectomics have opened new frontiers in understanding the structural and functional organization of the brain. With the emergence of high-resolution brain atlases, computational modeling techniques, and multimodal imaging datasets, researchers now have unprecedented opportunities to unravel neural pathways, characterize complex connectivity patterns, and decode the underlying processing mechanisms in the brain. However, these developments also raise fundamental questions about model validity and interpretability. In particular, there remains a critical need to rigorously validate if in silico computational models of brain connectivity actually provide a reliable surrogate for in vivo brain anatomy and dynamics. title: Music and Pro-sociality Volume II
summary: Music perception research bridges the gap between sensory neuroscience and the study of complex social behaviours. Recent advances have highlighted that music, as a structured auditory stimulus, is encoded through intricate perceptual pathways and has far-reaching effects on cognitive, emotional, and motivational systems. Although the neural underpinnings of basic sensory processing are well charted, how these processes translate into higher-order social behaviours, such as altruism and cooperation, remains an open question in neuroscience and psychology. Landmark studies utilizing neuroimaging, electrophysiology, and genetics have charted the engagement of reward and affective systems in response to music, suggesting a neurobiological foundation for social biases and group bonding. title: Psychological approaches to health misinformation
summary:
Health misinformation refers to demonstrably false or misleading information that is often shared unintentionally across social media and online platforms. Health misinformation has proliferated since the COVID-19 pandemic, posing a threat to public health and society. Despite the extensive investigation on this topic, it remains unclear how and why health misinformation spreads, and what strategies can be used to combat it.

 
This Collection welcomes original research articles on the psychological approaches to understand and fight health misinformation.

summary: Conservation Medicine is an emerging and increasingly relevant discipline within veterinary science, situated at the intersection of veterinary science, ecology, and public policy. Despite ongoing global efforts to address biodiversity loss driven by habitat destruction, climate change, emerging diseases, and human-wildlife conflict, traditional conservation approaches often prioritize population-level interventions while overlooking individual animal health, animal welfare, veterinary diagnostics, epidemiology, and cross-species disease dynamics. Recent studies demonstrate that veterinary input is critical in identifying and managing novel infectious threats, conducting health surveillance, interpreting pathology and clinical findings, monitoring health as a barometer of ecosystem change, and ensuring humane management practices. title: Advancements in the Diagnosis of Canine and Feline Idiopathic Epilepsy
summary: Epilepsy is one of the most common chronic neurological conditions encountered in small animal practice. Despite its prevalence, the diagnosis and management of epilepsy in dogs and cats remain challenging due to the variability in seizure manifestation and response to treatment. Traditional diagnostic tools, such as conventional MRI, provide limited insight into the disease processes at a cellular level. However, recent advances in neuroimaging techniques as well as the investigation of biomarkers, both in imaging and biologic tissues, may provide further insight into the disease process at the cellular level. Harnessing these novel techniques may bridge the gap between symptom observation and cellular pathology, leading to more targeted and effective therapies.

title: From Neuron-Glia Interaction to Metabolic Coupling Failure in Neurodegeneration
summary: Brain function has traditionally been interpreted within a neuron-centric framework; however, this view has shifted toward a model of neuron-glia interaction, in which neurons, astrocytes, microglia, and oligodendrocytes form interdependent cellular networks that sustain synaptic and metabolic homeostasis. In the healthy brain, astrocytes regulate neurotransmitter cycling and provide metabolic substrates, microglia modulate synaptic structure, and oligodendrocytes support axonal function, collectively maintaining network stability.

title: Peers as Bridges to Belonging: Fostering Community Through Near-Peer Mentorship in Large-Enrollment Courses
summary: Large-enrollment courses are a defining feature of undergraduate education worldwide, yet they pose well-documented psychological challenges for both students and instructors. Anonymity, limited instructor interaction, and competitive classroom climates can erode students' sense of belonging, which has consistently been linked to academic motivation, persistence, and achievement. These threats are magnified for students from historically underrepresented backgrounds, including first-generation college students, racial and ethnic minorities, and students navigating identity-based stereotype threats. In response, institutions have increasingly turned to peer-led instructional models—undergraduate teaching assistants, learning assistants, supplemental instruction leaders, and peer mentors—as a strategy for humanizing large courses and creating more supportive learning environments.

title: Emotional, Moral, and Social Development from Birth to Adolescence: Advances in Mechanisms, Contexts, and Trajectories
summary: The study of human development from birth through adolescence captures the critical trajectory along which emotional, moral, and social faculties emerge, interact, and consolidate. Recent advances in developmental psychology emphasize that emotional and moral development are not isolated processes nor the mere result of abstract rationality, but are deeply intertwined with emotional awareness, empathy, and dynamics of social interaction. Extensive empirical work points to a multidimensional understanding of children’s and adolescents’ abilities to discern right from wrong, regulate their own emotions, empathize with others, and cultivate prosocial behaviors within diverse contexts. title: Membrane Signaling in Neuroendocrine Development and Disease
summary: Membrane signaling is fundamental to neuroendocrine development and lifelong endocrine homeostasis. Within the hypothalamic and pituitary systems, neural and neurosecretory cells translate environmental, metabolic, and synaptic inputs into precisely regulated hormonal outputs. These processes depend on highly organized membrane platforms where GPCRs, RTKs, ion channels, transporters, and adhesion molecules coordinate with lipids, scaffold proteins, and cytoskeletal networks to control hormone synthesis, pulsatile secretion, receptor sensitivity, and feedback regulation. Proper membrane organization is essential for cell fate specification, maturation of neuroendocrine circuits, and integration of endocrine axes across the lifespan. title: Embodied Approaches to Intervention and Research Design in Clinical Psychology: Integrating Body, Context, and Measurement
summary: Clinical psychology has long recognized that psychological distress and therapeutic change involve more than cognitive processes alone. Emotion regulation, symptom expression, trauma responses, and treatment outcomes are shaped by bodily states, autonomic function, interoceptive awareness, and the lived contexts in which clients exist. Yet clinical research methods can overlook these embodied dimensions. Treating physiological variability, posture, breath, circadian timing, and relational dynamics as clinically meaningful variables can bring further insight into treatment and management pathways. When embodied dimensions are not systematically incorporated into research design and measurement, this can limit the precision of assessment, weaken treatment specificity, and contribute to unexplained variance in clinical outcomes.

title: Philosophy meets neuroscience in the study of consciousness
summary: Conscious experience is central to human life, yet the processes underlying its emergence remain among the most debated questions in behavioral neuroscience. Over the past decade, the field has moved beyond simple contrasts between “conscious” and “unconscious” states toward mechanistic accounts grounded in large-scale brain dynamics, multisensory integration, and the interaction between perception, action, and self-representation. Progress has been driven by converging approaches, including computational frameworks (e.g., predictive processing and global workspace–type architectures), causal perturbation methods (such as TMS, DBS, and intracranial stimulation), and high-dimensional analyses of neural data from EEG, MEG, fMRI, and single-unit recordings. In parallel, experimental paradigms involving anesthesia, sleep, psychedelics, meditation, and disorders of consciousness have provided structured and naturalistic perturbations of subjective experience.

Current research highlights growing concerns about maintaining motor stability in older adults and the need for innovative approaches to mitigate age-related declines in motor function.

title: Demyelinating Neuropathies: Pathophysiology, Diagnosis, and Treatment
summary: Demyelinating neuropathies represent a challenging area within neurology, encompassing a spectrum of acquired disorders and inherited forms that impact the peripheral nervous system. While advances in neurophysiological techniques, neuroimaging, and molecular profiling have enabled greater diagnostic accuracy, delayed recognition and inconsistent management outcomes remain persistent challenges. These developments promise to transform how we comprehend our physical, emotional, and mental well-being. As biophysical signals are measured with increasing accuracy, they offer profound implications for enhancing health and wellness, revolutionizing education, transforming transportation and communication, redefining entertainment, optimizing advertising strategies, and ensuring workplace safety.

title: Cognitive Processes in AI-Mediated Problem Solving
summary: The growing integration of artificial intelligence into educational, professional, and creative contexts is transforming fundamental aspects of human cognition and problem-solving. As AI systems become collaborative partners in tasks such as planning, coding, analysis, and reasoning, there are emerging questions about how individuals conceptualize problems, seek information, generate solutions, and reflect on their own thinking. Recent research in cognitive science and human–computer interaction has begun to reveal nuanced shifts in cognitive and metacognitive strategies, alongside new forms of human–AI socio-cognitive dynamics. Despite notable advances, the field still grapples with understanding the boundaries of uniquely human cognition, the risks of cognitive biases, and how AI can both scaffold and potentially undermine core reasoning capacities.

title: Educators in the Digital Age: The Role of Technology, Pedagogy, and Social Factors in Online Learning
summary: Digital transformation in education is changing the role of educators, the nature of student engagement, and the quality of instruction, particularly within virtual and hybrid environments. With advancements in technology such as artificial intelligence, educational software, and learning analytics, the educational landscape is undergoing major changes. These changes are influencing not only how and what we learn but also who teaches, how they teach, and the competencies required. In this changing context, educators' roles extend beyond merely transmitting knowledge to becoming mentors, support systems, and guides in the digital age. While some schools readily adapt to these changes, questions remain regarding educators' preparedness, the effectiveness of virtual instruction, and the impact on social interactions among learners.

From ideation to creation, GenAI promises to speed up development through tools for design, graphics, animation and textures, NPCs and dialogue. Alongside this rapid rise, GenAI has also raised questions about ethics and legal concerns, as well as debates around hype and overreach.

summary: Lifestyle factors are increasingly recognized as important contributors to both cardiometabolic and mental health. Physical activity and sport participation have been associated with a range of favorable health outcomes, whereas sedentary behavior has been linked to elevated cardiometabolic risk and poorer mental health. In addition to behavioral factors, health-related indices (including anthropometric and metabolic markers) are commonly used to assess disease risk at both individual and population levels. Emerging evidence suggests that lifestyle behaviors and health-related indices are closely interconnected and may jointly influence cardiometabolic and mental health outcomes across different populations. Given the rising prevalence of cardiometabolic disorders and mental health conditions worldwide, there is a growing need to better understand how these factors interact. title: Coastal Ecosystem Processes, Functions, Services and Protection
summary: Coastal ecosystems, characterized as dynamic and complex transitional zones where land meets the sea, are among the most productive and valuable environments on Earth. They encompass a diverse array of habitats, including mangrove forests, salt marshes, seagrass beds, estuaries, and coral reefs, which collectively support an extraordinary concentration of biodiversity and provide a wide range of critical ecosystem services. However, these ecosystems are increasingly subjected to unprecedented anthropogenic and climate-induced pressures that fundamentally alter the intricate biogeochemical cycles governing their health, productivity, and resilience.

title: Microbial and Fungal Drivers of Ecological Restoration in Polluted Environments: Advances, Challenges and Future Pathways
summary: Microbial and fungal communities are increasingly recognized as vital agents in the conservation and restoration of ecosystems facing anthropogenic pressures, especially pollution. Environmental contaminants, from legacy chemicals to emerging pollutants, are significant threats to biodiversity, ecosystem services, and the adaptive capacity of landscapes. At the same time, fungi and plant-associated microbes possess unique metabolic, ecological, and evolutionary traits that can facilitate resilience, accelerate recovery, and support the long-term restoration of degraded habitats. Recent advances have uncovered the far-reaching influence of pollution on microbial and fungal diversity, community structure, and their capacity to interact with plants and animals. Yet, the translation of this biological complexity into scalable, science-based restoration and conservation practice remains at an early stage. summary: Mindfulness-based approaches have become a significant focus within the field of psychotherapy, reflecting a cultural and scientific shift towards integrating contemplative practices with clinical interventions. Despite their widespread adoption in treating depression, anxiety, stress, and chronic pain, as well as their application in non-clinical settings, considerable heterogeneity persists in both research and practice. Key challenges involve clarifying the active mechanisms responsible for therapeutic change, delineating the factors that influence efficacy across different populations and contexts, and resolving ongoing debates about the optimal delivery and implementation of mindfulness interventions. Recent studies have begun to uncover the complex array of mediators and moderators that shape outcomes, while advancing theories have both expanded and complicated our understanding of mindfulness as an integrative and transdiagnostic process. title: Multimodal stimulation techniques
summary: Traditional neuromodulation techniques, such as transcranial magnetic stimulation (TMS) or transcranial direct current stimulation (tDCS), have revolutionized our ability to non-invasively probe and alter brain activity. However, single-modality approaches often face inherent limitations in achieving highly specific or sustained effects due to the brain's distributed nature and compensatory mechanisms. A new frontier is emerging at the intersection of various stimulation methods and sensory inputs: multimodal stimulation. By combining distinct neurostimulation techniques (e.g., electrical, magnetic, optical, acoustic) with or across various sensory domains (e.g., visual, auditory, somatosensory), we can potentially unlock more sophisticated and targeted modulation of neural circuits, leading to enhanced understanding of brain function and more effective therapeutic interventions.

title: Virtual reality as a tool for cognitive and sensory modulation
summary: Virtual Reality (VR) has emerged as a transformative medium in neuroscience, moving beyond entertainment into a robust tool for experimental manipulation. Traditionally, studying cognitive and sensory processes required a trade-off between controlled laboratory settings and real-world ecological validity. VR bridges this gap by providing immersive, three-dimensional environments that can be precisely modulated to isolate specific neural responses. By engaging multiple sensory modalities—visual, auditory, and increasingly somatosensory—VR creates a sense of "presence" that activates the brain in ways traditional 2D stimuli cannot. This immersive capacity allows researchers to investigate how the human brain processes complex sensory inputs and orchestrates cognitive functions in real-time.

title: Why the Autonomic Nervous System Should Not Be Overlooked in Modern Neuroscience
summary: The enteric nervous system (ENS) has gained broader visibility, notably through its designation as a “second brain” and growing interest in the gut microbiota. Despite this, this major component of the peripheral nervous system (PNS), both quantitatively and functionally, remains underrepresented in many university curricula and even within neuroscience. Its limited presence in schematic representations of the nervous system may further contribute to this lack of visibility. Even less attention is generally given to prevertebral ganglia (PVG), clusters of neurons located in the abdomen between the spinal cord and the gastrointestinal tract.

title: Unconscious versus conscious processing: Insights from sensory systems
summary: The human brain is a relentless processor of sensory information, yet only a small fraction of this input reaches the level of conscious awareness. The distinction between unconscious and conscious processing remains one of the most profound questions in cognitive neuroscience, with sensory systems providing the primary "laboratory" for this exploration. By precisely controlling stimulus properties, through techniques such as masking, binocular rivalry, or continuous flash suppression, researchers can dissociate physical input from subjective experience. Historically, we have known that the brain can perform complex tasks, such as emotional appraisal or motor priming, without explicit awareness. However, the exact neural architectures and temporal dynamics that allow a sensory signal to cross the threshold into consciousness are still fiercely debated. title: Generative models of neural activity: Using AI to simulate, interpret, and predict brain dynamics
summary: The advent of high-density recording technologies, such as Neuropixels and large-scale calcium imaging, has provided an unprecedented look into the simultaneous activity of thousands of neurons. However, the sheer dimensionality and non-linear nature of this data pose significant challenges for interpretation. Traditional analytical methods often focus on discriminative tasks, mapping neural activity to external stimuli or behavior. In contrast, generative models, including Variational Autoencoders (VAEs), Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs), and Diffusion Models, offer a powerful alternative by learning the underlying statistical distribution of neural firing patterns. These AI-driven frameworks allow researchers to move beyond description, enabling the synthesis of realistic neural activity and the discovery of latent manifolds that govern brain states. By treating neural activity as a generative process, we can better understand the intrinsic logic of biological computation.

title: Untethered Soft Robots: Embedded Actuation, Sensing, and Intelligence
summary: Recent progress in soft materials, fabrication, and bioinspired design has significantly expanded the capabilities of soft robots in locomotion, manipulation, wearable assistance, biomedical devices, and underwater systems. At the same time, the field is shifting from isolated demonstrations of soft actuators or soft structures toward integrated robotic systems that combine multifunctional materials, body-embedded sensing, flexible electronics, and intelligent control. Untethered operation is emerging as a critical milestone in this transition, because it directly relates to autonomy, portability, and deployment in complex environments. Achieving this goal requires not only improved soft actuators and sensors, but also new approaches to system integration, energy management, state estimation, and embodied or onboard intelligence.

The proposed research topic, “Neurofeedback-Driven Human-in-the-Loop Framework for Emotional Product Co-Design with Generative AI,” aims to address this limitation by integrating neuroscience, human-in-the-loop (HITL) control, and emotional design into a unified adaptive framework.

title: AI-Integrated Multi-Omics for Neurodegeneration: Mechanistic Insights to Clinical Innovation
summary: The field of neurodegeneration is witnessing rapid advancements thanks to the integration of multi-omics technologies alongside sophisticated artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) tools. While genomics, transcriptomics, proteomics and metabolomics provide unprecedented layers of insight into diseases such as Alzheimer’s, Parkinson’s, and related disorders, the sheer scale and complexity of these datasets create substantial analytical challenges. Current research is pushing the limits of AI in fusing diverse omics data; however, achieving clinically meaningful biomarker discovery and mechanistic understanding remains an unmet need. Furthermore, questions regarding interpretability, reproducibility and generalizability of AI-driven insights continue to fuel debate within the scientific community.

title: Beyond convention: novel biologics – targeted therapies for neuroimmune diseases
summary: Neuroimmune diseases, such as multiple sclerosis, myasthenia gravis, and autoimmune encephalitis, are debilitating conditions characterized by an aberrant immune response against the nervous system. For decades, treatment has relied on broad-spectrum immunosuppressants, which, while effective for some, are often associated with significant side effects and increased infection risk due to their non-specific mechanisms. This has left a substantial unmet need for many patients. The field is now undergoing a transformation with the introduction of targeted therapies, including monoclonal antibodies against specific immune molecules (e.g., CD20, complement proteins) and small molecule inhibitors. These novel agents promise greater efficacy and precision. Furthermore, next-generation approaches like bispecific antibodies and CAR-T cell therapy are emerging, pushing the boundaries of precision medicine in neurology.

title: Complex Neuropresentions in Hypermobility Spectrum Disorders: Interacting Mechanisms and Comorbid Conditions
summary: Hypermobility Spectrum Disorders (HSD) refer to a group of diagnoses in which connective tissue is compromised: hypermobile Ehlers-Danlos Syndrome, hypermobility spectrum disorders, and pre-2017 diagnoses of hypermobile joint syndrome. Because connective tissue is prevalent in all components of the nervous system, people with HSD often present with complex and unusual neurological manifestations, including: craniocervical and atlantoaxial instability, occult tethered cord, Chiari I malformation, dysautonomia, cerebrospinal fluid leaks, idiopathic intracranial hypertension, Eagle syndrome, Tarlov cysts, dystonia, and a variety of peripheral neuropathies. Sensory processing and interoceptive abnormalities may also provoke further physical stress and damage to the nervous system. title: Exploring oxytocin as a neuroendocrine integrator
summary: Oxytocin has been the subject of much research that has greatly expanded our understanding of its role in integrating brain-body interactions. Recent evidence identifies oxytocin as a critical modulator within the gut-brain-endocrine axis, regulating neuroendocrine and neuroimmune signaling pathways in both bottom-up (gut-to-brain) and top-down (brain-to-gut) directions. While oxytocin concentrations in the central brain are approximately three orders of magnitude higher than peripheral blood concentration, oxytocin receptors are widely distributed across many peripheral tissues. Indeed, recent studies have pointed to associations between oxytocin and gut microbiota-derived metabolites, vagal afferent signaling and hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal (HPA) axis activity, positioning oxytocin as a key modulator of metabolic and endocrine signals.

title: Extracellular Vesicles as Mediators and Biomarkers in Aging and Neurodegenerative Disorders: From Molecular Cargo to Clinical Translation
summary: Extracellular vesicles (EVs), including exosomes, microvesicles, apoptotic bodies, and many other EV subtypes, have emerged as critical mediators of intercellular communication in both physiological and pathological conditions. These membrane-bound nanoparticles transport a broad repertoire of molecular cargo - including proteins, DNA, multiple RNA species, lipids, and metabolites - between cells, thereby modulating signaling pathways, cellular phenotypes, and tissue homeostasis. In neurological and neurodegenerative disorders such as Alzheimer's disease and related tauopathies, Parkinson's disease, amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS), and multiple sclerosis (MS), EVs play complex and multifaceted roles. In addition, their roles in aging, the primary risk factor of most of these diseases, have only recently started to be explored.

title: Generative AI and Intelligent Control in Robotics for Deployment in Challenging Environments
summary: The rapid advancements in robotics and artificial intelligence (AI) over the past decade have unlocked new possibilities for autonomous systems across a wide range of applications. However, deploying robots in complex, dynamic, and unstructured environments remains a significant challenge. Such scenarios require robots to exhibit not only physical robustness but also advanced cognitive capabilities to perceive, reason, and act autonomously under uncertainty. Generative AI, with its ability to create realistic simulations, learn from limited data, and predict complex interactions, provides transformative potential to address these challenges. By integrating generative AI with intelligent control, researchers can develop innovative solutions to enable robots to operate effectively in demanding environments like disaster response, remote exploration, healthcare, and industrial automation. title: Immunity and Inflammatory Diseases in Dairy Cattle: Current Knowledge and Future Perspectives
summary: In the field of veterinary sciences, understanding the interplay between immunity and inflammatory diseases in dairy cattle is fundamental for improving both animal health and productivity. Dairy cattle are a critical resource for the agricultural industry; however, they are highly susceptible to inflammatory conditions linked to metabolic and infectious diseases—such as mastitis, metritis, lameness, ketosis, and milk fever—which are often triggered or worsened by immune dysfunction. These conditions not only compromise animal welfare and milk yield but also impose significant economic burdens on dairy farms.

title: Impact of Alcohol Exposure on Reward Circuits and Decision-Making
summary: As described by the National Institute on Alcohol Abuse and Alcoholism (NIAAA), alcohol use disorder is a chronic relapsing disorder characterized by loss of control over alcohol intake despite impairments in social, occupational, and health functions. Alcohol consumption that is heavy or frequent can lead a subset of people to transition from recreational to excessive use. In the United States alone, excessive alcohol use is responsible for nearly 140,000 deaths annually, according to estimates published by the Centres for Disease Control and Prevention (2022). It is therefore imperative to uncover the brain mechanisms behind alcohol use disorders to find novel therapeutic interventions. This Research Topic aims to unravel the neural mechanisms that mediate and change during chronic alcohol use and their impact on decision making.

Occupational Wellness Interventions to Promote Workforce Health, Safety and Productivity
summary: Occupational wellness and safety are foundational elements in contemporary workforce management, as modern working environments increasingly expose employees to physical, mental, and social risks stemming from lifestyle behaviors and demanding job conditions. The widespread adoption of sedentary and unhealthy lifestyles, combined with challenging and often suboptimal workplace environments, now presents pressing occupational health and safety concerns. This has led to significant declines in workers’ health-related quality of life, as well as to diminished productivity, intensifying both social and economic burdens. Ongoing debates highlight the complexities of integrating wellness with safety compliance, the optimal balance between personal health promotion and organizational responsibility, and the need to close persistent gaps in the implementation and efficacy of workplace interventions.

title: Promoting Replicability: Planning, Design, and Researcher Responsibility for Scientific Validity and Reliability - Vol II
summary: In psychological science, the ongoing replicability crisis has sparked critical reflection on the field’s methodological practices and the integrity of its research outputs. While recent discourse often gravitates toward data transparency and analytical sophistication, emerging evidence underscores that the replicability of scientific findings is deeply rooted in the quality of research planning and design. Major initiatives addressing open science and rigorous data analysis have illuminated substantial advances; yet, several high-profile replication failures reveal persistent gaps when foundational decisions about research design are insufficiently robust. In landmark projects and meta-analyses, misalignments between hypotheses, procedures, and analyses have consistently undermined the credibility of findings, despite transparency in reporting or access to advanced analytical tools. title: Radicalization of Youth and Mental Health
summary: Public mental health has increasingly become a focal point for addressing the complex and evolving challenges faced by youth, particularly as these relate to the phenomenon of radicalization. With rising concerns about the prevalence and impact of youth radicalization—spanning ideological, political, and social dimensions—questions remain about the interplay between individual mental health, cultural context, and societal influences. While current evidence highlights the importance of early interventions and health promotion strategies, the precise mechanisms linking public mental health frameworks with the prevention or mitigation of youth radicalization require further exploration. Recent studies have begun to examine the multifaceted nature of radicalization, the impact of digital environments, and the significance of community and cultural factors. title: Risk Assessment and Clinical Decision-Making in Mental Health
summary: Despite extensive research into risk assessment in mental health settings, a consensus has yet to be reached on the best way to apply the findings from this literature to everyday practice. There have been recent positive developments in the field of quantifying risk, but it remains unclear how to use a quantitative estimate in the provision of safe care to an individual patient. Some researchers alternatively advocate representing risk qualitatively (e.g. formulation), but how practitioners can best use these representations in their clinical roles has also not yet been determined. Consequently, researchers have started to turn their attention to how to integrate risk assessment approaches into practice, and in particular how to use the output of risk assessments to improve clinical decision-making.

title: The Future of Performance Science
summary: Performance Science is an integrative field focused on advancing our understanding and enhancement of human performance across domains such as the performing arts, sports, education, and the workplace. Recent years have seen a shift from narrowly defined disciplinary achievements to broader considerations of how performance is shaped by, and in turn shapes, society. This includes the evolving relationship between performance and societal values, the diversification and sustainability of performance careers, the transformation of education and training systems, and the centrality of health, wellbeing, and psychological resilience. Despite substantial progress, there remain important gaps in connecting fundamental skills with real-world outcomes and navigating the interdisciplinary challenges that define the future of the field. summary: This year marks the 11th International Day of Yoga, which embraces the theme, “Yoga for One Earth, One Health,” which spotlights the fundamental link between personal wellness, public mental health, and the well-being of our shared planet. Yoga, far beyond being a set of physical movements or a tool for individual stress management, represents a holistic and salutogenic approach to health and well-being. It encourages a lifestyle that integrates physical vitality, emotional resilience, psychological stability, and a sense of personal and social responsibility.

title: The Transcognitive Basketball Performance
summary: Elite basketball performance is rooted in the complex interaction between cognitive, physical, physiological, technical, and nutritional domains. Contemporary research underscores the centrality of cognitive functions—including decision-making, attention regulation, and situational intelligence—within the high-paced and cognitively demanding environment of competitive basketball. These mental capacities are not isolated; rather, they are dynamically shaped by an athlete’s fitness level, physiological readiness, nutritional status, technical execution, and tactical knowledge. While studies have demonstrated the effects of mental fatigue on motor skills, the role of nutrition in supporting sustained focus and energy, and the necessity of physical conditioning for cognitive resilience, there remain significant gaps in our understanding of how these components function as a unified whole. title: Advancing Safer Supply - Integrating Perspectives for a Comprehensive Harm Reduction Solution
summary: The increasingly unregulated global drug supply has contributed to unprecedented harms, including rising rates of overdose, and death. Safer supply initiatives—programs and policies that provide people who use drugs with regulated, pharmaceutical-grade substances—have emerged as a critical, evidence-based response to these harms. Yet despite their growing importance, safer supply interventions remain under-researched and unevenly implemented, and many aspects of their impact remain poorly understood. Lived and living experience continues to be one of the most vital, but underrepresented, sources of knowledge in this field. By integrating clinical, social, legal, and policy perspectives, as well as voices of those directly impacted, this Research Topic aims to advance scientific understanding of safer supply as an essential strategy in harm reduction, health equity, and public health.

title: Advancing methods in learning and memory neurophysiology
summary: Memory is classically defined as a complex cognitive process that involves multiple stages, including learning, memory consolidation and storage, retrieval, reconsolidation, and forgetting. As described by Eric Kandel, neurobiological research in this field over the past four decades has progressed through phases of increasing complexity, starting with the cellular biology of synaptic plasticity, advancing to the molecular mechanisms, then exploring genetic regulation in mammals, and culminating in systems-level approaches that integrate circuits and behavior. In recent years, the field has undergone another important transition. Beyond neurons and synapses, non-neuronal cell types, including astrocytes, oligodendrocytes, microglia, and pericytes, have emerged as critical contributors to learning and memory processes. title: Conservation and Adaptation of Mediterranean Coastal Extremophiles: Land-Use Pressures and the Future of Crop Wild Relatives
summary: The field of coastal Mediterranean conservation and restoration ecology is increasingly focusing on plant extremophiles species uniquely adapted to thrive under severe abiotic stresses such as high salinity, drought, temperature extremes, and poor soils. These plants, including many crop wild relatives and wild-harvested species, underpin local biodiversity and agricultural resilience but are often confined to specialized, vulnerable habitats. Current evidence highlights the essential role of these extremophiles in sustaining genetic diversity, inspiring climate-adaptive agriculture, and maintaining crucial ecosystem functions along Mediterranean coastlines. Yet, mounting anthropogenic pressures, habitat loss, land degradation, and accelerating climate change are outpacing conservation efforts, putting these plants at greater risk of extinction.

title: Environmental Risks and Resilience in Adolescent Mental Health
summary: Adolescence represents a critical developmental period characterized by heightened sensitivity to environmental influences. Research has increasingly shown that mental health outcomes during this stage are shaped by interactions among multiple ecological systems, including family relationships, peer networks, school environments, and neighborhood or urban contexts. At the same time, emerging exposures such as digital media environments, artificial intelligence interactions, environmental pollution, and climate-related stressors are becoming part of adolescents’ everyday experiences.

title: Establishing Reporting Standards for Emerging Neurotechnology Research
summary: In today’s scientific field, the ability to interact with the brain has become much more accessible. This accessibility has allowed for great leaps in understanding, diagnoses, and interventions in healthcare for the previously untreatable. Imaging allows for researchers to study and visualize the complex networks formed in the brain during different tasks. Electrical interventions allow for robotic prosthetics to predict movements from neural activity or to stop errant pain signals from causing a person undue distress. More recently, organoids have been able to create brains in dish allowing for even more detailed work in dissecting and diagramming the function of the brain. These avenues of investigation open up a world of possibilities for the future of health care.

title: Food Fight: Competition and Cooperation over Nutrients in the Gut-Brain Axis and Their Consequences for Health and Behavior
summary: The gut microbiome and host are continuously engaged in a negotiation for essential nutrients, and this dynamic interplay fundamentally shapes both health and behavior. Despite the central role of these interactions, a critical question remains unsolved: what determines whether the nutritional exchanges between host and microbes result in benefits or detriments to the host? Nutrients in the gut are sourced from dietary intake, but their availability is further impacted by digestion efficiency, microbial biosynthesis and consumption, host absorption capacity, and internal physiological state. As research demonstrates, the same microbial species can synthesize vitamins in fiber-rich settings, yet switch to competing for amino acids when protein is limited, or may provide metabolic support under malnutrition yet deplete crucial micronutrients in other conditions. title: Haptic Perception in VR: Virtual Presence and Immersion
summary: Recent advances in visual and auditory technologies have significantly enhanced user performance and experience in Virtual Reality (VR). However, fully immersive interaction remains constrained by the limited practicality, scalability, and generalizability of current haptic technologies. While haptic feedback is known to shape perception, cognition, and motor control during virtual interaction, the field is still developing principled approaches for delivering effective touch sensations using simple, adaptable, and context-aware solutions. In particular, growing evidence suggests that the human brain can reinterpret minimal haptic cues—such as vibrotactile stimulation—through multisensory integration with vision and sound, enabling convincing sensations even when feedback is spatially relocated or physically simplified.

title: Human-Centered AI in Cyber Security, Privacy, and Trust for Critical Infrastructures
summary: The intersection of Artificial Intelligence (AI) and human-centered design is reshaping strategies to protect critical infrastructures such as energy grids, transportation networks, healthcare systems, and financial services. With the rapid escalation of sophisticated cyber threats, current approaches often rely on automation and detection systems, but these can be limited by issues related to transparency, explainability, and human oversight. Recent research has demonstrated the benefits of combining AI technologies with human insight to establish resilience, manage privacy, and strengthen trustworthiness. However, the dynamic, high-stakes environments characteristic of critical infrastructures presents unique challenges for achieving effective human-AI collaboration.

title: Integrating Multi-scale Data for Soil Biodiversity and Ecosystem Function Across Diverse Landscapes: From Omics to Artificial Intelligence
summary: Global ecosystems are undergoing rapid transformation driven by intensified land use, climate change, and anthropogenic pressures. These shifts threaten soil biodiversity - the "biological engine" that underpins essential ecosystem functions, including nutrient cycling, carbon sequestration, water regulation, and contaminant remediation. While urban and peri-urban areas represent extreme examples of these transformations - projected to house two-thirds of the global population by 2050 - the need to understand and monitor soil health across all biomes, from managed agricultural lands to pristine natural reserves, has never been more urgent.

title: Intraspecific Trait Variation and Phenotypic Plasticity Across Environmental Gradients
summary: While the investigation of species-level traits has revealed broad effects of environmental disturbances on communities and ecosystems, it is vital to recognize that species traits are dynamic across space and time, varying among populations, individuals, and genotypes. Intraspecific Trait Variation (ITV) refers to the range of trait values and syndromes exhibited by individuals within a species, reflecting their capacity to respond to environmental changes and adapt to varying conditions.

title: Investigating Molecular Mechanisms and Therapeutic Strategies in Tuberculous Meningitis
summary: Tuberculous Meningitis (TBM) is the most severe form of extrapulmonary tuberculosis, posing a critical global health challenge. This devastating central nervous system infection frequently leads to severe disability, long-term neurological sequelae, and high mortality rates. The brain, an exceptionally energy-demanding organ, relies on precise regulation of neuroenergetics. In TBM, severe inflammation, hypoxic-ischemic injury, and direct mycobacterial effects profoundly disrupt these vital processes, significantly impacting diverse clinical characteristics, disease progression, and patient outcomes.

title: Multisensory Integration and Neural Dynamics in Prosodic Acquisition
summary: The field of early language acquisition has explored how infants and toddlers begin to understand and produce language, with a significant focus on their sensitivity to prosody, namely to rhythm, prominence and intonation. Prosody provides essential bootstrapping mechanisms that help infants to scaffold the learning of language, facilitating the tasks of segmenting speech and deriving meaning, even before they master specific sounds and vocabulary. Current understanding of the perception of prosody emphasizes its multisensory nature, where auditory information is enhanced by visual and tactile inputs, and coupled to speech motor information. There remains a gap, however, in understanding how these multisensory integrations develop, whether they might differ across languages with varying prosodic systems and across typically and atypically developing populations, such as children at risk for language impairments.
image_alt: Multisensory Integration and Neural Dynamics in Prosodic Acquisition

title: Navigating Urbanization Challenges: Strategies for Enhancing Urban Biodiversity through Integrated Planning, Ecological Theory, and Landscape Design

title: Exploring the link between tuberculosis and ischemic stroke: clinical perspectives and pathways
summary: Tuberculosis (TB) is a leading cause of infectious disease worldwide, significantly impacting both morbidity and mortality rates. In recent years, the focus has expanded from its respiratory manifestations to its systemic implications, particularly concerning the risk of acute ischemic stroke (AIS). The growing body of research indicates a significant correlation between TB, specifically its pulmonary and meningeal forms, and an increased risk of ischemic stroke. This includes the heightened probability among pulmonary TB patients and the even higher risk observed in those suffering from tuberculous meningitis (TBM). As the detailed mechanisms underlying this association remain partially understood, this Research Topic seeks to bridge that gap and foster a comprehensive examination of the interplay between TB and AIS.

Although there is a growing acknowledgment of the need for methodological pluralism, including the structured combination of first-person phenomenological accounts with the rigor of third-person empirical research, a fully unified framework remains elusive. title: Mechanosensitive channels in the gut–brain axis: From gut motility to interoceptive behavior
summary: The gut–brain axis is a bidirectional communication network linking gastrointestinal function with central nervous system circuits that regulate stress, affect, and behavior. Mechanical forces arising from gut motility, luminal distension, and tissue deformation are key drivers of this communication, sensed primarily by mechanosensitive channels such as Piezo1, Piezo2, TRPV4, and ASICs. These channels transduce mechanical stimuli into electrical and chemical signals in enteric neurons, glia, and epithelial cells, which are then conveyed to the brain via vagal and spinal pathways. Emerging evidence indicates that alterations in mechanosensitive signaling contribute to stress-related behaviors, visceral pain, and functional gastrointestinal disorders. Understanding how mechanotransduction in the gut shapes interoceptive signals that regulate affect, stress responsivity, and emotion processing, highlighting novel targets for therapeutic intervention in gut–brain disorders.

title: Understanding consciousness: neural, cognitive, and philosophical perspectives, Volume II
summary: Consciousness is a complex and multifaceted phenomenon that has intrigued scientists, philosophers, and thinkers for centuries. However, the debate continues as to how, and if, these physical processes translate into subjective experiences. Integrating philosophical perspectives with empirical research offers a more comprehensive understanding of consciousness, bridging the gap between objective observation and subjective experience.

In particular, we still lack a clear understanding of the neural dynamics that govern the transition from an evidence accumulation state to the commitment to a specific choice, a key step in the decision process.

title: Utility of non-invasive imaging techniques in diagnosis and management of neuromuscular disorders​​​​​​​
summary: Neuromuscular disorders have seen a major shift toward non-invasive imaging to support diagnosis and longitudinal care. Historically, evaluation relied heavily on invasive muscle and nerve biopsies and, in some settings, computed tomography (CT), which carries radiation exposure and offers limited soft-tissue contrast. Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) has become a key modality because it provides excellent soft-tissue resolution, multiplanar capability, and high sensitivity for detecting patterns of muscle and nerve involvement. However, unequal access to MRI—driven by cost, infrastructure, and availability—limits its use in many regions. In parallel, neuromuscular ultrasound has expanded as a portable, lower-cost tool that can be deployed at the bedside and in resource-limited settings, although it remains operator-dependent and requires dedicated training.

As these models are increasingly integrated into robotic systems, the long-envisioned goal of human-robot symbiosis, where humans and robots understand each other and collaborate in a mutually supportive and harmonious way, is now within reach.

title: Exploring the Link Between Infectious Diseases and Mental Health - Volume 2
summary: The field of psychiatry and infectious diseases explores the complex interactions between microbial infections and mental health outcomes. Historically, links such as those seen in neurosyphilis or AIDS Dementia Complex have been studied, but newer infectious agents like SARS-CoV-2 bring renewed focus and complexity. Both direct effects through biological mechanisms like neuroinflammation and indirect influences through societal disruptions highlight the intricate relationship between infectious diseases and mental health. Despite considerable advancements, significant gaps remain in understanding the full spectrum of neuropsychiatric consequences and in integrating findings into public health strategies.

summary: Space robotics has undergone a remarkable evolution over the past decades, expanding from simple fixed-arm manipulators on early space stations to a diverse ecosystem of robotic platforms. Today, the field encompasses everything from compact deployable systems and free-flying inspectors to mobile planetary explorers and, most recently, intelligent large-scale manipulators capable of constructing orbital infrastructure. On-orbit assembly enables building large space structures (telescopes, solar sails, antennas) by launching standard modules independently and assembling them in space, overcoming launch vehicle limitations. For intelligent space robots, complexity increases with spacecraft clusters comprising both rigid and flexible spacecraft, as flexible appendages introduce distinct dynamic behaviors during rendezvous and docking. title: Soft Robotic Sensing and Modeling: From Proprioception to Physiology-Informed Validation
summary: Soft robotics has emerged as a transformative paradigm where compliance, adaptability, and embodied intelligence are achieved through material and structural design. A critical frontier in this field is the integration of multimodal sensing with advanced modeling frameworks, enabling robots to perceive their own state (proprioception), interact safely with humans, and operate reliably in diverse environments. This Research Topic seeks contributions that advance the sensing–modeling–validation pipeline for soft robotic systems. We invite work that demonstrates how embedded sensing modalities, physics-based and data-driven models, and standardized validation approaches can together ensure reproducibility, robustness, and physiological relevance.

title: Understanding Proactive Behavior at Work: New Perspectives, Mechanisms, and Outcomes
summary: Proactive work behavior has become a central construct in organizational psychology, reflecting employees’ capacity to anticipate, initiate, and enact change rather than merely responding to situational demands. As contemporary organizations operate in increasingly dynamic, uncertain, and complex environments, proactive behaviors play a critical role in individual effectiveness, team functioning, and organizational adaptability. Prior research has highlighted that proactivity is not a unitary phenomenon, but a broad class of self-initiated, future-oriented actions shaped by both individual psychological processes and contextual factors. At the same time, empirical findings remain fragmented across theoretical traditions, levels of analysis, and methodological approaches. This Research Topic seeks to advance a more integrative understanding of proactive work behavior by bringing together diverse perspectives on its antecedents, underlying mechanisms, and outcomes. title: Landscape Pattern and the Sustainability of Coastal Cities
summary: Global urbanization has profoundly transformed the landscape patterns on the Earth's surface, and the resulting degradation of ecological functions has become a critical constraint on achieving urban sustainability. As the spatial manifestation of the interactions between human activities and natural processes, the optimization and regulation of landscape patterns are widely recognized as a key approach to enhancing urban sustainability. Understanding these landscape dynamics is essential for designing effective ecological restoration interventions. It determines where, when, and how to restore degraded ecosystems in urbanizing regions to recover ecosystem services and enhance ecological resilience.

title: Neuromorphic Computing at Cryogenic Temperatures: Bridging Neural Principles, Superconducting Systems, and Extreme-Environment Intelligence
summary: Neuromorphic computing has emerged as a transformative paradigm for achieving energy-efficient and adaptive intelligence by emulating the structure and dynamics of biological neural systems. Significant advances have been made in neuromorphic materials, devices, circuits, and learning algorithms. However, a largely unexplored frontier lies in the realization of neuromorphic systems operating at cryogenic temperatures. This represents a new interdisciplinary direction at the intersection of neuroscience, superconducting electronics, quantum engineering, and ultra-low-power computing, with emphasis on implementing biologically inspired neural computation in extreme environments.

title: One Paleopathology: Lessons from the Past
summary: One Paleopathology (OPP) expands the One Health perspective into the past. It is based on an understanding of the evolution-based susceptibilities, pathological manifestations, and contextual factors that determined the occurrences and impacts of human, animal and plant diseases across time. This rich, comprehensive perspective is based upon using an interdisciplinary approach that goes beyond descriptions and diagnoses to determine why diseases occurred when and where they did. Like One Health, its emphasis is on the connections between human, animal and plant health and the environment. Thus, in the same way that history explains the present, OPP exposes the origins of the health and disease landscapes of today.

However, a persistent challenge lies in ensuring a consistent and reliable alignment between physical and virtual environments. Current XR systems often exhibit discrepancies between sensed physical reality and virtual representations, affecting interaction fidelity and system robustness. Advances in multimodal perception, including computer vision, depth sensing, and other multimodal sensing approaches, combined with sensor fusion techniques, are opening new opportunities to bridge this gap. By enabling XR systems to capture, interpret, and maintain structured representations of the physical world, these approaches support more stable and context-aware interactions. title: Restoring the disconnected connectome: neuromodulation and engineering strategies for cognitive recovery in neurodegeneration
summary: Neurodegenerative disorders are increasingly understood as disorders of large-scale brain network disconnection rather than isolated regional damage. Structural and functional uncoupling within the connectome can give rise to selective cognitive deficits, such as impaired face recognition in frontotemporal dementia. Advances in computational neuroscience, particularly Network Control Theory (NCT), provide a powerful framework to model these disrupted networks and characterize how information flow breaks down. At the same time, emerging neuromodulation techniques, including transcranial alternating current stimulation (tACS) and transcranial magnetic stimulation (TMS), offer promising avenues to externally influence brain dynamics and potentially restore lost connectivity. This line of research is highly relevant, as it advances a mechanistic understanding of network dysfunction and paves the way for precision neuromodulation strategies. title: Nanomaterials for Parkinson’s Disease in the Aging Brain: Neuroprotection, Regeneration, and Targeted Delivery
summary: Parkinson’s disease (PD) presents a major challenge in aging neuroscience, particularly given the strong influence of age-related biological changes on disease incidence, progression, and therapeutic outcomes. Recent research highlights how cellular dysfunctions associated with the aging brain, including impaired mitochondrial dynamics, disrupted protein homeostasis, neuroinflammatory activation, compromised vascular integrity, and reduced clearance capacity, contribute to and exacerbate PD pathology. These aging-related alterations not only drive neurodegeneration but may also limit therapeutic effectiveness, as traditional interventions often do not fully address the added biological complexities of older age. Despite important advances, the precise mechanisms by which aging shapes PD pathogenesis and treatment response remain incompletely understood, highlighting the need for studies that more directly consider CNS aging within this disease context.

Many patients experience a wide range of neuropsychological and psychiatric comorbidities, including social dysfunction, which can negatively affect their quality of life, reduce life expectancy, increase healthcare utilization, and elevate medical costs. Cognitive and psychiatric changes in epilepsy are often linked to dysfunction in specific brain regions, including the hippocampus, amygdala, prefrontal cortex, and temporal lobe structures, which play key roles in learning, memory, emotion, and social behavior. To investigate the mechanisms underlying these comorbidities, preclinical studies often rely on rodent models of epilepsy. title: Machine-learning/Deep-learning methods in neuromarketing and consumer neuroscience: Volume III
summary: The fields of Consumer Neuroscience and Neuromarketing represent the frontier of understanding human behavior, merging advanced neuroscientific methodologies with behavioral science to decode the cognitive and emotional drivers of consumption. While Consumer Neuroscience provides the academic bedrock for understanding decision-making and choice preferences, Neuromarketing translates these insights into actionable business strategies, such as optimizing brand engagement and product design.

title: Multi-Target Therapeutic Strategies in Neurological Disorders: Beyond Single-Gene Paradigms
summary: Neurological disorders represent a highly complex area within medicine, characterized by multifactorial etiologies involving disruptions across numerous genes, molecular pathways, and brain networks. Traditional drug development has often relied on single-target interventions aimed at correcting isolated molecular defects. However, growing evidence from neurodegenerative, neuropsychiatric, epileptic, and cerebrovascular diseases underscores the limited efficacy and poor sustainability of these approaches, as these conditions rarely stem from singular molecular causes. Recent studies increasingly highlight the need for a paradigm shift—one that acknowledges the web of dysregulated processes and seeks to restore balance at the network level by engaging multiple biological nodes simultaneously.

title: Neuromorphic Computing and AI for Energy-Efficient and Adaptive Edge Intelligence
summary: Artificial intelligence (AI) has become a pivotal field in scientific research, yet its progress has been limited by reliance on massive datasets, high computational demands, and energy inefficiency. The growing need for real-time AI processing on edge devices—from autonomous vehicles to wearables—further exposes these limitations, particularly in terms of latency, as traditional AI systems struggle with power, memory, and responsiveness under constrained environments. Neuromorphic computing, inspired by the brain’s efficiency, offers a transformative solution by enabling parallel, adaptive learning with ultra-low power consumption, making it ideal for edge computing and real-time applications.

title: Advances and Applications of Artificial Intelligence in Comprehensive Stroke Care
summary: Artificial intelligence (AI) has emerged as a powerful enabler of innovation in stroke care, with growing applications across diagnosis, treatment, and recovery. Stroke remains a leading cause of death and long-term disability worldwide, underscoring the need for faster recognition, more accurate clinical decision-making, and personalized care strategies across all stages of management. Recent advances in machine learning and deep learning have accelerated progress in early stroke recognition, particularly in prehospital and telestroke settings, as well as in imaging interpretation and decision support during acute care. At the same time, AI-based approaches are increasingly being explored to support post-acute management, functional outcome prediction, and rehabilitation planning.

title: Behavior, context, plasticity: Environmental enrichment as a framework for Autism and ADHD treatment
summary: Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) and Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (ADHD) are prevalent, often co-occurring neurodevelopmental conditions where symptom severity and daily functioning are influenced by environmental context. While pharmacological interventions and structured psychotherapies are the traditional pillars of care, there is an emerging emphasis on the role of "environmental enrichment" (EE). Originally rooted in basic neuroscience, EE refers to the systematic enhancement of a subject’s surroundings through social, cognitive, and sensorimotor stimulation. In clinical settings, this translates to modifying a child’s daily experience through structured novelty, physical activity, and purposeful sensory input. Understanding how these contextual modifications leverage experience-dependent plasticity is essential for developing holistic, non-pharmacological interventions that stabilize arousal, improve self-regulation, and facilitate skill acquisition in neurodivergent po

title: Beyond Passive Sensory Processing: Active and Closed-Loop Modulation in Humans
summary: Sensory processing is fundamental to perception, action, and cognition, and its disruption contributes to a wide range of neurological, psychiatric, and movement disorders. Classical models of sensory neuroscience have largely conceptualized sensory systems as passive receivers of external stimuli, emphasizing feedforward encoding and stimulus–response relationships under controlled laboratory conditions. While this framework has yielded foundational insights, it offers limited explanatory power for context-dependent perception, rapid adaptation, and the role of action and internal state in shaping sensory experience. Recent advances in wearable sensing, mobile neurophysiology, and real-time data processing have enabled a reconceptualization of sensation as an active, regulated process embedded within perception–action loops. title: Cognition in Parkinson's disease - Vol II
summary: Cognitive impairment in Parkinson’s disease (PD) represents a growing area of interest within neuroscience and clinical research, given PD's evolution from being defined as a predominantly motor disorder to a recognized multisystem disease. Over recent years, it has become evident that cognitive symptoms, ranging from mild cognitive impairment to overt dementia, are common among individuals with PD and contribute substantially to patient morbidity, caregiver burden, and socioeconomic costs. Understanding the progression and mechanisms of cognitive decline in PD is complicated by its often subtle onset during the prodromal phase and the diverse clinical presentations linked to genetic, environmental, and biological factors. title: Formation and Maintenance Mechanisms of Biodiversity in Typical Ecological Barrier Zones-Ecological Barriers and Transboundary Biodiversity Conservation
summary: Ecological barrier zones, such as mountainous regions, karst landscapes, and transboundary biodiversity hotspots, play a vital role in maintaining ecological security and biodiversity patterns across large spatial scales. Despite their importance, the processes shaping biodiversity formation, maintenance, and response to environmental change in these zones remain insufficiently understood. Recent advances in phylogeography, evolutionary genetics, and ecosystem ecology have revealed complex biogeographic patterns and evolutionary trajectories that drive species diversification and ecological adaptation. However, challenges persist in linking such evolutionary mechanisms to spatial patterns of biodiversity and in understanding how ecosystems in these sensitive environments respond to anthropogenic pressures and climate-induced disturbances. title: Geospatial and Transport Modeling in Stroke Service Planning - Volume II
summary: Six years on from the first Volume of this Research Topic, the case for thoughtful, data-driven stroke service planning is stronger than ever. Endovascular thrombectomy has expanded into late time windows (up to 24 hours), into large ischaemic cores (SELECT2, RESCUE-Japan LIMIT, ANGEL-ASPECT), and into basilar artery occlusion (ATTENTION, BAOCHE). Tenecteplase is rapidly replacing alteplase as the thrombolytic of choice in many systems following AcT, TRACE-2, and ATTEST-2. Mobile Stroke Units have moved from proof of concept to demonstrated benefit on functional outcomes (BEST-MSU, B_PROUD), and the conversation has shifted from “should we?” to “where, how many, and for whom?”.

title: The Aging Brain-Immune Axis: Microglia and Neuron Crosstalk in Neurodegeneration
summary: Neuro-immune interactions play a fundamental role in maintaining central nervous system (CNS) homeostasis and dictating neurological disease progression in aging and degeneration. Immune cells within and at the borders of the CNS — particularly microglia and border-associated macrophages — are now recognized as key regulators of synaptic pruning, myelin integrity, metabolic support, and tissue repair, and their crosstalk with peripheral immune cells is increasingly implicated in age-related neurological decline.
