title: Synergizing Artificial Intelligence with Neuromodulation for Movement Disorder Management
summary: Neuromodulation has revolutionized the treatment of movement disorders such as Parkinson’s disease, dystonia, and essential tremor. With advancements in adaptive deep brain stimulation (DBS), spinal cord stimulation (SCS), and non-invasive neuromodulation techniques, treatment outcomes have significantly improved. Alongside these developments, artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning are expanding possibilities by enabling personalized treatment strategies and optimizing stimulation parameters. Despite these advancements, integrating AI algorithms into real-time neuromodulation systems, developing reliable biomarkers, and validating these approaches in large-scale clinical studies remain challenging. There exists enormous potential in the synergy between AI and neuromodulation to enhance therapeutic efficacy and improve patient outcomes.

title: The Response of Soil Erosion to Vegetation Restoration: Processes, Mechanisms, and Model Development
summary: Vegetation is a key regulator of soil erosion, and large-scale restoration programs such as the return of farmland to forest and grassland have produced substantial reductions in sediment delivery to river systems. These programs have also driven significant changes in near-surface characteristics, including soil physical and chemical properties, vegetation stems, litter layers, biological soil crusts, and root architecture.

title: Translational Research in Veterinary Medicine: Comparative Insights and Applications - Volume II
summary: Translational research is a fundamental driver of progress in veterinary medicine, effectively bridging the gap between biomedical discovery and clinical application. Within the Comparative and Clinical Medicine section, this collection seeks to highlight how veterinary science, grounded in rigorous methodologies and reinforced by cutting-edge technologies, can generate impactful knowledge with direct translational relevance for both animal and human health. In this context, the One Health paradigm, acknowledging the intrinsic interconnectedness of human, animal, and environmental health, provides a unifying and strategic foundation for both translational and comparative research. From the same perspective, the integration of veterinary clinical insights with laboratory animal science further strengthens experimental rigor, reproducibility, and translational validity. In addition, naturally occurring diseases in companion animals, livestock, and equines often mirror human conditions at

title: When brain clearance fails: glymphatic dysfunction in neurodegeneration
summary: The glymphatic system has emerged as a crucial pathway for metabolic waste clearance from the central nervous system, placing it at the forefront of neurodegenerative research. Growing experimental evidence suggests that impaired glymphatic transport contributes to the accumulation of neurotoxic proteins, including amyloid-β and tau, thereby potentially influencing the initiation and progression of neurodegenerative disorders such as Alzheimer’s disease, cerebral amyloid angiopathy (CAA), and related dementias. Despite rapid advances, fundamental questions remain regarding the mechanisms governing glymphatic dysfunction and its relevance to human pathology.

title: Harnessing Genomic and Coevolutionary Insights for Infectious Disease Management
summary: Infectious disease research has increasingly focused on understanding the evolutionary dynamics that contribute to disease emergence and persistence. This field encompasses a wide range of studies from the genomic level to entire populations, seeking to elucidate the driving forces behind infectious diseases' spread and development. Current studies highlight the importance of genomic insights in identifying how pathogens evolve and adapt, but there remains a significant gap in translating this knowledge into effective disease control strategies. By exploring host-pathogen interactions, researchers have begun to investigate the mechanisms of coevolution and its implications for the persistence and management of infectious diseases.

title: Opioids and the aging brain
summary: Opioid use among older adults has risen sharply over the past two decades, driven by long-term prescriptions for chronic pain, post-surgical recovery, and palliative care, as well as by the aging of populations affected by the broader opioid epidemic. Yet the aging brain is uniquely vulnerable to these compounds. Age-related changes in pharmacokinetics, blood-brain barrier integrity, receptor density, neuroinflammation, and reserve capacity all alter how opioids act on neural circuits, and how those circuits recover, or fail to recover, after exposure. The result is a growing but fragmented body of evidence linking opioid use in later life to cognitive decline, delirium, falls, mood disturbance, sleep disruption, and accelerated neurodegeneration.

title: Enhancing Models of Age-Related Neuroinflammation and Neurodegeneration: Bridging Translational Gaps Using Rodents and Zebrafish
summary: Age-related neuroinflammation is increasingly recognized as a central driver and modulator of neurodegenerative change, yet many preclinical studies continue to rely on young or middle-aged animals, limiting their ability to reflect the biology of the aging central nervous system. Aging profoundly alters neuroimmune signaling, glial function, blood–brain barrier integrity, vascular coupling, and mitochondrial homeostasis, reshaping vulnerability to conditions such as Alzheimer’s disease, Parkinson’s disease, and vascular cognitive impairment and dementia. As a result, preclinical models often diverge from the human disease context, contributing to enduring translational gaps between experimental findings and clinical outcomes.

title: Gender, Vulnerability, and Subjective Wellbeing in Educational and Social Contexts
summary: Subjective wellbeing has become a central construct in psychological and social sciences, serving as a key indicator of quality of life, mental health, and human development. However, wellbeing experiences are not uniformly distributed across individuals and social groups; they are deeply shaped by structural inequalities related to gender, socioeconomic vulnerability, educational exclusion, precarious employment, migration, and discrimination.

title: (Re-)Theorizing the Psyche: Exploring Foundational Shifts in Psychological Science
summary: The replication crisis has exposed deep-seated tensions within psychological science. Beyond technical or procedural flaws, it has raised fundamental questions about the epistemic architecture and ontological assumptions of the discipline. While most responses have focused on methodological refinement, such as improved statistical tools, preregistration, or open science initiatives, these efforts often leave unexamined the more foundational question: what the replication crisis reveals about psychological theory and about the assumptions psychology makes about its object of inquiry, the “psyche” beyond technical procedure.

title: Decoding Vagal Activity Across Scales: AI and Machine Learning Approaches to Autonomic Function
summary: The vagus nerve lies at the intersection of cardiovascular, neuroimmune, metabolic, and behavioral regulation, exerting influence across multiple levels of physiological organization. From single-fiber compound action potentials to network-level rhythms such as heart rate variability (HRV), vagal pathways provide measurable signatures of autonomic balance and adaptive state. Yet the translation of these signals into robust, clinically actionable predictors of health and disease remains fragmented. Preclinical electrophysiology, clinical HRV analytics, and closed-loop vagus nerve stimulation (VNS) each generate high-dimensional, richly patterned data — but these data streams often exist in isolation, limiting synthesis of principles that span scales, species, and experimental paradigms. This gap highlights the need for integrative frameworks capable of uniting autonomic physiology across the molecular, neural, and systemic domains.

title: Embodied Intelligence: Bridging Neuroscience, AI and Soft Robotics for Adaptive Physical AI
summary: The study of natural and artificial intelligence in physical agents has a great interest both from a scientific and technological point of view. On the one hand a better understanding of how intelligent behaviors evolved in nature, in particular in plants, animals and humans have the highest scientific interest, on the other hand the reverse engineering of the emergence of those behaviors in nature could lead to the development of deeply bio inspired artificial intelligent agents (a.k.a ‘intelligent robots’) much more reliable, adaptive and capable of those built so far. Recent advances in robotics and artificial intelligence have highlighted the critical role of embodiment and of the compliance of the physical bodied of agents (hence the success of ‘soft robotics’ ) in enabling more adaptive, flexible, and robust intelligent behavior. In contrast to traditional disembodied computational models, natural biological intelligence emerges through continuous interaction between brain, body,
image_alt: Embodied Intelligence: Bridging Neuroscience, AI and Soft Robotics for Adaptive Physical AI

title: Environmental and Lifestyle Modifiers of Immune Responses in Multiple Sclerosis
summary: Multiple sclerosis (MS) is a chronic inflammatory disease of the central nervous system characterized by substantial heterogeneity in disease course, immune activity, and response to therapy. While genetic susceptibility contributes to MS risk, environmental and lifestyle factors are increasingly recognized as important modifiers of disease onset, progression, and treatment outcomes. Factors such as obesity, smoking, infections, diet, and metabolic dysfunction can shape immune responses by altering innate and adaptive immune signaling, ultimately translating into distinct clinical effects among patients. Understanding how environmental and lifestyle exposures shape immune programming is therefore essential for explaining variability in disease risk, clinical heterogeneity, and the mechanisms that drive disease activity in MS.

title: Functional Neurosurgery and Epilepsy Surgery: Current and Emerging Therapies for Movement Disorders, Psychiatric Disorders, Epilepsy, and Pain
Ketogenic Diet Therapy in Pediatric Neurology: From Epilepsy to Emerging Indications
summary: The ketogenic diet (KD) is a high-fat, low-carbohydrate nutritional intervention that shifts systemic metabolism toward ketone body production, offering a powerful alternative energy substrate for the developing brain. Its most established indication remains refractory pediatric epilepsy, where it is recognised as a first-line therapy when antiseizure medications fail. Beyond epilepsy, clinical evidence supports its use in specific inherited metabolic disorders with neurological impact, including glucose transporter 1 (GLUT1) deficiency and pyruvate dehydrogenase deficiency, where it bypasses defective glucose-dependent pathways. More recently, interest has grown in its potential role in neurodevelopmental conditions, including autism spectrum disorder and ADHD, though evidence remains preliminary. Despite this expanding landscape, inconsistent protocols, limited long-term safety data, and the absence of standardised pediatric guidelines continue to hinder individualised implementation

title: NREM Sleep in the Aging Brain: Implications for Emotional Memory
summary: Sleep is not a passive period of neural quiescence but an active brain state essential for memory consolidation. This function becomes particularly critical in the context of aging, where alterations in sleep architecture and neural circuit integrity are closely linked to cognitive decline. Among behavioral paradigms used to probe sleep-memory interactions, fear conditioning provides a powerful framework to study how emotional memories are processed across the lifespan. NREM sleep, which constitutes the majority of total sleep time, contains key oscillatory events—slow oscillations, sleep spindles, and hippocampal ripples—that support systems-level memory consolidation. Notably, aging is associated with disruptions in these oscillatory dynamics, which may impair memory precision and emotional regulation. Understanding how sleep-dependent mechanisms evolve with age is therefore central to elucidating neurocognitive aging and vulnerability to neuropsychiatric and neurodegenerative disord
image_alt: NREM Sleep in the Aging Brain: Implications for Emotional Memory

title: Neuroimaging and Rehabilitation Mechanisms in Mood, Anxiety and Stress-related disorders
summary: Mood, anxiety and stress-related disorders, including major depressive disorder, generalized and social anxiety disorder, and post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD), represent a significant global burden. While pharmacological and psychological interventions remain the mainstay of treatment, the brain-network mechanisms that distinguish responders from non-responders, and first-episode from recurrent illness, are still not fully understood. Advances in multimodal magnetic resonance imaging, including resting-state and task-based fMRI, diffusion MRI (diffusion tensor imaging, DTI and diffusion spectrum imaging, DSI), and structural MRI, have opened new windows into how large-scale brain networks reorganize during the progression and remission of psychiatric symptoms. In parallel, targeted rehabilitation approaches such as cognitive remediation and mindfulness-based therapies, real-time fMRI neurofeedback, and pharmacological neuromodulation are showing promise in promoting network-level
image_alt: Neuroimaging and Rehabilitation Mechanisms in Mood, Anxiety and Stress-related disorders

title: Neuroinflammation in Peripheral Nerve Degeneration and Regeneration: Mechanisms and Therapeutic Perspectives
summary: Neuroinflammation within the peripheral nervous system (PNS) dynamically influences axon degeneration, tissue remodeling, and regeneration after injury and in various neuropathies. Interactions among Schwann cells, macrophages, and immune mediators can promote repair or exacerbate damage. Recent findings demonstrate that specific immune pathways critically regulate nerve recovery efficiency. Within this context, nodopathies - neuropathies involving autoimmune targeting of nodal and paranodal proteins such as neurofascin, contactin, and CASPR - represent a particularly informative model of peculiar immune-mediated mechanisms and their therapeutic implications, relevant to nodal integrity, nerve function, and repair processes. Nevertheless, the mechanisms by which immune activity shapes the balance between degeneration and regeneration remain incompletely defined. Understanding these processes is key to developing precise interventions that modulate neuroinflammatory responses and suppor

title: New Approaches to Diagnosis and Intervention for Age-Related Diseases in Animals
summary: Various age-related diseases have increased as animals live longer. Chronic inflammation is a common underlying pathology shared by age-related diseases, including obesity disease, chronic kidney disease, type 2 diabetes, and cancer. In aged animals, chronic inflammation tends to occur more readily, and age-related inflammation (inflammaging) appears to contribute the onset and progression of age-related disease. As age-related diseases are difficult to treat radically, early diagnosis and prevention of severe diseases are more important than curing the disease. The secretion of proinflammatory cytokines from senescent cells accumulated in tissues with age, the so-called ‘senescence-associated secretory phenotype’ (SASP), contributes to the onset of inflammaging. Serum amyloid A (SAA) as one of the SASP molecules appears to be a useful diagnostic marker for inflammaging in cats. title: New Insights into mitochondria-induced neuroimmune disorder：From mechanisms to phenotypes
summary: Mitochondria are multifunctional organelles that not only generate adenosine triphosphate (ATP) but are also integral to the production of reactive oxygen species (ROS), the maintenance of calcium homeostasis, and the regulation of apoptotic pathways. Although significant progress has been made in the regulation of mitochondrial function in the basis of neural regeneration, the mechanisms of regulating mitochondrial synthesis, metabolism and their regulation during the neuroimmune process remain poorly understood. In neurological diseases, such as trauma or degeneration, the functional remodeling of mitochondria or the differences in mitochondrial structure in different cells are also enormous. A major challenge lies in elaborating the mechanisms and phenotypic changes of mitochondria in the process of neuroimmune disorders. This effort requires collaboration across basic and clinical disciplines.

title: Photography as a tool in Mental Health Research and Intervention
summary: The intersection of visual arts and mental health has gained increasing recognition, with photography emerging as a promising instrument for both research and clinical practice. There has been growing interest in modalities such as photo-voice, therapeutic photography, and participatory visual storytelling within psychiatry and mental health care. Despite this progress, questions remain about the mechanisms by which photography supports emotional expression, self-understanding, and social connection, particularly among patients with depressive, anxiety, trauma-related, and adjustment disorders, including those with psychiatric comorbidity in the context of chronic illness and substance use disorders.

title: Psychosexual Disorders: Awareness, Attitudes, Comorbidity, and Care Across Populations
summary: Psychosexual disorders represent a heterogeneous group of conditions underpinned by psychological, social, and biological determinants. These disorders frequently remain underrecognized due to factors such as the pervasive stigma surrounding sexual health, sociocultural norms, limited accessibility of specialized sexual health services, inadequate awareness of therapeutic options, and prevailing negative attitudes toward sexuality. The manifestations of psychosexual disorders vary considerably across countries, communities, and social strata. Furthermore, numerous medical and psychiatric conditions, as well as their pharmacological treatments, may influence psychosexual health, either directly or through secondary mechanisms. Psychosexual issues can also arise within non-clinical populations, including individuals going through puberty, those with diverse sexual orientations, and individuals whose beliefs and behaviors are shaped by cultural influences.

title: Social and Geographic Determinants of Stroke: Disparities, Interventions, and Pathways to Equity Across the Stroke Care Continuum
summary: Stroke remains a leading cause of death and disability worldwide, yet its burden is distributed unequally across populations and regions. Recent statements from the American Heart Association/American Stroke Association and the American Academy of Neurology emphasize that social determinants of health (including education, economic stability, access to care, neighborhood environment, insurance status, and structural racism) are major drivers of inequities in stroke risk, treatment, and outcomes. These inequities affect systemically marginalized populations, including racial and ethnic minorities, rural communities, people with low socioeconomic status, and other historically underserved groups.
image_alt: Social and Geographic Determinants of Stroke: Disparities, Interventions, and Pathways to Equity Across the Stroke Care Continuum

title: Synapses in action: Mechanistic and translational insights into motor and cognitive functions - BraYn Conference 2025-2026 outputs
summary: Neural circuits translate the activity of individual synapses into coherent patterns of behavior. Synaptic plasticity governs how information is encoded and integrated at the microscopic level, while interconnected circuits sustain primarily motor control at the meso- and macroscopic levels. Disruption of this delicate balance, whether due to traumatic injury, tumor growth, inflammation, or therapeutic interventions, compromises circuit dynamics and leads to measurable impairments in motor performance and coordination. Recent technological and conceptual advances, including high-resolution imaging, multi-omics integration, and computational approaches to circuit analysis, now enable unprecedented insight into how these micro- and macro-level processes interact.
image_alt: Synapses in action: Mechanistic and translational insights into motor and cognitive functions - BraYn Conference 2025-2026 outputs

title: Synthetic, Wireless, and In-Situ Bioelectronics for Chronic Neuromodulation
summary: Over the past decade, neural technology has progressed at an extraordinary pace. However, despite the advent of flexible polymers and miniaturized CMOS hardware, a fundamental mismatch persists between the static nature of artificial implants and the dynamic, multi-scale organization of biological tissue. Traditional interfaces remain foreign, pre-fabricated objects that struggle to conform to the living parenchyma. This Research Topic aims to catalyze a paradigm shift from Implanted Bioelectronics to Integrated Synthetic Neurobiology, where the chronic stability problem is addressed not merely through material compliance, but through deep biological integration.

title: Targeting autonomic-immune regulation with neuromodulation in the perioperative period
summary: Autonomic neuroscience explores the complexities of the autonomic nervous system, which is essential for maintaining homeostasis and generating adaptive responses to physiological and pathophysiological challenges. The autonomic nervous system regulates numerous vital functions, including heart rate, blood pressure, temperature, and digestion, and interacts closely with the immune system. The perioperative period represents a well-defined model of acute autonomic and immune perturbation, providing a unique opportunity to investigate autonomic regulation and its modulation in a controlled clinical setting.

title: The Involvement of the Peripheral Nervous System in Parkinson's Disease: Mechanistic and Diagnostic Implications
summary: Parkinson’s Disease (PD) has traditionally been associated with the demise of central dopaminergic neurons. However, emerging evidence increasingly highlights the significance of the peripheral nervous system (PNS) in the disease’s pathogenesis and progression. Recent investigations, both clinical and preclinical, spotlight the manifestations of peripheral neural dysfunction such as autonomic failure, gastrointestinal issues, sensory disturbances, and neuropathies, which often predate or co-occur with the central motor and cognitive symptoms of PD. Peripheral tissue alterations–observed in muscles, skin, blood, kidneys, and autonomic nerves–shed light on early pathological changes, while systemic variations, including hepatic and metabolic dysfunctions, hint at extra-CNS contributions to neurodegeneration via neuroimmune and neurotoxic avenues. image_alt: The Involvement of the Peripheral Nervous System in Parkinson's Disease: Mechanistic and Diagnostic Implications

title: Towards Personalized Treatment of Cognitive Symptoms in Psychiatric Disorders: Usefulness of Clinical Indicators and Biomarkers
summary: Cognitive symptoms, such as impairments in memory, attention, and executive functioning, are prevalent across a wide range of psychiatric disorders, including schizophrenia, major depressive disorder, and bipolar disorder. These deficits significantly hinder daily functioning and overall quality of life and are often resistant to current standard treatments. Advances in neuroscience and biomedical research have uncovered a diverse array of clinical indicators and biomarkers—ranging from neuroimaging and genetic profiles to cognitive test performance—that may illuminate the underlying biological and clinical heterogeneity contributing to these symptoms. Integrating such insights has the potential to revolutionize how cognitive dysfunction in psychiatric conditions is diagnosed and treated.

title: Workers' Mental Health: Contemporary Challenges and Perspectives on Care
summary: The accelerated transformation of contemporary work dynamics, driven by digitalization and the demand for constant productivity, has reshaped the fields of Occupational Health and Organizational Psychology. Currently, work is not merely a means of subsistence, but a scenario of intense pressures where excessive workload and occupational exposure to psychosocial risks have become ubiquitous.
image_alt: Workers' Mental Health: Contemporary Challenges and Perspectives on Care

title: XR and Digital Experiences for Rehabilitation: Motivation, Engagement, Performance and Experience
summary: Extended Reality (XR), encompassing virtual, augmented, and mixed reality, is increasingly adopted in rehabilitation to enhance treatment effectiveness through immersive, adaptive, and motivating environments. Beyond motor and cognitive outcomes, successful XR-based rehabilitation critically depends on psychological factors such as motivation, engagement, emotional regulation, and perceived experience. At the same time, XR systems enable multimodal data acquisition, including behavioral metrics and neurophysiological signals such as EEG and MRI, offering unprecedented opportunities for objective, continuous, and ecologically valid assessment of psychological, behavioral, and physiological processes. However, the rapid technological development has outpaced the establishment of standardized, quantitative measures capable of capturing both subjective psychological processes and their underlying neural and physiological correlates within rehabilitation contexts.
image_alt: XR and Digital Experiences for Rehabilitation: Motivation, Engagement, Performance and Experience

title: Advanced Brain-Machine Interfaces (BMIs) for Neuromusculoskeletal Disorders
summary: Neuromusculoskeletal disorders—encompassing conditions such as stroke, spinal cord injury, amyotrophic lateral sclerosis, cerebral palsy, and traumatic limb loss—represent a profound challenge to global health, often resulting in significant and persistent impairment of motor function and sensory feedback. While traditional neurorehabilitation and prosthetic solutions have provided substantial benefits, they frequently fall short of restoring natural, intuitive, and coordinated movement. The convergence of neuroscience, engineering, and clinical medicine has now brought us to a pivotal moment where advanced Brain-Machine Interfaces (BMIs) offer a transformative pathway to bridge this gap.

title: Myotonic Disorders: Myotonic Dystrophies (DM1/DM2) and Non-Dystrophic Myotonias
summary: Myotonic Dystrophies, Non-Dystrophic Myotonias, and related Myotonic Syndromes are complex neuromuscular disorders marked by myotonia, progressive or episodic muscle weakness, and variable multisystem involvement. Beyond skeletal muscle symptoms, affected individuals may experience an important disease burden and reduced quality of life. Myotonic dystrophies (DM1 and DM2), the most prevalent adult-onset muscular dystrophies, are particularly characterized by marked phenotypic variability and multisystem involvement, which complicate early diagnosis, risk stratification, and long-term management. Cardiac, respiratory, endocrine, metabolic, gastrointestinal, ophthalmological, and central nervous system (CNS) manifestations — including cognitive and neuropsychiatric symptoms, sleep disturbances, fatigue, apathy, hypersomnolence, and anosognosia — profoundly influence morbidity, mortality, functional independence, and quality of life. Emerging evidence also suggests accelerated neurologica

title: Safe and Trustworthy Reinforcement Learning for Human–Robot Collaboration
summary: Reinforcement Learning (RL) has rapidly emerged as a powerful approach for enabling robots to acquire adaptive, data-driven behaviors in real-world environments. In Human–Robot Interaction (HRI), RL offers a pathway toward robots that can collaborate effectively with people, adapt to user preferences, and operate under changing task and environmental conditions. However, HRI introduces distinct challenges: human behavior is dynamic and diverse, interaction is often partially observable, and many settings are safety-critical and socially constrained. As a result, conventional autonomy pipelines—and RL methods optimized primarily for performance—can struggle to deliver interactions that are safe, predictable, and intuitive, especially under uncertainty and distribution shift.

title: Complex Soccer Motor Skills: Mechanisms, Measurement, and Field Performance
summary: Soccer is one of the world’s most cognitively and motorically demanding team sports, in which match outcomes often depend on a small number of decisive actions. Among these, scoring-related skills are especially important because they emerge under severe temporal pressure, variable environmental constraints, and strong psychological tension. Yet many complex soccer skills, particularly advanced finishing and airborne scoring techniques, remain underexplored scientifically despite their clear practical importance. As a result, coaches often rely on experiential knowledge rather than evidence-based training principles when teaching them. Recent advances in motion capture, wearable sensing, video analytics, and artificial intelligence now offer new opportunities to study these actions in more representative contexts and to generate knowledge that is directly usable in coaching. This Research Topic aims to strengthen the bridge between movement science and real-world soccer practice.

title: Deep learning strategies for multimodal image fusion in neuroimaging
summary: Neuroimaging has become a cornerstone of modern neuroscience, enabling detailed investigation of brain structure, function, and pathology. With advances in imaging modalities such as magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), functional MRI (fMRI), positron emission tomography (PET), and magneto- and electroencephalography (M/EEG), researchers now gather complementary data capturing diverse aspects of brain physiology. However, combining these heterogeneous sources into unified, meaningful representations remains a critical challenge due to differences in spatial resolution, contrast mechanisms, and signal characteristics.

title: Generative AI and Critical Literacy: Authorship, Media, and Education in an Era of Synthetic Content
summary: Generative AI systems are now embedded in everyday practice. They shape how texts are written, images produced, and content circulated—not as neutral tools, but as sociotechnical systems that redistribute agency and reconfigure what counts as knowledge, authorship, and expertise. This shift is unfolding faster than educational research and practice can adapt, and robust frameworks for understanding the new literacy demands placed on learners, teachers, and institutions remain underdeveloped.

title: Intelligent Robots and Digital Twin Technology for Fault Diagnosis under Industry 5.0
summary: Intelligent robots are central to modern industry, enabling precision manufacturing, flexible production, and human–robot collaboration. With the rise of Industry 5.0, increasing system complexity introduces significant challenges in ensuring reliability and safety. Traditional fault diagnosis methods struggle with high-dimensional, nonlinear data, while data-driven and AI-based approaches offer improved capabilities. Digital twin technology further enhances real-time monitoring and predictive maintenance through virtual–physical synchronization. However, challenges remain in multi-physics modeling, data fusion, model generalization, and ensuring real-time, secure, and scalable deployment in practical environments.

title: Recent Advances in Coprolite Research
summary: The study of ichnofossils such as coprolites provides a unique window into the palaeoecology and palaeoenvironment of ancient ecosystems. Coprolites—fossilized faecal matter preserved since the Cambrian—offer direct palaeobiological evidence of trophic interactions and dietary preferences of prehistoric organisms. Recent developments in non-destructive imaging technologies, particularly micro-computed tomography (Micro-CT), have enabled high-resolution analyses of inclusions within coprolites, yielding unprecedented insight into ancient food webs. Despite over two centuries of research, however, important gaps remain. Chief among these are challenges in confidently linking coprolites to their producer taxa, understanding the mineralisation pathways that lead from excrement to fossilization, and establishing a comprehensive global framework for their classification. title: AI-Enhanced Computational Tools for Early Detection of Mental and Neurological Disorders
summary: Mental and neurological disorders, including Alzheimer’s disease, Parkinson’s disease, depression, and schizophrenia, represent a growing global health challenge. Traditionally, diagnosis relies on clinical observation and standardized behavioral assessments, which often occur only after significant neurobiological changes have already manifested. The delay in detection limits the effectiveness of therapeutic interventions and increases the socioeconomic burden on healthcare systems. However, the rise of computational neuroscience and artificial intelligence (AI) offers a transformative opportunity. By leveraging high-dimensional data, ranging from neuroimaging and electrophysiology to digital phenotyping and speech patterns, AI-enhanced tools can identify subtle, non-linear biomarkers of pathology long before clinical symptoms emerge. This Research Topic focuses on the intersection of machine learning and neurobiology to develop the next generation of predictive diagnostic frameworks.

title: Advancing human neuroscience through open and reusable datasets
summary: Human neuroscience is producing increasingly rich and diverse datasets spanning neuroimaging, electrophysiology, cognition, behavior, clinical phenotyping, and multimodal study designs. The scientific value of these resources depends not only on data generation, but also on their transparency, documentation, interoperability, and long-term reuse.

title: Computational Approaches to Brain-Computer Interface Development
summary: Brain-Computer Interfaces (BCIs) represent a frontier in neurotechnology, establishing a direct communication pathway between the brain and external devices. By bypassing traditional neuromuscular channels, BCIs offer life-changing potential for individuals with motor impairments, spinal cord injuries, or locked-in syndrome. At the heart of every BCI is a computational engine responsible for translating complex neural signals, recorded via EEG, ECoG, or intracortical arrays, into actionable commands. Recent years have seen a surge in high-resolution neural recording and sophisticated signal processing. However, the field now faces a critical transition: moving from controlled laboratory demonstrations to robust, real-world applications. This requires innovative computational frameworks that can handle the inherent non-stationarity of brain signals, the low signal-to-noise ratio of non-invasive recordings, and the high-dimensional nature of population dynamics.

title: Digital Twins of the Brain: High-Fidelity Computational Models for Simulating Neural Disorders and Therapeutic Outcomes
summary: The "Digital Twin" concept, a virtual, high-fidelity representation of a physical system, is transforming engineering and is now gaining significant momentum in medicine. In neuroscience, creating a Digital Twin involves integrating a patient’s structural connectivity, functional dynamics, and physiological parameters into a personalized computational model. While traditional computational neuroscience has focused on generalized "average brain" models to understand fundamental principles, these often fail to account for the vast inter-individual variability seen in clinical populations. With the advent of high-resolution neuroimaging, long-term wearable sensing, and increased supercomputing power, we can now simulate the brain's activity at multiple scales. This paradigm shift allows for the in silico testing of interventions, moving us closer to a future where neurological and psychiatric treatments are tailored to the unique physiological landscape of each patient. title: Mechanisms and Interventions for Neurodevelopmental Disorders Following Early-Life Exposure to Risk Factors
summary: Neurodevelopmental disorders, including autism spectrum disorder, attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder, and intellectual disability, represent a pressing global public health issue with a steadily increasing prevalence in children. Early life is a critical window for neurodevelopment, during which exposure to diverse risk factors—such as surgical trauma, anesthetic agents, psychosocial trauma, heavy metal contamination, endocrine-disrupting chemicals, and nutritional inadequacies—can directly perturb the immature nervous system and trigger neurodevelopmental impairments. Despite growing recognition of this causal link, the complex pathogenic pathways connecting specific risk factors to distinct neurodevelopmental outcomes remain incompletely understood, highlighting the need for innovative research approaches to address this knowledge gap.

title: Modeling Neural Plasticity and Learning
summary: Neural plasticity, the brain's remarkable ability to modify its structure and function in response to experience, serves as the fundamental substrate for learning and memory. This dynamic process spans a wide array of mechanisms, from the rapid changes in synaptic strength (synaptic plasticity) to the slower reorganization of physical connections (structural plasticity) and the stabilization of firing rates (homeostatic plasticity). In computational neuroscience, capturing these processes is essential for understanding how the brain adapts to an ever-changing environment. While classic models like Spike-Timing-Dependent Plasticity (STDP) have provided a strong foundation, the real-world complexity of neural circuits involves the simultaneous interaction of multiple plasticity rules across different timescales and brain states. title: Personalised Surgical Care in Neuro-Oncology
summary: The management of brain tumours, particularly diffuse gliomas (WHO grades 2–4), remains one of the most complex challenges in modern neurosurgery. This Research Topic welcomes submissions addressing both adult and paediatric brain tumours, as well as primary and secondary brain tumours, including brain metastases from extracranial solid or haematological malignancies. Their infiltrative growth patterns and frequent proximity to eloquent brain regions often limit the extent of safe resection. While maximal tumour resection, defined radiologically, has consistently been associated with improved outcomes, the benefit of incomplete resection remains uncertain, highlighting the need for careful, individualised surgical decision-making. In many cases, stereotactic biopsy may represent a more appropriate approach when the risks of surgery outweigh potential oncological gains.

title: Cellular Mechanotransduction Mechanisms
summary:
Organisms can sense and respond to mechanical stimuli by converting physical forces into biochemical signals, which process is known as mechanotransduction. These mechanical cues regulate essential inter‑ and intracellular processes, including cell fate determination, migration, proliferation, and tissue morphogenesis. Nevertheless, the molecular mechanisms underlying mechanotransduction and how these signals are coordinated within tissues, remain to be fully elucidated. 

This Collection brings together studies that advance our understanding of cellular mechanotransduction mechanisms, from force sensing at the membrane to the clinical applications of diseases.

title: Complement at the Crossroads: Neuroinflammation vs Neuroprotection in CNS Injury and Disorders
summary: The complement system is a central component of innate immunity and plays a critical role in the central nervous system (CNS), both in normal physiology and across a wide spectrum of neurological conditions. Under homeostatic conditions (notably during brain development), complement contributes to synaptic refinement and clearance of cellular debris. In contrast, chronic or dysregulated complement activation in CNS injury or disease drives neuroinflammation, synapse loss, and neurodegeneration. These effects have been characterized across numerous conditions, including Traumatic Brain Injury (TBI), Spinal Cord Injury (SCI), Alzheimer's Disease (AD), Parkinson's Disease (PD), Stroke, Amyotrophic Lateral Sclerosis (ALS), Multiple Sclerosis (MS), and others. Recent advances in understanding complement's dual roles in the CNS have spurred development of targeted therapeutics, several of which are now in clinical trials, though most address rare diseases. summary: Veterinary neonatology is a rapidly advancing field that addresses the critical challenges of managing health and survival in newborn animals across species. Recent years have witnessed significant methodological shifts driven by reproductive management breakthroughs, precision diagnostics, neonatal intensive care, and the integration of ‘omics’ technologies. Despite this progress, neonatal morbidity and mortality continue to impact both animal welfare and production efficiency, especially due to complex conditions such as prematurity, failure of passive transfer, perinatal hypoxia, dysbiosis, sepsis, and birth defects. These problems are multifactorial, requiring a comprehensive approach that connects peripartum events with immediate and long-term neonatal outcomes. title: Silent Infections in Livestock and other Production Species
summary: Silent infections - those that progress without clear clinical signs in their early stages - pose a significant challenge to veterinary medicine and animal health management. These infections often remain undetected for extended periods, allowing pathogens to persist, spread within populations, and eventually cross species barriers. Subclinical carriers can act as reservoirs for zoonotic agents, complicating disease control and endangering food security, trade, and public health. In livestock and other production species, such as honey bees and fish, silent infections can compound the effects of secondary co-infections, cause significant losses in productivity, reproductive performance, and product quality, leading to substantial economic impact for producers. summary: The recent surge of interest in generative AI has brought unprecedented advances in content generation, reasoning, and multimodal interaction, while also exposing a growing set of concerns that extend well beyond model performance. As generative AI systems are increasingly deployed in real-world scenarios, issues such as fairness, privacy, safety, robustness, transparency, and accountability have become central to their responsible development and use. Although substantial efforts have been made to address these challenges, existing research remains scattered across different communities and often focuses on isolated aspects of the problem. There is still a clear need for a dedicated forum that brings together methodological advances, empirical evaluations, benchmarking efforts, and deployment-oriented studies in a unified manner. title: Advancing Soft Technology: Innovative Sensing Solutions for Next-Generation Biomedical Applications
summary: Soft and flexible sensors are transforming sensing technologies by addressing the limitations of rigid, traditional systems. Designed to mimic the mechanical properties of biological tissues or adapt to irregular surfaces, these sensors provide enhanced integration and functionality. Built from materials like elastomers, conductive polymers, and hydrogels, they use principles such as resistive, capacitive, optical, and piezoelectric sensing to detect pressure, strain, temperature, and chemical changes. Recent advances include self-healing materials, miniaturized fabrication techniques, wireless electronics, and energy-autonomous systems, enabling durable and multifunctional designs.

title: Digital Mental Health Interventions in Comorbid Chronic Physical Conditions
summary: Mental health problems are highly prevalent among individuals with chronic physical conditions (e.g., COPD, cardiovascular disease, and diabetes). Individuals with multimorbidity, defined as the co-occurrence of chronic physical conditions and mental health problems, frequently experience elevated psychological distress, including anxiety, depressive symptoms, and emotional strain, alongside the ongoing demands of managing and adapting to long-term illness. These combined challenges can negatively affect coping, daily functioning, and engagement with both psychological and somatic care. At the same time, mental health problems are not always adequately identified or treated, partly due to fragmentation between mental and physical healthcare, resulting in limited integration of psychological support within chronic care pathways.

title: Dissecting Dyshomeostasis in Neural Aging and Disease: Insights from Spatial Omics and Molecular Imaging

Historically, our understanding of lipid and small-molecule metabolism - and of protein alterations - has relied largely on measuring enzyme expression/activity and bulk protein abundance. While informative, these approaches often miss the spatiotemporal dynamics of molecular changes across the brain.

summary: Artificial intelligence tools and large language models are being deployed in infectious disease and critical care at a rate that outpaces the evidence base for their safety. Clinicians in these settings encounter AI-generated outputs — diagnostic suggestions, antimicrobial recommendations, sepsis risk scores — from systems whose performance has rarely been evaluated against the guidelines they are required to apply. Where clinical decisions are time-critical and directly consequential, this gap carries direct implications for patient safety.

title: From Digital Well-Being to Online Victimization: New Frontiers in Cyberpsychology
summary: Digital technologies have become deeply embedded in everyday life, shaping the way individuals communicate, form relationships, access information, seek psychological support, and engage with society. Following the COVID-19 pandemic, the use of digital technologies in mental health care, including online counseling and psychotherapy, has increased substantially, highlighting new opportunities for promoting psychological well-being and expanding access to care. At the same time, digital environments expose users to a range of risks, including cyberbullying, cybercrime, online victimization, technology-facilitated violence, and the non-consensual sharing of intimate content. These phenomena have significant implications for mental health, interpersonal relationships, and legal systems. title: Harnessing Agricultural Residues for Sustainable Livestock Feeding under Climate Change and Drought Conditions
summary: Due to climate change and droughts, livestock production systems are facing significant challenges in terms of sustainability. Nutritional strategies that optimize feed efficiency and precision feeding are necessary to mitigate the negative effects of climate change and feed scarcity. It is possible to reduce reliance on traditional feedstuffs by using alternative feedstuffs, particularly drought-tolerant forages. Agri-industrial by-products can also be strategically incorporated into animal diets to improve resource use efficiency and to support circular agriculture. It is therefore necessary to evaluate nutritional, managerial, and environmental aspects of livestock production to ensure effective drought management in the face of climate change.

title: Multidimensional Evaluation and Multimodal Interventions for Dysphagia, Oral Health, and Nutritional Management in Neurological Diseases - Volume II
summary: Dysphagia constitutes a significant and multifaceted challenge within the realm of neurological disease, frequently emerging alongside oral dysfunction and malnutrition to markedly worsen patient outcomes. This triad not only increases the likelihood of aspiration pneumonia, frailty, and extended hospitalization, but also contributes to increased mortality rates. Growing evidence from recent research underscores the pivotal roles that oral health, oral microbiome dynamics, and nutritional status play in both the onset and progression of dysphagia. While modern clinical practice is rapidly adapting by adopting comprehensive management strategies that encompass the interconnected domains of swallowing, oral care, and diet, important questions remain concerning the optimization and real-world applicability of these interventions.

title: Sensory-motor integration in human movement
summary: For desired and coordinated movements, the central nervous system integrates multiple sensory feedback with motor commands. Optimum integration of multi-sensory signals from visual, vestibular, and somatosensory systems is vital to performing activities of daily life and is commonly compromised due to aging, neuromuscular disorders, and traumatic injuries. Compromised sensor-motor integration can potentially lead to a stability control deficiency, increased risk of falling, tremors, rigidity, and decreased hand dexterity, just to name a few. However, there is a limited understanding of the mechanisms responsible for sensory-motor integration, specifically, how the central nervous system adapts to changes in environmental conditions (e.g., visual input is obstructed), physical and mental health, and cognitive status. A comprehensive study of sensory-motor integration can be beneficial to healthcare professionals, neuroscientists, and human health in general.

summary: Contemporary emotion science is increasingly moving beyond models that frame emotional functioning as an individual skill or stable trait. Competent emotionality offers an alternative perspective, conceptualizing emotional processes as dynamic, relational, and context-dependent capacities. Within this framework, creativity emerges not only as a cognitive ability but as an affective and social process through which individuals make sense of, transform, and respond to their emotional environment. Resilience, in turn, is understood as the distinctive capacity of individuals and communities to absorb adversity and emerge transformed from it. Despite growing evidence on each of these dimensions separately, the affective mechanisms that connect them — and how they jointly shape responses to systemic emotional distress — remain underexplored. While the central roles of mitochondria in energy production, redox balance, and apoptosis have long been recognized in the context of these conditions, emerging research highlights a fascinating new player: the cytochrome P450 (CYP) superfamily, traditionally studied in hepatic drug metabolism, but now understood as an integral contributor to brain physiology.

These approaches offer a valuable framework for understanding the neural basis of action representation and motor simulation, while also supporting the development of innovative therapeutic strategies for individuals with neurological disorders and functional limitations. Their increasing relevance in both research and clinical practice reflects a broader interest in the role of simulated and observed action in motor learning, neuroplasticity, and functional recovery.

title: The legacy of Dr. Paul Broca: Expanding views on language processing, Volume II
summary: Neuroscience and linguistics have benefited significantly from the foundational work of Dr. Paul Broca, whose research in the 19th century on the brain’s role in speech production paved the way for a modern understanding of language processing. Broca’s identification of the brain area responsible for coordinated speech movements — a region now termed “Broca’s area” — highlighted the cerebral localization of language function. Despite the advances since Broca’s time, questions linger about the precise mechanisms of speech production and the integration of linguistic processing with neural pathways, suggesting a need for ongoing research.

title: Prodromes in multiple sclerosis and related disorders
summary: Prodromal phases are well recognized in several diseases, but the possibility of a prodrome in autoimmune inflammatory demyelinating disorders of the CNS—multiple sclerosis (MS), aquaporin-4 antibody NMOSD (AQP4+NMOSD), and MOGAD—has received relatively little attention until the past few years. A prodromal phase in MS and AQP4+NMOSD, with increased health care use, was observed up to 5 years preceding the first clinical attack. In MOGAD, prodrome seems to onset in close temporal association to time of disease onset. Defining prodrome in MS, NMOSD and MOGAD will allow the diagnosis of these diseases to be made before standard clinic-radiological definition, shortening the lag phase between the biological and disease onset, starting early disease modifying therapies and delaying the onset of diseases and disability.

It is now recognized as a central feature that contributes to immunosenescence, impaired tissue repair, and increased susceptibility to age-related diseases, including cardiovascular, neurodegenerative, and metabolic disorders.

summary: In the context of accelerating global environmental change and the UN Decade on Ecosystem Restoration, ecosystem restoration has become a central challenge in ecology, evolution, and conservation biology. Restored ecosystems are increasingly expected to recover not only biodiversity, but also ecological integrity, multifunctionality, resilience, and the capacity to sustain ecosystem services under future environmental conditions. Traditionally, restoration outcomes have been evaluated using metrics such as species richness or vegetation cover, which provide only limited insight into the recovery of ecological processes and long-term ecosystem functioning. Current research increasingly recognizes that ecological interactions, functional diversity, and ecosystem services represent more robust indicators of restoration success and adaptive capacity. title: Molecular Frontiers in Tropical Estuaries: Integrating Applied Genetics and Resource Conservation
summary: Tropical coastal zones and estuaries are highly dynamic and heterogeneous environments that support critical life cycles of numerous marine and estuarine species. Understanding how these populations are structured, how they connect across space, and how they respond to environmental shifts is vital for their long-term conservation. However, tracing the ecological and evolutionary dynamics of coastal species using traditional monitoring methods can be remarkably challenging due to environmental turbidity, complex life histories, and morphological similarities among closely related taxa. Applied genetics provides a powerful toolkit to overcome these limitations, offering deep insights into the hidden mechanisms that govern population persistence and community structures in these vulnerable ecosystems.

This Research Topic aims to bring together contributions that advance criminological and forensic neuropsychology from a clearly defined, clinically grounded perspective. The Topic is organized around a forensic neuropsychological through-line, focusing on the assessment and interpretation of cognitive functioning in legally relevant contexts and on translating neuropsychological findings from clinical evaluation to court-related settings.

title: Decoding motor behavior: The impact of cognitive load and neuromuscular adaptations in rehabilitation and sport
summary: Motor behavior emerges from a continuous dialogue between cognitive processes, neuromuscular systems, and the environmental constraints in which movement unfolds. Cognitive load arising from attention, working memory, decision-making, and mental effort directly modulates motor execution, while repeated exposure to task demands drives experience-dependent neuroplasticity, structural compensation, and neuroprotection across central and peripheral pathways. Mechanosensitive and proprioceptive feedback, fatigue accumulation, and adaptation to novel mobility constraints further shape how the nervous system organizes movement in athletes, patients, and individuals using assistive technologies. Despite this trend, research has historically emphasized middle-aged and older adults as care recipients, often overlooking their vital role as caregivers. title: Understanding Myofascial Pain as a Primary Driver of Lameness in Animals: Integrating Biomechanics, Neurophysiology, and Fascial Research
summary: Musculoskeletal pain and lameness represent major causes of performance loss and welfare concerns in horses and dogs. A growing body of evidence suggests that myofascial trigger points (MTrPs)—hyperirritable foci within muscle or fascia—play an underrecognized yet central role in chronic pain and locomotor asymmetries. Despite increasing interest in fascial science and neuromuscular function, the integration of biomechanical and neurophysiological evidence remains limited in veterinary research. Current understanding of the pathophysiology, diagnostic features, and treatment response of MTrPs in animals lags behind that of human medicine, where such pain syndromes are widely acknowledged. The need to close this gap is pressing, as undiagnosed or misinterpreted myofascial pain may contribute significantly to persistent lameness and suboptimal performance in equine and canine patients.

title: Understanding the Molecular Mechanisms Underlying Important Phenotypic Traits in Aquatic Animals
summary: Aquatic genomics has become a central field in understanding how genome organization and regulatory dynamics shape phenotypic diversity and important phenotypic traits across aquatic animals. Despite substantial advances in genomic resources for fish, crustaceans, and mollusks, much remains unknown about how higher-order genome structure and epigenetic mechanisms contribute to complex traits such as growth, stress resilience, reproduction, and disease resistance. Recent evidence suggests that not only nucleotide variations but also dynamic genome organization — such as chromatin conformation, histone modification, DNA methylation, and non-coding RNA networks — play critical roles in regulating key physiological processes. However, the extent and mechanisms through which these genomic and epigenomic dynamics influence important phenotypic traits remain largely unexplored. Recent developments indicate that neurorobotics is no longer defined solely by physical platforms or control architectures, but is increasingly shaped by multimodal learning, interaction modeling, decision-making, and computational frameworks that generalize across tasks and environments. Research highlights growing interest in multimodal fusion, human–robot interaction, learning-based autonomy, and large-scale model integration, underscoring that data representation and model adaptability are now central scientific concerns. title: Alzheimer's disease-associated genes expression: A new direction in the ischemic etiology and therapy of Alzheimer's disease
summary: Increasing evidence supports a link between brain ischemia and the development of Alzheimer’s disease (AD). Experimental and clinical studies have shown that ischemic episodes trigger the overexpression of genes associated with AD pathology, including amyloid precursor protein (APP), β-secretase (BACE1), presenilin 1 and 2, and tau protein. These changes promote beta-amyloid peptide accumulation, neurofibrillary tangle formation, and progressive neurodegeneration in patterns that closely mirror the hallmarks of AD. Despite growing recognition that ischemia-reperfusion injury may represent a critical upstream trigger for AD-type pathology, the molecular cascades linking ischemic gene dysregulation to sustained neurodegeneration remain incompletely understood. This gap limits the development of targeted therapies that could intervene at the vascular and ischemic level to slow or prevent the onset of AD.

title: Epidemiology, Diagnosis, and Treatment of Toxoplasma gondii Infection in a One Health Context
summary: Toxoplasma gondii is a globally distributed protozoan that infects nearly all warm-blooded hosts, including humans. Understanding its epidemiology and phylogeny is essential for infection management and outbreak reduction. Recent advances in molecular biology have revealed the parasite's genotype diversity and virulence factors. The One Health approach highlights the interactions between the parasite, host, and environment, offering insights to enhance animal health and mitigate economic losses in agriculture. Significantly, T. gondii poses veterinary concerns, causing reproductive disorders in livestock, which leads to economic losses and potential zoonotic transmission through contaminated meat. Its environmental resilience, supported by robust oocyst production, underscores the importance of effective environmental management in controlling its spread.
image_alt: Epidemiology, Diagnosis, and Treatment of Toxoplasma gondii Infection in a One Health Context

The evolution of imaging technologies has long been central to driving early diagnosis, refining disease classification, and enabling rigorous monitoring of progression or response to therapy. Despite these advances, current imaging techniques often grapple with limitations in sensitivity, contrast, specificity, and the capacity to distinguish Alzheimer’s pathology from other neurodegenerative conditions. There is increasing interest in integrating innovative imaging agents, hybrid modalities, and nanotechnology-based approaches to overcome these challenges. title: Microglial Dynamics in Alzheimer's: Genetic Variants and Therapeutic Pathways
summary: Microglia are pivotal players in the neuroinflammatory landscape of Alzheimer’s disease (AD). Accumulating evidence underscores their complex role in modulating amyloid plaque dynamics, neuronal integrity, and synaptic function. Recent genome-wide association and sequencing studies have revealed that the majority of AD risk loci are highly expressed in microglia. Variants in a broad network of microglial genes—including TREM2, ABI3, PLCG2, INPP5D, CD33, SPI1 and the MS4A cluster—can fundamentally alter microglial behavior and reactivity. While activated microglia may drive beneficial amyloid clearance and neuroprotective signaling, they can also contribute to pathological synaptic pruning and chronic neuroinflammation, creating a spectrum of responses that complicates our understanding of their exact role in AD pathogenesis. summary: Research in neuroinflammation has increasingly highlighted the role of non-neuronal cells, such as microglia, astrocytes, oligodendrocytes, endothelial cells, and infiltrating immune cells, in shaping neural environments during aging and neurodegenerative diseases. Among the diverse mechanisms underlying glial and peripheral immune cell activity, recently characterized forms of regulated cell death, pyroptosis and ferroptosis, have attracted significant attention. Pyroptosis, a pro-inflammatory, gasdermin-mediated process, and ferroptosis, driven by iron-dependent lipid peroxidation, both induce cellular demise accompanied by the release of DAMPs and pro-inflammatory factors. Emerging evidence suggests that these distinct cell death pathways in non-neuronal populations can profoundly influence the initiation and propagation of neuroinflammatory cascades, which in turn impact synaptic function, neuronal survival, and cognitive resilience. summary: The intersection of informatics and mental health represents a burgeoning field poised to significantly transform the landscape of psychological disorder diagnosis and treatment. Advanced machine learning (ML) and deep learning (DL) techniques enable researchers to decipher intricate patterns and derive profound insights from vast, complex datasets. Such pioneering approaches promise to enhance the precision of diagnoses, facilitate personalized treatment plans, and markedly improve patient outcomes. This convergence is dismantling traditional barriers between data science, clinical psychology, and neuroscience, fostering the emergence of novel strategies that hold the potential to revolutionize mental health care. Despite these advances, gaps persist in fully integrating these technologies in routine clinical settings, and questions around ethical implications and data privacy demand attention.

title: Addressing the Transposition Challenge in Virtual Reality: Adaptive Scaffolding for Self-Regulation, Cognitive Load, and Emotions in Education
summary: The integration of immersive virtual reality (IVR) in educational contexts marks a substantial shift in learning environments, offering high sensory fidelity and interactive potential. However, as students transition from traditional physical classrooms to virtual settings, they frequently encounter the “Transposition Challenge,” losing access to familiar self-regulatory supports such as notes, clocks, and peer cues. This regulatory void, or “regulatory nakedness,” can elevate extraneous cognitive load and disrupt emotional equilibrium, hindering both engagement and learning outcomes. Recent work—guided by models such as the Cognitive Affective Model of Immersive Learning (CAMIL) and the Cognitive-Affective Theory of Learning with Media for VR (CATLM-VR)—underscores the need for a nuanced understanding of how immersion, embodiment, and interactivity modulate core learning variables including presence, interest, cognitive load, and motivation.

title: Artificial Intelligence for Medical Robotics: From Design Acceleration to Intelligent Perception and Control
summary: Artificial intelligence (AI) is rapidly transforming the field of medical robotics, extending its impact beyond traditional perception and control to earlier stages such as system design and modeling. Emerging approaches leverage machine learning to accelerate computationally intensive processes, including finite element analysis (FEA) for soft and continuum surgical robots and computational fluid dynamics (CFD) for medical devices such as blood pumps. In parallel, data-driven methods provide effective alternatives to analytical modeling for complex robotic systems with challenging kinematic and dynamic structures. These advances complement ongoing developments in AI-enabled perception, planning, and intraoperative decision-making. Together, they create new opportunities for improving the efficiency, intelligence, and clinical applicability of medical robotic systems, while also introducing challenges in reliability, interpretability, and integration.

By bridging microbiology, bioinformatics, and biomedicine, AI is creating new opportunities not only for understanding microbial communities, functions, and host–microbe interactions, but also for improving disease characterization, diagnosis, prognosis, and translational research.

Despite extensive research on immunosenescence, the molecular and systemic mechanisms governing CD8⁺ T cell function during healthy aging remain poorly defined. This Research Topic aims to gather high-quality contributions that elucidate how endogenous and environmental factors shape CD8⁺ T cell biology across the lifespan, with particular emphasis on maintaining immune resilience and neuro-immune homeostasis in aging.

title: Cognition, Exploration, and Collaboration of Multi-Agent Systems in Dynamic Open Environments
summary: The cognitive, exploratory, and collaborative capabilities of multi-agent systems are advancing rapidly, driven by the development of large models and the progress of embodied intelligence. These advances enable robots to be rapidly deployed in real-world applications such as healthcare, transportation, logistics, and rescue missions. Along this rapid development, multi-agent systems are expected to achieve multi-modal fusion representation at the cognitive level, enable proactive exploration at the learning level, and enhance task allocation, resource sharing, and collaborative coordination at the team level.

title: Computational modelling and AI for brain and behaviour: integrating prediction with inference
summary: Computational modelling, machine learning, and broader artificial (AI) intelligence approaches are now key approaches used to understanding and predicting cognitive function and behaviour. Although these approaches are closely related, they make distinct contributions. Computational modelling models provide theory driven accounts of cognitive and neural mechanisms. They do that by formalising hypotheses and testing them through algorithms development based on the findings and simulations. In contrast, machine learning and AI methods are successful in discovering structure in complicated and high dimensional data, enabling robust prediction, and supporting analysis across modalities. Together these tools can connect levels of explanation, strengthen inference, and improve reproducibility. Historically computational modelling has been used in computational neuroscience to explain brain processes and behaviour, including neural network and biologically inspired models. Despite these advances, a comprehensive understanding of the complex neural mechanisms underlying these disorders and their clinical progression remains elusive. Recent research highlights the value of AI approaches, including machine learning, deep learning, and generative models, in extracting meaningful patterns from multimodal neuroimaging and genomic data. Dynamics of neural oscillations: Theoretical and computational models of rhythmic brain activity
summary: Neural oscillations are a fundamental feature of brain activity, emerging from the synchronized rhythmic firing of neuronal populations across various frequency bands. From the slow oscillations of deep sleep to the high-frequency gamma rhythms associated with perception and cognition, these temporal patterns are critical for coordinating information transfer across spatially distributed brain regions. Advances in electrophysiology and neuroimaging have provided a wealth of data regarding these rhythms; however, the underlying biophysical mechanisms and their functional roles remain subjects of intense debate. Computational modeling serves as a vital bridge in this field, allowing researchers to simulate the complex interactions between excitatory and inhibitory populations that give rise to these dynamics. Understanding these rhythms is not only essential for basic neuroscience but also for identifying the "oscillopathies" associated with neurological and psychiatric disorders.

title: Ecological Restoration and Vegetation Feedback Mechanisms in Desertification Land: Bridging Conservation Ecology and Desertification Control
summary: Land desertification is a critical global challenge under climate change and intensified land use. In response, conservation and restoration ecology provide the theoretical and practical frameworks necessary to reverse degradation processes and enhance the resilience of dryland ecosystems. However, the long-term success of desertification control initiatives depends not only on the technical effectiveness of vegetation restoration measures but also on a mechanistic understanding of the interactions between vegetation and the desert environment - including soil-water-plant feedbacks, nutrient cycling, microclimate regulation, and biodiversity -ecosystem functioning relationships.

title: Epidemiology of Multiple sclerosis and related disorders
summary: Multiple sclerosis (MS) is a leading cause of non-traumatic neurologic disability in young adults worldwide. Marked variation in incidence and prevalence across geographic regions, ancestry groups, and sexes supports a multifactorial etiology in which genetic susceptibility interacts with environmental exposures. Recent syntheses suggest MS incidence and prevalence have increased over time, often driven by higher rates among women, yet these trends are not uniformly observed and are incompletely characterized in several regions, including the Middle East and North Africa (MENA), where newer data suggest a rapidly rising burden.

title: Expanding the Digital Sensorium: Alternative Visions for Human-Computer Interaction
summary: Digital communication and interaction research within Human-Computer Interaction (HCI) has increasingly focused on achieving high-fidelity re-presentations of complex human sensory and communicative experiences. This preoccupation has driven technical innovation across areas such as haptics, multisensory robotics, immersive realities, digital twins, and artificial intelligence. However, this dominant paradigm has also led to substantial conceptual and practical limitations. By reproducing a narrow, technically defined view of the human senses, this approach constrains the diversity of digital sensory experiences and reinforces a monocultural model of interaction that privileges certain bodies, identities, and ways of being. title: Fostering Health Literacy Through User-Centered Accessible Solutions
summary: Digital health solutions are transforming healthcare delivery, yet their effectiveness hinges on the ability of diverse populations to understand and use them effectively. Health literacy plays a crucial role in ensuring these technologies enhance, rather than hinder, user engagement, especially among individuals with limited health knowledge or technical skills. While digital health tools hold promise for improving health outcomes and promoting equitable care, challenges remain in designing accessible solutions that cater to varied literacy levels.

title: Future of Theoretical and Philosophical Psychology
summary: Psychological science is at a crossroads. The last two decades has brought a range of fundamental issues into focus, including the replication crisis highlighted by large-scale community efforts such as the Open Science Collaboration, problems with representativeness and diversity emphasized by researchers such as Apicella, Norenzayan, and Henrich, and concerns regarding the very nature of the construction of theories raised by Oberauer and Lewandowsky; and van Rooij and Baggio, and more recent contributions by van Dongen and colleagues. At the same time, long-standing questions about explanation, evidence, and mind-world relations are now intersecting with rapid developments in cognitive science, neuroscience, and artificial intelligence. These converging trends highlight both the urgency and the opportunity for rigorous theoretical and philosophical work that can clarify, critique, and guide the future of psychology.

title: How Does the Environment Modulate Feeding and Metabolism in Fish? Special Emphasis on the Impacts of Climate Change
summary: Feeding and metabolism in fish are vital physiological processes regulated by interactions between internal endocrine signals and external environmental cues. Fish are highly sensitive to environmental parameters such as temperature, oxygen availability, salinity, photoperiod, pollution, and food quality. These variables influence feeding behavior, nutrient assimilation, and energy allocation. The regulation of these functions involves an endocrine network that integrates signals from the brain, gut, liver, and adipose tissue. Hormones such as neuropeptide Y (NPY), agouti-related peptide (AgRP), CART, orexin, leptin, ghrelin, insulin, thyroid hormones, melanocortins, and insulin-like growth factors (IGFs) play central roles in modulating appetite and metabolism.

summary: Literacy acquisition and related disorders stand at the intersection of neuroscience, psychology, and education, forming a convergent field that investigates how brain systems support the development of literacy skills. Recent research has greatly advanced our understanding of the neural and cognitive substrates underlying reading, highlighting the complex interplay between speech perception, phonological processing, orthographic knowledge, and language comprehension. Yet, significant questions remain regarding how these processes coalesce to foster successful reading development and precisely how disruptions in these systems lead to disorders such as dyslexia. Notably, gaps persist in mapping the developmental trajectories of brain networks for reading, elucidating cross-linguistic differences, and translating mechanistic insights into practical frameworks for intervention and education.

Hypersaline habitats are characterized by salinities exceeding those of seawater, intense evaporation, and ionic imbalances, diminishing species richness but promoting specialized adaptations: osmotic regulation and metabolic plasticity. Hydrothermal vents occur along tectonically active seafloor regions where superheated, mineral-rich fluids fuel dense biological communities supported by chemosynthetic microorganisms rather than photosynthesis.

When bacteria develop mechanisms to survive antibiotic exposure, diseases once considered easily treatable - such as pneumonia, urinary tract infections, and tuberculosis - become increasingly difficult to manage, leading to prolonged illness, higher costs, and greater mortality. The overuse and misuse of antibiotics in medicine and agriculture, combined with inadequate infection control and limited public awareness, have accelerated the emergence and spread of resistant strains.

Minds, machines, and moral boundaries: Ethical challenges in computational neuroscience and neurotechnology
summary: Rapid advances in computational neuroscience and neurotechnology are fundamentally reshaping our ability to decode, model, and modify the human brain. Brain-computer interfaces, neural decoding algorithms, large-scale neural simulations, and AI-driven psychiatric tools now operate at a level of sophistication that raises profound ethical, legal, and societal questions. Neural data represent among the most intimate forms of personal information, capturing cognitive states, emotions, intentions, and identity in ways that conventional biomedical data cannot. Simultaneously, the proliferation of consumer neurotechnologies, AI-assisted diagnostics, and cognitive enhancement tools has outpaced regulatory and ethical frameworks designed to govern their use. As these technologies move from laboratory to clinic and everyday life, establishing robust ethical principles grounded in empirical neuroscientific understanding has become both urgent and necessary.
