title: Music and the Brain: From Neural Mechanisms to Clinical Applications
summary: The field of music neuroscience explores how music engages complex brain networks, making it a uniquely powerful tool for investigating neural processes that underpin perception, action, emotion, prediction, and reward. Recent advances in neuroscience demonstrate that music activates widespread brain systems, from the auditory cortex to motor and reward networks, enabling the study of core principles such as neural entrainment, oscillatory timing, and predictive processing. Large-scale, multimodal studies have begun to illuminate how music can serve as both a model for basic brain function and as a pathway for understanding neurological and psychiatric disorders. Yet, critical gaps persist in linking circuit-level findings to clinically meaningful outcomes, elucidating moderators across development, and leveraging music as a precision tool for diagnosis and intervention.

summary: G protein-coupled receptors (GPCRs) represent the targets of more than 30% of the drugs currently on the market. Much effort has been invested to better understand the molecular and cellular mechanisms underlying both types of effects in hope to design highly efficacious drugs with reduced or absent side effects. The current most prevalent hypothesis postulates that preferential activation of a given signalling pathway may help reaching this goal. Accordingly, new drugs have been designed and developed in hope to fulfil this criterion. A handful reached the clinics, but the endeavour often proved more complex than anticipated.

summary: Human-Computer Interaction (HCI) education is changing in response to new technologies and shifting social expectations. As digital systems become part of everyday life, the need for well-trained HCI professionals continues to grow. At the same time, HCI curricula, teaching methods, and assessment practices vary widely across institutions and countries. This makes it difficult to compare outcomes, share good practice, and ensure that learners develop core knowledge and skills. Research also points to a shortage of well-tested, reusable rubrics and assessment tools, particularly for areas such as ethics, accessibility, responsible design, and cultural awareness. In addition, the use of real-world projects and cross-disciplinary perspectives in HCI education remains uneven. There is still a need for teaching approaches that connect core HCI theory with practical application. title: Novel Pharmaceutical Strategies for Targeting Brain Metastases
summary: Brain metastases (BM) are a frequent and feared complication of many solid tumors. Their increasing incidence makes them a major therapeutic challenge. BM are associated with poor prognosis, substantial morbidity, and a significant deterioration in quality of life, highlighting the urgent need for more effective and innovative treatment strategies. The management of brain metastases remains particularly complex due to the limited access of therapeutic agents to the central nervous system, primarily because of the blood-brain barrier (BBB). This physiological barrier restricts the passage of many molecules, thereby compromising their efficacy within the brain compartment. Moreover, the heterogeneity of brain metastases across different tumor types further complicates treatment decisions, requiring highly individualized approaches. title: Phylogeny and Adaptive Evolution of Mollusks: Responses, Mechanisms, and Taxonomic Implications Under Environmental Changes
summary: Mollusks, as one of the most diverse and ecologically pivotal invertebrate groups, have evolved remarkable adaptive strategies to cope with environmental fluctuations and ecological challenges. Their phylogeny and adaptive evolution span multiple dimensions, including morphological innovation, physiological plasticity, biochemical regulation, and molecular divergence. Recent shifts in global climate, habitat degradation, biological invasions, and human-driven selection have intensified selective pressures on mollusks, reshaping their diversity and evolutionary trajectories. Meanwhile, advances in morphological taxonomy and molecular techniques have provided new insights into molluscan classification revisions and phylogenetic inferences at both higher and lower taxonomic levels. title: Physiological and Behavioral Functions of Oxytocin
summary: Oxytocin research stands at the intersection of neurobiology, endocrinology, and behavioral science. Traditionally recognized for its roles in childbirth and lactation, oxytocin has recently garnered attention for its complex influence on a variety of physiological processes and behavioral patterns. Emerging evidence highlights oxytocin as a critical modulator not only in pair-bonding and parent-child attachment but also in promoting animal-human and broader social bonding. Despite this progress, the full spectrum of oxytocin's effects and mechanisms remains a subject of dynamic investigation, with ongoing debates over its implications in human well-being and the biological bases of social relationships.

As our global environment undergoes significant shifts, including heightened temperatures, increased salinity, and altered precipitation patterns, plants are forced to contend with multiple, simultaneous stressors. Microbial communities associated with plants have been shown to support physiological adaptation, disease resistance, and holistic plant health. However, recent evidence reveals that while molecular and ecological research have both advanced rapidly, integration between detailed genetic or biochemical insights and larger-scale ecological or ecosystem outcomes remains limited. This lack of connectivity inhibits the development of comprehensive predictive frameworks and practical solutions essential for sustainable crop production and ecological stability. title: Polymorphic Strain Variation in Misfolded Proteins and Their Consequences in Neurodegenerative Diseases
summary: A defining feature of most age-related neurodegenerative diseases is the misfolding, aggregation, and prion-like propagation of specific proteins, including amyloid-β, tau, α-synuclein, TDP-43, and the prion protein. A growing body of evidence demonstrates that these proteins do not adopt a single pathological conformation; rather, they exist as distinct structural variants, or strains, with unique biochemical properties, seeding capacities, cellular tropisms, and patterns of spread. This polymorphic strain variation helps explain the striking clinical and neuropathological heterogeneity observed within disorders such as Alzheimer’s disease, Parkinson’s disease, frontotemporal dementia, and prion diseases, where different patients can present with markedly different progression rates, brain region involvement, and symptom profiles. title: Post-partum disorders in ruminants: Incidence analysis, risk assessment, and intervention strategies
summary: The critical post-partum period in ruminants significantly influences animal productivity and farm profitability, yet it remains fraught with numerous pathological conditions that adversely affect animal welfare and economic outcomes. Among the most concerning post-partum pathologies are metritis, retained placenta, uterine prolapse, mastitis, and hypocalcemia. These disorders often result from a complex interplay of physiological, environmental, managemental, and nutritional factors. Despite advancements in veterinary care and herd management practices, these pathologies continue to pose a major concern worldwide. Understanding the current incidence of these conditions, identifying predisposing factors, and evaluating existing preventive measures are essential steps in mitigating their impact and improving overall herd health and productivity.

title: The interplay between attention and language
summary: The capacities of awareness, selection, and sustained attention are critical for human communication, from an adult perceiving speech sounds and comprehending complex discourse, to an infant babbling surrounding speech sounds and associating new words with their meanings. When the brain is functioning atypically, due to developmental differences or an injury, the demands of linguistic processing can heavily tax attentional resources. A growing body of research highlights that deficits in one domain frequently co-occur with, and profoundly influence, impairments in the other. Understanding this dynamic interplay is important for advancing our theoretical models of typical human speech and language, and for developing more effective diagnostic and therapeutic strategies for a wide range of developmental and acquired speech and language disorders.

Transforming Genitourinary Surgery Through Advanced Robotic Systems
summary: The field of genitourinary (GU) surgery has undergone a transformative shift with the integration of robotic technology, which now serves as a cornerstone for minimally invasive procedures. Over recent decades, advancements have evolved from pioneering platforms like PUMA 560 and Probot to current industry standards, exemplified by the da Vinci system. Robotic approaches have been lauded for improved dexterity, enhanced visualization, and better ergonomics for surgeons, leading to increasing adoption. Despite their technical promise, clinical debates remain around appropriate patient selection, comparative benefits over other minimally invasive modalities, and the economic implications of broader deployment. Although early evidence points to advantages such as reduced blood loss and faster recovery, critical gaps persist, including inconsistent outcome definitions, limited long-term data, and a lack of standardized benchmarks for both clinical and technical success.

title: Vegetation Ecology and Conservation of Undervalued or Threatened Habitats in South-eastern Europe
summary: South-Eastern Europe is one of the continent’s most biodiverse regions - a mosaic of plant communities shaped by complex topography, climatic gradients, and centuries of land use. Yet many of its ecologically significant habitats remain poorly studied and underrepresented in conservation planning. Alpine fens, serpentine outcrops, thermophilic oak forests, and alluvial meadows are often fragmented, inadequately mapped, and increasingly exposed to climate change, land degradation, and development pressure.

title: Cerebral amyloid angiopathy, new insights into an evolving dynamic small vessel disease
summary: Cerebral amyloid angiopathy (CAA) is a critical vascular disorder in aging, recognized as a major cause of lobar intracerebral hemorrhage and a significant driver of cognitive and motor dysfunction in the elderly. Despite growing awareness, the diagnosis and management of CAA remain complex due to its dynamic interplay with Alzheimer’s disease and other vascular brain pathologies. Contemporary research highlights the heterogeneous clinical and imaging presentations of CAA, as well as emerging complexities related to amyloid-targeting therapies. Advances in neuroimaging, fluid biomarkers, and computational analysis have improved our ability to delineate CAA subtypes, track progression, and detect treatment-related changes like amyloid-related imaging abnormalities (ARIA). However, fundamental questions persist regarding the biological underpinnings of disease heterogeneity, reliable risk assessment, personalized care strategies, and optimal clinical trial design. title: Understanding aging and neurodevelopmental change in autistic adults: Language and cognition at the crossroads
summary: The study of aging in adults with autism, particularly in relation to language and cognitive challenges, represents a rapidly evolving field within neurodevelopmental and gerontological research. While much effort has been devoted to understanding autism spectrum disorder (ASD) in childhood, there is a notable lack of comprehensive research that tracks the experiences of autistic individuals as they age. Key questions remain about how typical aging processes interact with lifelong neurodevelopmental conditions, including issues such as the trajectory of language skills, changes in cognitive abilities, and the impact of co-occurring medical conditions. Recent studies suggest that autistic adults might experience aging differently than neurotypical peers, with possible variations in cognitive decline, language processing, and social communication. title: Wildlife as Sentinels and Vectors of Antimicrobial Resistance in a Changing Environment
summary: Antimicrobial Resistance (AMR) is universally recognized as one of the most pressing global health threats of the 21st century. While extensive research has historically focused on clinical settings, veterinary medicine, and livestock agriculture, the role of wildlife within the complex epidemiology of AMR remains a critical knowledge gap. Under the "One Health" framework, it is increasingly evident that wildlife populations are neither isolated nor immune to the anthropogenic spread of resistant determinants.
image_alt: Wildlife as Sentinels and Vectors of Antimicrobial Resistance in a Changing Environment

title: Advances in Sheep and Goat Reproduction Based on Omics Technologies
summary: The improvement of reproductive capacity is one of the most critical factors affecting economic benefits in the sheep and goat industry. Reproduction is a complex trait affected by many factors, and its mechanism still needs further elucidation. In recent years, with the development of multi omics technologies, such as genomics, transcriptomics, proteomics, and metabolomics, it has become possible to discover many new molecular biomarkers related to the ovulation mechanisms and disorders of reproduction in sheep and goats.
image_alt: Advances in Sheep and Goat Reproduction Based on Omics Technologies

title: Microbiome and Neuropsychiatric Health: Precision and Predictive Translational Strategies in the Gut-Brain Axis
summary: Over the past decade, the gut microbiome has emerged as a key modulator of brain function, shaping emotion regulation, cognition, stress physiology, and neuroinflammatory pathways. Altered microbiome-host interactions are linked to psychiatric and neurological conditions including depression, anxiety disorders, bipolar disorder, schizophrenia, neurodevelopmental conditions, and stress-related syndromes. Despite rapid scientific progress, major challenges remain in clarifying causal mechanisms and successfully translating these discoveries into clinically actionable diagnostics, biomarkers, and therapeutic strategies.

title: Vagus Nerve Stimulation: A Bioelectronic Approach to Regulate Autonomic Dysfunction and Inflammatory Diseases
summary: Vagus nerve stimulation (VNS) is a bioelectronic neuromodulation technique that leverages the vagus nerve’s extensive bidirectional connections between the central nervous system and peripheral organs. As the tenth cranial nerve, the vagus plays a critical role in regulating autonomic processes such as heart rate, gastrointestinal motility, respiration, and immune responses. Its unique neuroanatomical distribution enables targeted modulation of both visceral functions and brain activity, providing a foundation for therapeutic interventions in a range of conditions. VNS has FDA approval for drug-refractory epilepsy, treatment-resistant depression, and certain headache disorders, with ongoing research exploring its utility in autonomic dysfunction, inflammatory diseases, metabolic disorders, and neuroprotection.

title: AI-Assisted Drug Discovery, Target Identification, and Precision Therapy for Neurological Disorders and Neuro-Oncology
summary: Neurological disorders and neuro oncology impose a growing clinical and societal burden, while therapeutic development remains slow, costly, and uncertain. Major challenges include disease heterogeneity, limited human relevant models, blood brain barrier constraints, insufficient biomarkers, treatment resistance, and poor translation from computational or preclinical findings into clinical benefit. Recent advances in artificial intelligence, molecular representation learning, multimodal omics, single cell sequencing, spatial transcriptomics, medical imaging, and clinical data integration provide new opportunities to improve drug discovery and precision therapeutics. However, many current approaches still lack interpretability, robustness, biological validation, and clinical applicability. title: Automated and AI-driven analysis techniques in PET brain imaging
summary: Positron emission tomography (PET) brain imaging is a pivotal tool in neuroscience, enabling precise visualization and quantification of physiological processes in the human brain. However, traditional analysis of PET brain images relies heavily on manual workflows and expert interpretation, which can be both time-consuming and susceptible to inter- and intra-observer variability. The need for more robust, reproducible, and efficient analysis techniques has prompted considerable interest in automation and artificial intelligence (AI)-driven approaches. Recent advancements in machine learning, particularly deep learning, have demonstrated the potential to automate complex image processing tasks, improve diagnostic accuracy, and extract clinically relevant biomarkers from PET data. Despite these breakthroughs, integrating AI into clinical practice faces considerable hurdles, including the need for large annotated datasets, generalizability across diverse populations, and transparency in
image_alt: Automated and AI-driven analysis techniques in PET brain imaging

title: Bioactive phytochemicals with neuroimmunopharmacological properties
summary: Plants constitute a vast and still incompletely characterized reservoir of biologically active compounds. Among them are highly potent therapeutic agents such as paclitaxel, employed in oncology, and morphine, a cornerstone of severe pain management. Moreover, numerous plant-derived products contain complex phytochemical compositions that contribute to the maintenance of physiological homeostasis and may play a preventive role in the early stages of disease development. Accordingly, plant-derived substances – including crude extracts, enriched fractions, or isolated compounds – may be considered as valuable candidates for the development of therapeutics, dietary supplements, or functional food components. In any case, these substances exert measurable biological effects by modulating physiological functioning and molecular pathways.

title: Upper-Limb Sensorimotor Function as a Marker of Cognitive Aging
summary: The field of aging neuroscience has increasingly recognized the complex interplay between motor function, tactile sensory function, and cognitive processes across the human lifespan. With global populations aging rapidly, there is heightened interest in finding sensitive and accessible markers that can indicate early cognitive decline or differentiate typical versus pathological aging. Recent studies have revealed that upper-limb sensorimotor abilities—such as hand dexterity, fine motor control, tactile sensation/perception, and coordination—show strong associations with executive functions, memory, as well as global cognitive health in older adults. Longitudinal and intervention research suggests that changes in upper-limb sensorimotor performance may precede, predict, or co-occur with declines in cognitive domains, making these functions a promising, underutilized window into neurocognitive aging. AI for Computational Neuroscience: Methods, Applications, and Trustworthiness
summary: Signal analysis and processing constitute a foundational pillar of computational neuroscience, underpinning a wide range of tasks such as neural decoding, brain–computer interface (BCI) design, cognitive state estimation, and neurological disorder diagnosis. With the rapid advancement of neural recording technologies (e.g., EEG, fMRI, calcium imaging), the volume, dimensionality, and complexity of neural data have increased dramatically, posing significant challenges to traditional analytical methods.

title: Beyond Traditional Risk Factors: Unraveling Residual Vascular Risk After TIA and Minor Stroke
summary: Transient ischemic attack (TIA) and minor ischemic stroke are critical warning events that precede disabling strokes and major cardiovascular complications. While traditional risk factors (TRFs) — hypertension, diabetes, hypercholesterolemia, smoking, and atrial fibrillation — are well-established drivers of cerebrovascular disease, a growing body of evidence indicates that a substantial proportion of patients presenting with TIA or minor stroke carry none of these conventional risks. Strikingly, recent data from large international cohorts such as TIAregistry.org demonstrate that recurrent stroke rates in this population are comparable to those seen in patients with TRFs, particularly within the first year after the index event. This observation points to the existence of poorly understood, non-traditional mechanisms that contribute to residual vascular risk and recurrent cerebrovascular events.

title: Brain-inspired learning and adaptation in large models
summary: Recent advances in large-scale AI models, including large language and vision-language-action models, have significantly expanded the capabilities of artificial systems in perception, reasoning, and decision-making. However, these models remain limited in their ability adapt continuously, learn from limited data, and operate reliably in dynamic, real-world environments. In contrast, biological systems exhibit remarkable adaptability through mechanisms such as neural plasticity, efficient coding, and modular organization. This Research Topic focuses on the intersection of neuroscience principles and large-scale AI, exploring how brain-inspired mechanisms can address these limitations and support the development of more flexible and resilient intelligent systems.

title: Feline Mammary Neoplasia - From Disease Mechanisms to Clinical Management
summary: Feline mammary tumors (FMTs) represent a significant and evolving field within veterinary oncology. Although FMTs constitute one of the most common types of neoplasia in cats, the majority are malignant at the time of diagnosis, contributing to high morbidity and mortality. Despite historical progress in pathology, surgery, and clinical management, persistent challenges remain regarding early detection, optimization of therapeutic strategies, and robust prognostication. Recent studies have highlighted the translational relevance of FMTs due to similarities with aggressive subtypes of human breast cancer, supporting increased interest in comparative oncology. However, limited access to specialized care, incomplete integration of novel diagnostics, and a lack of consensus on standardized protocols continue to impede advances in outcomes and clinical decision-making.

title: Intracellular Dynamics as a Computational Substrate in Neural and Neuromorphic Systems
summary: Biological neurons perform extensive computation not only through spikes and synaptic interactions but also through rich internal dynamics unfolding across multiple spatial and temporal scales. Processes such as subthreshold integration, dendritic and compartmental computation, adaptation, and state retention shape how inputs are filtered, transformed, and transmitted. These within-neuron mechanisms form a computational substrate that works alongside spike-mediated communication to support learning, memory, and robust information processing. In neuromorphic computing, analog and hybrid circuits can emulate similar subthreshold and internal-state behaviors, potentially extending beyond purely spike-based abstractions toward more efficient and context-sensitive computation. Recognizing intracellular and internal-state dynamics as active computational elements opens new possibilities for designing neuromorphic systems that better mirror biological efficiency and flexibility.

title: Molecular Dysregulation of Neural Stem Cell Fate Decisions in Neurodegenerative and Neoplastic Brain Disorders
summary: Neural stem cells (NSCs) sustain cellular plasticity in the developing and adult brain through tightly coordinated molecular programs that regulate quiescence, activation, and lineage commitment. Disruption of these programs is increasingly recognized as a central feature of neurological disorders, including neurodegenerative diseases and brain tumors, yet the molecular logic by which disease states reshape NSC fate decisions remains incompletely understood. Neurodegenerative conditions, including Alzheimer’s and Parkinson’s disease, as well as neoplastic disorders such as glioblastoma, represent key disease contexts in which aberrant NSC regulation has been implicated, making them important frameworks for understanding how molecular programs break down in the diseased brain.
image_alt: Molecular Dysregulation of Neural Stem Cell Fate Decisions in Neurodegenerative and Neoplastic Brain Disorders

Diagnosis relies on a combination of advanced imaging, surgical biopsy, and histopathology, which remain essential for confirming tumor type, grade, and margins. These are complemented by immunohistochemistry, molecular profiling, and liquid biopsy to identify specific mutations and biomarkers. Such detailed characterization guides targeted therapies, like tyrosine kinase inhibitors, and supports the growing use of immunotherapy, which harnesses the animal’s immune system to recognize and combat cancer cells. Depending on the tumor, surgery represent an important step for the treatment and management of oncologic patients. title: AI in Human Neuroscience, Ethically Done: Neuroethical Risks, Safeguards, and Governance
summary: Artificial intelligence is revolutionizing human neuroscience, enabling unprecedented advances in brain imaging analysis, neural decoding, predictive modeling, and personalized neurological interventions. However, the rapid integration of AI into neuroscience research and clinical applications raises critical ethical concerns that remain inadequately addressed. These include privacy vulnerabilities with neural data, algorithmic bias in brain-based diagnostic tools, issues of informed consent in AI-driven neuroscience studies, and the potential misuse of neural information for non-medical purposes. As AI systems become increasingly sophisticated and widely deployed, there is an urgent need for comprehensive frameworks that balance scientific innovation with robust ethical safeguards. This Research Topic brings together neuroscientists, ethicists, technologists, and policymakers to advance the responsible integration of AI in human neuroscience.

title: Advancing Critical Military Suicide Studies: Challenging Assumptions and Innovating Prevention
summary: Suicide among military servicemembers and veterans is a profound and persistent public health challenge, manifesting across national and cultural contexts. Despite systematic surveillance, targeted research, and significant resource allocation over the past two decades, suicide rates within military and veteran populations have increased or remained elevated in many Western countries. Historically, efforts have concentrated on the identification of risk and protective factors, the development of clinical interventions, and the implementation of broad institutional prevention strategies. While substantial advancements have been made in clinical, policy, and programmatic domains, a deep-seated paradox persists: investments in conventional prevention strategies have not consistently produced meaningful reductions in suicide deaths or been sufficiently responsive to the unique needs of the military and veteran community, highlighting gaps in our theoretical and practical approaches.

title: Early detection of brain pathologies through deep learning and advanced neuroimaging approaches
summary: Recent advances in the field of medical imaging and computational neuroscience have transformed the landscape of brain pathology detection. The application of deep learning and artificial intelligence (AI) in the analysis of neuroimaging data has shown remarkable progress in identifying subtle biomarkers associated with early onset neurological and neurodegenerative disorders. Traditional diagnostic processes for conditions such as Alzheimer’s disease, Parkinson’s disease, brain tumors, and epilepsy are often time-consuming and reliant on clinical expertise, leading to delayed interventions. While significant studies have demonstrated the potential of AI to achieve high diagnostic accuracy, challenges remain in generalizability, interpretability, and integration of these models into clinical practice. The need for multidimensional frameworks combining diverse neuroimaging modalities such as MRI (sMRI and fMRI), CT, and DTI with robust machine learning (ML) pipelines underscores a major

title: Genomic and Evolutionary Perspectives on Invertebrate Responses to Environmental Change
summary: Invertebrate evolutionary and ecological research stands at the forefront of efforts to understand biological responses to rapid environmental change. As invertebrates form the bulk of global biodiversity and drive key ecosystem functions, elucidating their adaptation and resilience is critical amidst accelerating threats from climate change, habitat alteration, pollution, and other anthropogenic impacts. While significant research has addressed phenotypic and life-history variation, fundamental questions remain regarding the genetic and evolutionary processes facilitating adaptation in natural populations. Recent advances in evolutionary genomics and population genetics, including studies involving both model and non-model species, are starting to unravel the mechanisms of adaptation, population structure, gene flow, and genetic diversity in the context of dynamic and changing environments. Yet, there remain pronounced gaps in integrating genetic, ecological, and experimental approach

title: Growing Up Online: Social media, smartphones, and the adolescent brain, body, behavior loop
summary: Adolescence is a critical developmental period marked by profound changes in brain architecture, social cognition, and identity formation. Simultaneously, today's adolescents are the first generation to grow up immersed in social media and smartphone technology from early childhood. While digital platforms offer unprecedented opportunities for connection, learning, and self-expression, their rapid integration into adolescent life has raised significant concerns about potential neurobehavioral consequences. Emerging evidence suggests that social media use may impact dopaminergic reward pathways, sleep-wake cycles, attention regulation, and social-emotional development. Additionally, smartphones and digital content influence physical activity, body image, peer relationships, and mental health outcomes. title: Multimodal and Hybrid Brain-Computer Interfaces for Neurorehabilitation: From Signal Fusion to Clinical Translation
summary: Brain-computer interfaces (BCIs) hold significant promise for neurorehabilitation, yet most current systems rely on a single neuroimaging modality—typically electroencephalography (EEG)—which inherently limits the richness and reliability of the captured neural information. Multimodal and hybrid BCI approaches, which integrate complementary signals such as EEG, functional near-infrared spectroscopy (fNIRS), electromyography (EMG), magnetoencephalography (MEG), and electrooculography (EOG), offer a pathway to overcome these constraints by improving signal quality, decoding robustness, and the range of neural and physiological features available for clinical decision-making.

title: Neuroscience of learning: How the brain adapts and changes, Volume II
summary: The human brain is remarkably dynamic, constantly adapting to new experiences and environmental changes. This plasticity underlies our capacity to learn throughout the lifespan, shaping how we acquire knowledge and develop new skills. Recent advances in neuroscience have illuminated the cellular, molecular, and network-level changes that support learning, revealing a complex interplay between genetic, neurochemical, and experiential factors. Understanding these mechanisms provides crucial insights into cognitive development, educational strategies, and interventions for learning disorders, making the neuroscience of learning a vibrant and relevant field of research.

title: The Future of Brain Imaging: Techniques and Applications
summary: Brain imaging technologies have been instrumental in advancing our understanding of neural structure, function, and connectivity. Established techniques such as MRI, fMRI, PET, and EEG have provided invaluable insights into brain organization and dynamics in both health and disease. However, the field is rapidly evolving with the emergence of innovative imaging modalities and methodological refinements. Next-generation approaches—including ultra-high field imaging, multimodal integration, real-time imaging, functional ultrasound, and AI-enhanced analysis pipelines—promise unprecedented spatial and temporal resolution. These advances are expanding the frontiers of what we can measure and understand about the human brain, while simultaneously presenting new challenges in data interpretation, standardization, and clinical translation. This Research Topic explores the current state and future trajectory of brain imaging science.

title: The cholinergic anti-inflammatory pathway and neuro-immune regulation
summary: The immune system serves to protect the body from infection, to elicit a protective response to insult or injury, and to maintain homeostasis. A rapidly growing body of work suggests that the nervous and immune systems work synergistically and communicate reciprocally towards these ends. Similarly to the presence of both innate and adaptive immune cells that reside throughout the body, the sensory branch of the nervous system also innervates tissues and organs throughout the body, including the skin, gastrointestinal tract, heart, lungs, and the brain. Like the innate immune system, the sensory arm of the nervous system perceives and responds to environmental cues, as a constant surveillance for changes in the environment, monitoring damage, inflammation, and stressors. A hallmark of the sensory response to environmental alterations is pain, which can serve as the first indicator of infection or damage. title: The interplay between economic and biopsychosocial factors in brain health
summary: Financial well-being is a strong determinant of human. Individuals from lower socioeconomic backgrounds encounter a disproportionate amount of chronic stress, limited access to resources, and reduced opportunities for cognitive stimulation, all of which can profoundly influence brain development and functioning across the lifespan. At the same time, biological factors (e.g., genetic and biomarker-based risk factors), cognitive function and numerical abilities, and mental health variables like depression and anxiety, can influence an individual's ability to acquire and manage financial resources. There is likely a reciprocal relationship between financial well-being and the brain. Despite growing interest in this field, the bidirectional mechanisms linking economic factors to brain functioning, and health remain poorly understood.

title: Translational research of occupational therapy and psychiatric rehabilitation, Volume IV
summary: The field of occupational therapy (OT) has long recognized the importance of addressing mental health issues to improve overall well-being and functionality in individuals. Despite significant advancements, there remains a critical gap between basic scientific discoveries and their practical application in clinical settings. This gap underscores the need for translational research in the mental health domain of occupational therapy. Translational research serves as a bridge, facilitating the transfer of knowledge from fundamental research into real-world therapeutic interventions that can be effectively utilized by practitioners and benefit patients.

title: Updates on the Management of Glioblastoma Volume II
summary: Glioblastoma (GBM) remains the most common malignant primary brain tumor in adults and is associated with profound neurologic morbidity and a poor overall prognosis despite multimodal therapy. While maximal safe resection followed by radiotherapy and temozolomide remains the cornerstone of care, GBM’s intratumoral heterogeneity, adaptive resistance mechanisms, and the complex, dynamic tumor microenvironment continue to limit durable responses and complicate translation of promising preclinical findings into clinical benefit.
image_alt: Updates on the Management of Glioblastoma Volume II

title: Beyond the Average Brain: Person-Specific Mechanisms and Within-Person Prediction
summary: Traditional neuroscience research has relied on group-level analyses, identifying average patterns across populations. However, substantial heterogeneity exists in brain structure, function, connectivity, and neurobiology across individuals. This variability is not merely noise but reflects meaningful differences in genetics, development, experience, and biology that shape cognition and behavior. Person-specific (idiographic) approaches and within-person prediction models recognize that individuals follow unique neural trajectories and respond differently to interventions. Recent advances in computational modeling, machine learning, intensive longitudinal designs, and single-subject neuroimaging enable detailed characterization of individual brain patterns and their behavioral correlates. Precision neuroscience—tailored to the individual—promises more accurate prediction, more effective interventions, and deeper mechanistic understanding of brain-behavior relationships.

title: Developmental Signaling Pathways at the Intersection of Brain Aging and Neuro-Oncology: Biomarkers, Microenvironment, and Translational Implications
summary: Developmental signaling pathways, including Wnt, Notch, Hedgehog, PI3K/AKT/mTOR, TGF-β, and MAPK, serve as master regulators of neural specification, synaptic plasticity, and tissue homeostasis throughout life. Increasing evidence identifies these conserved molecular networks as a unifying biological framework linking neurodevelopment, brain aging, neurodegeneration, and neuro-oncology. Notably, many of the same signaling pathways that are hyperactivated in brain tumors to promote proliferation, invasion, and therapy resistance become dysregulated in Alzheimer’s, Parkinson’s, and Huntington’s diseases, often leading to opposing cellular outcomes: sustained growth and survival in cancer versus dysfunction, senescence, and cell death in neurodegeneration. title: Multisensory Integration in Aging: Implications for Cognitive, Motor, and Brain Health
summary: Multisensory integration (MSI) plays a critical role in perception, action, cognition, and emotion across the adult lifespan. While age-related changes in unisensory processing have been comprehensively documented, accumulating evidence suggests that changes in multisensory processing are not simply secondary consequences of sensory decline. We propose a special collection that aims to bring together diverse experimental, neuroimaging, and interventional approaches aimed at examining how MSI changes with aging, how such changes are related to cognitive and affective vulnerability, and how compensatory mechanisms may support functional performance in older adults.
image_alt: Multisensory Integration in Aging: Implications for Cognitive, Motor, and Brain Health

title: Neural control of locomotion in daily life: Gait variability, stability, and adaptability
summary: Locomotion is one of the most fundamental relevant motor behaviours in humans. Walking in daily life is rarely the steady, cyclical activity often examined in laboratory settings; rather, it requires continuous adjustments to varying terrains, environmental demands, cognitive loads, and concurrent tasks. The neural control of locomotion therefore involves a distributed network spanning spinal central pattern generators, brainstem locomotor regions, the cerebellum, the basal ganglia, and cortical areas, all of which interact dynamically with sensory feedback to produce gait patterns that are simultaneously stable, variable, and adaptable. Gait variability reflects the inherent fluctuations of step-to-step parameters, stability refers to the capacity to resist or recover from perturbations, and adaptability denotes the ability to flexibly modify gait in response to changing internal and external conditions. title: Neuroactive microbial metabolites and human brain function: mechanisms, biomarkers, and clinical implications
summary: In the rapidly evolving field of neurogastroenterology, mounting evidence highlights the profound influence of neuroactive microbial metabolites on human brain function. The gut-brain axis has become a focal point for understanding how metabolites produced by gut microbiota, reshaped by factors such as diet, medications, and stress, interact with the central nervous system. Recent studies have delineated pathways by which short-chain fatty acids, tryptophan metabolites, bile acids, and other molecules alter blood–brain barrier integrity, microglial activation, neurotransmitter systems, and neural connectivity. Despite promising insights, critical questions remain regarding the reproducibility of findings, individual susceptibility, and translation to clinical practice. There remains a significant gap in mapping specific metabolite signatures to neuropsychiatric phenotypes, as well as understanding how genetic and environmental factors modulate these effects.

title: Behavioural Data as Evidence for Good Husbandry and Management Practices Involving Ex Situ Animal Populations
summary: Behavioural data are central to understanding how animals respond to the care they receive in zoos, aquariums, and other ex situ environments. As global challenges to biodiversity intensify, ex situ facilities play an essential role in conservation breeding, public engagement and scientific research. Ensuring that animals under human care thrive requires the most complete understanding possible of their behavioural ecology, needs and preferences. Behavioural monitoring is a key tool to improve animal welfare output and the inputs from management practices across all taxa. By capturing how animals use space, interact socially, and respond to environmental changes, we gain insights that directly improve individual and group care, ultimately strengthening welfare outcomes in ex situ collections.
image_alt: Behavioural Data as Evidence for Good Husbandry and Management Practices Involving Ex Situ Animal Populations

title: Brain Iron in Neuropsychiatric Disorders
summary: Iron plays an essential role in neurodevelopment and the physiological functions of the brain by acting as a cofactor for enzymes involved in myelinogenesis, neurotransmitter synthesis, cellular respiration, and antioxidant defense. Iron deficiency hinders neurodevelopment, leading to cognitive, motor, and social performance deficits. Conversely, iron overload contributes to the formation of reactive oxygen species that induce oxidative stress and neuronal dysfunction. Abnormal iron levels also impact neurotransmitter systems by affecting synthesis and receptor activity. Brain iron imbalance has been reported in several neuropsychiatric disorders, highlighting the fundamental implications of this metal in mental health. However, the specific neurobiological and molecular pathways linking iron to neuropsychiatric disorders are only beginning to be elucidated. title: Learning from errors in Veterinary Diagnostic Imaging: Fostering a culture of socio-cultural growth
summary: Veterinary Diagnostic Imaging continues to advance in both technology and clinical applications, yet it faces numerous challenges, particularly when it comes to errors. These errors, which can be classified as either perception errors (changes that are not seen or are seen and ignored) or cognition errors (misjudgments, mistakes, or incorrect conclusions often caused by the brain’s simplification of information processing), can lead to false negative or positive reports and flawed clinical reasoning. A flock provides a compelling analogy for addressing these challenges, as it reflects how individuals dynamically adjust to one another in response to subtle cues; similarly, veterinary radiology teams can learn from errors through shared awareness and socio-cultural collaboration, fostering continuous improvement in diagnostic accuracy and patient care.
image_alt: Learning from errors in Veterinary Diagnostic Imaging: Fostering a culture of socio-cultural growth

title: The Endocannabinoid System as an Adaptive Hub: Beyond Canonical Cannabinoids in Neuropharmacology
summary: The endocannabinoid system (ECS) is increasingly recognized not merely as a receptor–ligand signaling pathway, but as a dynamic integrative network that coordinates neural, immune, and metabolic responses to environmental challenges. In the central nervous system, the ECS plays a crucial role in adaptive processes related to stress resilience, neuroinflammation, immune competence, and synaptic plasticity. While early pharmacological strategies predominantly focused on direct agonism or antagonism of cannabinoid receptors, clinical translation has been hindered by safety concerns, limited specificity, and context-independent modulation. Emerging evidence now suggests that functionally tuning the ECS, rather than globally activating or blocking it, may represent a more effective and physiologically aligned therapeutic approach.

title: Towards Autonomous and Trustworthy Robotic Systems: Intelligent Control, Motion Planning, and Embodied Decision-Making
summary: Intelligent control and planning constitute the decision-making core of modern robotic systems, enabling autonomous operation, adaptive behaviors, and optimized task execution in complex, dynamic environments. As robotics advances toward higher levels of autonomy, the synergy between perception, decision-making, and motion generation has become increasingly vital. In this context, sophisticated control and planning algorithms not only enhance operational efficiency but also empower robots to safely interact and adapt within unpredictable real-world scenarios.

Conversational and companion AI systems have created new possibilities for widening access to mental health resources, particularly for populations facing barriers linked to stigma, cost, or cultural mismatch. However, their growing emotional and relational presence raises critical questions for public mental health: how do interactions with AI affect users’ psychological autonomy, resilience, and well-being? Recent studies show both benefits,such as increased emotional expression, reinforcement of coping strategies, and accessible support,and risks, including dependency, parasocial attachment, over-trust, and diminished human connection. Although considerable advances have been made in acute care and neurorehabilitation, these disturbances remain among the most disabling and challenging consequences of ABI.

title: Emotional Engagement and Resilience: Addressing Mental Health Challenges in Global Crises
summary: Emotional engagement and resilience have emerged as key determinants of public mental health in the context of escalating global crises, including pandemics, climate emergencies, and political conflicts. Research underscores how collective stress, uncertainty, and loss can exacerbate psychological distress and erode community wellbeing. Advances in digital connectivity, teletherapy, and community-based support models have broadened access to care and introduced new avenues for prevention and response. Yet, significant gaps persist — unequal access to mental health services, stigma around help-seeking, systemic burnout among professionals, and the enduring effects of displacement continue to challenge global health equity. Recent studies emphasize that sustainable improvement in mental health outcomes requires approaches that are both culturally adaptive and systemically integrated, bridging behavioral science, technology, and policy innovation.

title: Long-Term Outcomes of Critically Ill Patients with Acute Brain Injury
summary: Neurocritical care has evolved into a discipline with clear benefits, with organised services linked to lower mortality and better functional outcomes. Yet, many survivors of acute brain injury (ABI) admitted to intensive care units continue to experience significant physical, cognitive, and emotional impairments long after discharge. Despite advances in acute management, long-term recovery trajectories remain poorly characterised, often measured by crude or inconsistent metrics that overlook patients’ quality of life and day-to-day functioning. Current evidence highlights a pressing need for better tools, standardised follow-up, and more nuanced understanding of how these patients recover over time and across different healthcare contexts.

title: Natural Products for Alzheimer's Disease, Depression, and Related Disorders: From Discovery to Mechanisms
summary: The incidence and mortality rates of neurological diseases are increasing annually, with a trend toward affecting younger populations, severely impacting patients' quality of life and exacerbating the societal healthcare burden. These diseases encompass neurodegenerative disorders such as Alzheimer's disease and Parkinson's disease, as well as various other types including depression and dementia due to cerebrovascular disease. Their pathogenesis is complex, involving neuroinflammation, oxidative stress, apoptosis, endoplasmic reticulum stress, mitochondrial dysfunction, deficiency in brain-derived neurotrophic factor, and reduced cholinergic activity. Natural products, as the oldest source of medicines, continue to provide crucial support for new drug development due to their rich chemical and functional diversity. title: Neutrophils: From Immune Sentinels to Agents of Neurodegenerative Diseases in the Aging CNS
summary: Neurodegenerative diseases represent one of the most pressing challenges in aging research, with advancing age the primary risk factor for disorders such as Alzheimer’s disease, Parkinson’s disease, amyotrophic lateral sclerosis, and vascular cognitive impairment. These conditions share a backdrop of inflammaging and immunosenescence, in which chronic low-grade inflammation, blood-brain barrier dysfunction, and impaired immune resolution converge on progressive neuronal injury. Within this immune landscape, neutrophils are increasingly recognised not as short-lived peripheral responders but as dynamic regulators of central nervous system (CNS) health.

title: PANS and PANDAS: Mechanisms, Biomarkers, and Integrated Therapeutic Strategies
summary: Pediatric acute-onset neuropsychiatric syndromes (such as PANS and PANDAS) represent a complex interplay of neuro and behavioural immunological, metabolic, genetic, microbiotal, nutritional, factors. These conditions illustrate how inflammatory triggers, including infections, psychosocial stress, and other immune-activating events, together with immune dysregulation, metabolic and mitochondrial dysfunction, and behavioral influences converge to produce sudden-onset neuropsychiatric symptoms in predisposed pediatric individuals. Although interest in these disorders is increasing, research remains fragmented and is often limited to individual disciplines or single treatment approaches.

title: Safety Critical Intelligent Control of Systems with Uncertain Dynamical Models
summary: Intelligent control has become a cornerstone of modern robotics and autonomous systems, where agents must operate safely and reliably despite uncertainty in their dynamics, environments, and sensing. From autonomous vehicles and aerial drones to robotic manipulators and assistive medical devices, the integration of adaptive, learning-based, and data-driven controllers has expanded the capabilities of these systems to function in highly dynamic contexts. However, achieving formal safety and stability guarantees within such frameworks remains a crucial and unsolved challenge. Uncertainties due to unmodeled dynamics, sensor noise, or real-time learning processes can threaten mission-critical reliability—especially when systems must make autonomous decisions without human oversight.

title: Freshwater Ecosystems Under Global Changes​​​​​​​
summary: Freshwater ecosystems, including rivers, lakes, ponds, and wetlands, play a critical role in sustaining biodiversity, regulating biogeochemical cycles, and providing services essential to human well-being. However, these systems are increasingly degraded by global environmental change and anthropogenic disturbances. Climate warming, urbanization, land-use transformation, and hydraulic engineering have collectively altered hydrological regimes, increased pollution levels, and undermined ecological balance. Recent studies demonstrate the accelerating loss of freshwater biodiversity and functional integrity, yet the interactive effects of multiple stressors remain insufficiently understood. This gap challenges efforts to predict ecological trajectories and design effective conservation responses. A deeper comprehension of ecosystem resilience mechanisms is therefore vital to guide restoration practices and promote adaptive management under ongoing global changes.

title: Multisensory Learning: XR, AI, and Cognitive Performance
summary: Extended reality (XR), including augmented reality (AR), mixed reality (MR), and virtual reality (VR), is moving learning research beyond screen-based presentation toward situated environments in which learners see, hear, smell, touch, move, collaborate, and receive adaptive feedback. These environments create new opportunities to examine learning as a multisensory, embodied, and socially mediated process across formal and informal contexts. At the same time, artificial intelligence and multimodal learning analytics are making it possible to model interaction traces that were previously difficult to interpret, including gaze, gesture, speech, motion, physiological signals, and haptic or olfactory engagement. However, much XR learning research still treats immersion as a broad intervention rather than examining how specific sensory cues and interaction patterns shape cognition, affect, attention, memory, spatial reasoning, motivation, and performance. title: Decoding Gene–Environment Interaction in Psychiatric Disorders: From Cross-Disorder Genetic Architecture to Precision Psychiatry
summary: Psychiatric disorders are highly heritable yet profoundly shaped by environmental exposures, with increasing evidence suggesting that shared genetic architectures underlie multiple diagnostic categories. Large-scale genome-wide association studies (GWAS), biobank resources, and advances in statistical genetics have revealed extensive pleiotropy and genetic correlations across disorders such as schizophrenia, bipolar disorder, major depressive disorder, substance use disorders, and suicidality. Meanwhile, environmental risk factors—including early-life adversity, substance exposure, stress, and social determinants—modulate genetic susceptibility through complex gene–environment (G×E) interactions. title: Multisensory interactions in speech and language: from theory to application
summary: Speech and language perception are inherently multisensory processes. The integration of auditory, visual, and somatosensory signals plays a fundamental role in how humans process and produce language across the lifespan. From the classic McGurk effect to the role of gesture in communication, converging evidence highlights that the brain does not process speech in isolation — rather, it continuously combines input across modalities to build robust and flexible linguistic representations. Despite significant advances in cognitive neuroscience, psycholinguistics, and computational modelling, key questions remain regarding the neural mechanisms underlying multisensory speech integration, how these processes break down in clinical populations, and how they can be harnessed in real-world applications.

title: Biodiversity Monitoring and Ecosystem Response to Non-Point Source Pollution: Integrating eDNA, Biomonitoring, and Ecological Indicators
summary: Non-point source (NPS) pollution from agriculture, urban runoff, atmospheric deposition, and diffuse industrial sources is one of the most pervasive and least controlled drivers of biodiversity loss and ecosystem degradation worldwide. Unlike point-source discharges, NPS pollution is spatially diffuse, temporally variable, and frequently undetected by conventional monitoring frameworks until ecological damage is already advanced. As international policy instruments such as the Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework and national water quality directives raise the bar for measurable biodiversity outcomes, there is an urgent need for monitoring approaches that can capture biological responses to NPS pollution at scale, with sensitivity, and across freshwater, soil, and terrestrial systems.

title: Emerging Perspectives in Psychopathy Research
summary: Psychopathy remains a central focus within forensic psychiatry, influencing the assessment, management, and treatment of individuals with severe personality pathology. Traditionally conceptualized following Cleckley’s framework, psychopathy encompasses affective, interpersonal, and behavioral traits associated with antisocial conduct and emotional deficits. The Hare Psychopathy Checklist-Revised (PCL-R) continues to guide clinical and forensic practice, evolving research underscores psychopathy’s multidimensional nature, shaped by neurobiological, psychological, and environmental factors. Advances in neuroimaging, genetics, and cognitive neuroscience have deepened our understanding of psychopathy’s underlying mechanisms, though gaps remain regarding how these findings translate into effective clinical practice. title: Innovations and Challenges in Canine Mammary Cancer Treatment: A New Frontier
summary: Canine mammary tumours represent the most common neoplasia in intact female dogs, with an incidence comparable to that of breast cancer in women. Malignant forms carry a lifetime risk ranging from 2% to 20%, while benign forms may affect up to 100% of susceptible individuals depending on hormonal status, age, and genetic predisposition. Surgical resection remains the cornerstone of curative treatment, though aggressive histotypes — such as solid carcinoma — often require adjuvant chemotherapy. Prognosis is influenced by tumour size, histological grade, lymphovascular invasion, and regional lymph node involvement. Lymphatic spread represents one of the primary metastatic routes in CMTs, making accurate nodal staging a critical determinant of both prognosis and treatment planning. Despite recent progress in the identification of biological markers, broader therapeutic advancements are necessary for effective treatment.

title: Innovative Applications of Gamification in Computational Psychiatry
summary: Computational psychiatry is an interdisciplinary field dedicated to modeling cognitive, emotional, and behavioral aspects of psychiatric conditions using quantitative approaches. While computational tasks are fundamental to research in this area, traditional tasks have often struggled with low engagement and limited ecological validity. This limitation has restricted the clinical utility and real-world applicability of findings. Gamification—ranging from enhanced visual and auditory design to fully narrative-driven gaming experiences—has emerged as a promising approach to address these issues, but systematic evaluation of its impact is still limited.

title: Linking Individual Responses to Climate Change to Whole-Ecosystem Dynamics in Marine and Coastal Habitats
summary: From mollusc shells to kelp holdfasts, individual marine organisms are on the front line of a rapidly changing ocean. Warming, acidification, deoxygenation, and intensifying extreme events act first on individuals, reshaping their behaviour, physiology, biomechanics, and the material properties of the structures they build. Yet the consequences rarely stop at the level of the organism. Individual-scale responses propagate through populations and communities to alter the structure and functioning of entire ecosystems, as when mass coral bleaching dismantles the habitat that thousands of reef-associated species depend on. Understanding how change at the smallest biological scales scales up to whole-ecosystem dynamics is one of the central challenges in marine global-change ecology, and a prerequisite for predicting and managing the future of coastal and marine systems.

title: Neuroinflammation and Therapeutic modulation in neuroprogressive disorders
summary: Neuroprogressive disorders, particularly Alzheimer’s disease and schizophrenia, are increasingly recognized as multifactorial conditions involving chronic neuroinflammation, oxidative stress, mitochondrial dysfunction, synaptic impairment, and progressive neuronal damage. Emerging evidence also highlights the critical role of the gut–brain axis in the pathophysiology of these disorders, demonstrating that alterations in gut microbiota composition, intestinal permeability, immune activation, and neuroimmune communication may contribute to cognitive decline, behavioral disturbances, and disease progression. In both Alzheimer’s disease and schizophrenia, dysregulation of gut–brain signaling has been associated with systemic inflammation, neurotransmitter imbalance, cholinergic dysfunction, and impaired neural plasticity, reinforcing the importance of understanding peripheral and central mechanisms involved in neuroprogression.

title: Neuromodulation: Neuroplasticity and Cognitive Enhancement in the Elderly
summary: Aging is accompanied by progressive changes in brain structure and function that may affect cognition, emotional regulation, and adaptive behavior. While mild cognitive decline is often considered a component of normal aging, many older adults experience impairments in memory, attention, executive function, and processing speed that can compromise independence and quality of life. In addition, neuropsychiatric manifestations such as apathy, depression, sleep disturbances, and reduced cognitive flexibility frequently emerge during aging and may precede or accompany neurodegenerative disorders.

summary: Urbanization is one of the most pervasive and rapidly expanding forms of global land-use change, fundamentally altering habitat structure, microclimatic conditions, biotic interactions, and resource availability across terrestrial ecosystem. The responses of invertebrate taxa—which constitute the vast majority of animal diversity and underpin critical ecosystem functions such as decomposition, pollination, nutrient cycling, and trophic energy transfer—remain comparatively understudied and poorly integrated into urban ecological theory. Invertebrates exhibit extraordinary diversity in their life histories, dispersal capacities, and physiological tolerances, resulting in highly variable and context-dependent responses to urban environmental gradients. title: Working memory mechanisms in speech and language acquisition and processing
summary: Working memory plays a central role in the cognitive and neural systems that support speech and language acquisition. It sustains transient representations of sounds, words, and syntactic structures, allowing learners to form stable linguistic knowledge while supporting the online processing of linguistic information during comprehension and production. Current neuroscience findings reveal that working memory is not a unitary construct but involves a dynamic interaction of the fronto-parietal control network, dorsal and ventral language streams, hippocampus, and cerebellum. Techniques such as high-resolution fMRI, MEG, intracranial recordings, and naturalistic neuroimaging have delineated how these distributed regions synchronize during word learning and sentence processing. summary: Concussion research in the context of para sports is an emerging field that seeks to address the complexities involved in understanding and managing head injuries among para athletes and individuals with disabilities. It is well-acknowledged that para athletes, who may have physical, intellectual, visual, or hearing impairments, are susceptible to concussions. during sport and daily life. However, the intricacies of how these injuries occur, their prevalence, and their impact on both sports and daily life activities remain inadequately explored. Compounding this issue is the absence of comprehensive concussion assessment protocols and management strategies tailored to athlete and non-athlete populations, including those with dual-sensory impairments. Digital Mental Health for People with Chronic Conditions: experiences, impact and interventions
summary: About 60% of people live with a chronic illness, such as eczema, epilepsy or a cleft lip. This ranges from 25% in children to 96% in people aged 75 and older. A chronic illness is defined as a condition that lasts longer than three months, recurs more than three times a year and/or is related to long-term use of medication, treatment or help (van Hal et al., 2019). According to the WHO, chronic conditions are conditions that require ongoing management over a period of years or decades. Living with a chronic illness often involves facing recurrent or long-term physical health issues, frequent medical treatment, and ongoing medication use. These experiences, alongside social and psychological stressors, contribute to an elevated risk of mental health difficulties, including depression, anxiety, and body image concerns.

title: Ecosystem Responses and Restoration under Environmental Change
summary: Ecosystems worldwide are increasingly shaped by a confluence of anthropogenic pressures — contamination, climate change, land-use transformation, resource overexploitation, and biological invasions. These stressors rarely act in isolation; their combined and cascading effects are altering biodiversity patterns, microbial community structure, biogeochemical cycling, and the capacity of ecosystems to recover from disturbance. Understanding how ecosystems respond, adapt, and can be restored under these multiple pressures is one of the most urgent challenges in ecology today.

title: Epigenetic-Immune Regulations in Neurological Disorders
summary: Neurological disorders represent a growing global health challenge, yet the molecular mechanisms underlying their onset and progression remain incompletely understood. Emerging evidence highlights a critical role for epigenetic modifications—including post-translational modifications, non-coding RNA-mediated regulation, and chromatin remodeling—in shaping neuroimmune responses. These epigenetic mechanisms govern microglial activation, astrocyte reactivity, peripheral immune cell infiltration, and blood-brain barrier integrity, thereby influencing disease trajectories across conditions. Understanding how epigenetic programs modulate neuroinflammation and immune tolerance in the central nervous system is essential for identifying novel biomarkers and developing precision therapeutic strategies.

title: Human-AI Symbiosis in the Workplace: Cognitive, Affective, and Relational Dynamics of Intelligent Collaboration
summary: While artificial intelligence is reshaping the workplace at an unprecedented pace, the psychological experience of working alongside AI remains poorly understood. AI now serves as a decision-support tool, collaborator, communication partner, and algorithmic management system across a wide range of organizational contexts. Existing studies have paid considerable attention to AI adoption, productivity improvement, and ethical risks, but less attention has been paid to the psychological dynamics through which employees experience, interpret, and adapt to intelligent collaboration in their everyday work. Human-AI collaboration is not merely a technological arrangement; it also involves cognitive sensemaking, emotional responses, trust calibration, autonomy negotiation, identity reconstruction, and relational adjustments within teams and organizations. title: Integrative Multi-Omics Methodologies for Decoding Genetic Pathways and Adaptations
summary: In evolutionary and molecular biology, multi-omics technologies, encompassing genomics, transcriptomics, proteomics, and metabolomics, bring transformative shifts to the analysis of biological systems. By integrating data across these molecular layers, researchers can achieve a detailed understanding of biosynthetic processes and evolutionary mechanisms that drive phenotypic diversity and organismal adaptation. This integrative approach enriches our comprehension of the complex interplay between genes, genomes, and their functional products, bridging significant gaps in our knowledge of how genomes regulate biological functions and interactions.

title: Psychedelic Medicine and Neuromodulation: From Bench to Bedside Advancing Real-World Implementation of Next-Generation Psychiatric Treatments
summary: Psychedelic medicine has emerged as one of the most promising frontiers in psychiatry and neurology, characterized by the capacity of compounds such as psilocybin, MDMA, LSD, DMT, and ketamine (including esketamine) to rapidly induce neuroplasticity, disrupt rigid maladaptive neural networks, and facilitate profound therapeutic change in conditions including treatment-resistant depression, PTSD, anxiety disorders, substance use disorders, eating disorders, and chronic pain syndromes. These agents engage serotonin 5-HT2A receptors, promote BDNF expression, and transiently dissolve the default-mode network, producing measurable changes in functional connectivity that correlate with sustained clinical improvement. Parallel to this renaissance, neuromodulation technologies—including repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation (rTMS), transcranial direct current stimulation (tDCS), focused ultrasound, vagus nerve stimulation (VNS), and deep brain stimulation (DBS)—offer precise, circuit-sp

title: Psychological Health and Safety at Work: A Systems-Level Approach to Psychosocial Risk, Organizational Context, and Employee Well-Being
summary: Psychological health and safety (PHS) has emerged as a critical priority in contemporary workplaces, reflecting growing recognition of psychosocial risks such as excessive workload, job insecurity, and poor organizational support. Traditionally, research on employee well-being has focused on individual-level stress and coping; however, there is increasing emphasis on organizational and system-level determinants of mental health at work. Frameworks such as the Job Demands–Resources (JD-R) model and psychosocial safety climate (PSC) highlight how work design, leadership, and human resource practices shape both risk and protective factors. Recent developments, including international standards such as ISO 45003, further underscore the need for integrated approaches to managing psychological health and safety. This Research Topic builds on this shift by examining how organizational systems create, sustain, or mitigate psychosocial risk and influence employee well-being.

title: Resilience and Psychological Recovery in Times of Stress and Uncertainty: Pathways to Mental Health and Human Flourishing
summary: The field of psychological resilience and adaptation has gained increasing relevance in recent years as individuals and societies face persistent stressors ranging from global crises to personal hardships. Research has illuminated the complex interplay between biological, psychological, and social processes that underpin human responses to adversity. Despite an expanding body of evidence, questions remain about how people rebuild wellbeing after disruption, the mechanisms that sustain recovery, and the factors that distinguish mere survival from genuine flourishing. Emerging studies challenge traditional deficit-oriented frameworks and instead highlight dynamic models of growth, flexibility, and meaning-making. Yet, gaps persist in understanding how contextual, cultural, and temporal factors influence the trajectories of psychological recovery and personal development.

title: Seronegative NMOSD: Emerging Mechanisms, Diagnostic Boundaries, and Therapeutic Opportunities
summary: Recent advances in neuroimmunology have revolutionized the classification and understanding of central nervous system inflammatory disorders, particularly with the identification of aquaporin-4 (AQP4) and myelin oligodendrocyte glycoprotein (MOG) antibodies in demyelinating diseases. Neuromyelitis optica spectrum disorder (NMOSD) remains a key diagnosis in this landscape; however, a clinically significant subset of patients with NMOSD-like syndromes are seronegative for both AQP4-IgG and MOG-IgG. These antibody-negative cases pose persistent challenges due to their biological heterogeneity, overlapping clinical features with other neuroinflammatory diseases, and the absence of standardized diagnostic and therapeutic frameworks. The pathogenesis of seronegative NMOSD is still poorly understood, with current evidence pointing to potential novel immune pathways, autoantibodies, or distinct endophenotypes. The lack of evidence-based guidelines leaves these patients at risk for under-recogn

title: Sleep as a Regulator of Stress and Emotion: Neurobiological Mechanisms of a Bidirectional Relationship
summary: Sleep and the brain’s capacity to process stress and regulate emotion are deeply intertwined. Psychosocial and physiological stressors disrupt sleep architecture, while disrupted sleep in turn impairs emotional regulation, threat appraisal, and stress coping. Although this bidirectional relationship is well-documented behaviourally and clinically, the underlying neurobiological mechanisms - spanning molecular, cellular, and circuit-level processes - remain incompletely understood.

title: Tetracyclines and their Non-Antibiotic Derivatives: Therapeutic Potential in Neurodegeneration and Neuronal Dysfunction
summary: Neurodegenerative disorders arise from interconnected pathological cascades involving neuroinflammation, protein misfolding, and progressive neuronal dysfunction. These processes, often exacerbated by aging, lead to irreversible declines in neural plasticity and resilience. In recent years, tetracyclines and their non-antibiotic derivatives have emerged as pharmacologically versatile molecules with strong potential for neuroprotection. Beyond their classical antibacterial effects, these compounds mitigate glial activation, suppress pro-inflammatory cytokine production, inhibit ferroptosis, and prevent protein aggregation, thereby targeting critical mechanisms underlying neurodegenerative progression. Despite these promising findings, it remains unclear how their molecular profiles interact with age-related changes in neuroimmune regulation, proteostasis, and metabolic homeostasis. title: The Role of the Cerebellum in Neurocognitive Disorders
summary: The cerebellum, historically linked only to motor control, is now recognized as a vital hub for executive function, emotion, and social cognition. Through dense, reciprocal loops, the cerebellum connects with prefrontal, temporal, and parietal areas to modulate thinking and attention. Disruptions in these networks contribute to several neurocognitive disorders. These include Alzheimer’s disease, frontotemporal dementia, vascular dementia, and mixed cognitive decline. Yet, we still do not fully understand structural, functional, and metabolic changes in specific cerebellar subregions. We also need to map how these changes manifest in patients. Advanced imaging tools like positron emission tomography (PET), multiparametric magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), and quantitative radiomics can map these alterations in vivo. They connect subtle cerebellar pathology with network dysconnectivity and cognitive decline. Studying these links helps us find early disease markers. It also helps us under

title: The enriched tank: Zebrafish welfare, sex-specific behavior, and neuroendocrine insights
summary: Zebrafish are becoming indispensable models in neuroscience and behavioral biology, enabling high-throughput studies on stress, cognition, and social behavior. Yet, variability in welfare conditions, environmental enrichment, rearing density, and tank design challenge reproducibility and cross-laboratory comparability.

title: Urban Forest Biodiversity – From Aboveground to Belowground, from Genes to Landscapes
summary: Against the backdrop of accelerating global urbanization, urban forests—as a core element of green infrastructure—are increasingly recognized for their profound biodiversity value. Urban forests represent far more than simple tree assemblages; they function as complex biotic communities supporting a diverse spectrum of life, spanning soil microbiomes, canopy-dwelling arthropods, and vertebrates. Collectively, vegetation diversity, habitat heterogeneity, and belowground microbial diversity lay the fundamental groundwork for the resilience of urban ecosystems. Nevertheless, urban environments pose unprecedented threats to the conservation of urban forest biodiversity, such as habitat fragmentation, biological invasions, environmental pollution, and extreme climatic events. At present, scientific understanding remains fragmented regarding three key aspects: the coupling relationships between aboveground and belowground biodiversity in urban forests, the regulatory role of functional diver

title: Advancing Marine Megafauna Monitoring and Conservation: Emerging Methods, Data Integration, and Assessment Frameworks
summary: Marine megafauna — cetaceans, sea turtles, sharks and rays, pinnipeds, and seabirds — are sentinels of ocean health and among the most vulnerable groups to human pressure. Their wide ranges, mobility, and often low detectability make them notoriously difficult to monitor, yet sound monitoring is the foundation of every conservation decision made on their behalf, from bycatch mitigation to the design of marine protected areas.

title: Artificial Intelligence and Assistive Robotics: Socio-Psychological and Educational Implications
summary: In recent years, AI and robotic systems have begun to transition from controlled laboratory settings into everyday contexts such as education, healthcare and assistive care. These technologies show potential for enabling adaptive learning, personalized support and social interaction, reshaping how individuals engage with digital systems. Socially Assistive Robots (SARs), in particular, have been explored in therapeutic and educational settings, suggesting positive effects on engagement, communication and socio-emotional development, especially among vulnerable populations such as children with autism. While there is a growing body of work in this direction, the practical deployment of SARs and AI in real-world settings remains limited and has not reached widespread adoption.
