title: Active Mobility in Older Age
summary: Active mobility — encompassing walking, bicycling, and related forms of human-powered transport — offers older adults an accessible route to incorporating physical activity into daily life in an environmentally sustainable way. Worldwide, policies and interventions promote active mobility within the United Nations’ Sustainable Development Goals framework. Yet, older adults engage in some forms of active mobility less than younger adults, and the psychological processes underlying this difference remain poorly understood. Limited knowledge about bicycling and its benefits, motivation, self-efficacy, fear of falling, social support, age stereotypes, and perceptions of the environment are among the key psychological factors shaping whether older adults take up or maintain active mobility, and whether they benefit from it socially, cognitively, and emotionally. title: Advances in Neural Repair after Stroke: Mechanisms and Clinical Translation
summary: Neural repair after stroke is a vital field focused on addressing persistent disability, which remains common despite progress in acute care. While acute treatments have improved survival and initial outcomes, many stroke survivors face long-term functional deficits due to gaps in repair strategies. Ongoing research has revealed important mechanisms—such as neuroplasticity, axonal sprouting, remyelination, neurogenesis, angiogenesis, and involvement of glial cells, inflammation, and the extracellular matrix—that drive recovery. Although these insights have suggested new avenues for therapy, effective clinical translation and integration of evolving interventions remain major challenges.

title: Human-AI Interaction in Agentic Transportation: Trust, Transparency, and Shared Decision-Making
summary: Advances in AI are giving rise to agentic mobility: intelligent vehicles, in-vehicle agents, automated shuttles, robotaxis, mobility assistants, and connected services that go beyond automating movement to infer user goals, communicate intent, adapt to context, and participate in decisions. These systems function not only as transportation technologies but also as interactive media through which goals, risks, and responsibilities are represented, conveyed, and negotiated. As mobility systems take on these communicative and decision-making roles, the human role shifts from driver and operator toward passenger, supervisor, collaborator, and orchestrator. This transition foregrounds three interrelated challenges for human-media interaction: how trust is established and maintained between people and AI-enabled mobility systems, how the reasoning and limitations of such systems are made transparent to users, and how control and decisions are shared in ways that preserve meaningful human ove

title: Immersive, Intelligent, and Interoperable Technologies in Rehabilitation: From Lab to Clinical Integration
summary: The convergence of immersive, intelligent, and interoperable technologies is redefining rehabilitation and performance recovery across sport, medicine, and active living. Extended reality (XR), artificial intelligence (AI), robotics, and wearable sensing enable the continuous assessment and optimization of movement, from clinical recovery to return-to-play. Virtual and augmented environments deliver graded, motivational therapy; AI and motion analytics allow real-time feedback and adaptation; and interoperable data infrastructures support connected rehabilitation between clinics, training facilities, and homes. Although laboratory evidence strongly supports these innovations, translation into clinical and athletic settings remains limited. Technical integration, user adoption, and health-system alignment remain key hurdles to widespread implementation.

title: Modeling, Sensing, Estimation, and Control of Soft and Continuum Robots
summary: Recent progress in materials, flexible sensors, and embedded intelligence has significantly accelerated the development of soft and continuum robots. Compared with conventional rigid robots, these systems offer superior compliance, dexterity, and adaptability but introduce unique challenges in kinematic and dynamic modeling, state estimation, sensing, and control due to their continuously deformable structures and strong nonlinearities. At the same time, emerging technologies such as machine learning, foundation models, digital twins, physics-informed learning, and multimodal perception are creating new opportunities to improve the performance, robustness, and autonomy of these robotic systems. As the field continues to evolve rapidly, there is an increasing need to integrate advances in modeling, estimation, sensing, and control into unified frameworks that enable reliable deployment in real-world applications.

title: Neural and cognitive foundations of human performance and safety in complex engineered systems
summary: The field of human performance in complex engineering systems has emerged at the intersection of neuroscience, cognitive psychology, engineering, and public health. As automation, digitalization, and artificial intelligence transform industries such as transportation, manufacturing, construction, and emergency response, the demands placed on human cognition and physiology have never been greater. Individuals must maintain attention, manage workload, calibrate trust in automation, and make critical decisions under uncertainty—processes that are deeply rooted in neural mechanisms. Recent neurophysiological and cognitive research has provided valuable insights into attentional control, executive functioning, stress responses, and fatigue dynamics that underpin performance and safety outcomes. title: Advances in MRI Radiomics for Non-Invasive Glioma Assessment
summary: Glioma research has rapidly evolved in recent years, particularly in the context of diagnostic imaging and personalized medicine. Gliomas, representing the most prevalent malignant primary brain tumors, are remarkably heterogeneous, posing significant challenges for classification, treatment, and prognosis. While magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) remains indispensable for diagnosing and monitoring gliomas, traditional visual assessments are often insufficient to uncover the full spectrum of tumor heterogeneity and correlate with underlying molecular features. With advances in computational methods, MRI radiomics has emerged as a transformative approach by extracting large sets of quantitative features from routine imaging, promising to bridge the gap between imaging phenotypes and the molecular landscape of brain tumors.
image_alt: Advances in MRI Radiomics for Non-Invasive Glioma Assessment

title: Brain Resilience: Understanding the Role of Brain, Cognitive, Motor, and Affective Reserves
summary: Brain resilience is a broad term encompassing concepts that seek to explain the brain’s capacity to maintain cognition and effective functioning despite aging, neurological disease, or other forms of adversity. Among the earliest and most influential concepts within this framework are brain reserve and cognitive reserve. Together, these constructs have been used to help explain why the degree of brain pathology does not always correspond directly to the severity of its clinical manifestations.
image_alt: Brain Resilience: Understanding the Role of Brain, Cognitive, Motor, and Affective Reserves

title: Eco-Evolutionary Dynamics of Plant Microbiomes: From the Friend–Foe Continuum to Sustainable Disease Management
summary: Plant microbiomes are a hidden frontier in the effort to secure global food production, offering a route to shift agriculture away from chemical-intensive practices toward more sustainable, biologically driven solutions. The microbial communities inhabiting seeds, the rhizosphere, and the phyllosphere form a dynamic “bio-barrier” that can suppress pathogens through competitive exclusion, the production of antagonistic metabolites, and the modulation of host immune responses.

title: The Augmented Human: Exploring the Frontiers of Human Performance Augmentation
summary: The concept of the Augmented Human encompasses various technological solutions that help enhance human performance by supporting the perceptual, cognitive and/or physical capabilities of their users. Recent years have seen a steep growth in this research area, especially when it comes to enhancing human performance using the immersive technology of Augmented Reality (AR) in combination with Artificial Intelligence (AI).

summary: Environmental factors play a pivotal role in shaping patient outcomes within neurocritical care, a discipline dedicated to the management of acute and life-threatening neurological conditions. Following the momentum of Volume 1, which explored how climate change influences neurological health and neurocritical management, a broader understanding of environmental stressors has emerged as an urgent frontier. Beyond global climate impacts, acute factors such as hospital air quality, noise levels, light exposure, thermal variability, and stress-inducing surroundings may directly influence pathophysiological mechanisms, neuroinflammation, and neurological recovery. Recent research has highlighted how these physical and psychological stressors contribute to altered cerebral perfusion, metabolic imbalance, and cognitive dysfunction post-injury. title: Early Detection of Cerebral Palsy: From Evidence to Equitable Implementation
summary: Cerebral palsy (CP) is the most common cause of physical disability in childhood worldwide, affecting approximately 1-4 per 1,000 live births, with prevalence significantly higher in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs). Although the condition is difficult to manage, early diagnosis can help prevent disability caused by the condition. Current international guidelines suggest diagnosis as early as 3-5 months of corrected age, using a combination of General Movements Assessment, Hammersmith Infant Neurological Examination, and magnetic resonance imaging. In high-income countries, early diagnosis of CP has demonstrated feasibility and high acceptability among families and professionals. In contrast, it remains severely underutilized in LMICs, where CP prevalence is higher and clinical presentations more severe.

title: From Genomes to Ecosystems: Harnessing Bioinformatics, Metagenomics, and AI for One Health AMR Surveillance
summary: Antimicrobial resistance (AMR) is now recognized as one of the greatest global health challenges of our time, threatening the effectiveness of antibiotics and other antimicrobial drugs in both human and veterinary medicine. The rapid spread of resistant bacteria and resistance genes across humans, animals, food systems, and the environment underscores the urgent need for integrated One Health strategies that consider the close connections between these ecosystems. In recent years, major advances in whole-genome sequencing (WGS), have transformed our ability to investigate resistance genes, mobile genetic elements, transmission routes, and the emergence of multidrug-resistant high-risk clones across diverse ecological settings.

title: From Shelter to Home: Companion Animal Welfare, Behaviour, and the Development of Human-Animal Bonds
summary: Many companion animals around the world end up in shelters. They are picked up as strays by animal control officers, they are relinquished by owners who no longer want the animal or do not have the ability or resources to provide the necessary care for the animal, or they are rescued from situations of neglect or cruelty. Shelters are meant to be safe places where animals can heal, be cared for and find new homes. These are the aims of all shelter workers and volunteers. Unfortunately, not all shelters meet these aims for all animals. Some animals enter a shelter with health and/or behaviour problems that may deteriorate within the shelter despite everyone’s best efforts. Also, adoptions are not always successful.

title: Sustainable and Innovative One Health Approaches in Veterinary Reproductive Therapeutics to Protect Environmental and Human Health
summary: Veterinary reproductive medicine forms a cornerstone of animal production and welfare, yet its reliance on pharmaceuticals, antimicrobials, and a variety of interventions introduces a cascade of potential challenges that extend well beyond animal health. Mounting evidence highlights concerns including the propagation of antimicrobial resistance and occupational exposures for veterinary and agricultural workers. Furthermore, the carbon footprint and waste associated with reproductive management contribute to broader environmental challenges, while efforts to maximize fertility underscore the delicate balance between productivity and sustainability. Although significant research has focused on optimizing reproductive success in various species, there remains a critical need to assess the holistic impact of these interventions, especially under the guiding principles of One Health, which emphasize the interconnectedness of animal, human, and environmental health.

title: The Gut–Brain Tumour Axis: Microbiome-Driven Mechanisms in Neuro-Oncology
summary: The gut microbiome, including commensal bacteria, archaea, viruses and fungi, is increasingly recognized as playing a key role in brain health, with distinct microbiota profiles associated in the development and treatment of brain tumours (i.e glioma, glioblastoma). Microbe-derived metabolites/products can reach the brain via neural pathways and systemic circulation or, as more recently proposed, through gut microbiota translocation that locally impact the tumour growth and its microenvironment. Within the brain, microbial products modulate systemic immunity, blood-brain barrier integrity, and inflammatory responses, shaping the tumour's immune landscape. Together, these interactions define the gut-brain-tumour axis as a promising therapeutic target. The brain tumour microenvironment (TME), composed of a milieu of different type of cells surrounding and interacting with the cancer cells, has become a central focus in cancer research. title: Affordable Cyber-Robotic Systems for Healthcare 5.0
summary: The integration of robots, cyber-physical systems, data-driven control, and artificial intelligence (AI) plays a key role in advancing healthcare delivery and training. Cyber-Robotic Systems (CRS) are robots with intelligent computational and control capabilities that can sense, process, and respond dynamically to the environment. With the rise of data-driven and learning-based control techniques, robotic systems can now operate effectively in environments characterized by uncertainty, variability, and user-specific requirements. This is particularly crucial in areas such as robot-assisted surgery (RAS), rehabilitation, eldercare, and remote diagnostics, where human safety, adaptability, and precision are of top priority. Therefore, CRS can support Healthcare 5.0 which emphasizes personalized care, preventive diagnostics, and patient-focused treatment.

title: Brain–Behavior–Environment Coupling in Neurodevelopment: From Multimodal Mechanisms to Precision Intervention
summary: Neurodevelopment is shaped by dynamic interactions among neural systems, behavioral functions, and environmental contexts. Recent advances in multimodal neuroimaging, computational modeling, and developmental science have highlighted that atypical development—particularly in conditions such as autism spectrum disorder (ASD), attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD), and language impairments—cannot be fully explained by isolated neural deficits. Instead, emerging evidence supports a coupling framework in which brain activity, behavioral adaptation, and environmental input form an integrated system. However, current research remains fragmented across modalities (e.g., EEG, fMRI, eye-tracking) and levels of analysis, limiting our understanding of how these components interact over developmental time and how such interactions can inform targeted interventions.

Optimizing Health and Well-Being Across the Lifespan: A Multidimensional Health Psychology Perspective
summary: Across modern life and work contexts - characterized by uncertainty, complexity, and accelerating demands- sustaining human performance and well-being has become both a psychological and public health priority. Human Performance Optimization (HPO) offers a unifying framework that views optimal functioning as the outcome of dynamic interactions among cognitive, emotional, physical, social, and spiritual domains. Originally rooted in performance-critical settings such as the military, HPO has evolved into a multidimensional approach relevant to healthcare, education, sport, and organizational life. Within health psychology, this paradigm resonates with holistic and positive health models that emphasize resilience, adaptability, and meaning as pillars of sustained human effectiveness and flourishing. Despite growing interest, there remains a need to better understand how these interwoven processes promote lasting well-being and to translate them into evidence-informed practices.

title: Transformations in Work, Workforce, and Workplace: The What, the Who, and the Where of Contemporary Organizations
summary: In an era marked by rapid technological advancements, increasing complexity, and unpredictability, business organizations and the workforce face challenges related to the nature of work, the ways in which work should be performed, and changing labor-force expectations and structures. These challenges serve as drivers of transformation for both organizations and employees in order to remain effective, sustainable, and supportive of well-being. As a result, organizations are rethinking traditional approaches to managing work, employees, and workplaces. Understanding these transformations is essential for addressing the opportunities and challenges associated with the future of work.

title: Carbon-based flexible neural interfaces for multimodal brain activity analysis
summary: Understanding the functionality and complexity of neural networks in the brain represents a significant frontier in neuroscience and neural engineering. Accurate and reliable assessment of neural activities demands innovative implantable devices capable of multimodal measurements over prolonged and varying timescales. Recent advances emphasize the integration of multiple modalities such as electrophysiological recording, neurochemical sensing, imaging, electrical stimulation, and optogenetics to yield richer insights into neuronal dynamics and brain function. Carbon-based flexible neural devices have emerged to address these demands, leveraging materials such as graphene, glassy carbon, boron-doped diamond (BDD), carbon nanotubes (CNTs), and fuzzy graphene. title: Gene–Environment Interplay in the Development of Behavioral and Psychiatric Disorders Across the Lifespan
summary: Behavioral and psychiatric disorders arise from dynamic interactions between genetic predisposition and environmental influences across development and aging. Increasing evidence highlights critical windows of vulnerability and plasticity during which environmental exposures—such as early-life stress, social context, nutrition, and age-related physiological changes—shape genetic risk. Advances in human genetics, longitudinal cohort studies, and multi-omics approaches, alongside mechanistic investigations in model organisms (e.g., rodents, zebrafish, and invertebrates), have provided new insights into conserved developmental pathways regulating behavior and psychiatric traits.

title: Precision Neuroscience: Bridging Lab Discoveries to Clinical Solutions for Neurodegenerative Disorders
summary: Neurodegenerative disorders represent one of the greatest medical and societal challenges of our time. Despite remarkable advances in neuroscience, the translation of laboratory discoveries into effective clinical interventions remains slow and fragmented. The increasing availability of high-throughput technologies, advanced neuroimaging, digital biomarkers, artificial intelligence, and innovative experimental models is rapidly transforming our understanding of disease mechanisms and opening new opportunities for precision medicine approaches across the spectrum of neurodegenerative diseases.

title: The Computational Principles of Brain Function: a Neuroinformatics Perspective
summary: Understanding the computational principles that govern brain function is one of neuroscience’s most enduring challenges. How do neural circuits encode information efficiently, sustain stable activity patterns over time, and support learning across multiple timescales? Addressing these questions demands a convergence of theoretical rigor, computational modeling, and large-scale data analysis. Neuroinformatics sits at precisely that intersection.

summary: The digital technology has profoundly transformed the social interaction patterns of children and adolescents, and has also given rise to new forms and developmental pathways of aggression. Issues such as cyberbullying, toxic behaviors, and social media conflicts are increasingly prominent, with aggressive behaviors no longer confined to real life but extending into the virtual world. Problematic internet use (e.g., gaming, short videos, social media, artificial intelligence) and exposure to adverse media factors (e.g., violence, competition) may exert significant effects on various types of aggression. Currently, there is a lack of systematic integration regarding the dynamic trajectories, typological differentiation, and psychological and physiological mechanisms of aggression development in the digital era. title: AI-Enabled XR for Industrial Operations and Applications
summary: Extended Reality (XR), including virtual reality (VR), augmented reality (AR), and mixed reality (MR), is increasingly gaining relevance in industrial environments. Rather than being viewed only as an immersive visualization technology, XR is now emerging as an interface layer that connects workers, engineers, and operators to product data, digital twins, work instructions, IoT telemetry, maintenance knowledge, and enterprise systems. Current evidence suggests that XR creates the strongest practical value in bounded industrial workflows such as training, assembly, inspection, maintenance, logistics, remote collaboration, and design review. At the same time, artificial intelligence (AI) is shifting XR from static visualization toward context-aware support through scene understanding, computer vision, speech interfaces, adaptive guidance, predictive analytics, and intelligent knowledge retrieval. title: Biomarkers In Neurodegenerative Disorders: Focus on Global Communities with Disparities
summary: Neurodegenerative diseases are witnessing a surge in prevalence, primarily driven by population aging, pressing the need for advancements in public health strategies. Early and accurate diagnosis of these diseases — including Alzheimer’s disease, Parkinson’s disease, and other dementias and movement disorders — is crucial for better therapeutic management. Research into disease-modifying treatments is increasingly focused on diagnosis at earlier stages, with developed countries adopting fluid biomarkers (plasma and CSF) as practical alternatives to expensive molecular imaging. However, current research largely overlooks diverse racial and socio-economic groups, particularly those from underdeveloped countries and vulnerable communities, such as individuals with lower educational backgrounds, leading to a substantial gap in the universal applicability of research findings.

title: Botulinum neurotoxin therapy in Parkinson’s disease and aging-related movement disorders: mechanisms, biomarkers, and treatment optimization
summary: Botulinum neurotoxin has become a cornerstone in addressing focal dystonias, sialorrhea, chronic migraine, and overactive bladder. Despite this established role, significant questions remain regarding its optimal application for the complex motor and non-motor symptoms seen in Parkinson’s disease and aging-related movement disorders. Current evidence is fragmented, with uncertainty around which patients benefit most, how underlying mechanisms influence clinical outcomes, and which biomarkers truly support precise and individualized therapy—particularly in the elderly, who often present with multifaceted symptom profiles encompassing both motor and non-motor domains, including neuropsychiatric features.

title: Bridging Menstrual Health and Mental Health: Towards Equitable, Inclusive, and Integrated Public Health Solutions
summary: Menstrual health is an essential yet often overlooked dimension of global public health and mental well-being, aligning with international goals for gender equity and sustainable development. It encompasses biological, psychological, social, cultural, and economic influences. Growing global evidence demonstrates that menstrual experiences affect not only physical well-being but also mental health, social inclusion, educational attainment, and economic participation. Persistent inequities,driven by period poverty, stigma, cultural taboos, and inadequate sanitation or healthcare infrastructure,continue to marginalize many, particularly adolescents, refugees, people with disabilities, and those in low-resource settings. Existing research has begun to uncover the links between menstrual experiences and mental distress, including anxiety, depression, and body image issues, yet fragmentation within research and policy responses often prevents comprehensive solutions. title: Combating Antimicrobial Resistance (AMR) – Increasing the Effectiveness of Antibiotics, Inventing Alternatives and Microbiome-Based Interventions
summary: Since their introduction into clinical and veterinary medicine, antibiotics have become indispensable for treating bacterial infections, protecting animal welfare and preventing economic losses in animal production. However, their use can develop and spread antimicrobial resistance (AMR). Within the One Health framework, the spread of resistant pathogenic bacteria is a multidirectional process as resistant bacteria and resistance determinants circulate among animals, humans, food and the environment, making the preservation of existing antibiotics essential for both human and animal health.

title: Exploring autonomic regulation in maternal mental health: Physiological pathways underlying pregnancy, stress, and neonatal outcomes
summary: The field of autonomic neuroscience provides a powerful framework to understand how physiological regulation underlies maternal mental health and perinatal adaptation. During pregnancy and the postpartum period, autonomic, neuroendocrine, and immune systems interact dynamically to maintain homeostasis in the face of emotional and physiological experiences and challenges. Maternal mental health conditions — including perinatal depression, anxiety, and stress-related conditions — have been increasingly recognized as significant contributors to adverse outcomes for both mothers and their infants. However, the underlying autonomic mechanisms that link psychological states to biological function remain insufficiently explored. Recent studies highlight that alterations in heart rate variability, vagal tone, and sympathetic–parasympathetic balance reflect the degree of stress adaptation and may predict emotional states, resilience, and perinatal outcomes. title: From Synapses to Silicon: Theoretical Foundations and Neuromorphic Implementations of Biological Learning
summary: Learning in biological neural systems emerges from the coordinated interaction of molecular, cellular, and circuit-level mechanisms that collectively give rise to adaptive behavior across timescales spanning milliseconds to years. At the most elementary level, synaptic efficacy is dynamically regulated through activity-dependent processes, including voltage- and calcium-mediated long-term potentiation (LTP) and long-term depression (LTD), spike-timing-dependent plasticity (STDP), and metaplasticity. These local synaptic rules, however, do not operate in isolation: neuromodulatory systems impose global signals that gate plasticity, encode reward prediction errors, and regulate the transition between exploratory and consolidative learning states. title: Integrating transcriptomics, epitranscriptomics, and spatial transcriptomics to decode plant regulatory complexity
summary: Plant molecular biology is entering a new era of transcriptomic precision. Over the past decade, the progression from bulk RNA sequencing to single-cell and spatial transcriptomics has profoundly changed how researchers map gene activity and regulation. Beyond traditional measures of transcript abundance, the discovery of epitranscriptomic mechanisms, chemical modifications such as m⁶A, m⁵C, and pseudouridylation, has revealed new layers of post-transcriptional control that modulate RNA stability, translation, and splicing. Together, these techniques offer multidimensional insights into how individual cell types and tissues orchestrate complex physiological and developmental programs. While transcriptomics has long illuminated what genes are expressed, the integration of epitranscriptomic and spatial data now enables investigations into how and where transcripts function, providing fine-scale views of regulatory logic in plant adaptation, growth, and stress response.

title: Learning and Cognitive Development in the Age of AI
summary: Human cognition is being reshaped as artificial intelligence becomes increasingly integrated into everyday life and cognitive work. This Research Topic will offer cutting-edge synthesis and theoretical articles addressing how human cognitive systems adapt, learn, and develop alongside artificial intelligence. Understanding these processes is both timely and practically important. AI is being integrated into our daily environments, and the long-term cognitive consequences of this integration may be undesirable. For that reason, this Research Topic will put special emphasis on cognitive and neural reorganization, learning, and decision-making frameworks. The topic is timely: artificial intelligence is rapidly transforming human society and increasingly carrying out tasks once performed exclusively by people, from problem-solving to reasoning and decision-making. title: Model Organisms in Translational Neuroscience: From Neural Circuits and Behaviour to Clinical Insight.
summary: Model organisms have transformed our understanding of the nervous system. Drosophila melanogaster, Caenorhabditis elegans, Danio rerio (zebrafish), and Xenopus tadpoles offer conserved neurological architectures combined with rapid development, genetic accessibility, and experimental scale that are impractical in mammalian systems. These properties make them uniquely powerful tools for dissecting the cellular and molecular mechanisms of neural circuits, behaviour, and disease - and, increasingly, for accelerating the translation of fundamental discovery into clinical insight. Mechanisms identified in invertebrate and lower-vertebrate models have already informed our understanding of Alzheimer’s, Parkinson’s, ALS, neurodevelopmental disorders, and inherited neuropathies, and have provided platforms for high-throughput drug screening and target validation.

Advancements in imaging, molecular profiling, and neuroimmune modeling have provided a clearer picture of these interactions, yet the translation of this knowledge into clinically relevant biomarkers and therapeutic solutions remains an ongoing challenge. title: Vascular Remodeling, Post-Thrombectomy Aneurysm Formation and Tumor Progression: Bridging Cerebrovascular Intervention and Neuro-Oncology
summary: Mechanical thrombectomy has reshaped the management of acute ischemic stroke, offering rapid recanalization and improved neurological outcomes. However, emerging clinical observations suggest that vascular alterations following thrombectomy particularly endothelial injury, hemodynamic stress redistribution, and inflammatory cascades may predispose certain patients to delayed vascular complications, including de novo or progressive aneurysm formation. These post-thrombectomy vascular changes remain insufficiently characterized, both mechanistically and clinically.

title: Probing Brain Asymmetry: Computational and Data-Driven Approaches
summary: Brain asymmetry — the structural and functional specialization of the left and right cerebral hemispheres — is one of the most fundamental organizing principles of the human brain. From language dominance and handedness to emotion regulation and spatial cognition, hemispheric lateralization shapes nearly every aspect of human behavior. Disruptions to typical asymmetry patterns have been implicated in a range of neurological and psychiatric conditions, including schizophrenia, autism spectrum disorder, dyslexia, and depression, making it a critical target for both basic and translational neuroscience research.

title: Trustworthy generative and explainable AI for neuroimaging and neural signal analysis
summary: Artificial intelligence is driving transformative change in neuroscience by revolutionizing the analysis of neuroimaging modalities—such as MRI, fMRI, PET—and electrophysiological recordings, including EEG and MEG. The integration of deep learning approaches into these data types has led to enhanced detection and characterization of neurological and psychiatric conditions, finer mapping of brain networks, and deeper understanding of brain-behavior relationships. Nevertheless, significant challenges persist: limited annotated datasets, data heterogeneity, model generalization issues, and a persistent demand for transparency undermine the reliable translation of AI methods into neuroscientific research and clinical workflows. Recent progress in generative artificial intelligence, encompassing GANs, VAEs, diffusion models, and foundation models, is helping to address some of these hurdles. title: Integrating Coastal Ecosystem Dynamics and Climate Risk Management
summary: Coastal ecology and evolution are increasingly shaped by interacting climate hazards, including sea-level rise, storm surges, erosion, saltwater intrusion, ocean warming, and changing disturbance regimes. These pressures affect biodiversity, ecosystem functioning, species distributions, evolutionary processes, and the services that coastal ecosystems provide to human communities. Recent research demonstrates that wetlands, dunes, mangroves, seagrass meadows, coral reefs, and other coastal habitats can reduce exposure to hazards while supporting ecological connectivity, carbon storage, and livelihood security. Advances in earth observation, ecological forecasting, high-resolution climate modeling, autonomous monitoring, and artificial intelligence are improving the detection and projection of coastal change. However, important gaps remain in understanding cumulative and cascading impacts, thresholds of ecological resilience, feedbacks between ecological and social systems, and the condi
image_alt: Integrating Coastal Ecosystem Dynamics and Climate Risk Management

title: Mental Health Across the Academic Career: Predictors, Protective Factors, and Intervention Strategies
summary: Academia is a demanding environment where students, doctoral candidates, and researchers may experience academic pressure, competitive evaluation, precarious career pathways, publishing demands, isolation, financial insecurity, and challenges associated with international mobility or caregiving responsibilities. Research indicates elevated levels of distress and burnout among different academic populations, particularly postgraduate and early-career researchers, although prevalence and risk vary across disciplines, countries, career stages, and social groups. Mental health in academia can be shaped by the interaction of individual characteristics, supervisory and peer relationships, workload, organizational cultures, and wider sociocultural influences. In response to growing concerns, universities and research institutions are implementing counselling services, peer-support, psychoeducation, and digital interventions, but evidence regarding their effectiveness, accessibility, sustainab
image_alt: Mental Health Across the Academic Career: Predictors, Protective Factors, and Intervention Strategies

title: Methods in Molecular Neuroscience
summary: Progress in molecular neuroscience depends as much on the questions we ask as on the tools we have to answer them. Over the past decade, the field has gained access to a remarkable set of methods that allow researchers to probe brain function with cellular and molecular precision, across systems ranging from invertebrates to brain organoids and human induced pluripotent stem cells. Genetic engineering, optogenetics and chemogenetics, advanced imaging, biosensors, single-cell and spatial transcriptomics, proteomics, behavioral assays, and bioinformatics now form the methodological backbone of work across the entire spectrum of molecular neuroscience, from basic signaling pathways to disease mechanisms, plasticity, and pain.
image_alt: Methods in Molecular Neuroscience

title: Microglia, Neuroinflammation, and Neurodegeneration in Brain Aging and Age-Associated Disease
summary: Aging of the central nervous system is characterized by intricate changes in immune regulation, molecular signaling, and neuronal integrity. Among the key players in this process are microglia, the resident immune cells of the brain, whose fundamental role in maintaining tissue homeostasis becomes progressively impaired with advancing age. Evidence from preclinical and clinical studies indicates that microglial dysfunction contributes to chronic low-grade neuroinflammation, synaptic deterioration, and neuronal loss; hallmarks of neurodegenerative pathologies such as Alzheimer’s disease, Parkinson’s disease, and other forms of dementia. Despite major advances in understanding these associations, significant gaps persist regarding how microglial state transitions, metabolic reprogramming, and regional heterogeneity shape disease progression and resilience. The growing body of research emphasizes the need to clarify the molecular and cellular circuits linking age-related changes in microg
image_alt: Microglia, Neuroinflammation, and Neurodegeneration in Brain Aging and Age-Associated Disease

title: Modeling Sensory Encoding: Computational Approaches to Feature Detection, Integration, and Adaptation
summary: Sensory encoding is the vital process by which the nervous system transforms physical stimuli into meaningful neural representations. Traditionally, computational neuroscience has characterized this through receptive fields and stimulus-response functions. However, sensory systems do not operate in a vacuum; they must extract relevant features from high-dimensional, noisy environments while constantly adjusting to changing contexts. From the retina’s light adaptation to the auditory system’s frequency tuning, the brain employs sophisticated computational strategies to ensure efficient information transmission. As our ability to record from large sensory populations grows, we are moving beyond simple linear models toward theories that encompass non-linear dynamics, population-level interactions, and the influence of feedback. Understanding these principles is essential for deciphering how the brain constructs a coherent internal map of the external world.

title: Nutritional Risks and Metabolic Disorders in Companion Animals: Diet Composition, Contaminants, and Clinical Outcomes
summary: Nutrition science in companion animals is a dynamic and increasingly important field owing to the pivotal role that diet plays in the health, longevity, and wellbeing of dogs and cats. With companion animals now living longer lives than ever before, there is heightened scrutiny of the ways dietary composition, feeding regimens, and food safety impact metabolic stability and organ function over the long term. While a wide variety of diet options exist—including commercial products, therapeutic foods, homemade meals, and raw or unconventional regimens—significant questions persist regarding the adequacy, safety, and long-term consequences of these practices. Recent studies have brought to light both the therapeutic potential of precision nutrition and the risks posed by nutrient imbalances or contaminants such as mycotoxins and processing byproducts. Ongoing debates continue about optimal formulations, the health value of novel and functional ingredients, and the need for more comprehens
image_alt: Nutritional Risks and Metabolic Disorders in Companion Animals: Diet Composition, Contaminants, and Clinical Outcomes

title: Sex Differences in Schizophrenia : Mechanisms, Trajectories, and Treatment Implications
summary: While sex differences in the presentation, prognosis and treatment of schizophrenia have been recognized for decades, there continues to be a gap in research further elucidating how sex influences the clinical presentation, neurobiology, response to treatment and prognosis of early psychosis and schizophrenia in general. Despite the rates of schizophrenia being roughly equal in males and females, research studies in psychotic disorders are frequently disproportionately male, further contributing to the knowledge gap.

title: Tumor associated neurobehavioral dysfunction in glioblastoma: reviewing mechanisms, models, and therapeutic targets
summary: Glioblastoma (GBM) is not only a highly aggressive brain tumor with poor prognosis but also a major contributor to neurobehavioral dysfunction, profoundly impacting cognition, emotion, and behavior, including impairments in memory, attention, language, and executive function. Despite growing recognition of these effects, the complex interactions between tumor biology and neural circuits remain poorly understood, and effective strategies to preserve neurocognitive function are limited. This Research Topic aims to integrate mechanistic insights, experimental models, and translational approaches to review and advance our understanding of tumor-associated neurobehavioral dysfunction in GBM. We particularly welcome full-length, mini, and systematic review articles exploring tumor-associated neurobehavioral dysfunction in glioblastoma, including underlying mechanisms, experimental models, and therapeutic opportunities. title: Advances in Forest Tree Genomics Evolution and Adaptation
summary: Forest trees are foundational to global terrestrial ecosystems, sustaining biodiversity, regulating climate, and providing essential ecosystem services. As climate change accelerates—bringing rising temperatures, extreme droughts, and shifting precipitation patterns—understanding how forest trees adapt to changing environments has become one of the most urgent scientific challenges of our time. Genomic approaches now offer unprecedented power to decode the genetic and epigenetic mechanisms underlying tree adaptation, enabling evidence-based strategies for forest conservation, restoration, and sustainable management.
image_alt: Advances in Forest Tree Genomics Evolution and Adaptation

title: Aging in Autism: Challenges, Needs, and Best Practices to Support Autistic Adults as they Transition from Mid-life to their Senior Years
summary: According to the U.S. Centers for Disease Control (CDC), 1 in 31 children is diagnosed with autism. But autistic adults remain understudied and under-supported, and these challenges often intensify with age. The transition from midlife to older adulthood (i.e., ages 50+) can bring increased vulnerability related to physical and mental health, access to healthcare and services, financial security, and societal barriers. These difficulties are often compounded by the aging, illness, or loss of family caregivers, placing many older autistic adults at greater risk for age-related diseases, poverty, housing instability, loneliness, and abuse. Despite this, relatively little is known about cognitive and behavioral trajectories in autistic adults as they age, or about the neural mechanisms and correlates that may underlie these changes.
image_alt: Aging in Autism: Challenges, Needs, and Best Practices to Support Autistic Adults as they Transition from Mid-life to their Senior Years

title: At the Nexus of Environment & Ethology: Considerations for the Role of Environmental Cues in Ethological Research
summary: The impact of environment on the health and welfare of nonhuman animals varies widely depending upon a series of species-specific factors, including the target species’ unique physiological needs, social structure, sensory perception, evolutionary history, and the ecological relevance of perceived cues. Thus, evaluating behavioral welfare indicators and the reliability of research conducted with animals in human care and laboratory environments must be founded in a species-specific context rooted in that species’ evolutionary and ecological history. This approach requires careful study design focused on evolutionary relevant and salient cues and/or target constructs accounting for environmental variations and other potential environmental confounds. Further, this requires thoughtful data analysis to account for and address the possibility of these environmental impacts on behavior and cognition.
image_alt: At the Nexus of Environment & Ethology: Considerations for the Role of Environmental Cues in Ethological Research

title: Dance as Medicine: Clinical, Physiological, and Social Perspectives
Mapping Pathways to Suicide Risk in Young Adults: Quarter-Life Crisis and NEET Experiences
summary: Suicide is one of the leading causes of death among people aged 15–29 worldwide. For many young people, suicidal thoughts and behaviours develop during the transition into adulthood, a period that is often associated with important decisions about education, work, relationships, housing and identity. Increasingly, these transitions are becoming longer, less predictable and more difficult to navigate. Some young people feel unable to move into the adult roles they want, while others feel trapped in commitments or circumstances that no longer suit them. These experiences are often described as the “locked-out” and “locked-in” forms of quarter-life crisis. They may contribute to feelings of defeat, entrapment, hopelessness, loneliness and a lack of belonging. Young people who are not in education, employment or training (NEET) may face similar challenges, including loss of routine, financial insecurity, social isolation and reduced contact with support services. title: Open and FAIR Data in Neuroscience, Volume II
summary: The first volume of Open and FAIR Data in Neuroscience brought together contributions showing how findable, accessible, interoperable and reusable data practices are reshaping the way neuroscience is conducted and shared. It closed with a strong body of work and wide readership, reflecting how central data stewardship has become to the field.

title: Sepsis and Septic Shock in Companion Animals: Early Recognition, Biomarkers, and Outcomes
summary: Sepsis and septic shock remain among the most challenging and highest-mortality presentations in veterinary emergency and critical care. Despite growing awareness, the field still lacks consensus on definitions, reliable early-warning biomarkers, and evidence-based resuscitation strategies for dogs, cats, and other companion species. This Research Topic aims to consolidate current knowledge and drive new evidence on the recognition, diagnosis, and management of sepsis across the critical-care continuum.

title: Adaptive Human-Robot Collaboration in Smart Manufacturing: Cognitive Feedback, Dynamic Task Allocation, and Industry 5.0 Integration
summary: The transition toward Industry 5.0 places human wellbeing and operator-centred design at the core of advanced manufacturing systems. Collaborative robots (cobots) are no longer simply tools for automation, they are partners in dynamic, shared workspaces where safety, adaptability, and trust must be continuously negotiated in real time.

title: Edge-Deployed Generative AI for Context-Aware Decision Support in Wearable Robotic Systems
summary: Recent advances in Generative Artificial Intelligence (GenAI), particularly large language models (LLMs), have transformed how machines interpret, reason, and communicate. At the same time, robotics research has made significant progress in edge computing, sensor fusion, and real-time perception systems, enabling deployment in dynamic and resource-constrained environments. Despite these developments, a critical gap remains in the integration of generative AI with embodied robotic systems operating at the edge, especially in wearable robotics such as smart helmets, assistive devices, and human-augmentation systems. Current research topics emphasise either cloud-based intelligence or isolated edge AI solutions, but lack a unified framework for real-time, context-aware decision support that combines perception, reasoning, and action under strict computational constraints.
image_alt: Edge-Deployed Generative AI for Context-Aware Decision Support in Wearable Robotic Systems

title: Effort, Attention, and Arousal: Brain–Body Mechanisms for Performance in the Real World
summary: Sustained performance in high-stakes, real-world environments places extraordinary demands on the human brain and body. Effort, attention, and arousal are three tightly interwoven constructs that together govern how individuals mobilize cognitive and physiological resources to meet these demands. Nowhere is this more critical than in contexts in which humans are expected to perform in high stakes environments. For example, military personnel, first responders, and individuals of the like must maintain peak cognitive performance under conditions of extreme stress, fatigue, sensory overload, and physical exertion. Despite decades of laboratory research, the neural and peripheral mechanisms underpinning the interaction between mental effort, attentional control, and arousal remain incompletely understood — particularly in the demanding and ecologically complex environments that are present in real-world scenarios.

title: From Mechanism to Management: Neuropsychological, Neurobiological, and Psychopathological Foundations of Geriatric Psychiatric Care
summary: Geriatric psychiatry sits at the intersection of neuroscience, psychology, and clinical medicine, addressing the complex mental health challenges that accompany aging. Older adults often present with multifactorial conditions, including depression, anxiety, cognitive decline, psychotic symptoms, medication effects, and sleep disruption, that rarely conform to a single explanatory level. Recent research highlights complex interactions among neurobiological changes, psychopathological presentations, psychopharmacological treatments, and psychosocial variables such as loneliness and autonomy. Despite growing evidence, clinical care models often remain fragmented, with limited integration between neuropsychological assessment, biological mechanisms, and treatment approaches. This integration gap underscores the need for a translational, multidisciplinary framework spanning the continuum from neuropsychological and neurobiological mechanisms to psychopathology and treatment in later life.

title: Functional Neuroimaging Frontiers: Bridging Minds, Methods and Medicine
summary: Functional neuroimaging is a rapidly evolving field at the intersection of neuroscience, engineering, psychology, medicine, and data science. Advances in acquisition, image analysis, functional connectivity, network neuroscience, and computational modelling are expanding the capacity to characterize brain function across scales and contexts. However, important challenges remain in improving reproducibility, interpretability, generalizability, and clinical utility. Current research addresses how brain dynamics support cognition, affect, development, and aging, while also investigating how functional alterations contribute to neurological and psychiatric disorders. Recent studies have demonstrated the value of multimodal integration, machine learning, normative modelling, and large-scale datasets for identifying biologically meaningful patterns and improving prediction. Nevertheless, methodological heterogeneity, limited external validation, unclear mechanistic explanations, and barriers

summary: We are now in the third decade of the 21st Century, and, especially in the last years, the achievements made by scientists have been exceptional, leading to major advancements in the fast-growing field of Adolescent and Young Adult Psychiatry.

title: Predictive motor control and internal models
summary: Skilled motor behaviour relies on the central nervous system’s capacity to predict, rather than merely react to, the sensory consequences of its own actions. From reaching for a cup of coffee to maintaining balance on a moving train, every voluntary movement relies on the central nervous system’s ability to anticipate the sensory consequences of its own actions. This predictive capacity is thought to be supported by internal models: neural representations of the body and the external world that allow the brain to estimate forthcoming states and select appropriate motor commands. Forward models predict the sensory outcomes of motor actions, while inverse models compute the motor commands required to achieve a desired sensory or kinematic goal. Together, they form the computational backbone of skilled, flexible, and adaptive behaviour, and their disruption is increasingly recognised as a hallmark of several neurological and psychiatric conditions.
image_alt: Predictive motor control and internal models

title: Psychological Factors in Physical Education and Sport - Volume VIII
Push the System: Stimulation, Pharmacology, and Closed-Loop Tests of Cognitive Mechanisms
summary: Cognitive processes such as attention, perception, memory, executive function, and social cognition emerge from dynamic interactions between distributed neural systems. While correlational methods like neuroimaging and electrophysiology have mapped these networks extensively, they cannot establish whether a given neural signature is necessary or sufficient for a cognitive function. Causal interventions—including non-invasive brain stimulation (TMS, tDCS, tACS), pharmacological manipulation, and closed-loop neurofeedback systems—offer a powerful complement, allowing researchers to directly perturb neural systems and observe the behavioral consequences. Advances in real-time signal processing and adaptive stimulation now make it possible to test cognitive theories with unprecedented precision and mechanistic specificity.

title: Shedding light on Myalgic Encephalomyelitis/Chronic Fatigue Syndrome (ME/CFS) Vol II
summary: Chronic Fatigue Syndrome (CFS), also called Myalgic Encephalomyelitis (ME) is a disabling neurological condition affecting millions of people worldwide. ME/CFS is characterized by persistent and unexplained fatigue, post-exertional malaise, cognitive impairments, and a range of other symptoms such as pain, sleep disturbances, and gastrointestinal issues. Despite the significant impact on patients' lives and the number of sufferers, ME/CFS remains poorly understood, stigmatized, and lacks effective treatments.

title: The Next Era of Remote Patient Monitoring: Wearables, Digital Biomarkers, Artificial Intelligence, and Personalized Chronic Disease Care
summary: Chronic diseases remain the dominant driver of healthcare utilization, disability, and cost, yet care delivery continues to rely heavily on episodic encounters, delayed symptom reporting, and reactive treatment adjustment. Remote patient monitoring is rapidly evolving from simple physiologic data capture into a broader infrastructure for continuous, personalized, and proactive care. This Research Topic aims to examine how wearables, connected sensors, digital biomarkers, artificial intelligence, and closed-loop therapeutic models can transform chronic disease management across clinical settings.
image_alt: The Next Era of Remote Patient Monitoring: Wearables, Digital Biomarkers, Artificial Intelligence, and Personalized Chronic Disease Care

title: Young Brains at Play: Advances in Pediatric Sports Concussion
summary: Sports-related concussions represent one of the most common injuries in children and adolescents participating in organized athletics. Each year, thousands of pediatric athletes worldwide experience concussive events, with the actual incidence likely underestimated due to underreporting and variances in awareness and diagnostic practices. Pediatric athletes are not simply “small adults”; their developing brains, unique biomechanics, and evolving cognitive and emotional profiles demand specialized approaches that consider both immediate safety and lifelong neurological health. This collection serves as a platform for multidisciplinary voices to address the complex medical, scientific, and societal challenges surrounding pediatric sports concussion.

title: Antimicrobial Therapy in Zoological Collections
summary: The management of infectious diseases in zoological collections has become increasingly complex, particularly as antimicrobial resistance (AMR) emerges as one of the most pressing global health threats. Zoological animals-ranging from large mammals to reptiles, amphibians, birds, fish, and invertebrates-present unique physiological and ecological characteristics that challenge conventional antimicrobial decision‑making. Yet, despite this diversity, antimicrobial therapy in these species often relies on extrapolations from domestic animals or empirical protocols, leaving substantial gaps in dosing accuracy, therapeutic efficacy, and stewardship.

title: Prenatal Maternal Factors and Offspring Brain Development: Neuroimaging and Neuropsychological Outcomes
summary: The maternal-fetal interface represents a dynamic environment where maternal health, lifestyle, and environmental exposures directly interact with fetal brain development. Emerging evidence suggests that maternal factors during pregnancy — including physical activity, nutrition, stress, and metabolic and immune profiles — play a crucial role in shaping the offspring’s neuropsychological outcomes. However, the precise cognitive, behavioral, and emotional consequences of these prenatal influences, and the brain pathways that underlie them, have yet to be fully elucidated.

title: Screen Time and the Developing Brain: Implications for Cognition, Mental Health, and Neurodevelopmental Disorders
summary: Children and adolescents are growing up in an environment saturated with screens. Smartphones, tablets, gaming consoles, and social media platforms now shape how young people learn, socialize, and regulate emotion, often from the first years of life. As recreational and educational screen use continues to climb, parents, educators, clinicians, and public health authorities are asking urgent questions about what this means for the developing brain. A growing body of evidence links excessive or poorly contextualized screen exposure to changes in attention, executive function, language acquisition, sleep, and socio-emotional regulation. At the same time, screens can support learning, connection, and access to health information when used well. The picture is further complicated for children with, or at risk of, neurodevelopmental conditions such as ADHD and autism spectrum disorder, where screen use patterns may both reflect and reinforce underlying vulnerabilities. title: Advancing Animal Welfare Assessment: From Biomarkers to Smart Monitoring Technologies - Volume II
summary: The definition of animal welfare has undergone a significant transformation, evolving from the focus on physical health to a more holistic approach that includes behavior, emotional states, and the ability of animals to cope with continuous and dynamic environmental changes. Respecting species-specific ethological needs has become central to the ethics and sustainability of animal husbandry and management systems. However, growing societal expectations and the climate emergency demand a deeper understanding of animal stress, including behavioral plasticity and physiological adaptations to environmental stressors. In this context, technologies such as wearable sensors and AI-driven behavioral analysis enable real-time, non-invasive monitoring of welfare indicators alongside the concurrent use of biomarkers and metabolites, assessed through robust and reliable techniques, provides valuable insights into animals’ stress conditions.

title: Connectome-Preserving Glioma Resection and Immunotherapy: Synergistic Strategies
summary: Gliomas remain among the most challenging malignancies in neuro-oncology due to their infiltrative growth, functional eloquence, and profound intratumoral heterogeneity. Advances in connectomics, functional neuroimaging, and awake mapping have shifted surgical paradigms from purely anatomical resection toward preservation of large-scale brain networks critical for cognition and quality of life. In parallel, immune-based therapies, including vaccines, cellular therapies, viral vectors, and checkpoint modulation, have expanded rapidly, yet with limited durable success in glioma. Increasing evidence suggests that the biological and immunological consequences of surgery, including extent and pattern of resection, may directly influence immune responsiveness. Understanding how connectome-preserving surgical strategies interact with tumor biology and host immunity is therefore essential to optimize combined multimodal treatment approaches.

title: Edge-AI Sensor Fusion for UAV-Based Perception in Large-Scale Surveillance and Environmental Monitoring
summary: Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) equipped with multi-sensor payloads (cameras, LiDAR, multispectral and thermal imagers) are increasingly deployed for large-scale surveillance and environmental monitoring, from infrastructure inspection to crop health assessment and wildlife tracking. These deployments generate large volumes of heterogeneous sensor data that must be processed reliably, often with limited onboard compute and intermittent connectivity to centralized systems. Edge-AI addresses this by moving perception and decision-making closer to the sensor, reducing latency and bandwidth demands while enabling real-time response in the field. Achieving robust perception under these conditions requires effective fusion of multiple sensor modalities, lightweight models suited to onboard hardware, and architectures that remain reliable across varied, often unpredictable environments.

title: Microbiomes in Animal Production: From Host Health and Welfare to Productivity and Resilience
summary: The animal microbiome has emerged as a key determinant of health, welfare, productivity, and resilience across diverse animal production systems. Beyond its traditional role in digestion and nutrient utilization, the microbiome influences immune function, disease susceptibility, behavior, stress responses, reproductive performance, and adaptation to environmental challenges. Growing advances in sequencing technologies, multi-omics approaches, and computational biology have expanded our understanding of host–microbiome interactions and their implications for sustainable animal production.

title: Promotion of Camelid Health for Enhanced Productivity and Well-Being of Communities
summary: Camelids—including dromedaries, Bactrian camels, alpacas, llamas, guanacos, and vicuñas—play an essential role in the livelihoods of millions of people, particularly in arid, semi-arid, and high-altitude regions. Their contribution spans food security, transportation, wool production, environmental adaptation, and socio-cultural heritage. However, the performance and productivity of camelid populations remain below their potential, hindered by persistent health constraints, limited disease surveillance, and insufficient institutional support. Despite their expanding significance in traditional and emerging production systems, camelid health research continues to lag behind that of other livestock species. The epidemiology of infectious and parasitic diseases, the economic impacts of production losses, and the zoonotic risks at the human–animal–ecosystem interface remain inadequately elucidated, representing critical gaps in knowledge and practice. title: Short-lived climate pollutants
summary: This Scientific Reports Collection invites research on short-lived climate pollutants (SLCPs) and their climate-air quality linkages. Topics include key SLCPs such as methane, tropospheric ozone and its precursors, and black carbon, as well as their dual impacts and underlying mechanisms.

title: The regulatory continuum: computational mechanisms of adaptive, pathological, and therapeutic brain state transitions
summary: The central challenge for the next generation of computational psychiatry is to move beyond descriptive accounts of dysfunction toward mechanistic models of brain-state regulation. While we recognize that adaptive cognition and clinical vulnerability exist along a regulatory continuum, the specific computational principles governing how the brain maintains stability while permitting necessary transitions remain underdeveloped.

title: Trends in behavioral endocrinology
summary: This Research Topic is part of the annual “Trends in Behavioral Endocrinology” series, which highlights new research on the neuroendocrine mechanisms underlying behavior. It brings together work on how hormones and neuropeptides interact with neural circuits, internal physiological state, developmental stage, and the social environment to regulate behavior. Behavioral neuroendocrinology continues to evolve as a field through the application of modern approaches to the study of endocrine regulation of behavior. Technical advances including transcriptomics, neural imaging, computational analyses and novel anatomical methods have enabled finer dissection of the neural circuitry that regulates hormone-dependent behavior and have helped reveal how hormones act through complex, context-dependent interactions with the nervous system. Comparative studies across diverse taxa continue to inform and deepen our understanding of general principles that underlie neural function.

title: Methods in Neuroergonomics
summary: The breadth of application contexts served by neuroergonomics ranges from controlled laboratory studies of cognitive load and fatigue to field deployments in aviation cockpits, clinical rehabilitation settings, and everyday consumer environments. Neuroergonomics draws on an unusually wide methodological repertoire. Researchers in the field routinely combine neuroimaging modalities, including electroencephalography, functional near-infrared spectroscopy, and functional magnetic resonance imaging with peripheral physiological measures such as electrocardiography, electrodermal activity, and electromyography, alongside eye tracking, behavioural instrumentation, and increasingly, wearable and mobile sensing platforms. This applicable breadth and methodological diversity places extraordinary demands on the methods themselves. The contributions span three complementary strands. The first addresses the science of creativity, contemplative practice, and embodied cognition, drawing on invited talks and working sessions that examined how music, dance, and meditation can serve as rigorous experimental paradigms rather than peripheral applications, and how brain-body dynamics unfold during live artistic and contemplative activity. summary: Animal health decision-making increasingly intersects with broader societal challenges such as food security, livelihoods, animal welfare, climate change, and public health. Traditional economic approaches, while essential, often capture only part of these multidimensional impacts. There is a growing need for frameworks that can jointly assess economic, social, and environmental consequences—reflecting the true societal burden of animal diseases and their control.

title: Surgical and Healthcare-Worker Neuroergonomics
summary: Healthcare is among the most cognitively demanding and high-stakes forms of skilled work. Surgeons, anaesthetists, nurses, intensive-care and emergency staff, and trainees must sustain attention, integrate complex information, make rapid decisions, and perform precise motor actions, often under time pressure, interruption, and fatigue. The consequences of momentary lapses can be severe for patients and clinicians alike. Neuroergonomics offers a powerful lens on these demands by measuring the brain and body at work, using electroencephalography, functional near-infrared spectroscopy, heart rate variability, electrodermal activity, eye tracking, pupillometry, and wearable sensing to quantify the cognitive and physiological states of healthcare workers during real and simulated clinical tasks.

title: Advancing Welfare Science for Understudied Species
summary: Animal welfare science has expanded rapidly over recent decades, yet significant gaps remain in our understanding of the needs and experiences of many taxa, particularly invertebrates, fish, amphibians, and reptiles. These groups comprise the vast majority of animal biodiversity and are increasingly represented across human-managed contexts, including laboratories, zoos and aquariums, veterinary practice, aquaculture and mini-livestock industries, and conservation programs both in situ and ex situ. Despite their widespread presence and growing ethical consideration, welfare research for these species remains comparatively fragmented, taxonomically uneven, and often siloed by discipline and setting.
image_alt: Advancing Welfare Science for Understudied Species

title: Computational and Theoretical Approaches to Autism: From Neural Mechanisms to Behavior
summary: Marking World Autism Awareness Day 2026, this Research Topic aims to bring together computational, theoretical, and data-driven studies that advance a mechanistic understanding of autism across multiple levels of analysis, from synaptic and circuit-level processes to large-scale brain dynamics, cognition, and behavior.

title: Decoding the Gut-Brain Axis: Implications for Neurodegenerative Disease Therapies, Volume II
summary: The gut-brain axis is a bidirectional communication network linking the gastrointestinal tract, its resident microbiota, and the central nervous system through neural, immune, endocrine, and metabolic routes. Disruption of this axis is increasingly implicated in the onset and progression of neurodegenerative diseases such as Alzheimer’s and Parkinson’s, as well as in neurodevelopmental conditions including autism spectrum disorder, ADHD, and Down syndrome. Building on the success of the first volume, which brought together advances on diet, microbial diversity, vagal signalling, and immune crosstalk, the field has moved rapidly toward translation. Live biotherapeutic products, postbiotics, faecal microbiota transplantation, and dietary interventions are entering clinical trials, while machine learning and multi-omics are reshaping how researchers model host-microbe-brain interactions. A second volume is therefore timely to capture the next wave of mechanistic, translational, and comput
image_alt: Decoding the Gut-Brain Axis: Implications for Neurodegenerative Disease Therapies, Volume II

title: Female Genital Mutilation/Cutting: Addressing the Evidence Gaps
summary: Female genital mutilation/cutting (FGM/C) is a serious, widespread and persistent threat to the health of women, girls, and communities worldwide. Existing evidence about FGM/C’s drivers, risk factors, epidemiologic profile, and health complications are well documented. However, there are areas of inquiry that remain under-explored in current evidence, limiting governments, institutions, and donors’ ability to make progress in both preventing the practice and improving the quality of life for people with FGM/C. This collection aims to address the specific gaps detailed below by focusing on under-explored areas of inquiry related to FGM/C, including life-course and social determinants perspectives.

title: Lipids in Cell Biology 2026
summary: Advances in lipid detection methods and techniques to probe lipid functions continues to uncover roles beyond containment, from organelle morphology, metabolic signaling, cell death, and energy metabolism. This collection invites submissions from all disciplines with insights into lipid function, regulation or detection.

title: Neurobiology of stress and resilience: Mechanisms and coping strategies from a Human Neuroscience perspective, Volume II
summary: The experience of stress is an inevitable part of human life, affecting individuals physically, emotionally, and psychologically. From brief tension-filled moments to chronic stress exposure, the resulting impact on the human brain is profound, influencing neural circuits and even altering brain function. Despite its potential detriments, stress also presents an opportunity for resilience—an adaptive response enabling individuals to maintain mental health despite adversity. This area of research is crucial for advancing our understanding of how resilience is cultivated and how stress can be managed effectively to prevent stress-related disorders. The field of human neuroscience offers valuable insights into the underlying biological mechanisms that govern stress responses and resilience building.

The introduction of newer technologies, software and increasing understanding of brain physiology in neurological and psychiatric conditions have shaped this rapidly growing field. To create a space where all stakeholders could freely interact to discuss challenges, advancements and opportunities in the field, the first Deep Brain Stimulation (DBS) Think Tank took place in 2012 in Gainesville Florida at the University of Florida. Since then, the meeting has grown to a hybrid virtual and in person meeting expanding the number of participants to over 200 world experts in the field.

summary: The field of embodied robotics has experienced a significant paradigm shift toward understanding how a robot’s physical structure (morphology) and its adaptive control mechanisms (learning) co-evolve to produce intelligent behaviors. Traditional approaches have often treated morphology and learning as separate design components, but recent perspectives emphasize that their interaction is essential for achieving higher levels of autonomy and adaptability. Studies inspired by natural developmental processes have demonstrated the potential of integrated developmental strategies in improving robot performance across dynamic tasks. However, key conflicts remain unresolved. title: Transdiagnostic affective neuroscience: from negative affect to anhedonia and cognitive control.
summary: Research in psychiatry and clinical neuroscience is increasingly recognizing that negative affect and anhedonia are not confined to a single diagnostic category. Traditionally, most research on these symptoms has been conducted within single-diagnosis frameworks, treating depression, bipolar disorder, schizophrenia spectrum disorders, and anxiety-related conditions as largely separate research literatures. This separation limits understanding of the shared neural and cognitive mechanisms that link reduced positive affect to impaired cognitive control across conditions. While several studies have pointed to overlapping reward and executive control circuits across diagnoses, critical questions remain about how these mechanisms interact, whether they follow a common trajectory, and how they can be reliably measured and targeted for intervention. title: Translational Advances in Alzheimer’s and other Neurodegenerative Dementias (NDDs): (Bio-)Molecular Mechanisms, Biomarkers and Therapies
summary: Alzheimer’s disease (AD) is the most common type of neurodegenerative dementia (NDD) afflicting the elderly, accounting for roughly 60% to 80% of cases irrespective of the collective prevalence of the other three NDD types: vascular dementia (VaD), Lewy body dementia (LBD) and frontotemporal lobar dementia (FTLD). NDD types are stratified according to their characteristic (bio-)molecular mechanisms of action, their direct or indirect dysregulation of basal cellular bioactivities and the biological pathways these subsume, their irreversible manifested symptoms, and the brain regions exhibiting unrelenting intracellular and extracellular dysfunction or disruptive breakdown of intercellular cross-talk, both of which ultimately yield, induce or arise from progressive neuronal cell death.

summary: Aquaculture is the fastest-growing animal food production sector globally and plays a critical role in food security, livelihoods, and economic development. As the sector continues to expand, ensuring high standards of animal welfare has become both a scientific priority and an increasingly important expectation of producers, retailers, policymakers, investors, and consumers. Fish and crustacean welfare are now recognised as a fundamental component of sustainable aquaculture, with implications not only for ethical food production, but also for animal health, resilience, productivity, product quality, environmental sustainability, and social licence to operate.

summary: Embodied intelligence arises from the dynamic coupling of brain, body, environment, and other agents. In biological systems, adaptive behaviour is grounded in sensorimotor loops through which neural processes continuously integrate perception, action, prediction, memory, and learning. Body morphology, material properties, and physical dynamics are not passive constraints, but active resources that shape computation and behaviour.

summary: Clinical research has long rested on a familiar triad: the randomized trial, the carefully curated cohort, and the cross-sectional survey. Each has its strengths, and each has its blind spots. Trials give us causality but often at great cost and with narrow generalizability. Cohorts offer longitudinal depth but can suffer from attrition and evolving practice patterns. Surveys provide breadth and currency but limited temporal insight. For decades, these data streams have largely run in parallel, occasionally informing one another but rarely being analyzed together with the tools now at our disposal.

title: Manifold Geometry and Scalable Computation for Brain Dynamics
summary: Understanding brain dynamics increasingly requires geometric methods to describe high dimensional activity. This is especially important for models and datasets that span multiple scales, from local circuits to whole-brain networks. These geometric approaches must also support comparisons across individual subjects, population-scale simulations, parameter ensembles, and perturbation studies. These approaches face three connected challenges: (1) brain activity is high dimensional and requires interpretable geometric descriptions, (2) manifold structure must be compared across subjects, models, parameters, and perturbations, and (3) multiarea simulations are computationally expensive and must be interpreted in biologically meaningful ways. Manifold approaches can help organize high-dimensional neural activity into interpretable structures.
