title: Tracing Begomovirus Evolution: Phylogeographic Insights and Computational Innovations
summary: Begomoviruses represent one of the most destructive and rapidly emerging groups of plant pathogens worldwide. Transmitted primarily by the whitefly (Bemisia tabaci) cryptic species complex, these single-stranded DNA viruses threaten global food security by causing devastating diseases in essential agricultural crops. The rapid diversification of begomoviruses is driven by high mutation rates, frequent genetic recombination, and interactions with DNA satellites. Furthermore, globalized agricultural trade and climate-driven range expansions of their insect vectors have accelerated the transcontinental dissemination of these pathogens, making them a pressing and continuous challenge for modern agricultural sustainability and global plant health.

title: Trustworthy AI for Human Behavior Understanding and Security
summary: Recent advances in artificial intelligence have significantly enhanced the ability of intelligent systems to perceive, model, and predict human behaviors using multimodal sensing data collected from cameras, wearable devices, mobile platforms, and immersive technologies. These capabilities have enabled numerous applications, including human activity recognition, behavioral biometrics, user authentication, healthcare monitoring, and human-computer interaction. However, the increasing reliance on AI-driven behavioral analysis also raises critical concerns regarding the trustworthiness, security, privacy, and robustness of these systems. Emerging threats such as adversarial attacks, synthetic behavior generation, AI-generated motion trajectories, and data manipulation challenge the reliability of AI-based decision-making. title: Advancing Smart Healthcare: Integrating AI and IoT for Enhanced Patient Care and System Efficiency
summary: Smart healthcare systems are undergoing rapid transformation through the convergence of the Internet of Things (IoT) and Artificial Intelligence (AI). Together, these technologies enable continuous patient monitoring, predictive analytics, and automated clinical decision support, promising improvements in care quality, operational efficiency, and personalization of treatment. Wearable sensors, connected medical devices, and remote monitoring platforms now generate vast streams of physiological data that, when processed with AI, can support early detection of clinical deterioration and better management of chronic diseases such as diabetes, cardiovascular conditions, and respiratory illness.

summary: The avian gastrointestinal microbiome is now recognized as a central regulator of physiological function in birds, exerting profound effects on nutrient metabolism, immune system development, endocrine signaling, barrier integrity, and overall health. As birds encounter nutritional imbalances, environmental stressors, and immunological challenges across diverse settings, host–microbiome interactions have become critical determinants of physiological resilience.

title: Aging brain: Brain health and neuroprotective strategies, Volume II
summary: As global life expectancy continues to rise, understanding the complexities of the aging brain has become increasingly critical. Aging, while a natural process, brings about structural and functional changes in the brain that can affect cognitive health and overall neurological function. These changes can lead to age-related cognitive decline and an increased risk of neurodegenerative diseases such as Alzheimer's and Parkinson's. Research in this area is crucial to unraveling the mechanisms that drive these changes and identifying the factors that can help maintain brain health and functionality throughout aging.

title: Biomarkers of Post-Traumatic Stress Disorder: Towards Translational Tools to Uncover Underlying Biochemical Profiles
summary: Advances in biotechnology in the era of Genome-Wide Association analyses and multi-omics investigations are shedding light on many previously inaccessible aspects of biomedicine, and this is particularly true for applied research in clinical psychiatry and mental illness. In fact, psychiatric disorders have revealed multifaceted features requiring interdisciplinary assessments and personalized healthcare platforms. If the constant updating of in-depth diagnostic tools for psychiatric illnesses with detailed and more precise criteria and the spread of the concept of psychopathological spectrum of a given behavioral health issue have significantly improved treatment strategies in psychiatry, in parallel, the discovery of new biological substrates underlying mental disorders through the application of emerging biotechnologies are supposed to provide the basis for developing increasingly appropriate therapies.

title: CNS Immune Cell Compartmentalization and Neuroinflammation
summary: Neuroimmunology has demonstrated that T cells residing in the human brain constitute a distinct, tissue-adapted lymphocyte population. Unlike their circulating counterparts, these resident T cells exist within a highly regulated and privileged central nervous system (CNS) environment. A surge in the availability of post-mortem brain tissue, alongside powerful omics and neuroimaging tools, has begun to clarify the unique attributes and behaviors of CNS-resident lymphocytes. In conditions such as multiple sclerosis (MS), there is mounting evidence that these populations do not merely infiltrate the CNS during acute inflammation but occupy specialized niches—most notably within the meninges and perivascular spaces—and interact closely with resident B cells and myeloid cells. Despite advances using both human samples and animal models, fundamental questions remain regarding the precise mechanisms of lymphocyte compartmentalization, their residency programs, and their persistent role in MS

title: Circadian–Melatonin Axis in Systemic Disease: From Molecular Mechanisms to Precision Medicine
summary: The circadian system orchestrates physiological processes across multiple organ systems, maintaining homeostasis through tightly regulated molecular clocks. As a primary endocrine signal, melatonin plays a pivotal role in synchronizing circadian rhythms with environmental cues and modulating diverse biological functions, including metabolism, immune surveillance, and cellular stress adaptation.
image_alt: Circadian–Melatonin Axis in Systemic Disease: From Molecular Mechanisms to Precision Medicine

title: Climate Change, Emerging Pollutant Exposure and Mental Health
summary: Climate change and emerging environmental pollutants are increasingly recognized as critical determinants of mental health worldwide. Rapid urbanization, rising ambient temperatures, and extreme weather events have been associated with elevated risks of depression, anxiety, sleep disturbances, and other neuropsychiatric outcomes. At the same time, exposure to emerging pollutants, including microplastics, per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS), endocrine-disrupting chemicals, artificial light at night (ALAN), and novel airborne contaminants, may adversely affect brain and mental health through pathways involving neuroinflammation, oxidative stress, endocrine disruption, circadian dysregulation, and alterations in brain structure or functional connectivity. Although growing evidence supports the independent effects of climate-related stressors and pollutant exposures on mental health, their combined and interactive impacts remain insufficiently understood. title: Climate Changes, Ecological Shifts, and Human Adaptation: Insights from Pleistocene to Holocene Paleoecology in Mediterranean and Central Europe
summary: The interactions between human populations and their environments across the Mediterranean Basin and Central Europe have been marked by significant climatic and ecological changes from the early Pleistocene to the Holocene. A palaeoecological perspective provides crucial insights into how ancient human communities adapted to these changing conditions. Current research emphasizes reconstructing past environments and understanding the intricacies of human adaptation through diverse evidence such as palynological and anthracological analyses, faunal studies, climatic reconstructions, and isotopic and biomolecular techniques. Despite advancements in these areas, comprehensive analyses that integrate multiple lines of evidence are needed to fully grasp how humans historically interacted with and adapted to diverse ecosystems.

title: Clinical Management in Huntington Disease: Experimental Therapies to Comprehensive Care
summary: Huntington Disease (HD) represents one of the most complex and debilitating hereditary neurodegenerative disorders, profoundly affecting motor control, cognition, and mental health. It is caused by an expanded CAG trinucleotide repeat in the huntingtin gene (HTT), which leads to progressive neuronal dysfunction and death. Although significant progress has been made in understanding the genetic and molecular underpinnings of HD, the translation of these findings into effective disease-modifying therapies remains an unmet challenge. Current interventions are limited to symptomatic treatment, supportive care, and lifestyle adaptations aimed at preserving functional capacity. Recent studies have highlighted evolving approaches such as RNA-based therapies, gene-editing technologies, and modulators of protein homeostasis as promising, yet still experimental, avenues. title: Computational and Mathematical Models in Vision (MODVIS)
Computational frameworks for decision-making: From bayesian inference to reinforcement learning models
summary: The ability to make adaptive decisions in uncertain environments is a fundamental characteristic of biological intelligence. Historically, computational neuroscience has utilized two dominant paradigms to explain this behavior: Bayesian Inference, which describes how organisms maintain and update internal representations of the world, and Reinforcement Learning (RL), which details how agents learn optimal actions through trial and error. While Bayesian models excel at capturing the integration of prior knowledge with sensory evidence, RL frameworks provide a robust account of value-based learning and the role of neuromodulators like dopamine. Recently, the boundary between these two fields has blurred, leading to "Bayesian Reinforcement Learning" and other hybrid architectures. Despite this progress, understanding how the brain physically implements these complex algorithms across different temporal and structural scales remains a cornerstone challenge in modern neuroscience.

title: Cybersickness and Wellbeing in Immersive XR and AR
summary: Immersive technologies, including virtual, augmented, and mixed reality, collectively known as extended reality (XR), are moving rapidly from laboratories and specialist applications into training, industry, healthcare, education, and everyday consumer life. As head-mounted displays and augmented-reality glasses become lighter, cheaper, and more capable, people are spending longer and more frequent periods in immersive environments. This shift brings the physiological and cognitive costs of immersion into sharp focus. The nausea, disorientation, and oculomotor discomfort that many users experience, known as cybersickness, remains one of the most persistent barriers to comfortable, sustained XR use. It sits alongside visual fatigue arising from vergence-accommodation conflict, cognitive fatigue during prolonged tasks, and broader questions of comfort, accessibility, and wellbeing.
image_alt: Cybersickness and Wellbeing in Immersive XR and AR

title: Depression and Mood Disorders in Neurological Comorbidities: Pathophysiology, Risk Prediction, and Intervention
summary: Depression and mood disorders represent the most prevalent neuropsychiatric complications of neurological disorders. The prevalence of post-stroke depression ranges from 27% to 33%, and up to 38% of patients with Parkinson’s disease experience comorbid depression — both rates are significantly higher than that observed in the general population. Comorbid mood disorders markedly impede neurological functional recovery, elevate disability and mortality rates, and exacerbate long-term healthcare burdens. Currently, clinical diagnosis relies heavily on subjective rating scales. The underlying pathophysiological mechanisms of these comorbid conditions remain incompletely elucidated, and there is a critical lack of reliable early biomarkers, individualized risk stratification tools, and precision intervention regimens in clinical practice.
image_alt: Depression and Mood Disorders in Neurological Comorbidities: Pathophysiology, Risk Prediction, and Intervention

title: Integrative Genomics, Data Science, and Systems Modeling for Plant Resilience in Changing Environments
summary: Plant resilience research increasingly examines how plants adapt to interacting abiotic and biotic stresses in changing environments. Climate change is producing more frequent combinations of heat, drought, salinity, flooding and pathogens, challenging conventional approaches to studying plant performance. Advances in genomics, transcriptomics, proteomics, metabolomics, epigenomics, phenomics and environmental sensing have generated extensive datasets, but these are often produced at different scales and analyzed separately. Recent studies indicate that integrating multi-omics, phenotypic and environmental information can reveal regulatory networks, stress-response pathways and biomarkers associated with adaptation. Machine learning, artificial intelligence, network inference and systems modeling offer further opportunities to predict genotype–phenotype–environment interactions. title: Integrative Perspectives on CSF Biomarkers in the Phenotyping and Management of Multiple Sclerosis
summary: Cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) analysis has long been an essential tool in the study and management of neurological diseases, particularly multiple sclerosis (MS). While the presence of CSF-restricted oligoclonal bands has historically played a role in MS diagnosis, emerging biomarkers such as kappa-neurofilament light chains and brain-specific proteins are increasingly recognized for their value in characterizing disease activity, predicting progression, and understanding underlying pathophysiological mechanisms. Despite significant advances, ambiguity remains in differentiating MS phenotypes and forecasting individual patient trajectories. Critical areas of debate persist regarding the specificity, sensitivity, and prognostic utility of a range of CSF biomarkers, as well as their utility in evaluating treatment response and disease modification. title: Intelligent Manipulation of Space Robots: Environmental Perception, Autonomous Decision-Making, and Dexterous Operations
summary: Space robots are becoming indispensable for next-generation space missions, including on-orbit servicing, station maintenance, spacecraft inspection, debris removal, and planetary exploration. These missions require robots to operate in unattended, safety-critical, and highly uncertain space environments. Non-cooperative targets, complex contact conditions, changing illumination, communication delay, limited onboard resources, and microgravity-induced coupling impose major challenges on environmental perception, motion planning, and closed-loop control. These characteristics make traditional operation modes based on ground planning and predefined trajectories insufficient for demanding on-orbit tasks. Recent advances in artificial intelligence, learning-based control, multi-sensor fusion, and digital twin technology offer promising pathways toward autonomous, dexterous manipulation in space. title: Interpretable and Explainable AI for Trustworthy Clinical Decision Support
summary: Artificial intelligence is transforming healthcare, supporting clinicians in diagnosis, prognosis, treatment planning, and monitoring. Yet clinical adoption remains limited by low transparency, insufficient trust, and uncertainty about the reliability of AI recommendations. Post-hoc methods such as SHAP, LIME, and Grad-CAM have improved interpretability, but attention is shifting toward intrinsically interpretable AI, where transparency is built into the model itself.

title: Legal and ethical reforms for neurotechnological advancements in the global south: perspective and challenges, Volume II
summary: Advancements in neurotechnology are heralding new possibilities for enhancing human health and cognitive abilities. However, these innovations also bring to the fore significant ethical, legal, and social challenges, particularly in the spheres of mental privacy and autonomy. Traditionally, the discourse on neuroethics has been shaped by perspectives from the global North, often overlooking the distinct socio-economic and cultural contexts of countries in the global South. These white spots in neuroethical deliberations are critical, seeing as these regions grapple with unique challenges such as high income inequality, limited healthcare infrastructure, and significant linguistic and cultural diversity.

title: Mental Health and Resilience in Aging Populations: Insurance Systems, Risk Factors, and Public Health Strategies
summary: Population aging is one of the defining public health challenges of this century: by 2050, the global population aged 60 and older will nearly double, and mental health conditions—particularly depression, anxiety, and social isolation—remain among the most under-recognized and under-treated health burdens in this group. The World Health Organization estimates that a significant share of older adults experience a mental or neurological disorder, yet mental health services for this population remain fragmented, underfunded, and inconsistently integrated with physical health care. A structural factor underlying much of this fragmentation has received comparatively little research attention: the design of health and long-term care insurance systems, which shapes who can access mental health services, at what cost, and with what downstream effect on care utilization and caregiver wellbeing. title: Metastatic Niches Uncovered: Organ-Specific Mechanisms Driving Brain, Bone, Lung, and Liver Metastases
summary: Metastasis remains the leading cause of cancer-related death, yet therapeutic progress continues to lag behind advances in our understanding of primary tumor biology. Growing evidence shows that metastatic spread is not a uniform process but is heavily influenced by organ-specific microenvironments, or metastatic “niches.” Unique biological, immunological, and metabolic characteristics within the brain, bone, lung, and liver actively affect tumor colonization, survival, and growth.

title: Microbial Regulation of Plant Stress Signaling: From Ethylene and Hormonal Control to Field-Resilient Crops
summary: Microbial regulation of plant stress signaling is emerging as a decisive lever in how crops withstand a changing climate. As drought, salinity, flooding, heat, and metal contamination become more frequent and more likely to occur together, plants respond through hormonal networks in which ethylene has a central role. The hormone governs germination, root development, nodulation, and senescence, yet its sustained accumulation under stress restricts root elongation, limits water and nutrient acquisition, and constrains yield. Plant-associated microorganisms intervene directly at this point: rhizobacteria and endophytes producing 1-aminocyclopropane-1-carboxylate (ACC) deaminase cleave the immediate precursor of ethylene and lower its stress-induced accumulation, while phytohormone production, osmolyte and exopolysaccharide synthesis, antioxidant activity, volatile signaling, and nutrient solubilization act on the same physiological outcome through complementary routes.

Myelitis especially idiopathic and immune mediated myelitis
summary: In the field of neurology, understanding the mechanisms of myelitis, particularly idiopathic and immune-mediated types, is crucial. Multiple sclerosis (MS) is a condition that can affect both the brain and spinal cord, yet approximately 20% of patients do not present with lesions in the spinal cord. Conversely, why do some patients have spinal cord predominant MS? Why do some cases of NMOSD present with area postrema, brainstem, or cerebral syndromes, while others present with longitudinally extensive cord lesions? This raises key questions about the factors that direct inflammation preferentially to the spinal cord instead of the brain.

title: Photobiomodulation in Stroke: Delivery, Dosimetry, and Clinical Validation
summary: Stroke remains a leading cause of long-term disability, and neurorecovery options remain sparse. Photobiomodulation therapy (PBMT), the application of red and near-infrared light (600–1100 nm) to biological tissue, has emerged as a non-invasive, adjunctive, and promising modality. In PBMT, photons are absorbed by cellular chromophores, including ion channels and mitochondrial complexes, which are then activated to produce ATP, signaling molecules, and transcription factors instrumental in cellular cascades that promote healing. PBMT reduces inflammation, pain, and edema, and enhances cellular and tissue regeneration and blood flow. Preclinical work in stroke has shown that PBMT contributes to increased cerebral blood flow, modulation of inflammatory cytokines, release of neurotrophic factors (BDNF, NGF, GDNF), vascular growth and endothelial repair factors, and synaptic plasticity. title: Psychobiotics and Food-Derived Neuroactives: Pharmacological Pathways to Mental Well-being
summary: The interplay between diet, the gut microbiome, and brain function has emerged as a promising frontier in neuropharmacology. Increasing evidence indicates that food-derived bioactive compounds and psychobiotics (beneficial microorganisms strains capable of synthesizing and delivering neuroactive compounds that act through the gut–brain axis) can influence neurotransmission, neuroinflammation, neuroplasticity, and the gut–brain axis. These findings highlight the potential of nutritional and microbial interventions as complementary or alternative approaches to support mood regulation, cognitive function, and emotional well-being. Unlike traditional pharmacological treatments, which often carry side effects or limited long-term efficacy, food-based and microbiome-targeted strategies may provide safe, accessible, and sustainable avenues for mental health promotion. Neuropharmacology increasingly relies on quantitative and mechanistic frameworks to connect biology, drug exposure, target modulation, biomarkers, and functional readouts across preclinical and clinical settings.

title: Sleep Quality and Architecture, Cognition, and Hormone Signaling in Endocrine Disorders
summary: Sleep is essential for brain function, cognitive performance, and memory consolidation, and these processes are closely shaped by endocrine signals. Among these, cortisol has a particularly important role in sleep regulation, linking circadian timing and hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal axis activity to the organization of sleep stages and next-day cognitive function. This interaction is especially relevant in endocrine disease. In Addison’s disease for example, lifelong glucocorticoid replacement does not fully reproduce normal physiological cortisol rhythms, and published data have associated altered night-time cortisol patterns with reduced slow-wave sleep, poorer sleep quality, and impaired memory-related outcomes. These findings have helped to position sleep disturbance not simply as a symptom, but as a plausible mechanistic pathway through which endocrine dysfunction may affect brain function and quality of life.

title: Speciation and Evolution of Montane Amphibians and Reptiles: Integrating Phylogeography, Systematics, and Conservation under Climate Change
summary: Mountain uplift and climatic oscillation have long shaped the evolution of amphibians and reptiles across the world’s montane regions, driving pulses of diversification with strongly lineage-specific evolutionary trajectories. The Hengduan Mountains and broader Himalaya-Tibet region exemplify these processes, where Miocene orogeny combined with Quaternary glacial-interglacial cycles repeatedly fragmented high-elevation habitats into “sky islands.” Although the roles of geographic isolation and ecological niche divergence in speciation are increasingly understood, the contributions of hybridization and introgression to adaptive radiation remain less resolved. Meanwhile, montane herpetofauna worldwide face mounting threats from climate-driven upslope displacement, habitat fragmentation, and emerging infectious disease.

title: The Glymphatic Failure Paradigm in Acute Brain Injury: Mechanisms, Biomarkers, Monitoring, and Therapeutic Restoration
summary: Acute brain injury (ABI) encompassing traumatic brain injury, ischemic stroke, and intracranial hemorrhage remains a leading cause of morbidity and long-term neurological disability worldwide. While traditional paradigms emphasize mechanical and vascular injury, recent advances in neurofluid research have redefined ABI as a multifactorial disorder involving failure of the glymphatic and meningeal lymphatic systems. These systems facilitate cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) and interstitial solute transport and depend on tightly regulated mechanisms, including aquaporin-4 (AQP4) water channel polarization, vascular pulsatility, and intact lymphatic drainage through the meninges. Disruption of these processes through AQP4 mislocalization, sleep–wake cycle disturbances, neuroinflammation, and hemodynamic instability contributes to impaired waste clearance, immune dysregulation, and progressive neurodegeneration following injury. title: Thriving While Work Is Rewritten: Innovation and Sustainable Work in the Adjacent Possible
summary: Work is being rewritten on several fronts at once, by technological developments such as digitalisation and generative AI, by organisational changes such as algorithmic management and hybrid work, and by broader societal pressures including sustainability demands and demographic change. These changes do not merely introduce new tools or procedures; they reshape expectations, relationships, employment lifecycles, opportunities, and constraints within organisations. This Research Topic adopts the lens of the adjacent possible to explore how innovation in work design, organisational processes, and structures unfolds from what already exists, opening new pathways for action, adaptation, and development while also generating new tensions, risks, and inequalities. At the centre of the Topic is the question of thriving, whether and under what conditions people and organisations can flourish rather than merely cope as work is reconfigured.

AI can identify unique, unbiased patterns in data, potentially discovering new biomarkers or intervention methods. These AI-driven systems are faster and more efficient than manual processes. title: AI-Driven Analysis of Electrodermal and Multimodal Biosignals for Autonomic and Neurocognitive State Monitoring
summary: The autonomic nervous system and the brain interact continuously to shape emotional, cognitive, and physiological states. Electrodermal activity (EDA), long recognized as a sensitive marker of sympathetic arousal, is now increasingly paired with EEG, fNIRS, and other neural signals to build richer, AI-driven models of autonomic-neural function. Advances in machine learning, deep learning, and nonlinear signal processing have made it possible to extract subtle, previously inaccessible patterns from these biosignals — enabling new tools for stress detection, pain assessment, cognitive workload estimation, sleep and arousal monitoring, and early detection of autonomic or neurocognitive dysfunction.

title: Affective Computing Meets Embodied Intelligence: Emotion Perception, Reasoning, and Interaction in Embodied Agents
summary: Affective computing aims to endow machines with the ability to recognize, interpret, and respond to human emotions, while embodied intelligence emphasizes that cognition emerges through an agent's physical interaction with its environment. Historically, these two fields have advanced along largely separate trajectories: affective computing has focused on emotion recognition from facial, vocal, physiological, and textual signals, whereas embodied intelligence has concentrated on perception, control, and manipulation in the physical world. Recent breakthroughs in large multimodal models, foundation models for robotics, and human-robot interaction have created unprecedented opportunities to unify the two. Emotion is no longer treated as a passive signal to be classified, but as an active component that shapes how embodied agents perceive, reason, decide, and act within dynamic, socially rich environments.

summary: Global climate change is reshaping biodiversity by altering temperature and precipitation regimes, habitat suitability, species interactions, and ecosystem functioning. title: Coevolutionary Dynamics in Parasitic or Mutualistic Interactions
summary: Coevolutionary interactions are shaped by reciprocal selection, which drives adaptive changes in the interacting species. Such changes can affect the interactants’ reproductive potential and consequently their population sizes. This research topic will investigate the dynamics of phenotype/genotype frequencies and of population sizes in mutualistic and parasitic interactions. Classical examples of such dynamics include the evolution of plant-pollinator morphological trait matching and of host-parasitoid population cycles.

At the same time, rapid advances in neural recording, computational modelling, brain–computer interfaces, neuroprosthetics, artificial intelligence, and adaptive neuromodulation are creating new opportunities to restore, substitute, or rehabilitate sensory and perceptual functions.

summary: Non-invasive brain stimulation (NIBS), including TMS, tDCS, and tACS, has become an established treatment option in psychiatry and a powerful tool for probing causal brain–behavior relationships. Yet most protocols remain open-loop and one-size-fits-all: stimulation parameters are fixed in advance and applied uniformly, which contributes to the well-documented variability in clinical and cognitive outcomes. Progress in brain-computer interfaces, real-time signal analysis, machine learning, and neurotechnology now permits the modulation of brain activity with unprecedented temporal and spatial precision, and allows stimulation to be adapted to the state of the individual brain. title: Emergency Psychiatry and Mental Health: Current Challenges, Innovations, and Pathways to Care
summary: Psychiatric emergencies represent a critical and growing challenge for health systems worldwide. The rising demand for emergency mental health services—driven by factors such as the COVID-19 pandemic, socioeconomic stressors, and reduced access to community-based care—has placed unprecedented pressure on emergency departments, crisis teams, and acute inpatient services. Despite this, emergency psychiatry remains an under-researched and often fragmented field, with significant gaps in evidence-based assessment, intervention, and care coordination.

title: Integrating Diagnostics and Therapeutics in Cerebral Vasospasm and Delayed Ischemia Post-Subarachnoid Hemorrhage
summary: Cerebral vasospasm (CVS) and delayed cerebral ischemia (DCI) remain prominent complications following subarachnoid hemorrhage (SAH), contributing significantly to poor neurological outcomes despite advances in acute neurocritical care. The pathophysiology of these secondary injuries continues to challenge clinicians, involving complex interactions between vascular constriction, microcirculatory failure, neuroinflammation, cortical spreading depolarizations, and autoregulatory disturbances. Diagnosing and managing CVS and DCI involve balancing early detection with avoidance of overtreatment, yet current diagnostic modalities including transcranial Doppler (TCD), CT perfusion, and angiography, have inherent limitations. Furthermore, while biomarkers, perfusion imaging, and multimodal neuromonitoring show emerging promise, accuracy and reproducibility remain variable. title: Neuro-immune crosstalk in peripheral neuropathy: from mechanisms to therapeutic opportunities: Volume II
summary: Peripheral neuropathy encompasses a variety of conditions marked by damage or lesions to peripheral nerves, resulting in symptoms such as pain, itch, and sensory disturbances. Diseases such as diabetes, visceral disorders, and the side effects of chemotherapy, along with conditions involving inflammation and peripheral nerve insults, are notable causes of peripheral neuropathy, affecting millions of individuals globally. Recent advances have underscored the critical role of neuro-immune interactions in driving the pathogenesis and progression of these conditions. Neuroinflammation, facilitated by the infiltration and activation of immune cells in neural tissues or by the immune capabilities of neurons themselves, plays a central role in the development and exacerbation of neuropathological symptoms. Cytokines, chemokines, and other inflammatory mediators contribute to a perpetuating cycle of inflammation and nerve damage. Peripheral innervation not only transmits sensory information bu

title: Neurocognitive and Psychological Foundations of Fluency Disorders: Stuttering and Cluttering
The cortical representation of speech and auditory perception: current developments, Vol II
summary: The interaction between speech and auditory perception and the brain’s cortical activity remains an important area of study in neuroscience. Speech and auditory perception, essential components of human communication and environmental awareness, involve the processing of sounds, neural activities, and interpretation. Understanding how the brain deciphers and makes sense of speech and auditory stimuli is crucial for cognitive neuroscience and has practical applications in treating speech and hearing disorders and improving speech recognition technology.

title: Trustworthy Neurological AI: Evidence Standards from Validation to Clinical Deployment
summary: Artificial intelligence is now being investigated across much of clinical neurology, including EEG interpretation, seizure detection, stroke imaging, neurodegenerative disease classification, neurocritical care monitoring, and clinical decision support. Many studies report high performance using metrics such as accuracy, sensitivity, specificity, or area under the ROC curve. Yet the number of systems with robust evidence of real-world clinical benefit remains comparatively small. This translational gap reflects recurrent methodological and implementation problems: reliance on narrowly characterized public datasets, limited demographic and technical diversity, insufficient external validation, incomplete calibration assessment, and evaluation strategies that do not map onto clinically meaningful decisions.

title: Understanding Cognitive and Executive Functioning in Neurodevelopmental Disorders: A focus on Cognitive, Social, and Inclusion Perspectives in Real-World Contexts
summary: Neurodevelopmental disorders (NDDs), including autism spectrum disorder (ASD), attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD), intellectual disability, and specific learning disorders, are characterized by early-onset differences in cognitive, behavioral, and social functioning. While substantial advances have been made in identifying neurobiological and cognitive mechanisms, significant gaps remain in understanding how these conditions unfold across real-world contexts—particularly within families, schools, and communities.

title: Application of Ecological Niche Models in Wildlife Disease Surveillance
summary: Wildlife populations serve as primary reservoirs for many emerging and endemic infectious agents, yet surveillance of pathogens in natural systems remains notoriously difficult, posing significant challenges for traditional statistical frameworks. Conventional wildlife health surveillance is often constrained by irregular sampling, remote geography, and sparse data. To overcome these limitations, Ecological Niche Modeling (ENM) has emerged as an essential computational framework. By integrating wildlife occurrence and infection data with high-resolution bioclimatic, landscape, and anthropogenic variables, ENM can elucidate the environmental drivers that constrain pathogen transmission, providing a rigorous basis for mapping disease risk and predicting its geographic shifts in wild reservoirs.

title: Biophysics and artificial intelligence: convergent approaches to characterize pathological protein aggregates in neurodegeneration
summary: To understand what has gone wrong in a neurodegenerative disease, one must first establish what is actually different. In many disorders, that difference is carried by the protein assemblies themselves: the same polypeptide arranged into a distinct conformer, polymorph, oligomeric state, or kinetic species. Detecting and quantifying these differences is therefore not a preliminary step, but the foundation on which mechanistic understanding, neuropathological marker development, and therapeutic strategies all rest. Before anything else, it is an analytical problem.

title: Toward Lifelong Autonomy: Advancing Continual Robot Learning for Adaptable Intelligent Systems
summary: Continual robot learning is an emerging interdisciplinary field that integrates advances from machine learning, robotics, and cognitive science to build agents capable of accumulating knowledge and skills throughout their lifetime. Unlike traditional training paradigms that assume static objectives, continual learning examines how robots can learn new tasks drawn from an evolving, potentially unbounded distribution. The key challenge lies in balancing stability and plasticity—learning new behaviours efficiently while retaining previously acquired competencies. Foundations from continual learning research have introduced three main families of methods: (1) regularization-based strategies that constrain updates to preserve past knowledge, (2) replay-based approaches that revisit experience memories to prevent forgetting, and (3) dynamic architectures that allocate specific model capacity to emerging tasks. Within robotics, these concepts have been reinterpreted to address domain-specific

title: Advancing Stroke Rehabilitation through Neuromodulation and Brain-Computer Interface Innovation
summary: Stroke ranks as the leading cause of adult disability globally. Post-stroke motor, cognitive, language and emotional deficits greatly impede patients’ recovery of activities of daily living (ADL). Driven by interdisciplinary progress in brain science, engineering medicine and neuroscience, targeted central neuromodulation and human-computer interactive brain-computer interfaces (BCI) have evolved as pivotal frontier strategies to facilitate post-stroke brain plasticity and overcome rehabilitation limitations for refractory post-stroke sequela.

title: Comparative Effectiveness and Precision Treatment in Clinical Hypnosis: What Works, for Whom, and Compared With What?
Contemplative and Non-Verbal Therapeutic Approaches in Community Mental Health: Transcultural Perspectives and Implementation in Underserved Settings
Disorders of motor circuit function: dystonia, ataxia, tremor, spasticity, and tic disorders
summary: Motor circuit disorders represent a heterogeneous group of neurological conditions characterised by disruptions in the neural pathways governing voluntary and involuntary movement. Dystonia, ataxia, spasticity, and tic disorders — despite their distinct clinical presentations — share common threads in their underlying pathophysiology, involving dysfunction across cortico-basal ganglia-thalamo-cortical and cerebellar circuits. Advances in neuroimaging, electrophysiology, genetics, and neuromodulation have significantly expanded our understanding of these conditions, yet many questions remain regarding their mechanisms, progression, and optimal management.

title: Neuroergonomics of Human-AI and Human-Machine-Robot Teaming
summary: As autonomous systems and AI become more capable, human operators are increasingly working alongside AI agents, collaborative robots, robotic swarms, powered exoskeletons, and intelligent decision-support systems across manufacturing, logistics, search and rescue, rehabilitation, healthcare, education, scientific discovery, and defense. Effective teaming in these settings demands more than task allocation. It requires real-time mutual understanding of intent, cognitive state, and situational awareness. The rapid growth of large language models has sharpened this challenge: AI agents are now active collaborators that interpret goals, generate plans, support learning and decision-making, and adapt in real time, raising distinct neuroergonomic questions around trust, coordination, mental model formation, explainability, and appropriate reliance.

title: Nitrogen vacancy centres in diamond systems
summary: This Collection highlights developments in NV‑centre generation, characterisation, and integration, as well as their emerging applications in precision measurements and quantum technologies.

title: Anthropogenic Noise Impacts on Marine Fauna: from Mechanisms to Conservation
summary: Human-generated underwater noise, from shipping, seismic surveys, sonar, offshore construction, and marine renewable energy, is now recognised as a pervasive and growing pollutant of the world’s oceans. As the acoustic footprint of human activity expands, so does concern about its consequences for marine life, which relies on sound for communication, orientation, foraging, predator avoidance, and reproduction. Understanding how noise affects marine fauna, and how those effects can be measured, regulated, and mitigated, has become a central challenge for marine ecology and conservation.

title: Artificial Intelligence and Deep Learning Innovations for Sustainable Aquaculture and Underwater Environments
summary: Artificial intelligence (AI) and deep learning are emerging as transformative forces in the modern landscape of aquaculture and underwater environmental management. This rapidly evolving field has redefined best practices, equipping researchers and aquaculture practitioners with powerful tools for automating complex processes, enhancing the precision of biomass estimation, and enabling comprehensive monitoring of aquatic and marine environments. Recent breakthroughs demonstrate how state-of-the-art neural network architectures, such as convolutional neural networks (CNNs) and transformer-based models, are overcoming traditional constraints in underwater visual analysis ranging from turbidity and poor illumination to multi-species differentiation and challenging habitat complexity. The integration of AI with intelligent sensor networks and robotics is not only boosting operational efficiency but also advancing sustainability, animal welfare, and ecosystem resilience at a time when globa

title: Beyond Symptom Control - Mechanistic Lessons from Failed and Emerging Disease-Modifying Therapies in Parkinson’s Disease
summary: Parkinson’s disease (PD) remains the second most common neurodegenerative disorder worldwide, yet despite decades of mechanistic insight, every clinical trial of a disease-modifying therapy (DMT) to date has failed to deliver unequivocal evidence of slowed neurodegeneration. Recent high-profile negative results — including trials of NLY01 (a GLP-1 receptor agonist targeting microglial activation) and deferiprone (an iron chelator targeting nigral iron accumulation and ferroptotic vulnerability) — have prompted a critical re-examination of the preclinical models, target validation strategies, and molecular hypotheses that underpin the DMT pipeline.

title: Cortical Plasticity in Retinal Disease: Mechanisms of Reorganization following Vision Loss
summary: Retinal disease, whether caused by age-related macular degeneration, retinitis pigmentosa, inherited macular and cone–rod dystrophies, or diabetic retinopathy, was long thought to leave the visual cortex it deprives essentially silent. Over the past two decades, that view has been overturned: neurons formerly driven by the lesioned retina begin responding to stimulation from surrounding, intact regions, receptive-field properties shift, and measurable functional and structural remodeling emerges across the visual pathway. Understanding the mechanisms, limits, and behavioral consequences of this plasticity is now central to both basic visual neuroscience and the design of restorative and rehabilitative therapies.
image_alt: Cortical Plasticity in Retinal Disease: Mechanisms of Reorganization following Vision Loss

title: Engineered In Vitro Platforms to Probe Neural Circuit Dysfunction in CNS Disorders
summary: Disorders of the central nervous system (CNS) - including neurodegenerative, neurodevelopmental, and neuropsychiatric conditions - arise from complex alterations in neuronal and glial function, synaptic communication, and circuit organization. Despite major advances in molecular neuroscience, how cellular dysfunction develops into aberrant network activity remains poorly understood, and conventional models often fail to reproduce human neural circuitry, cellular diversity, and patient-specific pathophysiology. Meeting this challenge requires new neurotechnologies capable of building and interrogating human neural circuits in vitro.

title: Immune cell plasticity
summary: This Collection welcomes work defining the molecular, cellular, and environmental factors that govern immune cell plasticity across health and disease.

title: Impact of rare disease genes on neural development and function
summary: Rare disease genes, though individually uncommon, collectively account for a substantial share of neurodevelopmental disorders, and each one offers a distinct and often underappreciated window into how the nervous system is built and maintained. These genes contribute to neural development and maturation at every stage of the process, from initial tissue patterning and progenitor proliferation through to the acquisition of mature cellular and circuit properties. Understanding how disruption of a single rare disease gene can cascade into complex developmental and cognitive phenotypes offers valuable insight into the biological basis of disorders such as autism, ADHD, and other neurocognitive symptoms that may arise due to altered gene function.

title: Integrative Psychiatry: Evidence, Mechanisms, and Clinical Application of Complementary and Lifestyle Approaches in Mental Health
summary: Mental disorders remain a major source of global disease burden, and despite substantial advances in contemporary psychiatry, many patients experience inadequate treatment response, adverse effects, or difficulties with long-term adherence to conventional interventions. Consequently, the use of complementary and integrative approaches to mental health care has grown considerably, driven by a perception of better tolerability and safety and patient preferences for holistic, person-centered, and culturally congruent models of care. At the same time, important concerns remain regarding the safety, efficacy, quality, and regulation of many complementary therapies, highlighting the need for rigorous scientific evaluation.

title: Reconciling Renewable Energy Expansion and Biodiversity Conservation: Ecological Impacts, Trade-offs, and Solutions
summary: The global transition to renewable energy is essential for climate mitigation, yet the rapid, large-scale deployment of solar, wind, hydropower, and associated transmission infrastructure is reshaping landscapes and seascapes with consequences for biodiversity that remain poorly quantified. Habitat loss and fragmentation, collision and displacement of wildlife, disruption of ecological processes, and cumulative effects across regions can place clean-energy goals in tension with conservation commitments.

title: The Fermentation of Carbohydrates and Proteins in the Gut of Monogastric Animals
summary: Gut microbial fermentation is a rapidly advancing field in monogastric animal nutrition, offering transformative insights into nutrient utilization, intestinal integrity, and overall metabolic regulation. Historically, research emphasized the contribution of dietary fibre and carbohydrates in fostering beneficial microbiota and generating short-chain fatty acids that support anti-inflammatory and energy-related functions. However, recent studies have revealed that an excess of undigested protein may skew fermentation toward proteolytic processes, producing metabolites such as ammonia, branched-chain fatty acids, phenols, and biogenic amines—compounds that can compromise health and efficiency. While nutritional science has substantially enhanced our understanding of carbohydrate fermentability, protein digestibility, and microbial interactions, knowledge gaps persist in elucidating how fibre and protein characteristics interact within the gut ecosystem to influence fermentation balance,

title: Advanced Molecular and Imaging Biomarkers for Neurological Disorders
summary: Neurological disorders are often driven by shared pathophysiological pathways, including immune dysregulation, glial activation, demyelination, and progressive neuronal loss. Imaging has become central to how these conditions are detected, staged, and monitored, with a comprehensive range of structural, functional, and molecular imaging modalities offering sensitive readouts of disease activity and progression. Yet the molecular meaning of many imaging signals is still only partly understood, which limits how far imaging can be used to reflect specific biological processes.

title: Advancement in Sim-to-Real, Modeling, and AI-Driven Control for Medical Soft/Continuum Robotics
summary: This research topic aims to resolve the critical sim-to-real transfer barrier and advance integrated modeling plus AI-driven control pipelines tailored exclusively for medical soft/continuum robots. The core unsolved challenge is the poor generalization of simulation-trained control logic when deployed on physical soft robotic hardware, stemming from mismatched continuum deformation dynamics, unmodeled tissue-robot interactions, and intraoperative imaging artifacts. To tackle this limitation, we seek innovative unified frameworks that combine high-fidelity patient-specific soft tissue modeling, sim-to-real domain adaptation strategies, and closed-loop AI control guided by real-time medical imaging. Key targets include data-efficient deformation modeling, robust vision-feedback adaptive control, safety-constrained autonomous manipulation, and validated cross-domain transfer workflows. title: Advances in Perinatal Psychopharmacology: Pharmacokinetics and Clinical Management
summary: Perinatal psychopharmacology explores the intricate challenges associated with prescribing psychotropic medications during pregnancy and the postpartum period. Managing psychiatric disorders in perinatal populations requires clinicians to balance the imperative of safeguarding maternal mental health against the potential risks these medications. One of the central problems in this area is the limited understanding of how pregnancy-induced physiological changes affect the pharmacokinetics—absorption, distribution, metabolism, and excretion—of psychotropic drugs. Research has recently highlighted the variability in drug plasma levels and therapeutic responses observed in pregnant and postpartum individuals, amplifying ongoing concerns about safety, efficacy, and long-term developmental outcomes for exposed children.

title: Developmental Origins and Immune Landscape of Pediatric Brain Tumors
summary: Pediatric brain tumors arise during critical periods of neural development and are increasingly recognized as biologically distinct from adult central nervous system (CNS) malignancies. Integrative genomic, transcriptomic, and epigenomic studies have shown that many pediatric brain tumors retain developmental programs reflective of their cells of origin. These programs influence tumor behavior, molecular heterogeneity, and clinical course, and are now understood to play a role in shaping the tumor immune landscape. Compared with adult tumors, pediatric brain tumors often display distinct patterns of antigen presentation, immune cell infiltration, and immune evasion. Understanding how developmental context intersects with tumor–immune interactions is therefore central to advancing biologically informed therapeutic strategies in pediatric neuro-oncology. Despite major advances in molecular classification of pediatric brain tumors, immune-based therapies have shown variable and often limi

title: Neuroimmune T cell dysregulation in multiple sclerosis: epigenetic mechanisms and antigen-specific interventions
summary: Multiple Sclerosis (MS) is, at its core, a disease of failed molecular immune regulation. Autoreactive T cells shaped by aberrant transcriptional programs and epigenetic remodeling escape peripheral tolerance, breach the blood-brain barrier, and sustain the neuroinflammation and demyelination that define the disease. The central challenge in MS research today is not simply to suppress this immune response, but to understand and correct the molecular machinery driving it. That is precisely what this Research Topic sets out to do.

title: Peptide and Peptidomimetic Strategies to Probe and Modulate Neurodegenerative Mechanisms
summary: Bioactive peptides and peptidomimetics play fundamental roles in biological signaling and have long demonstrated utility as molecular tools and therapeutic candidates. In neurodegenerative diseases—including Alzheimer’s disease, Parkinson’s disease, and amyotrophic lateral sclerosis—aberrant protein folding, aggregation, and peptide–protein interactions contribute directly to neuronal dysfunction, neuroinflammation, and progressive degeneration. Metal ions such as copper, zinc, and iron are closely bound up with these processes, influencing peptide conformation, aggregation propensity, and oxidative injury in vulnerable neuronal populations. Targeting these molecular processes using peptide-based strategies offers a powerful approach for dissecting disease mechanisms, identifying biomarkers, and validating novel therapeutic targets.

title: Perinatal Bereavement, Trauma, & Loss, volume III
summary: This is a continuation of our previous 2 collections - first volume (linked here) and second (linked here). The perinatal period (from antepartum through to the end of the first postpartum year) is a critical and often joyous time for families. However, for some this period can be marked by bereavement, trauma, and/or loss, which can have profound emotional, psychological, and psycho-social impacts. Bereavement, trauma, and loss can take many forms, including, but not limited to: infertility, pregnancy loss, perinatal death, confronting childhood abuse or neglect, reproductive coercion, intimate partner violence, relationship breakdown, complex family dynamics, traumatic birth experiences, obstetric violence, children being removed into care, and coinciding traumatic stressors such as forced migration or armed conflict. This Research Topic seeks to explore the multifaceted aspects associated with the breadth of women’s experiences.

title: Mechanisms Underlying Animal Responses to Heat and Environmental Stress and Advanced Management and Nutritional Strategies for Mitigation
summary: Heat stress and other environmental stressors exert profound effects on the physiological, metabolic, endocrine, immune, and molecular functions of animals, compromising health, welfare, reproductive performance, and productivity. Because these stressors act first and foremost on nutrient intake, digestion, absorption, and metabolic partitioning, understanding the biological mechanisms underlying animal adaptation, and the nutritional levers that can support it, has become a critical priority for sustainable animal production as climate change drives more frequent and severe extreme weather events.

title: Monoclonal Antibodies in Multiple Sclerosis and Related Diseases: Volume II
summary: Multiple sclerosis (MS) and its related neuroimmunological disorders including neuromyelitis optica spectrum disorder (NMOSD), clinically isolated syndrome (CIS), and myelin oligodendrocyte glycoprotein antibody-associated disease (MOGAD) continue to represent major causes of chronic neurological disability worldwide. Since the introduction of monoclonal antibodies (mAbs), the therapeutic landscape for these diseases has transformed, providing superior control of relapse activity, demyelination, and long-term disability progression. Building on the insights gained from the first volume, it is now evident that B-cell depletion, blockade of lymphocyte trafficking, and modulation of immune signaling pathways have redefined the treatment paradigm of MS. Recent studies have elucidated differential efficacy, mechanisms of resistance, and immunological sequelae associated with anti-CD20 agents (rituximab, ocrelizumab, ofatumumab, and ublituximab), as well as with alemtuzumab and natalizumab.

However, many of these conditions are associated with complex motor, cognitive, behavioral, and sensory impairments that profoundly affect functioning and social participation.

Produced by neurosecretory cells in the central nervous system, neuroendocrine organs, and peripheral tissues such as the gut and Malpighian tubules, neuropeptides exert their effects through G-protein-coupled receptors (GPCRs). Recent innovations in mass spectrometry, transcriptomics, and comparative genomics have greatly accelerated the discovery of novel neuropeptides and their evolutionarily conserved precursors, revealing both lineage-specific adaptations and deep homologies across the animal kingdom. title: Automated Reliable Reasoning and Verification Using Neurosymbolic Approaches for Software Engineering
summary: Software engineering has long relied on symbolic techniques (such as formal logic, program analysis, knowledge representation, and formal verification) to establish software properties. In parallel, machine learning has enabled systems to learn from code, specifications, execution traces, and operational data. However, learned models often lack explicit semantics, transparent reasoning, and verifiable guarantees, limiting their use in high-assurance settings. Neurosymbolic approaches combine data-driven learning with symbolic knowledge and reasoning, enabling systems that can both learn and provide structured explanations or evidence for their behavior. This integration offers opportunities to automate software engineering tasks while improving correctness, traceability, and interpretability. At the same time, it raises important questions regarding the representation of software knowledge, the interaction of neural and symbolic components, and the evaluation, verification, and assuran

title: Early-life Calf Health and Programming: Implications for Reproductive Development and Lifetime Productivity
summary: Early-life conditions play a critical role in shaping the future productivity and reproductive capacity of dairy cattle. The period from late gestation through weaning represents a sensitive developmental window, during which nutrition, immune protection, microbiome establishment, and environmental factors interact to influence long-term physiological outcomes. In particular, early-life feeding strategies, including colostrum management, milk composition, and the use of feed additives, are increasingly recognized as key determinants of gut health, metabolic function, and immune development. Despite advances in calf rearing practices, challenges such as early-life disease, inconsistent growth, and inadequate passive immunity transfer remain common. Growing evidence highlights the role of endocrine, metabolic, inflammatory, and microbiome-mediated pathways in linking early-life conditions with later reproductive performance, although the underlying mechanisms are not yet fully understood

title: Emerging Technologies in Music Cognition, Learning, and Performance
summary: Music cognition investigates how prediction, anticipation, attention, memory, sensorimotor processes, physiological regulation, and expressive control support musical learning, expertise, performance, and interaction. Music therefore offers a distinctive setting for examining cognition as an embodied, situated, and socially coordinated activity. Recent advances in artificial intelligence, eye tracking, physiological sensing, biofeedback, motion capture, wearable devices, and multimodal data analysis have enabled increasingly precise investigations of these processes across individual and collective musical contexts. However, important questions remain regarding how cognitive, embodied, sensorimotor, and physiological mechanisms develop across childhood, advanced training, and professional expertise. The field also continues to debate how these processes should be measured and integrated, how technology-mediated observations relate to ecologically valid musical activity, and how individ

title: Evolution of Cell Types, Developmental Mechanisms, and Functional Properties of Digestive Systems.
summary: The digestive system represents one of the most dynamic and functionally integrated organ systems in animals. Across metazoan evolution, digestive organs have undergone remarkable diversification in their cellular composition, molecular regulation, and physiological specialization, enabling organisms to adapt to distinct ecological niches, nutritional environments, and life-history strategies. Comparative research is revealing that the emergence and diversification of digestive cell types are closely linked to conserved gene regulatory networks and developmental signaling pathways that coordinate organogenesis and functional maturation. Recent advances in single-cell and spatial omics technologies have transformed our understanding of digestive tissue evolution, uncovering conserved and lineage-specific molecular programs governing epithelial differentiation, secretory specialization, immune integration, and neuroendocrine control. Furthermore, the digestive tract is increasingly recog

title: Intergenerational Pathways to Mental Health
summary: Mental health problems often develop within a family and social context, and their effects may extend from one generation to another. Parental mental health problems, adverse childhood experiences, family violence, substance use, socioeconomic hardship, and disrupted family relationships can influence mental health outcomes in subsequent generations. At the same time, intergenerational transmission is not inevitable. Positive parenting, stable and supportive relationships, social support, access to mental health care, and other protective factors may reduce risk and contribute to better outcomes. Although interest in intergenerational mental health has grown considerably, important questions remain about how these influences interact at different stages of life and across different social and cultural settings. title: Molecular Ecology and Evolution in Plants: From Genomes to Ecosystems
summary: Plants, as sessile organisms, are relentlessly shaped by environmental fluctuation, driving the evolution of sophisticated molecular mechanisms that govern adaptation, speciation, and ecological interactions. More than a century has passed since Darwin observed adaptive evolution in the feeding behavior of finches on the Galápagos Islands, and Linus Pauling first proposed the concept of molecular evolution. Today, the rapid breakthroughs in high-throughput sequencing, multi-omics, and computational biology have transformed the field of plant molecular ecology and evolution. These advances have not only made it possible to dissect the genomic architecture of adaptive traits, but also to trace evolutionary trajectories at fine temporal and spatial scales, and to link genetic variations to phenotypic plasticity and ecosystem-level dynamic processes. They can provide unprecedented opportunities to forecast plant responses to global change and to design evidence-based conservation strategie
image_alt: Molecular Ecology and Evolution in Plants: From Genomes to Ecosystems

title: Neurobiological mediators of clinical outcomes in psychedelic-assisted therapies
summary: Psychedelic-assisted therapies have demonstrated rapid and often sustained clinical benefit across depression, PTSD, and other conditions. Neuroimaging, electrophysiological, and molecular studies increasingly link these effects to structural and functional neuroplasticity, supported by theoretical frameworks such as the Entropic Brain Hypothesis and REBUS. In parallel, clinical and qualitative research emphasizes the centrality of the subjective, phenomenological experience to therapeutic outcome. These two literatures — neurobiological and phenomenological — have largely developed in parallel, with few studies directly testing how they relate within the same patient sample. Consequently, whether neurobiological changes are causally responsible for clinical improvement, merely predictive of it, or simply co-occurring alongside a distinct psychological process remains an open and clinically consequential question.
image_alt: Neurobiological mediators of clinical outcomes in psychedelic-assisted therapies

title: Neuroinflammation and psychotic disorders: mechanisms, biomarkers, and treatment targets
summary: Neuropsychiatric research increasingly recognizes neuroinflammation as a critical mechanism underlying psychotic disorders such as schizophrenia, schizoaffective disorder, and first-episode psychosis. Evidence from genetics, transcriptomics, neuroimaging, and peripheral immune profiling highlights the involvement of immune-related processes, particularly microglial activation, cytokine imbalance, blood-brain barrier dysfunction, and aberrant complement-mediated synaptic pruning, in shaping disease onset, cognitive impairment, and treatment resistance. These findings suggest that immune dysregulation is not merely a secondary phenomenon but a driving factor in illness progression. However, despite the surge of recent discoveries, the exact temporal dynamics, causal mechanisms, and the translational potential of immune signals remain incompletely understood. The integration of neurobiological, immunological, and clinical evidence offers a timely opportunity to bridge mechanistic insights

title: Pharmacology of thermoregulation and adaptive behavior
summary: Mammalian thermoregulation is the result of millennia of evolutionary interactions with challenging environments as it represents a core adaptive behavior crucial for survival, reproduction, and rest. This is achieved by controlling four main coordinated responses: endocrine, neuronal, metabolic, and immune, to address environmental and physiological variables such as motor activity, age, time, light, temperature, infections, food, and water supply.
image_alt: Pharmacology of thermoregulation and adaptive behavior

title: Robotics, Artificial Intelligence and Autonomous Systems for Intelligent Maintenance and Asset Management
summary: Industrial maintenance is undergoing a rapid transformation driven by advances in robotics, artificial intelligence (AI), autonomous systems, sensing technologies, and digitalization. While robotic automation has become well established in manufacturing, maintenance operations remain largely dependent on manual labour despite representing a significant proportion of operational costs across industries. Many maintenance activities continue to expose workers to hazardous environments, repetitive tasks, confined spaces, and ergonomically challenging conditions. At the same time, industries are facing increasing pressure to improve productivity, reduce downtime, enhance safety, and address shortages of skilled maintenance personnel. title: Survival without Major Morbidity or Neurodevelopmental Impairment in Preterm Infants – Current Landscape, Challenges, and Future Directions - Volume II
summary: The paradigm for evaluating success in neonatology has definitively shifted from survival alone to the achievement of intact survival—specifically, "Survival Without Major Morbidity or Neurodevelopmental Impairment" (SWMM-NDI). This composite endpoint, now central to major trials and quality benchmarks, rigorously defines the absence of severe bronchopulmonary dysplasia (BPD), serious brain injury, necrotizing enterocolitis requiring surgery, severe retinopathy of prematurity, nosocomial infection, and significant cognitive or motor impairment at 18-24 months.

The Research Topic will bring together behavioral, neuroscientific, developmental, computational, and applied perspectives to identify how communicative information is represented, integrated, predicted, and adapted in real time, and how these real-time processes shape, and are shaped by, learning and developmental trajectories. Particular attention will be given to multisensory integration, sensorimotor prediction and feedback, temporal coordination, interpersonal alignment, and the influence of social context and individual differences. title: Contextualizing Mental Health through Social and Environmental Perspectives
summary: Mental health and psychological well-being are shaped not only by biological and individual factors, but also by the social, cultural, linguistic, and environmental contexts in which people live. Socioeconomic disadvantage is consistently associated with poorer mental health outcomes, while stigma, discrimination, violence, victimization, and social exclusion can intensify psychological distress and hinder access to care. Religious and cultural worldviews, language, family relationships, and community conditions also influence how distress is expressed, understood, and treated. Recent research indicates that culturally adapted and linguistically appropriate interventions can improve engagement and therapeutic outcomes, while strong social support and community networks may promote resilience and recovery. Multi-robot systems (MRS) are emerging as powerful enablers for applications such as environmental monitoring, disaster response, precision agriculture, and smart manufacturing. title: Enteric Glial Cells in Brain Aging and Neurodegeneration: From Historical Roots to Neuroinflammatory Paradigms in the Gut-Brain Axis
summary: Enteric glial cells (EGCs) are increasingly recognized as vital communicators between the gut and the brain. Once thought to play only a supportive role in gastrointestinal physiology, EGCs are now understood as dynamic players that help regulate both gut homeostasis and central nervous system (CNS) function. Over the past decade, enteric neuroscience has revealed that these cells are key mediators of bidirectional signaling within the gut brain axis. Emerging evidence suggests that EGC dysfunction can contribute to the chronic neuroinflammatory processes associated with aging and neurodegenerative diseases. Despite their peripheral location, EGCs influence systemic inflammation through cytokine signaling, oxidative stress modulation, and effects on intestinal barrier integrity. Major open questions include how age related changes in EGC phenotype and activity affect gut brain communication and whether pharmacological modulation of these cells might delay neuronal decline in disorders
image_alt: Enteric Glial Cells in Brain Aging and Neurodegeneration: From Historical Roots to Neuroinflammatory Paradigms in the Gut-Brain Axis

title: Exploring Sleep-Dementia Link: Neurocognitive Mechanisms and Therapeutic Horizons
summary: The relationship between sleep disturbances and dementia represents a crucial domain in contemporary neuroscience and clinical research, with wide-reaching implications for patient care and disease management. Evidence consistently shows that disruptions in sleep and circadian rhythms are highly prevalent across all major types of dementia, including Alzheimer’s disease, Lewy body dementia, frontotemporal dementia, and vascular cognitive impairment, and may play an active role in accelerating neurodegenerative processes. Progress in advanced neuroimaging, biomarker discovery, and objective sleep assessments is shedding light on the complex neurocognitive mechanisms interlinking these conditions. However, significant knowledge gaps remain about the mechanisms involved, the heterogeneity among dementia subtypes, and the translation of mechanistic insights into effective therapies.

title: Advanced Neuroimaging and AI for Personalized Non-Invasive Brain Stimulation: From Biomarkers to Closed-Loop Strategies
summary: Non-invasive brain stimulation (NIBS) techniques, including transcranial magnetic stimulation (TMS), transcranial direct and alternating current stimulation (tDCS/tACS), and focused ultrasound, have emerged as powerful tools for both probing and modulating human neural circuits. Yet a central challenge has persisted: the considerable variability in individual responses to stimulation, driven by differences in neuroanatomy, brain state, network organisation, and underlying pathophysiology. Advanced neuroimaging now sits at the heart of efforts to address this challenge, offering unprecedented insight into the mechanisms of stimulation, its network-level effects, and the neural features that distinguish responders from non-responders.

title: Beyond Classical Monoamine Receptors: Emerging Regulators and Therapeutic Targets in Neuropharmacology
summary: Monoaminergic neurotransmission has traditionally been understood through the pharmacology of dopamine, serotonin, and adrenergic receptors. However, growing evidence indicates that monoaminergic function is shaped by a broader network of receptors, transporters, intracellular signaling pathways, metabolic enzymes, and interactions with other neurotransmitter systems. Emerging targets, including trace amine-associated receptors (TAARs) are revealing previously unrecognized mechanisms regulating neuronal activity, behavior, and therapeutic responses.

title: Integrating Spirituality into Public Mental Health: Toward Resilient and Holistic Systems of Care
summary: Spiritual well-being, encompassing meaning, purpose, connectedness, belonging, inner peace, and existential orientation, is increasingly recognized as an important determinant of mental health. Research across psychology, psychiatry, phenomenology, and public health demonstrates that spirituality can support resilience, coping, recovery, and social cohesion. Beyond serving as a protective factor, spirituality influences how individuals understand themselves, relate to others, and make sense of suffering and adversity. Nevertheless, public mental health frameworks continue to focus predominantly on biological and psychosocial determinants, while spiritual and existential dimensions remain largely overlooked. Phenomenological studies further suggest that mental health challenges often involve disruptions in selfhood, embodiment, agency, temporality, and connectedness. Available pharmacotherapeutic agents show limited efficacy in reducing compulsive intake, withdrawal-related distress, and relapse. While classical treatments target GABAergic, glutamatergic, and opioid signaling, a growing body of work points to a broader network of neuropeptide, stress, and neuroimmune pathways shaping the course of addiction.

title: Pathways to Well-Being in Inclusive Combat Sports and Martial Arts: Social and Psychological Perspectives
summary: Inclusive combat sports and martial arts are increasingly recognized as psychologically significant contexts for people with disabilities, with benefits that complement those related to physical, motor, and sociological dimensions. Emerging evidence, including research on structured inclusive judo and karate programs, indicates measurable improvements in motivation, self-esteem, resilience, social impairment, and sense of belonging among participants, including autistic individuals and people with intellectual and relational disabilities. However, the psychological mechanisms through which these activities influence wellbeing, identity, and long-term engagement require further investigation across different types of disability, disciplines, and age groups. Therefore, a multidisciplinary approach with a primary focus on psychological mechanisms is needed to consolidate the available evidence and clarify which mechanisms may be generalizable across different contexts.

title: Rethinking Tau in Alzheimer’s Disease: From Therapeutic Lessons to Biomarker-Guided and Combination Strategies
summary: Alzheimer’s disease remains one of the most prevalent and challenging neurodegenerative disorders, with the pathological aggregation of tau protein a defining feature that correlates closely with cognitive decline. For this reason, tau has attracted intense interest as a therapeutic target. Yet the clinical record has been sobering: across numerous human trials, single-target anti-tau strategies, including immunotherapies and aggregation inhibitors, have shown limited efficacy in halting or slowing disease progression. This gap between strong mechanistic rationale and disappointing clinical outcomes has prompted a reassessment of how tau should be approached. Two lessons are emerging. First, tau may be most powerful not as a standalone drug target but as one node within a wider pathological network, suggesting that combination and upstream strategies could succeed where mono-target approaches have not. title: Securing the Future of Bats: Research Trends in Diversity, Ecology, and Conservation Solutions
summary: Bats (order Chiroptera) are the second most diverse group of mammals and provide essential ecosystem services, including agricultural pest suppression, pollination, seed dispersal, and nutrient cycling. Despite their ecological and economic importance, bats remain among the most understudied and threatened mammals worldwide. Habitat loss and fragmentation, climate change, infrastructure expansion—including wind energy development—hunting, persecution, and disease-related pressures are contributing to population declines, particularly in regions where monitoring and conservation capacity are limited. At the same time, bats remain central to debates surrounding zoonotic disease emergence, highlighting the importance of accurately understanding bat diversity, distributions, behavior, and parasite communities without reinforcing unsupported associations between bats and disease. title: Sex as a biological Variable in Mood Disorders: Molecular Mechanisms and Therapeutic Targets
summary: Women are diagnosed with mood disorders, including major depressive disorder and bipolar disorder, at nearly twice the rate of men, yet the molecular mechanisms driving this disparity remain incompletely understood. Genetic risk factors, epigenetic regulation, and hippocampal neuroplasticity have each emerged as critical, and often sex-differential, contributors to mood disorder vulnerability and treatment response. Advancing precision psychiatry for women requires bringing these mechanisms together into a coherent and informed framework.
