title: Spasticity and Pain in Neurological Disorders: Shared Pathways and Multimodal Rehabilitation Strategies
summary: The field of neurorehabilitation increasingly recognizes the entwined nature of spasticity and pain as disabling complications arising from neurological disorders. Traditionally considered and managed as distinct entities, spasticity and neuropathic pain are now understood to be underpinned by common mechanisms, including maladaptive central sensitization, spinal disinhibition, neuroinflammation, and altered supraspinal modulation. Their co-occurrence not only worsens functional impairment but also significantly degrades patient quality of life, making effective intervention an urgent need. Recent literature originating from multiple sclerosis research has introduced the concept of ‘Spasticity-Plus Syndrome’, which groups spasticity with spasms, pain, sleep disturbances, and autonomic dysfunction into an interconnected symptom cluster sharing common neurobiological substrates. title: Headache and Cerebrovascular Disease: Stroke Risk, Vascular Mechanisms and Outcomes
summary: Headache disorders, particularly migraine, exhibit a complex and still incompletely understood relationship with cerebrovascular disease. Epidemiological studies have shown that migraine with aura is associated with an elevated risk of ischemic stroke, especially in young women, while acute or thunderclap headache may act as a sentinel symptom of vascular pathologies such as cervical artery dissection, cerebral venous thrombosis, or reversible cerebral vasoconstriction syndrome. Underlying mechanisms under investigation include endothelial dysfunction, cortical spreading depression, platelet activation, and hypercoagulable states, though causal pathways remain debated. Critical knowledge gaps persist in determining which patients with headache are at increased risk of stroke, how specific vascular or imaging markers should be interpreted, and how treatment strategies can be optimized to prevent cerebrovascular complications. title: Lasting Impact of Psychiatric Rehabilitation on System-wide Outcomes
summary: This Research Topic focuses on the enduring impact of psychiatric rehabilitation on system-wide outcomes, not solely at the individual level or the level of individual organizations, but at a system-wide or societal level. There has been a critique that these interventions have only had impact in the settings where effectiveness studies were implemented, but not more broadly in everyday practice settings where these services are now provided. Beyond the settings of controlled studies, when psychiatric rehabilitation interventions are funded and implemented in specific jurisdictions, do these empirically supported best practices produce measurable system- wide outcomes such as lower unemployment, less homelessness, better community integration and improved quality life among persons with serious mental illness?

title: Revisiting Solitude in the Digital Age
summary: Solitude and social relationships are equally important for individual well-being. With aging, people tend to spend more time alone and develop increasingly positive attitudes toward solitude. Solitude is widely regarded as “a coin with two sides”. It may represent a maladaptive response to social exclusion and isolation, manifested as loneliness and rumination. It can also be beneficial and constructive, enabling concentration, psychological restoration, self-reflection, personal autonomy, and self-transcendence. Alternatively, it can be a neutral situational state without obvious positive or negative valence.
image_alt: Revisiting Solitude in the Digital Age

title: The Impact of Mycotoxins on the Reproductive Function of Farm and Companion Animals
summary: Mycotoxins are chemical toxic compounds produced by filamentous fungi species. These toxins are ubiquitously distributed and present in all animal diets at variable levels and combinations. Most of the animal diets will contain these mycotoxins. Due to their variability in chemical composition and levels of exposure, their mode of action may vary from oxidative stress to carcinogenic activity. Some mycotoxins, like zearalenone (ZEN), are known for their reproductive toxicity due to their oestrogenic activity. However, other mycotoxins not considered as endocrine disruptors may also negatively impact animal reproduction. Additionally, most of the reproductive effects of mycotoxins are detected under acute exposure, and there is a paucity of information regarding chronic exposure.
image_alt: The Impact of Mycotoxins on the Reproductive Function of Farm and Companion Animals

title: Chronic stress, anhedonia, and reward-circuit dysfunction in depression: Mechanisms, models, and novel therapeutic approaches
summary: Chronic stress remains one of the most robust precipitants of major depressive disorder, in which anhedonia (the loss of motivation, pleasure, and interest) is a particularly disabling and treatment-resistant dimension. Converging evidence places the mesocorticolimbic reward system and connected hippocampal circuitry at the center of this pathology. Across the ventral tegmental area (VTA), nucleus accumbens (NAc), medial prefrontal cortex (mPFC), and hippocampus, sustained stress and allostatic load disrupt dopaminergic and glutamatergic signaling, functionally decoupling motivation, hedonic capacity, and reward learning.
image_alt: Chronic stress, anhedonia, and reward-circuit dysfunction in depression: Mechanisms, models, and novel therapeutic approaches

title: Avoidant/Restrictive Food Intake Disorder (ARFID): Mechanisms, Interventions, and Developmental Trajectories Across Contexts
summary: Avoidant/Restrictive Food Intake Disorder (ARFID) represents a rapidly evolving area in eating behavior and disorder research, with increasing attention since its inclusion in the DSM-5 in 2013. ARFID is distinct from other eating disorders, as sensory sensitivities, fears surrounding adverse experiences with food, or lack of interest in eating, lead to considerable nutritional, physical, and psychosocial impacts rather than weight/shape concerns. Recent studies have highlighted complex neurobiological processes, atypical interoceptive awareness, and strong associations with neurodevelopmental and anxiety conditions underlying ARFID, yet its etiology, maintenance mechanisms, public health impact, treatment response, and presentation variation require further research exploration. title: Social Development and Mental Health: Policy Responses to Emerging Health Challenges
summary: Mental health is increasingly recognized as both a precondition and an outcome of social development. However, global advances have been uneven, reflecting deep structural inequalities in exposure to social risks and in the capacity of welfare systems to buffer their effects. A growing body of evidence shows that mental health outcomes are strongly shaped by social policies that regulate income security, employment conditions, education, housing, human mobility, and social protection across the life course. In many low- and middle-income countries, recurrent economic shocks, labor informality, weak social safety nets, and persistent uncertainty undermine psychological well-being at the population level. Despite the explicit inclusion of mental health within the Sustainable Development Goals, its integration into social and economic policy agendas remains limited, calling for more policy-relevant and context-sensitive research.

These processes arise from complex interactions among neural circuits, neurotransmitter systems, environmental influences, and learned experience, and are fundamental both to adaptive behavior and to neuropsychiatric disorders such as substance use disorders, compulsive behaviors, depression, and stress-related conditions. Progress depends not only on conceptual advances but on rigorous methods and high-quality data able to interrogate these mechanisms across behavioral, neurobiological, and computational levels.

title: AI and Social Well-Being: Opportunities and Risks for Connection, Support, and Inclusion
summary: Artificial intelligence is increasingly shaping how people form, maintain, and navigate social relationships and communities. Conversational agents, social robots, recommender systems, matching platforms, and other AI applications now mediate communication, provide companionship and support, influence access to information and communities, and affect participation in social life. Social well-being—encompassing social relationships, perceived and received support, belonging, inclusion, participation, and social networks—is therefore influenced not only by interpersonal and community structures but also by human-AI interaction and AI-mediated communication.

title: Advances in cell rejuvenation and cell reprogramming for cellular regeneration
summary: The field of neuroscience is witnessing dynamic advancements in understanding and promoting neuronal regeneration by leveraging innovative cellular resetting and reprogramming strategies. Persistent challenges in treating neurodegenerative diseases and neurological injuries stem from the limited capacity of the adult central nervous system for self-repair and regeneration. Recent research has illuminated pathways for overcoming these barriers, including reprogramming somatic cells into neuronal phenotypes and manipulating the epigenetic landscape to influence cell fate. Key breakthroughs demonstrate that targeted resetting of cellular identity can generate functionally relevant neurons, opening possibilities for reversing the effects of neurological disorders. title: Artificial Intelligence and Autonomous Agricultural Robots: Path Planning, Task Scheduling, and Intelligent Decision-Making
summary: However, compared to structured environments such as industrial manufacturing and warehousing logistics, agricultural environments are far more complex and unpredictable. Scenarios such as farmlands, orchards, greenhouses, and hilly or mountainous areas typically present challenges including uneven terrain, severe crop obstruction, highly variable lighting conditions, unpredictable obstacle distribution, unstable communication conditions, and biological variability in the objects being handled. These factors significantly increase the difficulty of autonomous operation for agricultural robots and place higher demands on path planning, task scheduling, and intelligent decision-making methods. Therefore, it is necessary to conduct systematic thematic discussions on artificial intelligence and autonomous agricultural robots to promote the deep integration of theoretical innovation, technological breakthroughs, and engineering applications.

title: Artificial Intelligence for Next-Generation Digital Health: From Predictive Analytics to Personalized Care
summary: Over the past decade, artificial intelligence (AI) has become a major driver of digital health transformation, enabling more predictive, preventive, personalized, and participatory models of care. Advances in machine learning, deep learning, and generative AI, - paired with the rapid evolution of wearables, connected devices, and digital health infrastructure - have expanded AI’s role across clinical decision support, computer-assisted diagnosis, precision medicine, remote patient monitoring, biomedical data analytics, and care delivery optimization. Yet widespread adoption brings real challenges: data quality and governance, interoperability, model explainability, privacy protection, and unresolved ethical, regulatory, and clinical implementation questions.

Artificial intelligence, including machine learning, reinforcement learning, computer vision, multimodal sensing, and data-driven modeling, offers new opportunities to improve robot perception, planning, control, adaptation, and decision-making. Meanwhile, wireless power transfer and energy management technologies are becoming critical for enabling untethered, miniaturized, implantable, and long-duration robotic systems. title: Big Cats in a Changing World: Ecology, Conservation, and Coexistence
summary: Big Cats are among the most charismatic, and most endangered, mammal groups on Earth. As top predators and keystone species, they act as natural coordinators of the ecological connections within their ecosystems. Their obligate carnivory and large body size make coexistence with people difficult, and human activity has reduced their numbers for centuries, a decline that has greatly accelerated during the Anthropocene. Their unique position means that their decline rarely happens in ecological isolation. The irony is sharp: we are the single greatest cause of their decline, yet we prize them culturally, economically, and politically. That regard has fueled a level of public and scientific interest in Big Cat conservation that few other endangered mammals enjoy. Alongside it sits a genuine scientific question: how does Big Cat biology itself shift under intense, often harmful, human pressure?

title: Brain-Organ Communication: Neural Regulation of Metabolism and Developmental Programming
summary: The central nervous system (CNS) plays a fundamental role in the regulation of systemic metabolism, operating through autonomic efferent pathways (sympathetic and parasympathetic) governing the function of peripheral metabolic organs including the liver, adipose tissue, pancreas, and skeletal muscle. Rather than a unidirectional communication, CNS continuously integrates afferent signals arising from peripheral tissues, including vagal sensory inputs, circulating humoral factors, and organ-derived metabolites, forming a dynamic bidirectional brain-organ axis.

title: Dexterous Manipulation and Adaptive Robotic Grasping: From Mechanisms to Intelligent Control
summary: Manipulation is central to robotics applications ranging from industrial automation to service, logistics, healthcare, and human–robot collaboration. Conventional parallel-jaw grippers and rigid end-effectors are effective for structured tasks, but often lack adaptability when handling diverse objects, deformable items, or cluttered scenes. In response, the community has developed dexterous multi-finger hands, underactuated and compliant grippers, and soft robotic end-effectors that exploit morphology and compliance to simplify control while improving robustness.

title: Diagnosing and managing Neuroinfectious Diseases in Travelers and Migrants: Challenges in Non-Endemic Settings
summary: The field of neuroinfectious diseases is profoundly affected by the dynamics of global travel, tourism, and migration, which have reshaped how endemic diseases and neurotropic pathogens spread and manifest in geographically distant populations. Infections once confined to specific regions are now regularly observed in non-endemic settings, altering both epidemiological patterns and clinical practice. The emergence and establishment of West Nile virus with associated neurological syndromes in the United States after 1999 exemplify this trend, as do increasing reports of central nervous system (CNS) tuberculosis and parasitic infections in high-income countries linked to migration. Simultaneously, climate change and urbanization are expanding the range of vectors such as mosquitoes and ticks, thereby modifying the global distribution of CNS infections. Advances in portable EEG, artificial intelligence, digital biomarkers, cloud and edge computing are creating new opportunities for continuous brain-health monitoring and personalized management of neurological, psychiatric, cognitive and sleep-related conditions. However, challenges related to signal quality, clinical validation, interoperability, explainability, usability, privacy, cybersecurity and responsible integration into healthcare workflows continue to limit widespread adoption.

title: Evolution of High Diversity in Tropics and Alpine Regions
summary: The tropics and alpine regions rank among the most species-rich environments on Earth, yet the processes that generate and sustain their exceptional diversity remain a central puzzle in evolutionary biology. Both systems act as natural laboratories: the tropics through their vast age, climatic stability, and structural complexity, and alpine regions through steep environmental gradients, isolation, and rapid ecological turnover. Understanding why diversity accumulates so dramatically in these settings speaks directly to fundamental questions about speciation, adaptation, and the assembly of biological communities. Thus, comparing patterns between tropical and alpine systems offers a powerful way to test whether similar diversity outcomes arise from shared or contrasting evolutionary mechanisms.
image_alt: Evolution of High Diversity in Tropics and Alpine Regions

title: Exploring Telemedicine's Impact on Healthcare Access, Outcomes, and Innovation

By enabling remote diagnosis, consultation, and monitoring, it directly addresses some of the sector’s most pressing structural challenges: aging populations, shortages of healthcare professionals, and uneven distribution of care across geographies. Beyond convenience, telemedicine has demonstrated measurable benefits across chronic disease management, acute care, and mental health services, improving both clinical outcomes and access for underserved and rural populations.

title: Motivational aspects of balancing eating and physical exercise in health and disease
summary: Food intake is an essential behavior for acquiring the energy required for survival. Because animals must expend energy through physical movement to obtain food, behavior is inherently constrained by the need to balance energy acquisition and expenditure. Maintaining this balance is fundamental for health. Traditionally, it has been framed from nutritional and metabolic perspectives. From a systems neuroscience perspective, however, it can be understood as a process in which neural circuits continuously allocate motivational resources between feeding and physical activity.

We are moving away from a "one-size-fits-all" approach to opioids and volatiles, and toward a mechanistic understanding of how these powerful drugs interact with neural circuits, the blood-brain barrier, and the immune system.

title: Non-Motor Symptoms and Neuropsychiatric Features in Parkinson’s Disease: From Prodromal Indicators to Therapeutic Targets
summary: Parkinson’s disease (PD) has traditionally been defined by its motor symptoms and nigrostriatal dopaminergic degeneration, yet a growing body of research highlights the central importance of non-motor manifestations and dysfunctions of other neural pathways and neurotransmitter systems. Symptoms such as pain, sleep disturbances, autonomic dysfunction, and affective symptoms (like apathy, anhedonia, depression, and anxiety) often arise in the prodromal phase, before the onset of motor deficits. Frequently underdiagnosed and undertreated, these non-motor features can significantly diminish patients’ quality of life and complicate disease management. Progress has been made in understanding their links to neurodegenerative changes and dysfunctions in different neurotransmitter systems (including the dopaminergic, serotonergic, cholinergic, histaminergic, glutamatergic, and noradrenergic systems) and neural circuits (such as the mesolimbic and mesocortical circuits implicated in affective s

title: Phenotypes and Neural Mechanisms of Hyperacusis
summary: Sound tolerance disorders, particularly hyperacusis, are increasingly recognized as heterogeneous conditions involving altered responses to everyday sounds. However, the clinical and neurobiological distinctions between loudness hyperacusis and pain hyperacusis remain incompletely understood, and their relationship with related conditions such as misophonia, tinnitus, and other sound tolerance disorders is still debated. Recent studies suggest that differences in auditory processing, affective and autonomic reactivity, sensory gain, and central neural networks may contribute to distinct hyperacusis phenotypes. title: Rare Neuro‑Inflammatory and Neuromuscular Disorders: Pathways to Precision Therapies
summary: Rare neuro-inflammatory and neuromuscular disorders comprise a diverse group of conditions affecting the central and peripheral nervous systems and represent a major unmet need in neurology. Although clinically and biologically heterogeneous, emerging research is revealing meaningful mechanistic overlap across subsets of these disorders, including immune dysregulation, antibody- and complement-mediated injury, impaired neuromuscular transmission in selected conditions, and interactions between genetic susceptibility and environmental factors. Disorders within this scope include neuromyelitis optica spectrum disorder, myasthenia gravis, multifocal motor neuropathy, autoimmune encephalitides, hereditary neuropathies, rare ataxias, and rare motor neuron diseases. At the same time, these conditions retain important disease-specific features, underscoring the need for both cross-disease perspectives and disorder-specific investigation.

title: Rumination, Negative Cognition, and Cognitive Rigidity in Adolescent Mental Health: Mechanisms, Assessment, and Intervention
summary: Rumination, negative cognition, and cognitive rigidity are each established correlates and prospective predictors of adolescent psychopathology. Rumination, defined as perseverative attention to negative affect and its causes and consequences, predicts the onset, persistence, and recurrence of depressive and anxious symptoms. Negative cognitive content, including negative self-schemas, hopelessness, self-criticism, and interpretive bias, confers vulnerability that is typically activated under stress. Cognitive rigidity refers to difficulty disengaging from prepotent mental sets, shifting attentional or response set, and updating beliefs in light of disconfirming evidence, and has been implicated in depression, obsessive-compulsive and eating-related presentations, and suicidal thinking. Each construct carries independent explanatory and predictive value. Each may also interact with the others, or reflect shared substrates in cognitive control and self-referential processing. title: Senolytics and Senomorphics: Pharmacological Targeting of Cellular Senescence in Brain Aging and Neurodegeneration
summary: Cellular senescence has emerged as an important biological process in brain aging and neurodegeneration. Senescent cells are characterized by stable cell-cycle arrest and persistent metabolic activity, accompanied by the secretion of pro-inflammatory cytokines, chemokines, and matrix-remodeling factors known as the senescence-associated secretory phenotype (SASP). In the central nervous system, this chronic inflammatory state may impair neuronal and glial function, disturb tissue homeostasis, and promote pathological progression in disorders such as Alzheimer’s disease, Parkinson’s disease, tauopathies, and age-related cognitive decline.
image_alt: Senolytics and Senomorphics: Pharmacological Targeting of Cellular Senescence in Brain Aging and Neurodegeneration

title: Targeting Tryptophan Metabolism via Serotonin and Kynurenine Pathways in Neuropsychiatric, Neurological, and Neuro-Oncological Disorders
summary: Tryptophan is a biologically and pharmacologically relevant amino acid involved in multiple pathways that influence central nervous system (CNS) function, immune regulation, tumour biology, and behaviour. Although widely recognized as a precursor of serotonin, most tryptophan is metabolized through the kynurenine pathway, leading to the production of bioactive metabolites such as kynurenic acid, quinolinic acid, and picolinic acid. These metabolites modulate glutamatergic signalling, neuroinflammation, oxidative stress, immune responses, and cellular metabolism.
image_alt: Targeting Tryptophan Metabolism via Serotonin and Kynurenine Pathways in Neuropsychiatric, Neurological, and Neuro-Oncological Disorders

title: The Exercising Brain: Cognitive Neuroscience Perspectives on Physical Activity and Mental Health
summary: The relationship between physical activity and mental health has long been recognized; however, it has only been in recent decades that cognitive neuroscience has begun to elucidate the underlying neural mechanisms. Converging evidence from neuroimaging, electrophysiology, and neurochemical studies indicates that exercise induces profound changes in brain structure and function. These biological processes are increasingly understood to mediate the beneficial effects of physical activity on mood, cognitive function, and resilience to psychological stress. However, despite this progress, the cognitive neuroscience of exercise remains an underexplored frontier, with the precise mechanisms through which physical activity promotes mental health still incompletely understood.

title: Translating Desire – Psychology, Arts, and the Neuroscience of Pleasure
summary: Subjectively and phenomenologically, sexual arousal is a state of pleasure, joy, passion, and bodily excitement, followed by delight, positive exhaustion, and relaxation. Biologically, it involves changes in physiological arousal, the release of hormones and neurotransmitters in the autonomic nervous system and the central nervous system. In dimensional biological emotion theories, it represents the highly positive endpoint in the affective space defined by valence and physiological arousal, triggered by internal or external pleasurable and erotic stimuli. From an evolutionary perspective, the purpose of sexual arousal and pleasure is to prime action disposition for approach or avoidance, thereby supporting survival and driving perceptual, cognitive, and emotional resources through motivational systems that prioritize mating and influence decision-making about sexual behaviors.

summary: Digital monitoring is rapidly reshaping psychiatric research by enabling continuous, real-world assessment of behavior, sleep, activity, social rhythm, and self-reported symptoms through smartphones, wearables, and other connected devices. In contrast to conventional clinic-based evaluations, these approaches offer the possibility of longitudinal, ecologically valid measurement that may improve symptom tracking, relapse detection, and personalized care. Nevertheless, the current evidence base remains methodologically fragmented and has only been partially translated into clinical psychiatry. Many studies remain proof-of-concept, rely on relatively small and selective samples that may increase the risk of overfitting, use short monitoring periods, and adopt heterogeneous sensing, preprocessing, and modeling pipelines. These approaches prioritize self-determination, empowerment, and the promotion of personal recovery. They recognize lived experience as an essential resource both for the development of research and for the provision of care, promoting collaborative approaches and peer support practices. However, clinicians still face many challenges in translating these principles into real-world care and implementing these new practices. title: The hypothalamus as a hub for motivation, reward, and compulsion
summary: The hypothalamus has traditionally been viewed as a regulator of homeostatic functions and survival behaviors. Evidence now identifies the hypothalamus, with the lateral hypothalamus as one key node, as a hub that integrates interoceptive signals with circuits governing motivation, reward, learning, and behavioral selection. Through interactions with mesolimbic, limbic, and cortical networks, hypothalamic circuits shape adaptive behavior and, when dysregulated, can contribute to compulsive responding.

summary: Neural interface technologies have rapidly progressed from experimental tools to clinically relevant systems capable of interacting with the human nervous system. While most current applications focus on symptomatic treatment or functional restoration after disease onset, emerging evidence suggests that neural interfaces may also enable early intervention, functional preservation, and the delayed onset of neurological dysfunction. This paradigm shift has the potential to transform neurological care from reactive treatment toward preventive and disease modifying strategies, working through biological mechanisms such as adaptive neuroplasticity, brain resilience, network reorganization, and functional preservation.

title: Adverse Childhood Experiences and Addiction in Adolescence and Adulthood: from Research to Clinical Practice
summary: Traumatic experiences are recognized as a significant risk factor for the development of substance-related and behavioral addictions in both adolescence and adulthood. Despite extensive research, much work remains to be done to clarify the mechanisms underlying the relationship between trauma and the onset and maintenance of addictive behaviors. It is also necessary to understand the association between trauma and the emerging forms of behavioral or substance addiction observed in recent years. Further research should extend current knowledge to different cultural contexts and promote the development or adaptation of culturally sensitive tools for investigating the trauma–addiction relationship. Moreover, more scientific evidence is needed regarding the effectiveness of prevention and intervention programs, such as psychotherapeutic, social, or pharmacological interventions, for individuals with addictions who have been exposed to traumatic experiences.

title: Extracellular Vesicles in Ocular Physiology, Pharmacology, and Therapeutics
summary: Extracellular vesicle (EV) is a cell-released biological nanoparticle exploiting intrinsic mechanisms for molecular transport in the body. EVs are protected from extracellular degradation and can deliver RNA, DNA, protein, lipid cargo across the blood-brain and blood retinal barriers, making them an attractive carrier for biomolecules and drug delivery to the back of the eye. Recent research has suggested possible use of extracellular vesicles as biomarkers of various hereditary, metabolic and degenerative eye diseases. Currently, there are expected values to use them in the interpretation of disease severity level, progression and treatment responses, and to understand cellular and molecular mechanisms underlying a variety of ocular pathologies. Moreover, extracellular vesicles may open novel treatment options and drug delivery ways.

title: GPCR Receptor Complexes: Emerging Therapeutic Paradigms in Neuropsychiatry
summary: G protein-coupled receptors (GPCRs) represent the largest pharmacologically exploited receptor superfamily in the human genome, accounting for the targets of approximately 35% of all approved drugs. In neuropsychiatry, GPCRs have long underpinned therapeutic strategies across a broad disease spectrum, from dopamine and serotonin receptor-based antipsychotics and antidepressants to opioid receptor-targeting therapies for addiction and pain. Despite this legacy, the conventional “one drug, one receptor” model has shown fundamental limitations: incomplete efficacy, dose-limiting side effects, high inter-individual variability, and persistent treatment resistance continue to burden clinical neuropsychiatric practice.

However, much research remains fragmented across different populations and life stages. We need to consolidate findings to understand how high performance is maintained in athletes, how mobility can be preserved in aging populations (e.g., gait and balance), and how physical activity supports healthy development in youth. Targeting Neuroinflammation in Spinal Cord Injury: From Inflammatory Mechanisms to Pharmacological Interventions
summary: Spinal cord injury (SCI) triggers a devastating secondary neuroinflammatory cascade—driven by microglial activation, immune infiltration, and sustained pro-inflammatory mediator release—that exacerbates tissue damage and impedes neurological recovery. The dynamic balance between pro-inflammatory (M1) and reparative (M2) phenotypes of microglia/macrophages has emerged as a critical determinant of injury outcome. Key signaling pathways, including NF-κB, NLRP3 inflammasome, TLR4, and the CCL2/CCR2 axis, represent promising pharmacological targets. Despite encouraging preclinical advances, effective clinical translation remains limited. This Research Topic aims to bridge mechanistic insights into SCI neuroinflammation with innovative pharmacological interventions, fostering the development of targeted therapies that can ultimately improve functional recovery after SCI.

summary: Growing environmental threats and public health challenges have intensified interest in the psychological determinants of ecological awareness and sustainable living. While social and cultural influences have been widely studied, the role of cognitive functioning in shaping how individuals perceive, evaluate, and respond to environmental and health-related demands remains underexplored. Core cognitive processes, including executive functions, cognitive control, dual-process reasoning, episodic future thinking, attentional bias, and cognitive appraisal, are increasingly recognized as foundational to environmentally responsible decision-making and the adoption of healthy behavioral routines. Alongside these, personality dimensions such as empathy, emotional intelligence, and pro-environmental values operate as important modulators that shape the expression and efficiency of these cognitive mechanisms. title: Transplantation, Immunity, and the Nervous System
summary: Transplantation has transformed the treatment of end-stage organ failure, hematologic disease, and selected immune-mediated disorders. While advances in surgical technique, immunosuppression, and graft monitoring have improved survival, increasing attention is being directed toward the neurological and neurocognitive consequences of transplantation. Transplant recipients may experience cognitive decline, delirium, neuropathy, pain, neuroinflammation, sleep disturbance, mood symptoms, and neurodegenerative changes that arise from complex interactions among systemic inflammation, ischemia-reperfusion injury, immune activation, infection, metabolic dysfunction, rejection, and long-term immunosuppressive therapy. Conversely, neural and neuroimmune pathways may influence graft tolerance, rejection, recovery, and patient-centered outcomes.

title: Visually Guided Walking in Complex Environments: Neural, Biomechanical, and Translational Insights for Neuroprosthetics
summary: Walking is a deceptively complex behavior. Each step depends on the continuous integration of visual input, vestibular and proprioceptive signals, and motor commands distributed across cortical, subcortical, and spinal circuits. Vision plays a particularly central role: it anticipates obstacles, calibrates foot placement, and tunes locomotor control before the foot contacts the ground. When this visuomotor loop is disrupted by injury, neurological disease, aging, limb loss, or the use of a prosthetic or exoskeletal device, gait becomes slower, more variable, and metabolically costly. Mobile brain/body imaging (MoBI) including high-density EEG, fNIRS, EMG, inertial sensors, and motion capture, enables in-situ measurement of the brain and body during complex realistic behaviours. These advances have direct implications for neuroprosthetics: powered prostheses, exoskeletons, and brain–machine interfaces must ultimately operate inside the user’s own visuomotor control loop.

title: Brain-Cancer Interactions in Cancer Hosts
summary: This Research Topic focuses on cancers originating outside the central nervous system across the lifespan (including paediatric, adolescent, and adult populations) and their mechanistic and clinical interactions with the brain, including systemic effects and secondary central nervous system involvement. Emerging evidence demonstrates that cancers outside the central nervous system profoundly influence the cancer host’s brain, producing cognitive, affective, and neural alterations even in the absence of direct metastasis. Cancer-related cognitive impairment (CRCI) affects up to one-third of patients and survivors, with measurable deficits in memory, executive function, and processing speed. Neuroimaging studies reveal structural and functional changes (including gray matter loss, disrupted white matter integrity, and altered connectivity) across multiple cancer types. title: Federated and Privacy-Preserving Learning for Next-Generation Intrusion and Phishing Detection
summary: Machine learning and deep learning have become central to modern intrusion detection and phishing defense, but most deployed systems still rely on centralizing sensitive network and user data to train effective models. This creates real tension between detection performance and data privacy, particularly for organizations bound by regulatory, competitive, or ethical constraints on data sharing. Federated learning offers a path around this trade-off, allowing multiple parties to collaboratively train detection models without exposing raw traffic, logs, or user behavior. Realizing this potential at scale, however, raises open questions around communication efficiency, robustness to non-independent and heterogeneous data across clients, resistance to poisoning and adversarial participants, and how to preserve model interpretability once training is distributed.

summary: In recent years, Virtual Reality has transitioned from niche and technologically limited applications into a powerful, affordable and sophisticated ecosystem for human development. This evolution is driven by the convergence of high-fidelity hardware and the psychological principles of Gamification - the application of game-design elements in non-game contexts. When these two forces meet, they create a unique medium capable of simulating complex realities that are too dangerous, expensive, or physically impossible to recreate in the real world.

title: From Genomes to Neurons: ‘Omics Resources and Discovery in Non-Traditional Models
summary: High-throughput sequencing has democratized genomic research, enabling investigators to generate comprehensive 'omics datasets for virtually any species. Yet the development and curation of robust genomic and transcriptomic resources for non-traditional model organisms remains a significant challenge. Unlike established models such as Drosophila, C. elegans, or Mus musculus, many taxa with extraordinary biological traits, from cave-adapted species with convergent sensory evolution to marine invertebrates with remarkable neural plasticity, still lack well-annotated reference genomes, standardized transcriptomic atlases, or computational pipelines tailored to their biology. Bridging this gap is essential for unlocking comparative and evolutionary approaches to fundamental questions in genetics and neuroscience.

title: The Brain-Body Axis in Neuroscience: Bidirectional Regulation Between the Brain and Peripheral Organs in Health and Disease
summary: The nervous system orchestrates a continuous and dynamic exchange of information with peripheral organs through neural, immune, endocrine, metabolic, vascular, and extracellular-vesicle-mediated signaling. Traditionally, research on brain–organ interactions has been conducted in isolation, focusing on distinct axes such as the lung–brain, heart–brain, liver–brain, ovary–brain, gut–brain, kidney–brain, muscle–brain, and adipose–brain axes. However, mounting evidence reveals that these communication routes are deeply interdependent, with disruptions in one system capable of influencing neuroinflammation, cognition, behavior, and neurological disease progression. Conversely, changes in brain states and neural disorders can modulate the physiology and pathology of peripheral organs by altering autonomic balance, hormonal secretion, immune reactivity, circadian rhythms, and metabolic regulation. title: Single-cell and Multi-omics Insights into Cardio-Cerebral Development and Disease: Genetic Regulation, Redox Signaling and S-nitrosylation
summary: The heart and brain are among the earliest and most metabolically demanding organs in human development. Though historically studied in isolation, both systems are developmentally and functionally intertwined, sharing vascular, inflammatory, metabolic, and genetic mechanisms. Disruption of these shared programs underlies a broad spectrum of cardiocerebral disorders, from congenital heart disease and stroke to Alzheimer’s disease, vascular dementia, and neurodevelopmental conditions.

title: Exploring therapeutic effects of low-frequency sound on psychological and physiological health
summary: An emerging field exploring the psychological and physiological effects of music and of low-frequency sound pulsation on well-being highlights the fundamental role vibration plays in human functioning. Music as cultural cognitive process and as vibratory stimulant affects humans at multiple levels. While music can affect cognitive psychological states, low-frequency pulsation can have effects at the cellular level and is intrinsic to bodily functioning: from heart contractions, to nerve impulses, sensorial perception, speech, and hearing. Physiologically, external sonic pulsations can stimulate bodily response—innate vibrations within the body—to influence haemodynamic, neurological, and musculoskeletal functions. While single frequencies can target region-specific bodily resonant responses, music (complex tones of rhythmic, melodic and harmonic combinations) can influence resonance across multiple areas simultaneously. title: Neuro-immune modulation in immune-mediated neurological disorders: mechanisms, pathways, and therapeutic frontiers
summary: The rapidly advancing field of neuroimmunology has revealed that the nervous, immune, and endocrine systems maintain continuous, bidirectional communication essential for central and peripheral homeostasis. Disruption of this neuro-immune dialogue contributes to the onset and progression of immune-mediated neurological disorders such as multiple sclerosis, autoimmune encephalitis, and neuromyelitis optica spectrum disorders. Meanwhile, neuromodulation technologies—including Deep Brain Stimulation (DBS), Transcranial Magnetic Stimulation (TMS), and Vagus Nerve Stimulation (VNS)—have emerged as promising tools to restore disrupted neural circuits. However, a key frontier remains underexplored: how targeted modulation of neural activity influences peripheral and central immune networks, glial cell behavior, and neuroinflammation. Understanding this interface between electrical or magnetic signaling and immune modulation could reshape therapeutic paradigms for neuroimmunological diseases.

While immunotherapy has transformed cancer care, its efficacy in brain cancers remains limited by a multitude of factors, including restricted immune cell infiltration, immunosuppressive microenvironment, tumor-intrinsic resistance, and treatment-related neurotoxicity. This Research Topic seeks to showcase innovative research and perspectives that leverage emerging technologies to overcome these barriers and advance immunotherapy for brain tumors.

title: Brain Rhythms Across Time Scales: From Chronobioengineering to Clinical Applications
summary: Biological rhythms are ubiquitous in living systems. Cycles and oscillations of different amplitudes and frequencies are not peripheral features: they are central components of command, control, and communication in physiological and behavioral processes. A chronobioengineering approach, combining the principles of biological rhythms with engineering methods and biomedical applications, offers a powerful framework to study, model, and ultimately translate this knowledge into medicine and public health.

Despite these developments, challenges remain in ensuring robustness, interpretability, and clinical reliability of AI systems in real-world diagnostic and therapeutic settings.

title: Mitochondrial Dysfunction and Cerebral Energy Failure in Traumatic Brain Injury
summary: Traumatic brain injury (TBI) encompasses a broad spectrum of neurological insults ranging from mild concussions to repeated head traumas, all of which induce complex metabolic disturbances in the brain. Mitochondria, as the cellular powerhouses, play a critical role in maintaining cerebral energy homeostasis by orchestrating oxidative phosphorylation, the tricarboxylic acid (TCA) cycle, and the electron transport chain (ETC). Following TBI, metabolic disruptions often manifest as glucose dysmetabolism, hyperglycolysis, and mitochondrial malfunctioning, leading to energy deficits that hinder neuronal recovery and neuroplasticity. Recent studies using advanced neuroimaging, metabolomics, and cellular analyses have revealed that impaired mitochondrial quality control, reduced pyruvate dehydrogenase activity, and altered lactate transporter function collectively drive energy failure and contribute to secondary injury cascades such as oxidative stress and neuroinflammation. title: Neuroinflammation and cellular senescence in aging: Mechanisms and therapeutic opportunities
summary: Chronological aging is a major risk factor for many neurodegenerative disorders affecting both the brain and the eye, including Alzheimer’s disease, Parkinson’s disease (PD), retinal degeneration, multiple sclerosis , glaucoma, and age-related macular degeneration, and more. Growing evidence suggests that chronic and dysregulated immune activation plays a central role in the development and progression of these diseases. In the aging brain, retinal and optic nerve tissues, sustained activation of innate immune pathways, glial reactivity, complement signaling, and senescence-associated inflammatory responses can disturb tissue homeostasis and contribute to neurodegeneration. Aging-related cellular stressors, such as impaired glucose metabolism, iron accumulation, lipid peroxidation, mitochondrial dysfunction, and defective autophagy, may further intensify inflammatory signaling and immune-mediated tissue damage. Peromyscus species serve as important natural reservoirs for the agents of several zoonotic diseases—including hantavirus cardiopulmonary syndrome and Lyme disease— rendering suitable models to study both their tolerance of these agents and how they spread to human populations. title: AI for Decoding the Brain: Advances in Neural Signal Interpretation and Cognitive State Modelling
summary: Recent advances in artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) have transformed our ability to decode complex neural signals, opening new frontiers in understanding brain function and enabling practical applications such as brain-computer interfaces, neuroprosthetics, cognitive monitoring, and data security. Sophisticated deep learning architectures, generative models, and multimodal data fusion now allow the extraction of speech, imagery, emotional states, and intent directly from neural activity with unprecedented precision. Despite these breakthroughs, significant challenges remain in data acquisition, algorithmic transparency, and real-time deployment. Integrating heterogeneous data sources, such as fMRI, EEG, MEG, and intracranial recordings, while ensuring robust performance across individuals and tasks requires innovative methods that bridge neuroscience, computational modelling, and clinical translation.

summary: Cancer pain is a multifaceted and often debilitating symptom that significantly impairs the quality of life of patients. Despite advancements in pain management techniques, achieving optimal pain control remains challenging due to the complex nature of cancer pain and the need for highly individualized treatment plans. Artificial Intelligence (AI) presents a promising frontier in this domain, offering novel solutions to enhance the accuracy, efficiency, and personalization of pain management strategies for cancer patients.

title: AI-Assisted International Exchanges: Rethinking the Future of Intercultural Language Education
summary: Language education is undergoing significant changes as digital technologies expand the possibilities for intercultural collaboration and communication beyond physical mobility. Technology Enhanced Language Learning (TELL) practices such as Virtual Exchange (VE)/ Collaborative Online International Learning (COIL) offer students meaningful opportunities to participate in global classrooms, engage with diverse peers, and develop intercultural competences. Within these contexts, Internationalization at Home (IaH) and Internationalization of the Curriculum (IoC) have become central in redefining how institutions provide access to internationalized learning experiences. At the same time, the rapid rise of Artificial Intelligence (AI) adds a new dimension, enabling personalized pathways, adaptive scaffolding, and greater learner autonomy. title: AI-Driven Models Transforming Perceptual Science: Self-Organizing Intelligence for Sensory Cognition
summary: Artificial Intelligence (AI) is transforming perceptual science by offering novel ways to understand sensory perception and cognition. As computational power increases, so does our ability to model and simulate complex human perception processes. Self-organizing AI systems, particularly those utilizing machine learning algorithms like Self-Organizing Maps, have shown promise in mimicking complex perceptual phenomena. These advancements address fundamental questions about how neural mechanisms underlie sensory experiences and highlight ongoing debates concerning the limitations and capabilities of AI in replicating human-like sensory processing. While significant progress has been made in this field, gaps remain, particularly in integrating AI-driven models with empirical findings from neuroscience and psychology.

Recent advancements, including deep learning and machine learning algorithms, supplemented by tools like AlphaFold, have revolutionized our grasp on biomolecular pathways, gene interactions, and protein structures. As an illustration of such advancements, microRNAs have increasingly become prominent as crucial disease biomarkers, providing a new layer of precision in identifying pathophysiological processes.

title: Acute Vertigo and Imbalance
summary: Acute vertigo and imbalance are among the most common yet challenging neurological complaints faced in clinical practice and emergency settings. Patients with sudden onset vertigo, dizziness, and gait instability may harbor a wide range of underlying etiologies - from benign peripheral vestibulopathies to potentially life-threatening central causes, such as posterior circulation stroke. The accurate and timely differentiation between these causes is crucial to preventing both unnecessary investigations and missed diagnoses with serious consequences. Recent studies have highlighted the shortcomings of traditional diagnostic algorithms and have led to the development of new bedside examination techniques and imaging protocols. Despite these advances, significant diagnostic challenges remain, particularly in distinguishing central from peripheral causes. image_alt: Acute Vertigo and Imbalance

title: Adaptive robotics: A computational intelligence perspective
summary: Adaptive robotics marks a fundamental shift in artificial intelligence and intelligent control, positioning robots not just as programmed agents but as autonomous systems capable of learning and evolving within dynamic and uncertain environments. This evolution is pivotal not only for control robustness but also for enabling autonomous agents to exhibit real-time learning and adaptive reasoning. This new generation of robots leverages the integration of artificial intelligence, machine learning, metaheuristic algorithms, and fuzzy logic, enabling continuous interaction among perception, decision-making, and action.
image_alt: Adaptive robotics: A computational intelligence perspective

title: Addressing End-of-Life Challenges: Advancing Person-Centered Care Through Public Health Frameworks
summary: The field of public health has witnessed substantial advancements in medical knowledge and technology, contributing to a notable increase in human life expectancy. While these advancements have extended lives, they have not proportionately enhanced the quality of life, especially in the crucial end-of-life stages. This disparity highlights significant challenges in addressing person-centered care during life-limiting conditions, which often lack adequate attention within broader healthcare goals.
image_alt: Addressing End-of-Life Challenges: Advancing Person-Centered Care Through Public Health Frameworks

title: Advanced Computational Framework and AI Model: Powering Breakthroughs in Neurological Disorders Healthcare
summary: Neurological disorders, including Alzheimer's disease, Parkinson's disease, stroke, multiple sclerosis, epilepsy, etc., represent a leading cause of disability and death worldwide. Their profound complexity, heterogeneity in presentation, and multifaceted pathophysiology pose significant challenges for diagnosis, prognosis, and treatment. Traditional approaches often struggle to capture the intricate dynamics of the nervous system and the individual variability among patients. The advent of high-throughput technologies has generated vast amounts of multimodal data, including neuroimaging, genomics, electrophysiology. This data deluge presents an unprecedented opportunity to redefine neurological care through a precision medicine lens. However, harnessing this potential requires moving beyond conventional analytical methods, necessitating the development of sophisticated, intelligent computational frameworks.

title: Advanced Computational Models for Neural Dynamics and Cognition
summary: Computational neuroscience is a rapidly evolving field that seeks to understand neural dynamics and cognitive processes through mathematical and computational approaches. With advances in neuroimaging, electrophysiological techniques, and machine learning, researchers are now able to explore the intricate relationships between neuronal activity and complex cognitive functions at ever finer spatial and temporal scales. However, despite significant technological progress, deciphering the full mechanisms underlying how the brain generates cognition from dynamic neural activity remains a major scientific challenge. Key questions persist regarding how different scales of neural organization—from single neurons to large-scale brain networks—interact to support learning, memory, perception, and decision-making.

title: Advanced Computational Pathology in Neuroscience: From Algorithms to Clinical Applications
summary: Recent advances in digital pathology and computational imaging have significantly enhanced our ability to analyze complex tissue structures in neuroscience and beyond. High-resolution whole-slide images (WSIs), combined with machine learning and deep learning techniques, are enabling more objective, reproducible, and scalable insights into disease mechanisms. Despite these advancements, traditional computational methods often suffer from limited generalizability, heavy annotation requirements, and a lack of interpretability in clinical contexts.

title: Advanced Technologies in Wireless Neural Interfaces: From Animal Models to Human Applications
summary: Wireless neural recording and neuromodulation represent a rapidly evolving field within bio-engineering, driven by significant advancements in integrated wireless technology over the past decade. These advancements have led to improvements in power consumption, data rates, data integrity, and reliability, which are crucial for the development of wireless neural interfaces. However, the technical design requirements for closed-loop wireless neural interfaces are more stringent compared to their tethered counterparts. Challenges such as limited signal bandwidth, power consumption, battery and power supply designs, transmitter system weight, noise floor, and enclosure design must be addressed. Recent studies have shown promising results with custom mixed-signal integrated device technologies and open-source ARM core processors, which have significantly reduced power consumption. Despite these advancements, there remains a need for further research to optimize these technologies and addres
image_alt: Advanced Technologies in Wireless Neural Interfaces: From Animal Models to Human Applications

title: Advancements in Stress Evaluation and Welfare in Equids
summary: Any condition that disrupts an animal's homeostasis triggers a stress response, which can vary in duration and intensity depending on the stressor. While stress is a natural and protective physiological reaction, prolonged exposure to stress can negatively impact health and welfare, potentially leading to life-threatening conditions. Early identification of stress responses in equids is essential to prevent the onset of stress-related diseases. Chronic stress can predispose horses, donkeys, and mules to abnormal behaviors such as stereotypies, as well as gastrointestinal issues like gastric ulcers, diarrhea, and weight loss.
image_alt: Advancements in Stress Evaluation and Welfare in Equids

title: Advancements in neuroimaging and stimulation for MCI and other neurocognitive disorders
summary: Neurocognitive disorders, including Mild Cognitive Impairment (MCI) and neurodegenerative diseases such as Alzheimer's and related dementias, pose an increasingly significant global health challenge. Early and accurate diagnosis, alongside effective therapeutic interventions, is critical in delaying progression and improving the quality of life for affected individuals.
image_alt: Advancements in neuroimaging and stimulation for MCI and other neurocognitive disorders

title: Advances in Bio-Inspired Robotics: Innovations at the Intersection of Bionics and Cybernetics
summary: This Research Topic is dedicated to the confluence of bionics, cybernetics, and biorobotics—three intertwined fields that leverage biological paradigms to push the boundaries of robotic technology. The fusion of bionics’ structural emulation of biological entities, cybernetics’ feedback and control systems, and biorobotics’ application of these principles to achieve autonomous, adaptive locomotion forms the cornerstone of this research initiative. The aim is to advance the functional integration of these disciplines to create innovative robotic systems resembling biological locomotion and functionality.

title: Advances in Brain PET imaging for quantification of physiological processes
Advances in Computational Modelling of Neurological Diseases
summary: Computational modelling has driven significant advances in our understanding of the complexity of the human nervous system, enabling researchers to capture and explore interactions from the single-cell level to large-scale neuronal networks and behavior. These developments have provided mechanistic insights into nervous system function. In parallel, the advent of modern machine learning and data-driven methods promises to extract subtle relationships from vast neuro-behavioral datasets. However, there remains a scarcity of computational models specifically addressing neurological diseases, limiting our understanding of the underlying pathophysiology and the development of effective, individualized interventions.
image_alt: Advances in Computational Modelling of Neurological Diseases

title: Advances in Design, Modeling, Sensing, and Control for Underwater Bio-inspired Robotic Systems
summary: The Earth's oceans, covering over 70% of the planet's surface, represent a vast frontier for scientific discovery and resource utilization, yet remain largely unexplored. This is due in large part to the formidable challenges the marine environment presents, including complex and unpredictable currents, pervasive turbulence, and extreme hydrostatic pressures. Conversely, millions of years of evolution have endowed aquatic organisms with remarkably efficient and versatile locomotion mechanisms to navigate these very conditions. These biological systems demonstrate superior performance in terms of speed, agility, and stealth. The underlying principles of locomotion, sensing, and neural control found in these creatures offer a rich source of inspiration for developing the next generation of underwater robots. While recent years have witnessed significant progress in applying underwater bio-inspired robots to tasks like deep-sea exploration and environmental monitoring, a substantial perfo

title: Advances in Immune Cell Engineering for Treating Cancers and Other Diseases
summary: The adoptive transfer of chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) T-cells has marked a significant breakthrough in the treatment of haematological malignancies, with promising strides also being made against solid tumors. Recent years have seen considerable advancements in CAR T-cell therapy, driven by the development of cutting-edge gene-engineering tools, innovative CAR constructs such as remote-controlled and logic-gated designs, and strategies aimed at enhancing T-cell persistence, leveraging endogenous immune mechanisms, mitigating T-cell exhaustion, and navigating the complex tumor microenvironment. Additionally, the exploration of CAR T-cell co-engineering techniques and combined treatment methodologies is showing encouraging clinical results, alongside the pioneering use of CAR-engineered macrophages and NK cells.
image_alt: Advances in Immune Cell Engineering for Treating Cancers and Other Diseases

title: Advances in Noninvasive Intracranial Pressure Monitoring Techniques
summary: Intracranial pressure (ICP) monitoring is a critical aspect of managing patients with conditions such as traumatic brain injury, cerebral lesions, and intracranial hypertension. The gold standard for ICP monitoring involves invasive techniques, which are often unavailable in resource-limited settings. Noninvasive techniques, such as measuring the optic nerve sheath diameter (ONSD) with ultrasound or using transcranial Doppler techniques, have been extensively evaluated. However, concerns about bias, variations in ONSD thresholds, and inconsistencies in the literature have limited their routine use in clinical practice. Furthermore, no current noninvasive technology can fully replace invasive ICP monitoring, highlighting a significant gap in the field.

title: Advances in Retinal Treatments: Addressing Visual Impairments and Neuronal Therapies
summary: The retina, a key component of the central nervous system, is ideally suited for advanced neuronal therapies due to its organized layers of neurons and glia, consistent structural organization across vertebrate species, and easily accessible monitoring capabilities.
image_alt: Advances in Retinal Treatments: Addressing Visual Impairments and Neuronal Therapies

title: Advances in Understanding and Combat of Swine Viral Infections
summary: Swine viruses remain a major threat to animal health, food security, and global trade, with substantial economic impacts on pork-producing regions. This article collection spotlights mechanistic and translational advances in the pathogenesis, transmission, and control of key porcine viruses. Particular emphasis is placed on respiratory and systemic pathogens of high consequence—including swine influenza A virus (swIAV), porcine reproductive and respiratory syndrome virus (PRRSV), and African swine fever virus (ASFV)—that drive complex disease ecologies in farm settings. By integrating molecular virology, host–pathogen interactions, and population-level dynamics, the collection aligns with the section’s mission to elucidate infectious agents’ biology and inform evidence-based interventions that curb disease burden across production systems. These converging lines of inquiry are essential to mitigate outbreaks, safeguard animal welfare, and enhance agricultural sustainability.
image_alt: Advances in Understanding and Combat of Swine Viral Infections

summary: This Research Topic is the second volume of the Research Topic "Advances in Vascular Anomalies of Head and Neck Region: From Bench to Bedside". Please see the first volume here .

Advances in the Psychiatric Perspective on the Relationship Between Mental Health in Population with Systemic Diseases: Mechanisms and Therapeutic Innovations
summary: The intricate relationship between the central nervous system (CNS) and systemic diseases, brain-gut-axis, cardiovascular diseases or diabetes, is a rapidly expanding field with profound implications for psychiatry and public mental health. Emerging research highlights that neurological and psychiatric disorders extend beyond the brain, significantly influencing systemic health through direct neural interactions and indirect pathways, including immune dysregulation, metabolic disturbances, and chronic inflammation. Conversely, systemic diseases such as cardiovascular disorders, diabetes, autoimmune diseases, and cancer exert substantial effects on brain function, contributing to psychiatric manifestations such as depression, anxiety, and cognitive impairment.

title: Advancing Agronomy: Robotics and AI in Crop Management and Sustainability
summary: Agronomy is now embracing advanced technologies to enhance the production and management of crops for food, fibre, and energy. Robotics and AI in agronomy are not just about mechanising tasks; they represent a paradigm shift towards precision agriculture, where every aspect of farming, from soil health to plant growth, can be monitored and managed with unprecedented accuracy and efficiency. This approach dovetails with the agronomic emphasis on understanding and manipulating the complex interplay of biotic and abiotic factors in ecosystems. However, integrating such technologies also brings challenges in terms of adaptability, cost, and the need for specialised skills. Furthermore, it raises crucial questions about the future training of agronomists and the role of these technologies in sustainable and equitable food production, especially in the face of global challenges like climate change. This field of study is crucial for propelling agronomy forward, expanding the limits of sustai
image_alt: Advancing Agronomy: Robotics and AI in Crop Management and Sustainability

title: Advancing Marine Mammal Welfare Through Ethological Insights: Behavioral Responses to Stressors in Wild, Rehabilitation, and Managed Care Settings
summary: Marine mammals, as critical sentinel species, reflect the health of our marine ecosystems. However, these remarkable creatures are facing escalating threats in both wild and managed environments. Their welfare is increasingly compromised, necessitating deeper understanding of behavioral responses to environmental stressors.
image_alt: Advancing Marine Mammal Welfare Through Ethological Insights: Behavioral Responses to Stressors in Wild, Rehabilitation, and Managed Care Settings

title: Advancing Nature-Based Solutions to Address the Impacts of Climate Change within the Global South
summary: The Global South encounters significant vulnerabilities to climate change, including severe weather events, biodiversity decline, food and water scarcity. Nature-based solutions (NbS) harness the power of natural ecosystems to address these pressing societal challenges, thereby providing a sustainable and economically viable channels to mitigate climate. Such channels include the restoration of forests, implementation of agroforestry practices, conservation of wetlands, and protection of coastal ecosystems e.g. mangroves, all of which can bolster climate resilience, decrease carbon emissions, enhance human livelihoods and foster the attainment of sustainable development goals. However, the widespread adoption of NbS in the Global South is hindered by challenges such as limited financial resources, poor governance, and knowledge deficits. This special issue aims to highlight how NbS can effectively impact biodiversity conservation through the integration of local knowledge, and the stre
image_alt: Advancing Nature-Based Solutions to Address the Impacts of Climate Change within the Global South

title: Advancing Neurorehabilitation Through Motion Tracking and Virtual Reality: Innovations in Biomechanics and Sensor Technology
summary: The field of neurorehabilitation is undergoing a transformative evolution due to recent breakthroughs in biomechanics and sensor technology. Motion tracking and virtual reality (VR) are at the forefront of these innovations, offering precise and comprehensive tools for analyzing human movement in real-time. These technologies hold great promise for advancing the treatment and assessment of individuals with neurological impairments due to injury or disease, opening the door to new modalities of biomechanical evaluation and therapeutic intervention. While their potential is immense, ongoing research is required to fully integrate these technologies into clinical practice and to rigorously evaluate their impacts through biomechanical analysis.

title: Advancing Personal Health Data Spaces for Enhanced Care Continuity
summary: Personal Health Data Spaces (PHDSs) are emerging as key infrastructures for secure, patient-centred continuity of care. Unlike traditional Electronic Health Records, PHDSs enable individuals to own and control their health information across institutional and national contexts. They provide a unified environment for integrating heterogeneous data sources, including clinical records, genomic data, data from wearable sensors, and patient-reported outcomes. In this way, PHDSs can support patients in managing their health while also enhancing the work of clinicians, researchers, and health system operators.
image_alt: Advancing Personal Health Data Spaces for Enhanced Care Continuity

title: Affective-Sexual Education for Childhood and Adolescence: Psychoeducational Implications from Early Childhood Education to University
summary: Affective-sexual education is a critical component of human development, encompassing knowledge, attitudes, and behaviors related to emotions, relationships, and sexuality. During childhood and adolescence, individuals undergo significant physical, emotional, and social changes that shape their understanding of identity, intimacy, and interpersonal connections. Despite its importance, affective-sexual education often varies greatly across cultural, institutional, and familial contexts, leading to gaps in knowledge and support. Early and comprehensive approaches to this education are essential to promote emotional well-being, prevent misinformation, and foster respectful relationships. This Research Topic aims to explore the psychoeducational implications of affective-sexual education from early childhood to university, addressing its role in promoting holistic development and equipping young people with the tools to navigate complex social and emotional landscapes.

title: Anatomical Variability, Sex-Based Differences, and Age-Specific Therapies in Stroke
summary: Stroke remains a leading cause of death and disability worldwide, but outcomes are far from uniform across patient populations. Traditional stroke research has predominantly centered on generalized mechanisms and treatment strategies. However, mounting evidence highlights that anatomical heterogeneity, sex-linked biological differences, and age-dependent physiological variations critically influence stroke onset, severity, therapeutic responsiveness, and recovery. Recent advances in neuroimaging, molecular biology, and precision medicine now allow us to disentangle these dimensions with greater clarity. For instance, structural vascular variability can alter collateral flow and infarct progression; hormonal influences and chromosomal differences underlie divergent stroke phenotypes between men and women; and age shapes neurovascular resilience, neuroplasticity, and responses to pharmacological or interventional therapies. A systematic exploration of these factors is urgently needed to

title: Animal Models of Anxiety and Depression: Exploring the Underlying Mechanisms of Sex Differences - Volume II
summary: This Research Topic is the second volume of Research Topic "Animal Models of Anxiety and Depression: Exploring the Underlying Mechanisms of Sex Differences". Please see the first volume here .

title: Anthropogenic Disruptions and Changes to Circadian Entrainment Cues and Their Effects on Animals
summary: Circadian rhythms are an evolutionarily adaptive trait most animals possess. The circadian clock allows animals to synchronize their internal environment with the external one to optimize ecological and physiological processes for best survival, reproduction, and well-being. To synchronize these rhythms, animals use entrainment cues from the environment such as light, food availability, temperature, social cues, and other arousal cues. However, humans, through our actions, have very rapidly disrupted and changed these environmental cues. Some instances of these disruptions are light pollution, changes in the seasonal cycles of temperature through climate change, and changes to food availability through habitat destruction. These changes to external cues have the potential to cause desynchrony of the circadian system and disrupt behavioural interactions, physiological homeostatic processes, and potentially even ecosystem processes.
image_alt: Anthropogenic Disruptions and Changes to Circadian Entrainment Cues and Their Effects on Animals

title: Applications of Stable Isotopes in Zooarchaeology and Historical Ecology
summary: Stable isotope analyses of historical archives (e.g., tissues from specimens held in natural history collections and faunal remains recovered from archaeological and subfossil contexts) enable researchers to reconstruct the diets of animals in the past, from previous decades to several millennia. These analyses can provide important information on the historic relationships between humans and animals, but can also offer a temporal perspective on contemporary environmental and ecological issues. For example, researchers are able to compare animal diets under different environmental conditions or levels of anthropogenic disturbance, and hence assess the impacts on different species and predict future trends.
image_alt:

title: Applied Neuroimaging Biomarkers for Neurodegenerative Parkinsonian Disorders
summary: The domain of neuroimaging has recently seen significant advancements in the study of neurodegenerative Parkinsonian disorders. Despite these advances, accurately diagnosing neurodegenerative Parkinsonian conditions like PD or other Parkinsonian syndromes like progressive supranuclear palsy or multisystem atrophy remains a formidable challenge, primarily due to the overlap in clinical symptoms among the disorders. Recent investigations have spotlighted MRI biomarkers, such as unique imaging patterns, as important tools for improved diagnostic precision. However, the pathogenesis of these disorders continues to be a major challenge, creating a pressing need for more accurate diagnostic methodologies and innovative treatment strategies. Current research is expanding into the association between advanced imaging biomarkers, genetic susceptibilities, environmental influences, and the pathology associated with proteins like alpha-synuclein (PD, MSA) or tau (PSP), with the goal to refine cli

title: Applied Psychology of Places: Situating Well-Being in Natural, Built and Digital Environments
summary: Understanding the interplay between human psychology and the environments we inhabit forms a critical research frontier across psychology, neuroscience, and the social sciences. As individuals navigate daily life, both natural and built places act not only as the backdrop but as active agents shaping thoughts, emotions, and behaviors. A growing body of evidence shows that specific settings can enhance psychological and physiological well-being, influence cognitive functions, and foster social connection. This has prompted an increasing appreciation for research grounded in real-world, ecologically valid contexts. However, there remains much to learn about the mechanisms by which diverse environments contribute to well-being, particularly as contemporary society faces rapid changes in urbanization, work, education, and digital simulation of spaces.
image_alt: Applied Psychology of Places: Situating Well-Being in Natural, Built and Digital Environments
